chapters.title: CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde is Surprised
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：雷切尔·林德太太大吃一惊

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived just where the Avonlea main road dipped down into a little hollow, fringed with alders and ladies' eardrops and traversed by a brook that had its source away back in the woods of the old Cuthbert place; it was reputed to be an intricate, headlong brook in its earlier course through those woods, with dark secrets of pool and cascade; but by the time it reached Lynde's Hollow it was a quiet, well-conducted little stream, for not even a brook could run past Mrs. Rachel Lynde's door without due regard for decency and decorum; it probably was conscious that Mrs. Rachel was sitting at her window, keeping a sharp eye on everything that passed, from brooks and children up, and that if she noticed anything odd or out of place she would never rest until she had ferreted out the whys and wherefores thereof.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔·林德太太住在阿文莉主干道拐进一条小山谷的地方，山谷边镶嵌着桤木和倒挂金钟，一条小溪穿流而过。

paragraphs.en: There are plenty of people in Avonlea and out of it, who can attend closely to their neighbor's business by dint of neglecting their own; but Mrs. Rachel Lynde was one of those capable creatures who can manage their own concerns and those of other folks into the bargain. She was a notable housewife; her work was always done and well done; she "ran" the Sewing Circle, helped run the Sunday-school, and was the strongest prop of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. Yet with all this Mrs. Rachel found abundant time to sit for hours at her kitchen window, knitting "cotton warp" quilts—she had knitted sixteen of them, as Avonlea housekeepers were wont to tell in awed voices—and keeping a sharp eye on the main road that crossed the hollow and wound up the steep red hill beyond. Since Avonlea occupied a little triangular peninsula jutting out into the Gulf of St. Lawrence with water on two sides of it, anybody who went out of it or into it had to pass over that hill road and so run the unseen gauntlet of Mrs. Rachel's all-seeing eye.
paragraphs.zh: 埃文利内外有很多人，他们可以通过忽视自己的事情而专注于邻居的事情；但雷切尔·林德夫人是一位能干的人，她能够兼顾自己和其他人的利益。她是一位著名的家庭主妇。她的工作总是完成并且做得很好；她“经营”缝纫圈，帮助经营主日学校，并且是教会援助协会和外国传教辅助机构最有力的支柱。然而，尽管如此，雷切尔夫人还是找到了充足的时间，在厨房的窗前坐了好几个小时，编织“棉经”被子——她已经编织了十六条，正如埃文利的管家们习惯于用敬畏的声音讲述的那样——并密切关注着穿过山谷、蜿蜒通向远处陡峭的红色山丘的主干道。由于埃文利占据了一个伸入圣劳伦斯湾的小三角形半岛，两侧都有水，所以任何人出入该半岛都必须经过那条山路，并接受雷切尔夫人全视之眼看不见的挑战。

paragraphs.en: She was sitting there one afternoon in early June. The sun was coming in at the window warm and bright; the orchard on the slope below the house was in a bridal flush of pinky-white bloom, hummed over by a myriad of bees. Thomas Lynde—a meek little man whom Avonlea people called "Rachel Lynde's husband"—was sowing his late turnip seed on the hill field beyond the barn; and Matthew Cuthbert ought to have been sowing his on the big red brook field away over by Green Gables. Mrs. Rachel knew that he ought because she had heard him tell Peter Morrison the evening before in William J. Blair's store over at Carmody that he meant to sow his turnip seed the next afternoon. Peter had asked him, of course, for Matthew Cuthbert had never been known to volunteer information about anything in his whole life.
paragraphs.zh: 六月初的一个下午，她坐在那里。阳光从窗户照进来，温暖而明亮；房子下面山坡上的果园开满了粉白色的花朵，无数的蜜蜂嗡嗡作响。托马斯·林德——一个温顺的小个子男人，埃文利人称他为“雷切尔·林德的丈夫”——正在谷仓外的山地上播种晚熟的萝卜种子。马修·库斯伯特应该在绿山墙那边的大红溪田里播种。雷切尔夫人知道他应该这样做，因为前一天晚上她在卡莫迪威廉·J·布莱尔的商店里听到他告诉彼得·莫里森，他打算第二天下午播种萝卜种子。当然，彼得问过他，因为马修·库斯伯特一生中从来没有主动提供过任何信息。

paragraphs.en: And yet here was Matthew Cuthbert, at half-past three on the afternoon of a busy day, placidly driving over the hollow and up the hill; moreover, he wore a white collar and his best suit of clothes, which was plain proof that he was going out of Avonlea; and he had the buggy and the sorrel mare, which betokened that he was going a considerable distance. Now, where was Matthew Cuthbert going and why was he going there?
paragraphs.zh: 然而，马修·库斯伯特却在忙碌的一天下午三点半，平静地开车穿过山谷，上山。而且，他穿着白领子，穿着他最好的衣服，这清楚地证明他是要离开埃文利的。他还带着马车和栗色母马，这表明他要走很远的路。现在，马修·库斯伯特要去哪里以及他为什么要去那里？

paragraphs.en: Had it been any other man in Avonlea, Mrs. Rachel, deftly putting this and that together, might have given a pretty good guess as to both questions. But Matthew so rarely went from home that it must be something pressing and unusual which was taking him; he was the shyest man alive and hated to have to go among strangers or to any place where he might have to talk. Matthew, dressed up with a white collar and driving in a buggy, was something that didn't happen often. Mrs. Rachel, ponder as she might, could make nothing of it and her afternoon's enjoyment was spoiled.
paragraphs.zh: 如果是埃文利的其他人，雷切尔夫人巧妙地将这个和那个放在一起，可能会对这两个问题做出很好的猜测。但马修很少离开家，一定是有什么紧迫和不寻常的事情需要他去做。他是世界上最害羞的人，讨厌去陌生人中间或任何可能需要说话的地方。马修一身白领打扮，开着一辆越野车，这种情况并不常见。雷切尔夫人尽管想了想，却什么也没明白，她下午的愉快时光就这样被破坏了。

paragraphs.en: "I'll just step over to Green Gables after tea and find out from Marilla where he's gone and why," the worthy woman finally concluded. "He doesn't generally go to town this time of year and he NEVER visits; if he'd run out of turnip seed he wouldn't dress up and take the buggy to go for more; he wasn't driving fast enough to be going for a doctor. Yet something must have happened since last night to start him off. I'm clean puzzled, that's what, and I won't know a minute's peace of mind or conscience until I know what has taken Matthew Cuthbert out of Avonlea today."
paragraphs.zh: “喝完茶后我就去绿山墙，从玛丽拉那里查出他去了哪里以及为什么，”这位可敬的女人最后总结道。 “每年的这个时候他一般不会进城，也从来不会去拜访；如果他的萝卜籽用完了，他也不会打扮得漂漂亮亮，开着马车去买更多；他的车速不够快，无法去看医生。然而，从昨晚开始，肯定发生了什么事情让他出发了。我很困惑，就是这样，在我知道是什么让马修·库斯伯特离开埃文利之前，我不会知道一分钟的内心平静或良心平静。今天。”

paragraphs.en: Accordingly after tea Mrs. Rachel set out; she had not far to go; the big, rambling, orchard-embowered house where the Cuthberts lived was a scant quarter of a mile up the road from Lynde's Hollow. To be sure, the long lane made it a good deal further. Matthew Cuthbert's father, as shy and silent as his son after him, had got as far away as he possibly could from his fellow men without actually retreating into the woods when he founded his homestead. Green Gables was built at the furthest edge of his cleared land and there it was to this day, barely visible from the main road along which all the other Avonlea houses were so sociably situated. Mrs. Rachel Lynde did not call living in such a place LIVING at all.
paragraphs.zh: 喝完茶后，雷切尔夫人就出发了。她还有不远的路要走；卡斯伯特一家住的那座杂乱无章、果园环绕的大房子距离林德山谷仅不到四分之一英里。可以肯定的是，长长的车道使它更进一步。马修·库斯伯特的父亲和他身后的儿子一样害羞而沉默，在他建立自己的家园时，他已经尽可能远离他的同胞，而没有真正退入树林。绿山墙建在他清理过的土地的最边缘，直到今天，从主干道上几乎看不见它，而沿着这条主干道，所有其他埃文利的房子都位于如此社交的位置。雷切尔·林德夫人根本不称住在这样的地方为“生活”。

paragraphs.en: "It's just STAYING, that's what," she said as she stepped along the deep-rutted, grassy lane bordered with wild rose bushes. "It's no wonder Matthew and Marilla are both a little odd, living away back here by themselves. Trees aren't much company, though dear knows if they were there'd be enough of them. I'd ruther look at people. To be sure, they seem contented enough; but then, I suppose, they're used to it. A body can get used to anything, even to being hanged, as the Irishman said."
paragraphs.zh: “这只是留下来，就是这样，”她一边说，一边沿着布满车辙、长满野玫瑰丛的青草小路行走。 “难怪马修和玛丽拉两个人都住在这儿，都有点奇怪。树木并不是什么陪伴，虽然亲爱的知道，如果有树的话，树就足够了。我宁愿看看人。当然，他们看起来很满足；但是，我想，他们已经习惯了。身体可以适应任何事情，甚至适应被绞死，正如爱尔兰人所说。”

paragraphs.en: With this Mrs. Rachel stepped out of the lane into the backyard of Green Gables. Very green and neat and precise was that yard, set about on one side with great patriarchal willows and the other with prim Lombardies. Not a stray stick nor stone was to be seen, for Mrs. Rachel would have seen it if there had been. Privately she was of the opinion that Marilla Cuthbert swept that yard over as often as she swept her house. One could have eaten a meal off the ground without overbrimming the proverbial peck of dirt.
paragraphs.zh: 说完，雷切尔夫人走出小巷，来到绿山墙的后院。那个院子绿油油的，整洁而精确，一侧种着父权制的大柳树，另一侧种着古板的伦巴第人。没有看到一根杂乱的棍子或石头，因为如果有的话，雷切尔夫人一定会看到的。私下里，她认为玛丽拉·卡斯伯特打扫那个院子的次数和打扫她房子的次数一样多。人们可以在地上吃一顿饭，而不会沾满众所周知的泥土。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel rapped smartly at the kitchen door and stepped in when bidden to do so. The kitchen at Green Gables was a cheerful apartment—or would have been cheerful if it had not been so painfully clean as to give it something of the appearance of an unused parlor. Its windows looked east and west; through the west one, looking out on the back yard, came a flood of mellow June sunlight; but the east one, whence you got a glimpse of the bloom white cherry-trees in the left orchard and nodding, slender birches down in the hollow by the brook, was greened over by a tangle of vines. Here sat Marilla Cuthbert, when she sat at all, always slightly distrustful of sunshine, which seemed to her too dancing and irresponsible a thing for a world which was meant to be taken seriously; and here she sat now, knitting, and the table behind her was laid for supper.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔太太轻快地敲了敲厨房的门，并按照要求走了进去。绿山墙的厨房是一间令人愉悦的公寓——或者说，如果它不是那么干净得令人痛苦，以至于看起来像是一个闲置的客厅，那么厨房本来会很令人愉悦。它的窗户朝东，朝西；六月柔和的阳光透过西边的窗户望向后院。但东边的果园里，你可以瞥见左边果园里盛开的白色樱桃树，还有小溪旁洼地里的细长白桦树，上面爬满了缠结的藤蔓。玛丽拉·库斯伯特坐在这里，当她坐下时，她总是对阳光有些不信任，在她看来，对于一个本应严肃对待的世界来说，这似乎太跳舞了，也是不负责任的事情；她现在坐在这里，正在编织，她身后的桌子上已经摆好了晚饭。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel, before she had fairly closed the door, had taken a mental note of everything that was on that table. There were three plates laid, so that Marilla must be expecting some one home with Matthew to tea; but the dishes were everyday dishes and there was only crab-apple preserves and one kind of cake, so that the expected company could not be any particular company. Yet what of Matthew's white collar and the sorrel mare? Mrs. Rachel was getting fairly dizzy with this unusual mystery about quiet, unmysterious Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人在关上门之前，已经在心里记下了桌子上的所有东西。三个盘子摆好了，玛丽拉一定是在等有人和马修一起回家喝茶。但菜品都是日常菜肴，只有海棠蜜饯和一种糕点，所以预计来的人不可能是什么特定的公司。那么马修的白领和栗色母马呢？雷切尔夫人对这个关于安静、不神秘的绿山墙的不寻常的谜团感到相当头晕。

paragraphs.en: "Good evening, Rachel," Marilla said briskly. "This is a real fine evening, isn't it? Won't you sit down? How are all your folks?"
paragraphs.zh: “晚上好，雷切尔，”玛丽拉轻快地说。 “这真是一个美好的夜晚，不是吗？你不坐下吗？你的家人还好吗？”

paragraphs.en: Something that for lack of any other name might be called friendship existed and always had existed between Marilla Cuthbert and Mrs. Rachel, in spite of—or perhaps because of—their dissimilarity.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉·卡斯伯特和雷切尔夫人之间存在着某种无法用其他名字来称呼的友谊，而且一直存在着，尽管——或者也许正是因为——她们的不同之处。

paragraphs.en: Marilla was a tall, thin woman, with angles and without curves; her dark hair showed some gray streaks and was always twisted up in a hard little knot behind with two wire hairpins stuck aggressively through it. She looked like a woman of narrow experience and rigid conscience, which she was; but there was a saving something about her mouth which, if it had been ever so slightly developed, might have been considered indicative of a sense of humor.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉是个又高又瘦的女人，棱角分明，没有曲线。她的黑发露出了一些灰色的条纹，总是在后面盘成一个坚硬的小结，并用两根金属发夹猛烈地穿过它。她看起来像是一个经验狭隘、良心顽固的女人，她也确实如此。但她的嘴里有一种保留的东西，如果它稍微发达一点，可能会被认为是幽默感的表现。

paragraphs.en: "We're all pretty well," said Mrs. Rachel. "I was kind of afraid YOU weren't, though, when I saw Matthew starting off today. I thought maybe he was going to the doctor's."
paragraphs.zh: “我们都很好，”雷切尔夫人说。 “不过，当我今天看到马修出发时，我有点担心你不是。我想也许他要去医生那里。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla's lips twitched understandingly. She had expected Mrs. Rachel up; she had known that the sight of Matthew jaunting off so unaccountably would be too much for her neighbor's curiosity.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉理解地抽动嘴唇。她原以为雷切尔夫人会起床；但她没想到会这样。她知道，看到马修如此莫名其妙地走开，她的邻居会感到好奇。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, no, I'm quite well although I had a bad headache yesterday," she said. "Matthew went to Bright River. We're getting a little boy from an orphan asylum in Nova Scotia and he's coming on the train tonight."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，不，虽然我昨天头痛得很厉害，但我很好，”她说。 “马修去了布赖特河。我们从新斯科舍省的一家孤儿院得到了一个小男孩，他今晚要乘火车来。”

paragraphs.en: If Marilla had said that Matthew had gone to Bright River to meet a kangaroo from Australia Mrs. Rachel could not have been more astonished. She was actually stricken dumb for five seconds. It was unsupposable that Marilla was making fun of her, but Mrs. Rachel was almost forced to suppose it.
paragraphs.zh: 如果玛丽拉说马修去布赖特河去见一只来自澳大利亚的袋鼠，雷切尔夫人一定会感到更加惊讶。她竟然愣了五秒钟。玛丽拉不可能取笑她，但雷切尔夫人几乎不得不这么认为。

paragraphs.en: "Are you in earnest, Marilla?" she demanded when voice returned to her.
paragraphs.zh: “你是认真的吗，玛丽拉？”当声音恢复时，她问道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, of course," said Marilla, as if getting boys from orphan asylums in Nova Scotia were part of the usual spring work on any well-regulated Avonlea farm instead of being an unheard of innovation.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，当然，”玛丽拉说，仿佛从新斯科舍省的孤儿院接收男孩是任何管理良好的埃文利农场春季工作的一部分，而不是闻所未闻的创新。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel felt that she had received a severe mental jolt. She thought in exclamation points. A boy! Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of all people adopting a boy! From an orphan asylum! Well, the world was certainly turning upside down! She would be surprised at nothing after this! Nothing!
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人感到自己受到了严重的精神震动。她用感叹号想道。一个男孩！玛丽拉·库斯伯特和马修·库斯伯特是所有收养男孩的人中的佼佼者！来自孤儿院！好吧，世界确实天翻地覆了！从此之后，她就不会再感到惊讶了！没有什么！

paragraphs.en: "What on earth put such a notion into your head?" she demanded disapprovingly.
paragraphs.zh: “到底是什么让你产生了这样的想法？”她不以为然地问道。

paragraphs.en: This had been done without her advice being asked, and must perforce be disapproved.
paragraphs.zh: 这是在没有征求她意见的情况下进行的，因此肯定会遭到拒绝。

paragraphs.en: "Well, we've been thinking about it for some time—all winter in fact," returned Marilla. "Mrs. Alexander Spencer was up here one day before Christmas and she said she was going to get a little girl from the asylum over in Hopeton in the spring. Her cousin lives there and Mrs. Spencer has visited here and knows all about it. So Matthew and I have talked it over off and on ever since. We thought we'd get a boy. Matthew is getting up in years, you know—he's sixty—and he isn't so spry as he once was. His heart troubles him a good deal. And you know how desperate hard it's got to be to get hired help. There's never anybody to be had but those stupid, half-grown little French boys; and as soon as you do get one broke into your ways and taught something he's up and off to the lobster canneries or the States. At first Matthew suggested getting a Home boy. But I said 'no' flat to that. 'They may be all right—I'm not saying they're not—but no London street Arabs for me,' I said. 'Give me a native born at least. There'll be a risk, no matter who we get. But I'll feel easier in my mind and sleep sounder at nights if we get a born Canadian.' So in the end we decided to ask Mrs. Spencer to pick us out one when she went over to get her little girl. We heard last week she was going, so we sent her word by Richard Spencer's folks at Carmody to bring us a smart, likely boy of about ten or eleven. We decided that would be the best age—old enough to be of some use in doing chores right off and young enough to be trained up proper. We mean to give him a good home and schooling. We had a telegram from Mrs. Alexander Spencer today—the mail-man brought it from the station—saying they were coming on the five-thirty train tonight. So Matthew went to Bright River to meet him. Mrs. Spencer will drop him off there. Of course she goes on to White Sands station herself."
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我们已经考虑这个问题有一段时间了——事实上整个冬天，”马里拉回答道。 “圣诞节前一天，亚历山大·斯宾塞夫人来到这里，她说春天她要从霍普顿的精神病院接一个小女孩。她的表弟住在那里，斯宾塞夫人来过这里，知道这一切。所以从那时起，马修和我就断断续续地谈论过这件事。我们认为我们会生一个男孩。马修已经好几年了，你知道的——他已经六十岁了——而且他不再像以前那么活泼了。他的心脏有问题。你知道，除了那些愚蠢的、半大的法国小男孩之外，找人帮忙是多么困难；一旦你遇到了一个人，他就会去龙虾罐头厂或美国。对我来说是阿拉伯人，”我说，“至少给我一个土生土长的人，不管我们找谁，都会有风险，但如果我们有一个土生土长的加拿大人，我会感觉更轻松，晚上睡得更香。”所以最后我们决定请斯宾塞夫人去接她的小女儿时帮我们挑选一个。上周我们听说她要走了，所以我们通过卡莫迪的理查德·斯宾塞的人给她发了话，让她给我们带来一个聪明的、可能十岁或十一岁左右的男孩。我们认为这将是最好的年龄——足够大，可以立即做家务，并且足够年轻，可以接受适当的培训。我们的意思是给他一个好的家庭和良好的教育。今天我们收到了亚历山大·斯宾塞夫人的一封电报——邮递员从车站送来的——说他们今晚乘五点三十分的火车来。于是马修就去光明河去见他。斯宾塞夫人会把他送到那里。当然，她自己也会前往白沙车站。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel prided herself on always speaking her mind; she proceeded to speak it now, having adjusted her mental attitude to this amazing piece of news.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人为自己总是说出自己的想法而感到自豪。她调整了心态，适应了这个惊人的消息，现在开始说道。

paragraphs.en: "Well, Marilla, I'll just tell you plain that I think you're doing a mighty foolish thing—a risky thing, that's what. You don't know what you're getting. You're bringing a strange child into your house and home and you don't know a single thing about him nor what his disposition is like nor what sort of parents he had nor how he's likely to turn out. Why, it was only last week I read in the paper how a man and his wife up west of the Island took a boy out of an orphan asylum and he set fire to the house at night—set it ON PURPOSE, Marilla—and nearly burnt them to a crisp in their beds. And I know another case where an adopted boy used to suck the eggs—they couldn't break him of it. If you had asked my advice in the matter—which you didn't do, Marilla—I'd have said for mercy's sake not to think of such a thing, that's what."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，玛丽拉，我就直截了当地告诉你，我认为你正在做一件非常愚蠢的事情——一件冒险的事情，就是这样。你不知道你会得到什么。你把一个陌生的孩子带进你的房子和家里，你对他一无所知，也不知道他的性格是什么样的，也不知道他有什么样的父母，也不知道他可能会变成什么样子。嘿，就在上周，我在报纸上读到一对夫妇如何在西部的艾兰从孤儿院带了一个男孩，他在晚上放火烧了房子——玛丽拉，是故意的——而且我还知道另一个案例，一个被收养的男孩曾经吸过鸡蛋——他们无法阻止他在这件事上——但你没有这样做，玛丽拉——我会说看在仁慈的份上不要考虑这样的事情，就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: This Job's comforting seemed neither to offend nor to alarm Marilla. She knitted steadily on.
paragraphs.zh: 约伯的安慰似乎既没有冒犯玛丽拉，也没有让她惊慌。她稳稳地织着。

paragraphs.en: "I don't deny there's something in what you say, Rachel. I've had some qualms myself. But Matthew was terrible set on it. I could see that, so I gave in. It's so seldom Matthew sets his mind on anything that when he does I always feel it's my duty to give in. And as for the risk, there's risks in pretty near everything a body does in this world. There's risks in people's having children of their own if it comes to that—they don't always turn out well. And then Nova Scotia is right close to the Island. It isn't as if we were getting him from England or the States. He can't be much different from ourselves."
paragraphs.zh: “我不否认你说的有道理，雷切尔。我自己也有一些疑虑。但是马修的态度很糟糕。我看得出来，所以我屈服了。马修很少下定决心做任何事情，所以当他这样做时，我总是觉得我有责任屈服。至于风险，一个人在这个世界上所做的几乎所有事情都存在风险。如果涉及到人们拥有自己的孩子，那么就有风险。那——他们的结果并不总是很好，而且新斯科舍离这个岛很近，我们从英格兰或美国引进他，他和我们没有太大不同。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I hope it will turn out all right," said Mrs. Rachel in a tone that plainly indicated her painful doubts. "Only don't say I didn't warn you if he burns Green Gables down or puts strychnine in the well—I heard of a case over in New Brunswick where an orphan asylum child did that and the whole family died in fearful agonies. Only, it was a girl in that instance."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我希望一切都会好起来。”雷切尔夫人的语气明显地表明了她痛苦的疑虑。 “只是别说我没有警告过你，如果他烧毁了绿山墙，或者在井里放了马钱子碱——我听说过新不伦瑞克省的一个案例，一个孤儿院的孩子这么做了，全家人都在可怕的痛苦中死去。只不过，那是一个女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, we're not getting a girl," said Marilla, as if poisoning wells were a purely feminine accomplishment and not to be dreaded in the case of a boy. "I'd never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, SHE wouldn't shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我们不会生女孩，”玛丽拉说道，仿佛在井里下毒纯粹是女性的成就，对于男孩来说并不可怕。 “我从来没有梦想过要收养一个女孩。我对亚历山大·斯宾塞夫人这样做感到好奇。但在那里，如果她脑子里有这个想法，她就不会犹豫收养整个孤儿院。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel would have liked to stay until Matthew came home with his imported orphan. But reflecting that it would be a good two hours at least before his arrival she concluded to go up the road to Robert Bell's and tell the news. It would certainly make a sensation second to none, and Mrs. Rachel dearly loved to make a sensation. So she took herself away, somewhat to Marilla's relief, for the latter felt her doubts and fears reviving under the influence of Mrs. Rachel's pessimism.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人想留下来，直到马修带着他进口的孤儿回家。但考虑到距离他到达至少还有两个小时，她决定沿着路去罗伯特·贝尔家告诉这个消息。这肯定会引起无与伦比的轰动，而雷切尔夫人非常喜欢引起轰动。于是她就离开了，这多少让马里拉松了口气，因为后者感到在雷切尔夫人的悲观主义影响下，她的怀疑和恐惧又重新燃起。

paragraphs.en: "Well, of all things that ever were or will be!" ejaculated Mrs. Rachel when she was safely out in the lane. "It does really seem as if I must be dreaming. Well, I'm sorry for that poor young one and no mistake. Matthew and Marilla don't know anything about children and they'll expect him to be wiser and steadier that his own grandfather, if so be's he ever had a grandfather, which is doubtful. It seems uncanny to think of a child at Green Gables somehow; there's never been one there, for Matthew and Marilla were grown up when the new house was built—if they ever WERE children, which is hard to believe when one looks at them. I wouldn't be in that orphan's shoes for anything. My, but I pity him, that's what."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，在所有曾经存在或将要存在的事物中！”当雷切尔夫人安全地来到小巷时，她射精了。 “看来我确实是在做梦。嗯，我为那个可怜的年轻人感到抱歉，没有错误。马修和玛丽拉对孩子一无所知，他们会期望他比他自己的祖父更聪明、更稳定，如果他真的有祖父的话，这是值得怀疑的。不知怎么的，在绿山墙想到一个孩子似乎很奇怪；那里从来没有一个孩子，因为马修和玛丽拉在新房子建成时就已经长大了——如果他们曾经是孩子，当你看到他们的时候，我很难相信我不会站在那个孤儿的立场上，但我可怜他，就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: So said Mrs. Rachel to the wild rose bushes out of the fulness of her heart; but if she could have seen the child who was waiting patiently at the Bright River station at that very moment her pity would have been still deeper and more profound.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人对野玫瑰花丛如此说道，心里充满了满足。但如果此刻她能看到那个在光明河车站耐心等待的孩子，她的怜悯就会更加深刻。

chapters.title: CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert is surprised
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：马修·卡斯伯特大吃一惊

paragraphs.en: Matthew Cuthbert and the sorrel mare jogged comfortably over the eight miles to Bright River. It was a pretty road, running along between snug farmsteads, with now and again a bit of balsamy fir wood to drive through or a hollow where wild plums hung out their filmy bloom. The air was sweet with the breath of many apple orchards and the meadows sloped away in the distance to horizon mists of pearl and purple; while
paragraphs.zh: 马修·库斯伯特和栗色母马轻松地慢跑了八英里，到达了布赖特河。这是一条漂亮的路，沿着舒适的农庄蜿蜒而行，时不时可以驶过一些香脂杉木，或者是一个空地，那里野李子挂着薄薄的花朵。空气中弥漫着许多苹果园的芳香，草地在远处倾斜，一直延伸到地平线上的珍珠色和紫色的薄雾。尽管

paragraphs.en: "The little birds sang as if it were
paragraphs.zh: “小鸟们唱着歌，仿佛

paragraphs.en: The one day of summer in all the year."
paragraphs.zh: 一年中唯一的夏天。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew enjoyed the drive after his own fashion, except during the moments when he met women and had to nod to them—for in Prince Edward island you are supposed to nod to all and sundry you meet on the road whether you know them or not.
paragraphs.zh: 马修按照自己的方式享受开车的乐趣，除了在他遇到女人并不得不向她们点头的那一刻之外——因为在爱德华王子岛，你应该向路上遇到的所有人点头，无论你是否认识她们。

paragraphs.en: Matthew dreaded all women except Marilla and Mrs. Rachel; he had an uncomfortable feeling that the mysterious creatures were secretly laughing at him. He may have been quite right in thinking so, for he was an odd-looking personage, with an ungainly figure and long iron-gray hair that touched his stooping shoulders, and a full, soft brown beard which he had worn ever since he was twenty. In fact, he had looked at twenty very much as he looked at sixty, lacking a little of the grayness.
paragraphs.zh: 马修害怕除了玛丽拉和雷切尔夫人之外的所有女人。他有一种不舒服的感觉，那些神秘生物正在偷偷地嘲笑他。他的想法也许是对的，因为他是一个相貌奇特的人物，身材笨拙，铁灰色的长发垂到弯腰的肩膀上，还有从二十岁起就一直留着的浓密柔软的棕色胡须。事实上，他二十岁的样子和六十岁的样子很像，少了一点灰色。

paragraphs.en: When he reached Bright River there was no sign of any train; he thought he was too early, so he tied his horse in the yard of the small Bright River hotel and went over to the station house. The long platform was almost deserted; the only living creature in sight being a girl who was sitting on a pile of shingles at the extreme end. Matthew, barely noting that it WAS a girl, sidled past her as quickly as possible without looking at her. Had he looked he could hardly have failed to notice the tense rigidity and expectation of her attitude and expression. She was sitting there waiting for something or somebody and, since sitting and waiting was the only thing to do just then, she sat and waited with all her might and main.
paragraphs.zh: 当他到达布赖特河时，没有任何火车的迹象。他觉得来得太早了，便把马拴在亮河小旅馆的院子里，朝车站房走去。长长的平台上几乎空无一人。视野中唯一的生物是一个女孩，她坐在最末端的一堆木瓦上。马修几乎没有注意到那是一个女孩，他以最快的速度从她身边侧身而过，没有看她。如果他看的话，他几乎不可能不注意到她的态度和表情中的紧张僵硬和期待。她坐在那里等待某事或某个人，因为此时唯一能做的就是坐着等待，所以她全力以赴地坐着等待。

paragraphs.en: Matthew encountered the stationmaster locking up the ticket office preparatory to going home for supper, and asked him if the five-thirty train would soon be along.
paragraphs.zh: 马修遇到了正在锁着售票处准备回家吃晚饭的站长，他问他五点三十分的火车是否很快就会到站。

paragraphs.en: "The five-thirty train has been in and gone half an hour ago," answered that brisk official. "But there was a passenger dropped off for you—a little girl. She's sitting out there on the shingles. I asked her to go into the ladies' waiting room, but she informed me gravely that she preferred to stay outside. 'There was more scope for imagination,' she said. She's a case, I should say."
paragraphs.zh: “半小时前五点三十分的火车已经进站了。”那位活泼的官员回答道。 “但是有一位乘客为你下车——一个小女孩。她坐在外面的木瓦上。我让她去女士候诊室，但她严肃地告诉我，她更愿意呆在外面。‘有更多的想象空间，’她说。我应该说，她是一个例子。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm not expecting a girl," said Matthew blankly. "It's a boy I've come for. He should be here. Mrs. Alexander Spencer was to bring him over from Nova Scotia for me."
paragraphs.zh: “我没想到会是个女孩。”马修茫然地说。 “我是为了一个男孩而来的。他应该在这里。亚历山大·斯宾塞夫人要为我把他从新斯科舍省带过来。”

paragraphs.en: The stationmaster whistled.
paragraphs.zh: 站长吹了一声口哨。

paragraphs.en: "Guess there's some mistake," he said. "Mrs. Spencer came off the train with that girl and gave her into my charge. Said you and your sister were adopting her from an orphan asylum and that you would be along for her presently. That's all I know about it—and I haven't got any more orphans concealed hereabouts."
paragraphs.zh: “猜猜有什么错误，”他说。 “斯宾塞夫人和那个女孩一起下了火车，把她交给我照顾。说你和你姐姐从孤儿院领养了她，你很快就会跟着她。我只知道这些——而且我没有再在这附近藏匿任何孤儿了。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't understand," said Matthew helplessly, wishing that Marilla was at hand to cope with the situation.
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白，”马修无奈地说，希望玛丽拉能在场应付这种情况。

paragraphs.en: "Well, you'd better question the girl," said the station-master carelessly. "I dare say she'll be able to explain—she's got a tongue of her own, that's certain. Maybe they were out of boys of the brand you wanted."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你还是问问那姑娘吧。”站长漫不经心地说。 “我敢说她能够解释——她有自己的舌头，这是肯定的。也许他们不是你想要的那种类型的男孩。”

paragraphs.en: He walked jauntily away, being hungry, and the unfortunate Matthew was left to do that which was harder for him than bearding a lion in its den—walk up to a girl—a strange girl—an orphan girl—and demand of her why she wasn't a boy. Matthew groaned in spirit as he turned about and shuffled gently down the platform towards her.
paragraphs.zh: 他饿着肚子，兴高采烈地走开，不幸的马修被迫去做比在洞里养狮子更难的事——走到一个女孩面前——一个陌生的女孩——一个孤儿——质问她为什么她不是男孩。马修在心里呻吟了一声，转身轻轻地走下站台，朝她走来。

paragraphs.en: She had been watching him ever since he had passed her and she had her eyes on him now. Matthew was not looking at her and would not have seen what she was really like if he had been, but an ordinary observer would have seen this: A child of about eleven, garbed in a very short, very tight, very ugly dress of yellowish-gray wincey. She wore a faded brown sailor hat and beneath the hat, extending down her back, were two braids of very thick, decidedly red hair. Her face was small, white and thin, also much freckled; her mouth was large and so were her eyes, which looked green in some lights and moods and gray in others.
paragraphs.zh: 自从他经过她身边以来，她就一直看着他，现在她的目光也落在了他身上。马修没有看她，如果他看的话，也不会看到她真正的样子，但一个普通的观察者会看到这个：一个十一岁左右的孩子，穿着一件非常短、非常紧、非常难看的黄灰色皱褶连衣裙。她戴着一顶褪了色的棕色水手帽，帽子下面有两条辫子，辫子很粗，明显是红色的，一直延伸到她的背上。她的脸又小又白又瘦，还有很多雀斑。她的嘴很大，眼睛也很大，在某些光线和情绪下看起来是绿色的，而在另一些光线和情绪下看起来是灰色的。

paragraphs.en: So far, the ordinary observer; an extraordinary observer might have seen that the chin was very pointed and pronounced; that the big eyes were full of spirit and vivacity; that the mouth was sweet-lipped and expressive; that the forehead was broad and full; in short, our discerning extraordinary observer might have concluded that no commonplace soul inhabited the body of this stray woman-child of whom shy Matthew Cuthbert was so ludicrously afraid.
paragraphs.zh: 到目前为止，普通观察者；一个非凡的观察者可能会发现他的下巴非常尖且明显；那双大大的眼睛充满了精神和活力；嘴唇甜美，富有表现力；额头宽阔而饱满；简而言之，我们敏锐的非凡观察者可能会得出结论，这个流浪女婴的身体里没有平凡的灵魂，害羞的马修·库斯伯特对她如此可笑的害怕。

paragraphs.en: Matthew, however, was spared the ordeal of speaking first, for as soon as she concluded that he was coming to her she stood up, grasping with one thin brown hand the handle of a shabby, old-fashioned carpet-bag; the other she held out to him.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，马修却没有先开口，因为当她断定他要向她走来时，她就站了起来，用一只瘦瘦的棕色手抓住了一个破旧的老式地毯袋的把手；然后她就站了起来，用一只瘦瘦的棕色手抓住了一个破旧的老式地毯袋的把手。她把另一只递给了他。

paragraphs.en: "I suppose you are Mr. Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables?" she said in a peculiarly clear, sweet voice. "I'm very glad to see you. I was beginning to be afraid you weren't coming for me and I was imagining all the things that might have happened to prevent you. I had made up my mind that if you didn't come for me to-night I'd go down the track to that big wild cherry-tree at the bend, and climb up into it to stay all night. I wouldn't be a bit afraid, and it would be lovely to sleep in a wild cherry-tree all white with bloom in the moonshine, don't you think? You could imagine you were dwelling in marble halls, couldn't you? And I was quite sure you would come for me in the morning, if you didn't to-night."
paragraphs.zh: “请问您就是绿山墙的马修·卡斯伯特先生吗？”她用一种格外清晰甜美的声音说道。“见到您我真是太高兴了。我刚才还在担心您不会来接我呢，一直在想象各种可能阻止您来的意外。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew had taken the scrawny little hand awkwardly in his; then and there he decided what to do. He could not tell this child with the glowing eyes that there had been a mistake; he would take her home and let Marilla do that. She couldn't be left at Bright River anyhow, no matter what mistake had been made, so all questions and explanations might as well be deferred until he was safely back at Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: 马修笨拙地握着那只骨瘦如柴的小手。当场他就决定要做什么。他无法告诉这个眼睛发光的孩子，这是一个错误；他会带她回家，让玛丽拉去做。无论如何，她不能被留在光明河，无论犯了什么错误，所以所有的问题和解释不妨推迟到他安全返回绿山墙为止。

paragraphs.en: "I'm sorry I was late," he said shyly. "Come along. The horse is over in the yard. Give me your bag."
paragraphs.zh: “很抱歉我迟到了，”他羞涩地说。“跟我来吧，马车就在院子里，把你的包交给我吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I can carry it," the child responded cheerfully. "It isn't heavy. I've got all my worldly goods in it, but it isn't heavy. And if it isn't carried in just a certain way the handle pulls out—so I'd better keep it because I know the exact knack of it. It's an extremely old carpet-bag. Oh, I'm very glad you've come, even if it would have been nice to sleep in a wild cherry-tree. We've got to drive a long piece, haven't we? Mrs. Spencer said it was eight miles. I'm glad because I love driving. Oh, it seems so wonderful that I'm going to live with you and belong to you. I've never belonged to anybody—not really. But the asylum was the worst. I've only been in it four months, but that was enough. I don't suppose you ever were an orphan in an asylum, so you can't possibly understand what it is like. It's worse than anything you could imagine. Mrs. Spencer said it was wicked of me to talk like that, but I didn't mean to be wicked. It's so easy to be wicked without knowing it, isn't it? They were good, you know—the asylum people. But there is so little scope for the imagination in an asylum—only just in the other orphans. It was pretty interesting to imagine things about them—to imagine that perhaps the girl who sat next to you was really the daughter of a belted earl, who had been stolen away from her parents in her infancy by a cruel nurse who died before she could confess. I used to lie awake at nights and imagine things like that, because I didn't have time in the day. I guess that's why I'm so thin—I AM dreadful thin, ain't I? There isn't a pick on my bones. I do love to imagine I'm nice and plump, with dimples in my elbows."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我可以自己拿，”孩子爽朗地回答。“它一点也不重。我所有的家当都在里面了，但这并不沉。要是拿的手势不对，把手就会掉出来——所以我最好自己拿，我知道拿它的诀窍。”

paragraphs.en: With this Matthew's companion stopped talking, partly because she was out of breath and partly because they had reached the buggy. Not another word did she say until they had left the village and were driving down a steep little hill, the road part of which had been cut so deeply into the soft soil, that the banks, fringed with blooming wild cherry-trees and slim white birches, were several feet above their heads.
paragraphs.zh: 说到这里，马修的同伴不再说话了，部分是因为她气喘吁吁，部分是因为他们已经到了马车旁。她没有再说一句话，直到他们离开村庄，驶下一座陡峭的小山，部分道路深深地切入松软的土壤中，河岸上长满了盛开的野樱桃树和纤细的白桦树，距离他们的头顶有几英尺。

paragraphs.en: The child put out her hand and broke off a branch of wild plum that brushed against the side of the buggy.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子伸出手，折断了擦着马车侧面的一根野梅枝。

paragraphs.en: "Isn't that beautiful? What did that tree, leaning out from the bank, all white and lacy, make you think of?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “那不是很漂亮吗？那棵树从岸边探出来，全是白色，有花边，让你想到了什么？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno," said Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道，”马修说。

paragraphs.en: "Why, a bride, of course—a bride all in white with a lovely misty veil. I've never seen one, but I can imagine what she would look like. I don't ever expect to be a bride myself. I'm so homely nobody will ever want to marry me—unless it might be a foreign missionary. I suppose a foreign missionary mightn't be very particular. But I do hope that some day I shall have a white dress. That is my highest ideal of earthly bliss. I just love pretty clothes. And I've never had a pretty dress in my life that I can remember—but of course it's all the more to look forward to, isn't it? And then I can imagine that I'm dressed gorgeously. This morning when I left the asylum I felt so ashamed because I had to wear this horrid old wincey dress. All the orphans had to wear them, you know. A merchant in Hopeton last winter donated three hundred yards of wincey to the asylum. Some people said it was because he couldn't sell it, but I'd rather believe that it was out of the kindness of his heart, wouldn't you? When we got on the train I felt as if everybody must be looking at me and pitying me. But I just went to work and imagined that I had on the most beautiful pale blue silk dress—because when you ARE imagining you might as well imagine something worth while—and a big hat all flowers and nodding plumes, and a gold watch, and kid gloves and boots. I felt cheered up right away and I enjoyed my trip to the Island with all my might. I wasn't a bit sick coming over in the boat. Neither was Mrs. Spencer although she generally is. She said she hadn't time to get sick, watching to see that I didn't fall overboard. She said she never saw the beat of me for prowling about. But if it kept her from being seasick it's a mercy I did prowl, isn't it? And I wanted to see everything that was to be seen on that boat, because I didn't know whether I'd ever have another opportunity. Oh, there are a lot more cherry-trees all in bloom! This Island is the bloomiest place. I just love it already, and I'm so glad I'm going to live here. I've always heard that Prince Edward Island was the prettiest place in the world, and I used to imagine I was living here, but I never really expected I would. It's delightful when your imaginations come true, isn't it? But those red roads are so funny. When we got into the train at Charlottetown and the red roads began to flash past I asked Mrs. Spencer what made them red and she said she didn't know and for pity's sake not to ask her any more questions. She said I must have asked her a thousand already. I suppose I had, too, but how you going to find out about things if you don't ask questions? And what DOES make the roads red?"
paragraphs.zh: “啊，当然是新娘了——穿着白衣，戴着可爱的薄纱的新娘。我从没见过，但我能想象她会是什么样子。我从来没想过自己会成为一名新娘。我太相貌平庸，没有人愿意嫁给我——除非是外国传教士。我想外国传教士可能不会很挑剔。但我确实希望有一天我能拥有一件白色的裙子。那是我对尘世幸福的最高理想。我一生中从来没有穿过漂亮的衣服，但当然更值得期待，不是吗？然后我可以想象，今天早上我离开精神病院时，我感到非常羞愧，因为我不得不穿这件可怕的旧裙子，你知道，去年冬天霍普顿的一位商人向该机构捐赠了三百码的裙子。有人说这是因为他卖不出去，但我宁愿相信这是出于他的善意，不是吗？当我们上了火车时，我觉得好像每个人都在看着我，可怜我，但我只是去上班，想象我穿着最漂亮的淡蓝色丝绸连衣裙——因为当你想象的时候，你不妨想象一些值得的东西——还有一顶满是花朵和点头羽毛的大帽子，还有一只金表和一个孩子。戴上手套和靴子，我立刻感到很高兴，我在船上也没有感到有点不适，尽管她说她没有时间生病，但她说她从来没有看到我在船上徘徊，但如果这能让她不晕船，不是吗？看到那艘船上的一切，因为我不知道我是否还有机会。哦，这里有更多的樱花树，我已经很喜欢它了，我很高兴我要住在这里。我一直听说爱德华王子岛是世界上最美丽的地方，我曾经想象过我会住在这里，但我从未真正想到过，当你的想象成真时，我真的很高兴。不是吗？但是当我们在夏洛特敦上火车时，红色的道路开始闪过，她说她不知道，看在怜悯的份上，不要再问她了。她说我肯定已经问了她一千个问题了，但是如果你不问问题，你怎么能知道这些事情呢？

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno," said Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道，”马修说。

paragraphs.en: "Well, that is one of the things to find out sometime. Isn't it splendid to think of all the things there are to find out about? It just makes me feel glad to be alive—it's such an interesting world. It wouldn't be half so interesting if we know all about everything, would it? There'd be no scope for imagination then, would there? But am I talking too much? People are always telling me I do. Would you rather I didn't talk? If you say so I'll stop. I can STOP when I make up my mind to it, although it's difficult."
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，这是有时需要找出的事情之一。想到所有需要找出的事情不是很棒吗？这让我感到很高兴活着——这是一个如此有趣的世界。如果我们知道一切，那就没有那么有趣了一半，不是吗？那就没有想象的余地了，不是吗？但我是不是说太多了？人们总是告诉我我这样做。你宁愿我不说话吗？如果你这么说我会当我下定决心时，我可以停下来，尽管这很困难。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew, much to his own surprise, was enjoying himself. Like most quiet folks he liked talkative people when they were willing to do the talking themselves and did not expect him to keep up his end of it. But he had never expected to enjoy the society of a little girl. Women were bad enough in all conscience, but little girls were worse. He detested the way they had of sidling past him timidly, with sidewise glances, as if they expected him to gobble them up at a mouthful if they ventured to say a word. That was the Avonlea type of well-bred little girl. But this freckled witch was very different, and although he found it rather difficult for his slower intelligence to keep up with her brisk mental processes he thought that he "kind of liked her chatter." So he said as shyly as usual:
paragraphs.zh: 令马修自己惊讶的是，他玩得很开心。像大多数安静的人一样，他喜欢健谈的人，因为他们愿意自己说话，并且不希望他继续说下去。但他没想到会喜欢和一个小女孩交往。凭良心来说，女人已经够糟糕的了，但小女孩更糟糕。他讨厌他们胆怯地从他身边侧过，斜视着，仿佛他们期待着如果他们敢说一句话，他就会把他们吞掉。那是埃文利类型的有教养的小女孩。但这个长着雀斑的女巫却非常不同，尽管他发现自己较慢的智力很难跟上她敏捷的思维过程，但他认为自己“有点喜欢她的喋喋不休”。于是他像往常一样害羞地说：

paragraphs.en: "Oh, you can talk as much as you like. I don't mind."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，你想讲多少就讲多少，我不介意。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm so glad. I know you and I are going to get along together fine. It's such a relief to talk when one wants to and not be told that children should be seen and not heard. I've had that said to me a million times if I have once. And people laugh at me because I use big words. But if you have big ideas you have to use big words to express them, haven't you?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我很高兴。我知道你和我会相处得很好。当一个人想说话的时候，而不是被告知孩子应该被看到而不是被听到，这是一种解脱。如果我有一次，我已经被这样说过一百万次了。人们会嘲笑我，因为我使用了大词。但是如果你有伟大的想法，你就必须使用大词来表达它们，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, that seems reasonable," said Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “现在看来，这似乎很合理，”马修说。

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Spencer said that my tongue must be hung in the middle. But it isn't—it's firmly fastened at one end. Mrs. Spencer said your place was named Green Gables. I asked her all about it. And she said there were trees all around it. I was gladder than ever. I just love trees. And there weren't any at all about the asylum, only a few poor weeny-teeny things out in front with little whitewashed cagey things about them. They just looked like orphans themselves, those trees did. It used to make me want to cry to look at them. I used to say to them, 'Oh, you POOR little things! If you were out in a great big woods with other trees all around you and little mosses and Junebells growing over your roots and a brook not far away and birds singing in you branches, you could grow, couldn't you? But you can't where you are. I know just exactly how you feel, little trees.' I felt sorry to leave them behind this morning. You do get so attached to things like that, don't you? Is there a brook anywhere near Green Gables? I forgot to ask Mrs. Spencer that."
paragraphs.zh: “斯宾塞夫人说我的舌头必须悬在中间。但事实并非如此——它牢牢地固定在一端。斯宾塞夫人说你的地方叫绿山墙。我问了她所有的情况。她说周围都是树。我比以前更高兴了。我只是喜欢树。精神病院里根本没有树，只有一些可怜的小东西在前面，周围有粉刷成白色的小东西。他们看起来就像孤儿，那些树曾经让我想哭，“哦，可怜的小东西！如果你在一片大树林里，周围长着小苔藓和六月铃，不远处有一条小溪，你的树枝上唱歌，你可以生长，不是吗？但我不知道你在哪里，小树。”今天早上我把他们抛在了身后，我感到很遗憾。你确实对这样的事情很执着，不是吗？绿山墙附近有小溪吗？我忘了问斯宾塞夫人这个问题了。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, yes, there's one right below the house."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，是的，房子下面就有一个。”

paragraphs.en: "Fancy. It's always been one of my dreams to live near a brook. I never expected I would, though. Dreams don't often come true, do they? Wouldn't it be nice if they did? But just now I feel pretty nearly perfectly happy. I can't feel exactly perfectly happy because—well, what color would you call this?"
paragraphs.zh: “太棒了。住在小溪附近一直是我的梦想之一。不过，我从来没想过我会实现。梦想并不经常成真，不是吗？如果成真不是很好吗？但现在我感觉几乎完全幸福。我不能感到完全幸福，因为——好吧，你会管它叫什么颜色？”

paragraphs.en: She twitched one of her long glossy braids over her thin shoulder and held it up before Matthew's eyes. Matthew was not used to deciding on the tints of ladies' tresses, but in this case there couldn't be much doubt.
paragraphs.zh: 她把一根光滑的长辫子拉过她瘦弱的肩膀，把它举到马修眼前。马修不习惯决定女士头发的颜色，但在这种情况下，毫无疑问。

paragraphs.en: "It's red, ain't it?" he said.
paragraphs.zh: “是红色的，不是吗？”他说。

paragraphs.en: The girl let the braid drop back with a sigh that seemed to come from her very toes and to exhale forth all the sorrows of the ages.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩把辫子放下来，叹了口气，仿佛从脚趾间发出来，吐出了多年来所有的悲伤。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, it's red," she said resignedly. "Now you see why I can't be perfectly happy. Nobody could who has red hair. I don't mind the other things so much—the freckles and the green eyes and my skinniness. I can imagine them away. I can imagine that I have a beautiful rose-leaf complexion and lovely starry violet eyes. But I CANNOT imagine that red hair away. I do my best. I think to myself, 'Now my hair is a glorious black, black as the raven's wing.' But all the time I KNOW it is just plain red and it breaks my heart. It will be my lifelong sorrow. I read of a girl once in a novel who had a lifelong sorrow but it wasn't red hair. Her hair was pure gold rippling back from her alabaster brow. What is an alabaster brow? I never could find out. Can you tell me?"
paragraphs.zh: “是的，它是红色的，”她无奈地说。 “现在你明白为什么我不能完全幸福了。没有人有红头发。我不太介意其他的事情——雀斑、绿眼睛和我的瘦骨嶙峋。我可以想象它们消失。我可以想象我有美丽的玫瑰叶肤色和可爱的紫罗兰色眼睛。但我无法想象那红头发消失。我尽力了。我对自己说，“现在我的头发是光亮的黑色，黑得像乌鸦的翅膀。但我一直知道它只是普通的红色，这让我心碎。这将是我一生的悲伤。我曾经在一本小说里读到过一个女孩，她一生充满悲伤，但那不是红头发。她的头发是纯金色的，从她雪花石膏般的额头上垂下来。什么是雪花石膏眉？我始终无法找到答案。你能告诉我吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I'm afraid I can't," said Matthew, who was getting a little dizzy. He felt as he had once felt in his rash youth when another boy had enticed him on the merry-go-round at a picnic.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，恐怕我不能，”马修说，他有点头晕。他的感觉就像他年轻时鲁莽的时候，在野餐时另一个男孩引诱他坐旋转木马时的感觉一样。

paragraphs.en: "Well, whatever it was it must have been something nice because she was divinely beautiful. Have you ever imagined what it must feel like to be divinely beautiful?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，不管是什么，那一定是件好事，因为她美丽非凡。你有没有想象过，美丽非凡是什么感觉？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, no, I haven't," confessed Matthew ingenuously.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，不，我没有，”马修坦率地承认。

paragraphs.en: "I have, often. Which would you rather be if you had the choice—divinely beautiful or dazzlingly clever or angelically good?"
paragraphs.zh: “我经常这样。如果你有选择的话，你更愿意成为哪一个——神圣的美丽、耀眼的聪明还是天使般的善良？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I—I don't know exactly."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我——我不太清楚。”

paragraphs.en: "Neither do I. I can never decide. But it doesn't make much real difference for it isn't likely I'll ever be either. It's certain I'll never be angelically good. Mrs. Spencer says—oh, Mr. Cuthbert! Oh, Mr. Cuthbert!! Oh, Mr. Cuthbert!!!"
paragraphs.zh: “我也不知道。我永远无法决定。但这并没有什么太大的区别，因为我也不太可能成为那样的人。可以肯定的是，我永远不会成为天使般的好人。斯宾塞夫人说——哦，卡斯伯特先生！哦，卡斯伯特先生！！哦，卡斯伯特先生！！！”

paragraphs.en: That was not what Mrs. Spencer had said; neither had the child tumbled out of the buggy nor had Matthew done anything astonishing. They had simply rounded a curve in the road and found themselves in the "Avenue."
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞夫人可不是这么说的。孩子既没有从马车上摔下来，马修也没有做出任何令人惊讶的事情。他们只是绕过了道路的一个弯道，发现自己来到了“大道”。

paragraphs.en: The "Avenue," so called by the Newbridge people, was a stretch of road four or five hundred yards long, completely arched over with huge, wide-spreading apple-trees, planted years ago by an eccentric old farmer. Overhead was one long canopy of snowy fragrant bloom. Below the boughs the air was full of a purple twilight and far ahead a glimpse of painted sunset sky shone like a great rose window at the end of a cathedral aisle.
paragraphs.zh: 纽布里奇人所谓的“大道”是一段四五百码长的路，完全呈拱形，上面种植着巨大而广泛的苹果树，这些苹果树是多年前由一位古怪的老农种植的。头顶上是一长长的树冠，开满了雪白的芬芳花朵。树枝下方的空气中弥漫着紫色的暮色，前方远处瞥见彩绘落日的天空，像大教堂过道尽头的一扇巨大的玫瑰窗一样闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: Its beauty seemed to strike the child dumb. She leaned back in the buggy, her thin hands clasped before her, her face lifted rapturously to the white splendor above. Even when they had passed out and were driving down the long slope to Newbridge she never moved or spoke. Still with rapt face she gazed afar into the sunset west, with eyes that saw visions trooping splendidly across that glowing background. Through Newbridge, a bustling little village where dogs barked at them and small boys hooted and curious faces peered from the windows, they drove, still in silence. When three more miles had dropped away behind them the child had not spoken. She could keep silence, it was evident, as energetically as she could talk.
paragraphs.zh: 它的美丽似乎让孩子目瞪口呆。她靠在马车上，瘦弱的双手紧握在身前，脸上欣喜若狂地仰望着头顶白色的光彩。即使他们昏倒了，沿着长长的斜坡开车前往新桥，她也没有动弹，也没有说话。她仍然全神贯注地凝视着远处的夕阳西下，眼睛里看到了在发光的背景上华丽地游行的景象。他们开车穿过纽布里奇，这是一个熙熙攘攘的小村庄，那里有狗对着他们狂吠，小男孩们在叫，好奇的面孔从车窗里张望。当他们身后又走了三英里时，孩子还是没有说话。很明显，她可以保持沉默，就像她可以说话一样充满活力。

paragraphs.en: "I guess you're feeling pretty tired and hungry," Matthew ventured to say at last, accounting for her long visitation of dumbness with the only reason he could think of. "But we haven't very far to go now—only another mile."
paragraphs.zh: “我猜你感觉很累又饿了，”马修最后大胆地说，用他能想到的唯一原因解释了她长时间的沉默。 “但我们现在还没有走多远——只剩下一英里了。”

paragraphs.en: She came out of her reverie with a deep sigh and looked at him with the dreamy gaze of a soul that had been wondering afar, star-led.
paragraphs.zh: 她深深地叹了口气，从沉思中回过神来，用一颗星辰引导的灵魂在远方徘徊的梦幻般的目光看着他。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Mr. Cuthbert," she whispered, "that place we came through—that white place—what was it?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，卡斯伯特先生，”她低声说道，“我们经过的那个地方——那个白色的地方——那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, you must mean the Avenue," said Matthew after a few moments' profound reflection. "It is a kind of pretty place."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你指的是大街，”马修沉思了一会儿后说道。 “这是一个美丽的地方。”

paragraphs.en: "Pretty? Oh, PRETTY doesn't seem the right word to use. Nor beautiful, either. They don't go far enough. Oh, it was wonderful—wonderful. It's the first thing I ever saw that couldn't be improved upon by imagination. It just satisfies me here"—she put one hand on her breast—"it made a queer funny ache and yet it was a pleasant ache. Did you ever have an ache like that, Mr. Cuthbert?"
paragraphs.zh: “漂亮？哦，漂亮这个词似乎不太合适。也不漂亮。它们还不够远。哦，太棒了——太棒了。这是我见过的第一件无法通过想象来改进的东西。它在这里让我很满足”——她把一只手放在胸前——“它产生了一种奇怪而有趣的疼痛，但又是一种愉快的疼痛。你有过这样的疼痛吗，卡斯伯特先生？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I just can't recollect that I ever had."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，我只是记不起我曾经有过。”

paragraphs.en: "I have it lots of time—whenever I see anything royally beautiful. But they shouldn't call that lovely place the Avenue. There is no meaning in a name like that. They should call it—let me see—the White Way of Delight. Isn't that a nice imaginative name? When I don't like the name of a place or a person I always imagine a new one and always think of them so. There was a girl at the asylum whose name was Hepzibah Jenkins, but I always imagined her as Rosalia DeVere. Other people may call that place the Avenue, but I shall always call it the White Way of Delight. Have we really only another mile to go before we get home? I'm glad and I'm sorry. I'm sorry because this drive has been so pleasant and I'm always sorry when pleasant things end. Something still pleasanter may come after, but you can never be sure. And it's so often the case that it isn't pleasanter. That has been my experience anyhow. But I'm glad to think of getting home. You see, I've never had a real home since I can remember. It gives me that pleasant ache again just to think of coming to a really truly home. Oh, isn't that pretty!"
paragraphs.zh: “我有很多时间——每当我看到任何皇家美丽的东西时。但他们不应该称那个可爱的地方为大道。这样的名字没有任何意义。他们应该称它——让我想想——白色的快乐之路。这不是一个很好的富有想象力的名字吗？当我不喜欢一个地方或一个人的名字时，我总是想象一个新的名字，并且总是这样想他们。精神病院里有一个女孩，她的名字叫赫普兹巴·詹金斯，但我总是其他人可能会称这个地方为“欢乐大道”，但我很高兴，也很抱歉，因为这段旅程结束后，可能还会有更愉快的事情发生，但无论如何，这都是我的经历。我很高兴想到要回家，你看，自从我记事起，我就再也没有过真正的家了。哦，这不是很美好吗？

paragraphs.en: They had driven over the crest of a hill. Below them was a pond, looking almost like a river so long and winding was it. A bridge spanned it midway and from there to its lower end, where an amber-hued belt of sand-hills shut it in from the dark blue gulf beyond, the water was a glory of many shifting hues—the most spiritual shadings of crocus and rose and ethereal green, with other elusive tintings for which no name has ever been found. Above the bridge the pond ran up into fringing groves of fir and maple and lay all darkly translucent in their wavering shadows. Here and there a wild plum leaned out from the bank like a white-clad girl tip-toeing to her own reflection. From the marsh at the head of the pond came the clear, mournfully-sweet chorus of the frogs. There was a little gray house peering around a white apple orchard on a slope beyond and, although it was not yet quite dark, a light was shining from one of its windows.
paragraphs.zh: 他们已经驶过山顶。他们下面是一个池塘，看起来几乎就像一条河，又长又蜿蜒。一座桥横跨在中间，从那里一直延伸到低端，那里有一条琥珀色的沙丘带将它与远处的深蓝色海湾隔开，海水呈现出多种变幻色彩的光彩——最有灵性的番红花色、玫瑰色和空灵的绿色，还有其他难以捉摸、至今无人知晓的色彩。桥上的池塘一直延伸到边缘的冷杉和枫树丛中，在它们摇曳的阴影中呈黑色半透明。岸边时不时地探出一株野梅，像一个白衣少女踮着脚尖对着自己的倒影。池塘头的沼泽地里传来青蛙们清脆、哀伤、甜美的合唱。有一座灰色的小房子，俯瞰着远处斜坡上的白色苹果园，虽然天还没有完全黑，但它的一扇窗户却透出一丝灯光。

paragraphs.en: "That's Barry's pond," said Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “那是巴里的池塘，”马修说。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I don't like that name, either. I shall call it—let me see—the Lake of Shining Waters. Yes, that is the right name for it. I know because of the thrill. When I hit on a name that suits exactly it gives me a thrill. Do things ever give you a thrill?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我也不喜欢这个名字。我会叫它——让我想想——闪亮水域湖。是的，这就是它的正确名字。我知道是因为兴奋。当我想到一个完全适合的名字时，它会让我兴奋。有什么事情能让你兴奋吗？”

paragraphs.en: Matthew ruminated.
paragraphs.zh: 马修沉思着。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, yes. It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds. I hate the look of them."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，是的。看到这些丑陋的白色幼虫在黄瓜床上爬行，总是让我感到兴奋。我讨厌它们的样子。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I don't think that can be exactly the same kind of a thrill. Do you think it can? There doesn't seem to be much connection between grubs and lakes of shining waters, does there? But why do other people call it Barry's pond?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我不认为这可以是完全相同的刺激。你认为可以吗？幼虫和波光粼粼的湖泊之间似乎没有太多联系，不是吗？但是为什么其他人称它为巴里池塘？”

paragraphs.en: "I reckon because Mr. Barry lives up there in that house. Orchard Slope's the name of his place. If it wasn't for that big bush behind it you could see Green Gables from here. But we have to go over the bridge and round by the road, so it's near half a mile further."
paragraphs.zh: “我想是因为巴里先生就住在那栋房子里。果园坡是他那地方的名字。如果不是后面那棵大灌木，你从这里就能看到绿山墙。但我们必须过桥，绕着路走，所以又走了近半英里。”

paragraphs.en: "Has Mr. Barry any little girls? Well, not so very little either—about my size."
paragraphs.zh: “巴里先生有小女孩吗？嗯，也不是很小——和我差不多大。”

paragraphs.en: "He's got one about eleven. Her name is Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “他有一个大约十一点。她的名字叫戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh!" with a long indrawing of breath. "What a perfectly lovely name!"
paragraphs.zh: “哦！”长长地吸气。 “多么可爱的名字啊！”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno. There's something dreadful heathenish about it, seems to me. I'd ruther Jane or Mary or some sensible name like that. But when Diana was born there was a schoolmaster boarding there and they gave him the naming of her and he called her Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道。在我看来，这有一些可怕的异教色彩。我宁愿选择简或玛丽或类似的合理名字。但是当戴安娜出生时，有一位寄宿在那里的校长，他们给了他名字，他称她为戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: "I wish there had been a schoolmaster like that around when I was born, then. Oh, here we are at the bridge. I'm going to shut my eyes tight. I'm always afraid going over bridges. I can't help imagining that perhaps just as we get to the middle, they'll crumple up like a jack-knife and nip us. So I shut my eyes. But I always have to open them for all when I think we're getting near the middle. Because, you see, if the bridge DID crumple up I'd want to SEE it crumple. What a jolly rumble it makes! I always like the rumble part of it. Isn't it splendid there are so many things to like in this world? There we're over. Now I'll look back. Good night, dear Lake of Shining Waters. I always say good night to the things I love, just as I would to people. I think they like it. That water looks as if it was smiling at me."
paragraphs.zh: “那么，我希望我出生时身边就有这样一位校长。哦，我们在桥上。我要闭上眼睛。我总是害怕过桥。我情不自禁地想象，也许当我们到达中间时，它们会像折刀一样崩溃并咬住我们。所以我闭上眼睛。但当我认为我们已经接近中间时，我总是必须睁开眼睛。因为，你看，如果桥确实塌了，我想看看它发出的隆隆声，这世界上有那么多值得喜欢的东西，这不是很美妙吗？现在我回想一下，晚安，亲爱的闪亮水域。我总是对我所爱的人说晚安，就像我对人们微笑一样。我。”

paragraphs.en: When they had driven up the further hill and around a corner Matthew said:
paragraphs.zh: 当他们驶上更远的山坡并拐过一个拐角时，马修说：

paragraphs.en: "We're pretty near home now. That's Green Gables over—"
paragraphs.zh: “我们现在已经离家很近了。《绿山墙》就这样结束了——”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, don't tell me," she interrupted breathlessly, catching at his partially raised arm and shutting her eyes that she might not see his gesture. "Let me guess. I'm sure I'll guess right."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，别告诉我，”她气喘吁吁地打断道，抓住他半举起的手臂，闭上眼睛以免看到他的动作。 “让我猜一下。我相信我会猜对的。”

paragraphs.en: She opened her eyes and looked about her. They were on the crest of a hill. The sun had set some time since, but the landscape was still clear in the mellow afterlight. To the west a dark church spire rose up against a marigold sky. Below was a little valley and beyond a long, gently-rising slope with snug farmsteads scattered along it. From one to another the child's eyes darted, eager and wistful. At last they lingered on one away to the left, far back from the road, dimly white with blossoming trees in the twilight of the surrounding woods. Over it, in the stainless southwest sky, a great crystal-white star was shining like a lamp of guidance and promise.
paragraphs.zh: 她睁开眼睛，环顾四周。他们在山顶上。太阳已经落山有一段时间了，但在柔和的余光中，风景仍然清晰。西边，一座黑色的教堂尖顶在万寿菊色的天空下拔地而起。下面是一个小山谷，后面是一个缓慢上升的长斜坡，沿着斜坡散布着舒适的农庄。孩子的目光从一个地方扫到另一个地方，充满渴望和渴望。最后，他们在左边的一处徘徊，远离道路，在周围树林的暮色中，树木绽放出淡淡的白色。在它的上方，在无污染的西南天空中，一颗巨大的水晶白色星星像一盏指引和希望的灯一样闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: "That's it, isn't it?" she said, pointing.
paragraphs.zh: “就是这样，不是吗？”她指着说。

paragraphs.en: Matthew slapped the reins on the sorrel's back delightedly.
paragraphs.zh: 马修高兴地把缰绳拍在酢浆草背上。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, you've guessed it! But I reckon Mrs. Spencer described it so's you could tell."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，你已经猜到了！但我认为斯宾塞夫人描述了它，所以你可以看出来。”

paragraphs.en: "No, she didn't—really she didn't. All she said might just as well have been about most of those other places. I hadn't any real idea what it looked like. But just as soon as I saw it I felt it was home. Oh, it seems as if I must be in a dream. Do you know, my arm must be black and blue from the elbow up, for I've pinched myself so many times today. Every little while a horrible sickening feeling would come over me and I'd be so afraid it was all a dream. Then I'd pinch myself to see if it was real—until suddenly I remembered that even supposing it was only a dream I'd better go on dreaming as long as I could; so I stopped pinching. But it IS real and we're nearly home."
paragraphs.zh: “不，她没有——真的没有。她说的可能只是其他大多数地方的事。我根本不知道它是什么样子。但我一看到它，就觉得那是家。哦，看来我一定是在梦中。你知道吗，我的手臂从肘部以上一定是青一块紫一块的，因为我今天掐了自己很多次。每隔一会儿，一种可怕的、令人作呕的感觉就会袭上心头，我会很害怕。”然后我掐自己一下，看看这是否是真的——直到我突然想起，即使这只是一个梦，我也最好尽可能地继续做梦，所以我不再掐自己了，但它是真的，我们快到家了。”

paragraphs.en: With a sigh of rapture she relapsed into silence. Matthew stirred uneasily. He felt glad that it would be Marilla and not he who would have to tell this waif of the world that the home she longed for was not to be hers after all. They drove over Lynde's Hollow, where it was already quite dark, but not so dark that Mrs. Rachel could not see them from her window vantage, and up the hill and into the long lane of Green Gables. By the time they arrived at the house Matthew was shrinking from the approaching revelation with an energy he did not understand. It was not of Marilla or himself he was thinking of the trouble this mistake was probably going to make for them, but of the child's disappointment. When he thought of that rapt light being quenched in her eyes he had an uncomfortable feeling that he was going to assist at murdering something—much the same feeling that came over him when he had to kill a lamb or calf or any other innocent little creature.
paragraphs.zh: 她欣喜若狂地叹了口气，又陷入了沉默。马修不安地动了动。他很高兴，是玛丽拉，而不是他，必须告诉这个世界上的流浪儿，她所渴望的家毕竟不是她的。他们开车经过林德山谷，那里已经很黑了，但还没有黑到雷切尔夫人从窗外看不到他们的地步，然后上了山，进入了绿山墙的长巷。当他们到达房子时，马修正以一种他无法理解的能量来躲避即将到来的启示。他想到的不是这个错误可能给他们带来的麻烦，而是孩子的失望。当他想到她眼中的全神贯注的光芒被熄灭时，他有一种不舒服的感觉，他要协助谋杀什么东西——就像他不得不杀死一只羔羊、小牛或任何其他无辜的小动物时所产生的感觉一样。

paragraphs.en: The yard was quite dark as they turned into it and the poplar leaves were rustling silkily all round it.
paragraphs.zh: 他们走进院子时，院子里一片漆黑，周围的白杨树叶丝般沙沙作响。

paragraphs.en: "Listen to the trees talking in their sleep," she whispered, as he lifted her to the ground. "What nice dreams they must have!"
paragraphs.zh: “听听树木在睡梦中说话，”当他把她抱到地上时，她低声说道。 “他们一定做了多么美好的梦啊！”

paragraphs.en: Then, holding tightly to the carpet-bag which contained "all her worldly goods," she followed him into the house.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，她紧紧抓住装着“她所有世俗物品”的地毯袋，跟着他进了屋。

chapters.title: CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert is Surprised
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：玛丽拉·卡斯伯特大吃一惊

paragraphs.en: Marilla came briskly forward as Matthew opened the door. But when her eyes fell of the odd little figure in the stiff, ugly dress, with the long braids of red hair and the eager, luminous eyes, she stopped short in amazement.
paragraphs.zh: 马修打开门时，玛丽拉轻快地走了过来。但当她的目光落到那个奇怪的小身影上时，她穿着僵硬丑陋的衣服，留着长长的红发辫子，眼睛热切而明亮，她惊讶地停了下来。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew Cuthbert, who's that?" she ejaculated. "Where is the boy?"
paragraphs.zh: “马修·库斯伯特，那是谁？”她射精了。 “那男孩在哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: "There wasn't any boy," said Matthew wretchedly. "There was only HER."
paragraphs.zh: “没有男孩。”马修可怜兮兮地说。 “只有她。”

paragraphs.en: He nodded at the child, remembering that he had never even asked her name.
paragraphs.zh: 他对孩子点点头，记得自己从来没有问过她的名字。

paragraphs.en: "No boy! But there MUST have been a boy," insisted Marilla. "We sent word to Mrs. Spencer to bring a boy."
paragraphs.zh: “没有男孩！但一定有一个男孩，”玛丽拉坚持说。 “我们通知斯宾塞夫人带一个男孩来。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, she didn't. She brought HER. I asked the station-master. And I had to bring her home. She couldn't be left there, no matter where the mistake had come in."
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，她没有。她把她带来了。我问了站长。我必须把她带回家。她不能被留在那儿，不管错误出在哪里。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, this is a pretty piece of business!" ejaculated Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，这真是一笔不错的生意！”玛丽拉射精了。

paragraphs.en: During this dialogue the child had remained silent, her eyes roving from one to the other, all the animation fading out of her face. Suddenly she seemed to grasp the full meaning of what had been said. Dropping her precious carpet-bag she sprang forward a step and clasped her hands.
paragraphs.zh: 在这段对话中，孩子一直保持沉默，她的眼睛从一个地方转到另一个地方，所有的生气都从她脸上消失了。突然间，她似乎明白了刚才所说的话的全部含义。她扔下珍贵的地毯包，向前迈出一步，紧握双手。

paragraphs.en: "You don't want me!" she cried. "You don't want me because I'm not a boy! I might have expected it. Nobody ever did want me. I might have known it was all too beautiful to last. I might have known nobody really did want me. Oh, what shall I do? I'm going to burst into tears!"
paragraphs.zh: “你不要我了！”她哭了。 “你不想要我，因为我不是男孩！我可能已经预料到了。从来没有人想要我。我可能知道这一切都太美丽了，无法持久。我可能知道没有人真正想要我。哦，我该怎么办？我要哭了！”

paragraphs.en: Burst into tears she did. Sitting down on a chair by the table, flinging her arms out upon it, and burying her face in them, she proceeded to cry stormily. Marilla and Matthew looked at each other deprecatingly across the stove. Neither of them knew what to say or do. Finally Marilla stepped lamely into the breach.
paragraphs.zh: 她确实泪流满面。她坐在桌边的椅子上，伸出双臂，把脸埋在里面，放声大哭起来。玛丽拉和马修隔着炉子不屑地看着对方。他们都不知道该说什么或该做什么。最后，玛丽拉一瘸一拐地走进了缺口。

paragraphs.en: "Well, well, there's no need to cry so about it."
paragraphs.zh: “好了好了，不用哭那么多了。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, there IS need!" The child raised her head quickly, revealing a tear-stained face and trembling lips. "YOU would cry, too, if you were an orphan and had come to a place you thought was going to be home and found that they didn't want you because you weren't a boy. Oh, this is the most TRAGICAL thing that ever happened to me!"
paragraphs.zh: “是的，有这个需要！”孩子迅速抬起头，露出一张满是泪痕的脸和颤抖的嘴唇。 “如果你是一个孤儿，来到一个你以为会回家的地方，却发现他们不想要你，因为你不是男孩，你也会哭。哦，这是发生在我身上最悲惨的事情！”

paragraphs.en: Something like a reluctant smile, rather rusty from long disuse, mellowed Marilla's grim expression.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉冷酷的表情像是一种不情愿的微笑，由于长期未使用而显得有些生锈。

paragraphs.en: "Well, don't cry any more. We're not going to turn you out-of-doors to-night. You'll have to stay here until we investigate this affair. What's your name?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，别再哭了。今晚我们不会把你赶出家门。你必须留在这里，直到我们调查这件事。你叫什么名字？”

paragraphs.en: The child hesitated for a moment.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子犹豫了片刻。

paragraphs.en: "Will you please call me Cordelia?" she said eagerly.
paragraphs.zh: “你可以叫我科迪莉亚吗？”她急切地说。

paragraphs.en: "Call you Cordelia? Is that your name?"
paragraphs.zh: “叫你科迪莉亚吧？这是你的名字吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No-o-o, it's not exactly my name, but I would love to be called Cordelia. It's such a perfectly elegant name."
paragraphs.zh: “不-o-o，这不完全是我的名字，但我很想被称为Cordelia。这是一个非常优雅的名字。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't know what on earth you mean. If Cordelia isn't your name, what is?"
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道你到底是什么意思。如果你的名字不是科迪莉亚，那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley," reluctantly faltered forth the owner of that name, "but, oh, please do call me Cordelia. It can't matter much to you what you call me if I'm only going to be here a little while, can it? And Anne is such an unromantic name."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，”这个名字的主人不情愿地支吾其词，“但是，哦，请叫我科迪莉亚。如果我只在这里待一会儿，你怎么称呼我并不重要，不是吗？而且安妮这个名字实在是太不浪漫了。”

paragraphs.en: "Unromantic fiddlesticks!" said the unsympathetic Marilla. "Anne is a real good plain sensible name. You've no need to be ashamed of it."
paragraphs.zh: “不浪漫的小提琴手！”毫无同情心的玛丽拉说道。 “安妮是一个真正善良、简单、明智的名字。你不必为此感到羞耻。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm not ashamed of it," explained Anne, "only I like Cordelia better. I've always imagined that my name was Cordelia—at least, I always have of late years. When I was young I used to imagine it was Geraldine, but I like Cordelia better now. But if you call me Anne please call me Anne spelled with an E."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我并不为此感到羞耻，”安妮解释道，“只是我更喜欢科迪莉亚。我一直想象我的名字叫科迪莉亚——至少，最近几年我总是这样。年轻的时候，我常常想象它是杰拉尔丁，但现在我更喜欢科迪莉亚了。但是如果你叫我安妮，请叫我拼写为 E 的安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "What difference does it make how it's spelled?" asked Marilla with another rusty smile as she picked up the teapot.
paragraphs.zh: “它的拼写有什么区别？”玛丽拉拿起茶壶，脸上又带着生锈的微笑问道。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, it makes SUCH a difference. It LOOKS so much nicer. When you hear a name pronounced can't you always see it in your mind, just as if it was printed out? I can; and A-n-n looks dreadful, but A-n-n-e looks so much more distinguished. If you'll only call me Anne spelled with an E I shall try to reconcile myself to not being called Cordelia."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，这真是天壤之别。它看起来好多了。当你听到一个名字被念出来时，你不能总是在你的脑海中看到它，就像它被打印出来一样吗？我可以；A-n-n看起来很可怕，但A-n-n-e看起来更尊贵。如果你只叫我安妮，拼写一个E，我会尽力让自己不叫科迪莉亚。”

paragraphs.en: "Very well, then, Anne spelled with an E, can you tell us how this mistake came to be made? We sent word to Mrs. Spencer to bring us a boy. Were there no boys at the asylum?"
paragraphs.zh: “那好吧，安妮拼写了一个E，你能告诉我们这个错误是怎么造成的吗？我们派人通知斯宾塞夫人给我们带来一个男孩。精神病院里没有男孩吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, yes, there was an abundance of them. But Mrs. Spencer said DISTINCTLY that you wanted a girl about eleven years old. And the matron said she thought I would do. You don't know how delighted I was. I couldn't sleep all last night for joy. Oh," she added reproachfully, turning to Matthew, "why didn't you tell me at the station that you didn't want me and leave me there? If I hadn't seen the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters it wouldn't be so hard."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，是的，有很多。但是斯宾塞太太明确地说，你想要一个十一岁左右的女孩。女护士长说她认为我会做。你不知道我有多高兴。我昨晚高兴得睡不着觉。哦，”她转向马修，责备地补充道，“你为什么不在车站告诉我你不想要我，然后把我留在那里呢？如果我没有看到白色之路的话喜悦和闪亮水域湖就不会这么难了。”

paragraphs.en: "What on earth does she mean?" demanded Marilla, staring at Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “她到底是什么意思？”玛丽拉盯着马修问道。

paragraphs.en: "She—she's just referring to some conversation we had on the road," said Matthew hastily. "I'm going out to put the mare in, Marilla. Have tea ready when I come back."
paragraphs.zh: “她——她只是指我们在路上的一些谈话。”马修急忙说道。 “我要出去把母马放进去，玛丽拉。我回来时，请准备好茶。”

paragraphs.en: "Did Mrs. Spencer bring anybody over besides you?" continued Marilla when Matthew had gone out.
paragraphs.zh: “除了你之外，斯宾塞夫人还带了其他人过来吗？”马修出去后，玛丽拉继续说道。

paragraphs.en: "She brought Lily Jones for herself. Lily is only five years old and she is very beautiful and had nut-brown hair. If I was very beautiful and had nut-brown hair would you keep me?"
paragraphs.zh: “她给自己带来了莉莉琼斯。莉莉只有五岁，她很漂亮，有一头坚果棕色的头发。如果我​​很漂亮，有一头坚果棕色的头发，你会留下我吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I'll lay it and your bag on the hall table."
paragraphs.zh: “不。我们想要一个男孩在农场里帮助马修。女孩对我们来说没有任何用处。摘下你的帽子。我会把它和你的包放在大厅的桌子上。”

paragraphs.en: Anne took off her hat meekly. Matthew came back presently and they sat down to supper. But Anne could not eat. In vain she nibbled at the bread and butter and pecked at the crab-apple preserve out of the little scalloped glass dish by her plate. She did not really make any headway at all.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮温顺地摘下了帽子。马修很快回来了，他们坐下来吃晚饭。但安妮不能吃饭。她徒劳地啃着面包和黄油，又从盘子旁边的小扇形玻璃盘里啄食海棠蜜饯。她根本没有取得任何进展。

paragraphs.en: "You're not eating anything," said Marilla sharply, eying her as if it were a serious shortcoming. Anne sighed.
paragraphs.zh: “你什么也没吃，”玛丽拉尖锐地说，看着她，仿佛这是一个严重的缺点。安妮叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "I can't. I'm in the depths of despair. Can you eat when you are in the depths of despair?"
paragraphs.zh: “我不能，我在绝望的深渊里，你在绝望的深渊里还能吃东西吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I've never been in the depths of despair, so I can't say," responded Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有陷入过绝望的深渊，所以我不能说，”玛丽拉回答道。

paragraphs.en: "Weren't you? Well, did you ever try to IMAGINE you were in the depths of despair?"
paragraphs.zh: “不是吗？那么，你有没有尝试过想象自己正处于绝望的深渊？”

paragraphs.en: "No, I didn't."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我没有。”

paragraphs.en: "Then I don't think you can understand what it's like. It's very uncomfortable feeling indeed. When you try to eat a lump comes right up in your throat and you can't swallow anything, not even if it was a chocolate caramel. I had one chocolate caramel once two years ago and it was simply delicious. I've often dreamed since then that I had a lot of chocolate caramels, but I always wake up just when I'm going to eat them. I do hope you won't be offended because I can't eat. Everything is extremely nice, but still I cannot eat."
paragraphs.zh: “那我想你无法理解那是什么感觉。这确实是一种非常不舒服的感觉。当你试图吃东西时，喉咙里突然出现一个肿块，你无法吞咽任何东西，即使是巧克力焦糖。我两年前吃过一次巧克力焦糖，它真的很好吃。从那以后我经常梦见我有很多巧克力焦糖，但我总是在要吃它们的时候醒来。我真的希望你不会被冒犯了，因为我不能吃东西。一切都非常好，但我仍然不能吃东西。”

paragraphs.en: "I guess she's tired," said Matthew, who hadn't spoken since his return from the barn. "Best put her to bed, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “我猜她累了，”马修说，自从他从谷仓回来后，他就没有说过话。 “最好让她上床睡觉，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla had been wondering where Anne should be put to bed. She had prepared a couch in the kitchen chamber for the desired and expected boy. But, although it was neat and clean, it did not seem quite the thing to put a girl there somehow. But the spare room was out of the question for such a stray waif, so there remained only the east gable room. Marilla lighted a candle and told Anne to follow her, which Anne spiritlessly did, taking her hat and carpet-bag from the hall table as she passed. The hall was fearsomely clean; the little gable chamber in which she presently found herself seemed still cleaner.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉一直在想应该把安妮安放在哪里睡觉。她在厨房里为心仪的男孩准备了一张沙发。不过，虽然干净整洁，但把一个女孩子放在那里似乎不太合适。但对于这样一个流浪儿来说，空余房间是不可能的，所以只剩下东山墙的房间了。玛丽拉点燃一支蜡烛，让安妮跟着她，安妮无精打采地照做了，在她经过时，从大厅的桌子上拿走了她的帽子和地毯袋。大厅干净得可怕。她现在发现自己所在的小山墙房间看起来更加干净。

paragraphs.en: Marilla set the candle on a three-legged, three-cornered table and turned down the bedclothes.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉把蜡烛放在一张三腿三角的桌子上，然后把床单翻下来。

paragraphs.en: "I suppose you have a nightgown?" she questioned.
paragraphs.zh: “我想你有睡衣吧？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: Anne nodded.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮点点头。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I have two. The matron of the asylum made them for me. They're fearfully skimpy. There is never enough to go around in an asylum, so things are always skimpy—at least in a poor asylum like ours. I hate skimpy night-dresses. But one can dream just as well in them as in lovely trailing ones, with frills around the neck, that's one consolation."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我有两件。是收容所的女护士为我做的。它们极其简陋。收容所里永远都没有足够的东西，所以东西总是简陋的——至少在像我们这样的贫穷的收容所里是这样。我讨厌简陋的睡裙。但一个人穿着它们可以做梦，就像穿着可爱的拖尾睡裙一样，脖子上有褶边，这是一种安慰。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I'll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren't trust you to put it out yourself. You'd likely set the place on fire."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，尽快脱掉衣服，然后去睡觉。几分钟后我会回来拿蜡烛。我不敢相信你会自己把它扑灭。你很可能会放火烧了这个地方。”

paragraphs.en: When Marilla had gone Anne looked around her wistfully. The whitewashed walls were so painfully bare and staring that she thought they must ache over their own bareness. The floor was bare, too, except for a round braided mat in the middle such as Anne had never seen before. In one corner was the bed, a high, old-fashioned one, with four dark, low-turned posts. In the other corner was the aforesaid three-corner table adorned with a fat, red velvet pin-cushion hard enough to turn the point of the most adventurous pin. Above it hung a little six-by-eight mirror. Midway between table and bed was the window, with an icy white muslin frill over it, and opposite it was the wash-stand. The whole apartment was of a rigidity not to be described in words, but which sent a shiver to the very marrow of Anne's bones. With a sob she hastily discarded her garments, put on the skimpy nightgown and sprang into bed where she burrowed face downward into the pillow and pulled the clothes over her head. When Marilla came up for the light various skimpy articles of raiment scattered most untidily over the floor and a certain tempestuous appearance of the bed were the only indications of any presence save her own.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉走后，安妮若有所思地环顾四周。粉刷成白色的墙壁光秃秃的，令人痛苦，她想它们一定会因为自己的光秃秃而感到痛苦。地板也光秃秃的，除了中间有一个安妮以前从未见过的圆形编织垫。角落里放着一张床，一张高高的老式床，有四根深色的低矮床柱。另一个角落里是前面提到的三角桌，上面装饰着一个厚重的红色天鹅绒针垫，其硬度足以转动最冒险的针尖。上面挂着一面六乘八的小镜子。桌子和床之间是窗户，上面覆盖着冰冷的白色平纹细布褶边，对面是盥洗台。整个公寓僵硬得无法用言语来形容，但却让安妮感到骨髓里一阵颤抖。她抽泣着，连忙脱掉衣服，穿上那件暴露的睡衣，跳到床上，把脸埋进枕头里，把衣服拉到头上。当玛丽拉走到灯光处时，地板上散落着各种破烂的衣服，床上的样子有些暴躁，这是除了她自己的床之外还有其他人存在的唯一迹象。

paragraphs.en: She deliberately picked up Anne's clothes, placed them neatly on a prim yellow chair, and then, taking up the candle, went over to the bed.
paragraphs.zh: 她故意拿起安妮的衣服，整齐地放在一张古板的黄色椅子上，然后拿起蜡烛，走到了床边。

paragraphs.en: "Good night," she said, a little awkwardly, but not unkindly.
paragraphs.zh: “晚安，”她说，有点尴尬，但并不不友善。

paragraphs.en: Anne's white face and big eyes appeared over the bedclothes with a startling suddenness.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮苍白的脸和大眼睛突然出现在床单上。

paragraphs.en: "How can you call it a GOOD night when you know it must be the very worst night I've ever had?" she said reproachfully.
paragraphs.zh: “当你知道这一定是我度过的最糟糕的夜晚时，你怎么能称之为美好的夜晚呢？”她责备地说。

paragraphs.en: Then she dived down into invisibility again.
paragraphs.zh: 然后她再次潜入隐形状态。

paragraphs.en: Marilla went slowly down to the kitchen and proceeded to wash the supper dishes. Matthew was smoking—a sure sign of perturbation of mind. He seldom smoked, for Marilla set her face against it as a filthy habit; but at certain times and seasons he felt driven to it and them Marilla winked at the practice, realizing that a mere man must have some vent for his emotions.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉慢慢地走到厨房，开始洗晚饭的盘子。马修在抽烟——这是精神错乱的明显表现。他很少抽烟，因为玛丽拉坚决反对抽烟，认为这是一种肮脏的习惯。但在某些时候和某些季节，他感到有动力这样做，而玛丽拉则对这种做法眨眼，意识到一个普通的男人必须有一些发泄自己情绪的机会。

paragraphs.en: "Well, this is a pretty kettle of fish," she said wrathfully. "This is what comes of sending word instead of going ourselves. Richard Spencer's folks have twisted that message somehow. One of us will have to drive over and see Mrs. Spencer tomorrow, that's certain. This girl will have to be sent back to the asylum."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，这真是一锅漂亮的鱼，”她愤怒地说。 “这就是发消息而不是我们自己去的后果。理查德·斯宾塞的家人不知何故扭曲了这条信息。我们中的一个人明天必须开车过去见斯宾塞夫人，这是肯定的。这个女孩将不得不被送回精神病院。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I suppose so," said Matthew reluctantly.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我想是的，”马修不情愿地说。

paragraphs.en: "You SUPPOSE so! Don't you know it?"
paragraphs.zh: “你是这么认为的！你不知道吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, she's a real nice little thing, Marilla. It's kind of a pity to send her back when she's so set on staying here."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，她是一个非常好的小东西，玛丽拉。当她如此决定留在这里时，将她送回去有点遗憾。”

paragraphs.en: "Matthew Cuthbert, you don't mean to say you think we ought to keep her!"
paragraphs.zh: “马修·库斯伯特，你并不是说你认为我们应该保留她！”

paragraphs.en: Marilla's astonishment could not have been greater if Matthew had expressed a predilection for standing on his head.
paragraphs.zh: 如果马修表示喜欢倒立的话，马里拉会更加惊讶。

paragraphs.en: "Well, now, no, I suppose not—not exactly," stammered Matthew, uncomfortably driven into a corner for his precise meaning. "I suppose—we could hardly be expected to keep her."
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，现在，不，我想不是——不完全是，”马修结结巴巴地说，他因为自己的确切意思而感到不舒服地被逼到了角落里。 “我想——我们很难指望留住她。”

paragraphs.en: "I should say not. What good would she be to us?"
paragraphs.zh: “我应该说不会。她对我们有什么好处呢？”

paragraphs.en: "We might be some good to her," said Matthew suddenly and unexpectedly.
paragraphs.zh: “我们可能会对她好一些，”马修突然出乎意料地说。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew Cuthbert, I believe that child has bewitched you! I can see as plain as plain that you want to keep her."
paragraphs.zh: “马修·库斯伯特，我相信那个孩子已经迷住了你！我很明显地看出你想留住她。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, she's a real interesting little thing," persisted Matthew. "You should have heard her talk coming from the station."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，她是一个非常有趣的小东西，”马修坚持说。 “你应该听听她从车站传来的谈话。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, she can talk fast enough. I saw that at once. It's nothing in her favour, either. I don't like children who have so much to say. I don't want an orphan girl and if I did she isn't the style I'd pick out. There's something I don't understand about her. No, she's got to be despatched straight-way back to where she came from."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，她说话速度够快的。我立刻就看出了这一点。这对她也没什么好处。我不喜欢有那么多话要说的孩子。我不想要一个孤女，如果我想要的话，她也不是我会挑选的风格。我有一些不明白的地方。不行，她必须被直接送回她来的地方。”

paragraphs.en: "I could hire a French boy to help me," said Matthew, "and she'd be company for you."
paragraphs.zh: “我可以雇一个法国男孩来帮助我，”马修说，“她会陪着你。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm not suffering for company," said Marilla shortly. "And I'm not going to keep her."
paragraphs.zh: “我不需要陪伴，”玛丽拉简短地说。 “而且我不会留着她。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, it's just as you say, of course, Marilla," said Matthew rising and putting his pipe away. "I'm going to bed."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，当然，正如你所说的，玛丽拉，”马修站起身来，把烟斗收了起来。 “我要去睡觉了。”

paragraphs.en: To bed went Matthew. And to bed, when she had put her dishes away, went Marilla, frowning most resolutely. And up-stairs, in the east gable, a lonely, heart-hungry, friendless child cried herself to sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 马修上床睡觉了。玛丽拉把盘子收好后，就上床睡觉了，眉头皱得很坚决。楼上的东山墙里，一个孤独、心饥渴、没有朋友的孩子哭着睡着了。

chapters.title: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：绿山墙的清晨

paragraphs.en: It was broad daylight when Anne awoke and sat up in bed, staring confusedly at the window through which a flood of cheery sunshine was pouring and outside of which something white and feathery waved across glimpses of blue sky.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮醒来时，已经是大白天了，她从床上坐起来，困惑地盯着窗户，窗外洒满了明快的阳光，窗外有一些白色的、羽毛般的东西在蓝天上飘荡。

paragraphs.en: For a moment she could not remember where she was. First came a delightful thrill, as something very pleasant; then a horrible remembrance. This was Green Gables and they didn't want her because she wasn't a boy!
paragraphs.zh: 一时间她记不起自己身在何处。首先是一种令人愉快的兴奋，这是一件非常令人愉快的事情。然后是一个可怕的回忆。这是绿山墙，他们不想要她，因为她不是男孩！

paragraphs.en: But it was morning and, yes, it was a cherry-tree in full bloom outside of her window. With a bound she was out of bed and across the floor. She pushed up the sash—it went up stiffly and creakily, as if it hadn't been opened for a long time, which was the case; and it stuck so tight that nothing was needed to hold it up.
paragraphs.zh: 但那是早晨，是的，她窗外有一棵盛开的樱花树。她一跃下床，穿过地板。她把窗带推了起来——它僵硬地、嘎吱作响地升起来，好像已经很长时间没有打开了，事实确实如此；而且它粘得很紧，不需要任何东西来支撑它。

paragraphs.en: Anne dropped on her knees and gazed out into the June morning, her eyes glistening with delight. Oh, wasn't it beautiful? Wasn't it a lovely place? Suppose she wasn't really going to stay here! She would imagine she was. There was scope for imagination here.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮跪下，凝视着六月的早晨，她的眼睛闪烁着喜悦的光芒。哦，那不是很漂亮吗？那不是一个可爱的地方吗？假设她真的不打算留在这里！她会想象她是。这里有想象的空间。

paragraphs.en: A huge cherry-tree grew outside, so close that its boughs tapped against the house, and it was so thick-set with blossoms that hardly a leaf was to be seen. On both sides of the house was a big orchard, one of apple-trees and one of cherry-trees, also showered over with blossoms; and their grass was all sprinkled with dandelions. In the garden below were lilac-trees purple with flowers, and their dizzily sweet fragrance drifted up to the window on the morning wind.
paragraphs.zh: 外面长着一棵巨大的樱桃树，离得很近，树枝轻拍着房子，花朵茂密，几乎看不到一片叶子。房子的两边都是一个大果园，一棵苹果树，一棵樱桃树，也开满了鲜花。他们的草地上撒满了蒲公英。下面的花园里有紫丁香树，开着紫色的花，带着令人晕眩的甜香，随着晨风飘到窗外。

paragraphs.en: Below the garden a green field lush with clover sloped down to the hollow where the brook ran and where scores of white birches grew, upspringing airily out of an undergrowth suggestive of delightful possibilities in ferns and mosses and woodsy things generally. Beyond it was a hill, green and feathery with spruce and fir; there was a gap in it where the gray gable end of the little house she had seen from the other side of the Lake of Shining Waters was visible.
paragraphs.zh: 花园下面是一片长满三叶草的绿色田野，一直延伸到小溪流过的洼地，那里生长着几十棵白桦树，它们从灌木丛中轻快地生长出来，暗示着蕨类植物、苔藓和木本植物的令人愉快的可能性。远处是一座小山，绿意盎然，长满了云杉和冷杉。那里有一个缺口，可以看到她在光辉湖的另一边看到的那座小房子的灰色山墙端。

paragraphs.en: Off to the left were the big barns and beyond them, away down over green, low-sloping fields, was a sparkling blue glimpse of sea.
paragraphs.zh: 左边是大谷仓，谷仓的远处，在绿色、低坡度的田野上，可以看到闪闪发光的蓝色大海。

paragraphs.en: Anne's beauty-loving eyes lingered on it all, taking everything greedily in. She had looked on so many unlovely places in her life, poor child; but this was as lovely as anything she had ever dreamed.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮那双爱美的眼睛在这一切上徘徊，贪婪地吸收着一切。可怜的孩子，她在她的生活中看过那么多不可爱的地方；现在她已经看到了。但这就像她所梦想的一切一样可爱。

paragraphs.en: She knelt there, lost to everything but the loveliness around her, until she was startled by a hand on her shoulder. Marilla had come in unheard by the small dreamer.
paragraphs.zh: 她跪在那里，除了周围的可爱之外，什么都失去了，直到她被一只放在她肩膀上的手吓了一跳。玛丽拉进来了，小梦想家没有听到。

paragraphs.en: "It's time you were dressed," she said curtly.
paragraphs.zh: “你该穿衣服了。”她简短地说。

paragraphs.en: Marilla really did not know how to talk to the child, and her uncomfortable ignorance made her crisp and curt when she did not mean to be.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉真的不知道如何和孩子说话，而她的无知让她在无意的时候变得干脆而生硬。

paragraphs.en: Anne stood up and drew a long breath.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站了起来，长长地吸了一口气。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, isn't it wonderful?" she said, waving her hand comprehensively at the good world outside.
paragraphs.zh: “噢，这不是很棒吗？”她一边说着，一边向外面的美好世界挥了挥手。

paragraphs.en: "It's a big tree," said Marilla, "and it blooms great, but the fruit don't amount to much never—small and wormy."
paragraphs.zh: “这是一棵大树，”玛丽拉说，“花开得很好，但结的果子却很少——又小又长虫子。”
