paragraphs.en: "Oh, I don't mean just the tree; of course it's lovely—yes, it's RADIANTLY lovely—it blooms as if it meant it—but I meant everything, the garden and the orchard and the brook and the woods, the whole big dear world. Don't you feel as if you just loved the world on a morning like this? And I can hear the brook laughing all the way up here. Have you ever noticed what cheerful things brooks are? They're always laughing. Even in winter-time I've heard them under the ice. I'm so glad there's a brook near Green Gables. Perhaps you think it doesn't make any difference to me when you're not going to keep me, but it does. I shall always like to remember that there is a brook at Green Gables even if I never see it again. If there wasn't a brook I'd be HAUNTED by the uncomfortable feeling that there ought to be one. I'm not in the depths of despair this morning. I never can be in the morning. Isn't it a splendid thing that there are mornings? But I feel very sad. I've just been imagining that it was really me you wanted after all and that I was to stay here for ever and ever. It was a great comfort while it lasted. But the worst of imagining things is that the time comes when you have to stop and that hurts."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我指的不仅仅是那棵树；当然，它很可爱——是的，它非常可爱——它绽放得就像它所指的那样——但我指的是一切，花园、果园、小溪、树林，整个可爱的大世界。在这样的早晨，你不觉得你就像爱这个世界吗？我能听到小溪一路欢笑。你有没有注意到小溪是多么令人愉快的东西？它们总是即使在冬天，我也能听到他们在冰下的声音。也许你认为，当你不留我的时候，这对我来说没有什么区别，但我会永远记住，即使我再也见不到那条小溪，我也会感到不舒服。今天早上我永远无法陷入绝望，这不是一件美妙的事情吗？但我一直在想象，你真正想要的是我，而我要永远留在这里，但最糟糕的是，当你必须停下来的时候，那会很痛苦。”

paragraphs.en: "You'd better get dressed and come down-stairs and never mind your imaginings," said Marilla as soon as she could get a word in edgewise. "Breakfast is waiting. Wash your face and comb your hair. Leave the window up and turn your bedclothes back over the foot of the bed. Be as smart as you can."
paragraphs.zh: “你最好穿好衣服下楼，别在意你的想象。”玛丽拉一能插话就说道。 “早餐已经准备好了。洗脸、梳头。把窗户打开，把床单翻回到床脚上。尽可能聪明点。”

paragraphs.en: Anne could evidently be smart to some purpose for she was down-stairs in ten minutes' time, with her clothes neatly on, her hair brushed and braided, her face washed, and a comfortable consciousness pervading her soul that she had fulfilled all Marilla's requirements. As a matter of fact, however, she had forgotten to turn back the bedclothes.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮显然在某些方面很聪明，因为十分钟后她就下楼了，衣服穿得整整齐齐，头发梳理好，编成辫子，洗了脸，她的灵魂中弥漫着一种舒适的感觉，她已经满足了玛丽拉的所有要求。但事实上，她忘记把床单翻回去了。

paragraphs.en: "I'm pretty hungry this morning," she announced as she slipped into the chair Marilla placed for her. "The world doesn't seem such a howling wilderness as it did last night. I'm so glad it's a sunshiny morning. But I like rainy mornings real well, too. All sorts of mornings are interesting, don't you think? You don't know what's going to happen through the day, and there's so much scope for imagination. But I'm glad it's not rainy today because it's easier to be cheerful and bear up under affliction on a sunshiny day. I feel that I have a good deal to bear up under. It's all very well to read about sorrows and imagine yourself living through them heroically, but it's not so nice when you really come to have them, is it?"
paragraphs.zh: “今天早上我很饿，”她一边说，一边坐进玛丽拉为她安排的椅子上。 “世界不再像昨晚那样荒凉。我很高兴这是一个阳光明媚的早晨。但我也很喜欢下雨的早晨。各种各样的早晨都很有趣，你不觉得吗？你不知道这一天会发生什么，想象的空间很大。但我很高兴今天没有下雨，因为更容易快乐，更容易忍受苦难。阳光明媚的一天，我觉得我有很多事情要承受，读到悲伤并想象自己勇敢地经历它们是很好的，但当你真正经历它们时，情况就不太好了，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "For pity's sake hold your tongue," said Marilla. "You talk entirely too much for a little girl."
paragraphs.zh: “看在怜悯的份上，闭嘴吧，”玛丽拉说。 “对于一个小女孩来说，你说得太多了。”

paragraphs.en: Thereupon Anne held her tongue so obediently and thoroughly that her continued silence made Marilla rather nervous, as if in the presence of something not exactly natural. Matthew also held his tongue,—but this was natural,—so that the meal was a very silent one.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，安妮乖乖地、彻底地闭嘴了，她持续的沉默让玛丽拉相当紧张，仿佛遇到了一些不自然的事情。马修也保持沉默——但这很自然——所以这顿饭吃得非常安静。

paragraphs.en: As it progressed Anne became more and more abstracted, eating mechanically, with her big eyes fixed unswervingly and unseeingly on the sky outside the window. This made Marilla more nervous than ever; she had an uncomfortable feeling that while this odd child's body might be there at the table her spirit was far away in some remote airy cloudland, borne aloft on the wings of imagination. Who would want such a child about the place?
paragraphs.zh: 随着时间的推移，安妮越来越心不在焉，机械地吃着东西，她的大眼睛一动不动地盯着窗外的天空。这让玛丽拉比以往更加紧张。她有一种不舒服的感觉，虽然这个奇怪的孩子的身体可能就在餐桌旁，但她的精神却在遥远的某个遥远的、通风的云国里，乘着想象的翅膀高高飞翔。谁会想要一个这样的孩子？

paragraphs.en: Yet Matthew wished to keep her, of all unaccountable things! Marilla felt that he wanted it just as much this morning as he had the night before, and that he would go on wanting it. That was Matthew's way—take a whim into his head and cling to it with the most amazing silent persistency—a persistency ten times more potent and effectual in its very silence than if he had talked it out.
paragraphs.zh: 然而马修却想留下她，这是最不负责任的事情！马瑞拉觉得他今天早上和前一天晚上一样想要它，而且他会继续想要它。这就是马修的方式——脑子里突发奇想，然后以最惊人的沉默坚持不懈——这种坚持在沉默中比他把它说出来要强大和有效十倍。

paragraphs.en: When the meal was ended Anne came out of her reverie and offered to wash the dishes.
paragraphs.zh: 吃完饭后，安妮从沉思中回过神来，主动提出要洗碗。

paragraphs.en: "Can you wash dishes right?" asked Marilla distrustfully.
paragraphs.zh: “你会洗碗吗？”玛丽拉怀疑地问道。

paragraphs.en: "Pretty well. I'm better at looking after children, though. I've had so much experience at that. It's such a pity you haven't any here for me to look after."
paragraphs.zh: “很好。不过，我更擅长照顾孩子。这方面我有很多经验。可惜你这里没有我照顾的孩子。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I've got at present. YOU'RE problem enough in all conscience. What's to be done with you I don't know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
paragraphs.zh: “我觉得我不想再照顾比现在更多的孩子了。从良心来说，你已经够麻烦了。我不知道该拿你怎么办。马修是个最可笑的人。”

paragraphs.en: "I think he's lovely," said Anne reproachfully. "He is so very sympathetic. He didn't mind how much I talked—he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him."
paragraphs.zh: “我觉得他很可爱。”安妮责备地说。 “他非常富有同情心。他并不介意我说了多少——他似乎很喜欢。我一见到他就觉得他是志同道合的人。”

paragraphs.en: "You're both queer enough, if that's what you mean by kindred spirits," said Marilla with a sniff. "Yes, you may wash the dishes. Take plenty of hot water, and be sure you dry them well. I've got enough to attend to this morning for I'll have to drive over to White Sands in the afternoon and see Mrs. Spencer. You'll come with me and we'll settle what's to be done with you. After you've finished the dishes go up-stairs and make your bed."
paragraphs.zh: “你们俩都够奇怪的了，如果这就是你们所说的志趣相投的话。”玛丽拉嗤之以鼻地说。 “是的，你可以洗碗。多带些热水，一定要把它们擦干。今天早上我有足够的事情要做，因为下午我得开车去白沙见斯宾塞太太。你跟我来，我们会解决你要做什么。你洗完碗后，上楼去整理床铺。”

paragraphs.en: Anne washed the dishes deftly enough, as Marilla who kept a sharp eye on the process, discerned. Later on she made her bed less successfully, for she had never learned the art of wrestling with a feather tick. But is was done somehow and smoothed down; and then Marilla, to get rid of her, told her she might go out-of-doors and amuse herself until dinner time.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮洗碗的动作非常熟练，玛丽拉敏锐地观察着整个过程，她发现了这一点。后来她整理床铺就不那么成功了，因为她从来没有学过与羽毛蜱摔跤的艺术。但不知怎的，它被完成并平滑了；然后玛丽拉为了摆脱她，告诉她可以到户外去娱乐一下，直到晚饭时间。

paragraphs.en: Anne flew to the door, face alight, eyes glowing. On the very threshold she stopped short, wheeled about, came back and sat down by the table, light and glow as effectually blotted out as if some one had clapped an extinguisher on her.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮飞奔到门口，脸上容光焕发，眼睛闪闪发光。就在门口，她突然停了下来，转了个身，回来坐在桌边，光线和光芒实际上被遮蔽了，就像有人把灭火器拍到了她身上一样。

paragraphs.en: "What's the matter now?" demanded Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “现在怎么了？”马瑞拉问道。

paragraphs.en: "I don't dare go out," said Anne, in the tone of a martyr relinquishing all earthly joys. "If I can't stay here there is no use in my loving Green Gables. And if I go out there and get acquainted with all those trees and flowers and the orchard and the brook I'll not be able to help loving it. It's hard enough now, so I won't make it any harder. I want to go out so much—everything seems to be calling to me, 'Anne, Anne, come out to us. Anne, Anne, we want a playmate'—but it's better not. There is no use in loving things if you have to be torn from them, is there? And it's so hard to keep from loving things, isn't it? That was why I was so glad when I thought I was going to live here. I thought I'd have so many things to love and nothing to hinder me. But that brief dream is over. I am resigned to my fate now, so I don't think I'll go out for fear I'll get unresigned again. What is the name of that geranium on the window-sill, please?"
paragraphs.zh: “我不敢出去。”安妮的语气就像一位放弃了尘世一切欢乐的烈士。 “如果我不能留在这里，我心爱的绿山墙就没啥用了。如果我出去熟悉那些树木、鲜花、果园和小溪，我就会情不自禁地爱上它。现在已经够难了，所以我不会再让它变得更难了。我太想出去了——一切似乎都在呼唤我，‘安妮，安妮，到我们身边来。安妮，安妮，我们想要一个玩伴’——但是如果你不得不离开它们，那么爱是没有用的，不是吗？这就是为什么当我想到我要住在这里时我会如此高兴，我以为我会拥有这么多东西来爱我，但现在我已经听天由命了，所以我不认为我会再出去，因为我担心我会再次不甘心。窗台上那朵天竺葵，可以吗？”

paragraphs.en: "That's the apple-scented geranium."
paragraphs.zh: “那是苹果香味的天竺葵。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I don't mean that sort of a name. I mean just a name you gave it yourself. Didn't you give it a name? May I give it one then? May I call it—let me see—Bonny would do—may I call it Bonny while I'm here? Oh, do let me!"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我的意思不是那种名字。我的意思只是你自己给它起的一个名字。你没有给它起一个名字吗？那么我可以给它起一个名字吗？我可以叫它——让我想想——邦尼会行——我可以在这儿的时候叫它邦尼吗？哦，请让我来吧！”

paragraphs.en: "Goodness, I don't care. But where on earth is the sense of naming a geranium?"
paragraphs.zh: “天哪，我不在乎。但是给天竺葵命名到底有什么意义呢？”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I like things to have handles even if they are only geraniums. It makes them seem more like people. How do you know but that it hurts a geranium's feelings just to be called a geranium and nothing else? You wouldn't like to be called nothing but a woman all the time. Yes, I shall call it Bonny. I named that cherry-tree outside my bedroom window this morning. I called it Snow Queen because it was so white. Of course, it won't always be in blossom, but one can imagine that it is, can't one?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我喜欢有把手的东西，即使它们只是天竺葵。这让它们看起来更像人。你怎么知道，仅仅被称为天竺葵而不是别的，会伤害天竺葵的感情？你不会喜欢一直被称为女人。是的，我会叫它邦尼。今天早上我把卧室窗外的那棵樱桃树命名为雪之女王，因为它太白了。当然，它不会总是这样盛开，但人们可以想象它是这样的，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I never in all my life saw or heard anything to equal her," muttered Marilla, beating a retreat down to the cellar after potatoes. "She is kind of interesting as Matthew says. I can feel already that I'm wondering what on earth she'll say next. She'll be casting a spell over me, too. She's cast it over Matthew. That look he gave me when he went out said everything he said or hinted last night over again. I wish he was like other men and would talk things out. A body could answer back then and argue him into reason. But what's to be done with a man who just LOOKS?"
paragraphs.zh: “我一生中从未见过或听到过任何能与她相提并论的东西，”马里拉嘟哝道，吃完土豆后就撤退到地窖。 “正如马修所说，她有点有趣。我已经感觉到我在想她接下来会说什么。她也会对我施咒。她对马修施了咒语。当他出去时，他给我的眼神又说了一遍他昨晚所说或暗示的一切。我希望他能像其他人一样，能把事情说出来。当时一个人可以回答并说服他讲道理。但是，一个只看外表的男人该怎么办呢？”

paragraphs.en: Anne had relapsed into reverie, with her chin in her hands and her eyes on the sky, when Marilla returned from her cellar pilgrimage. There Marilla left her until the early dinner was on the table.
paragraphs.zh: 当玛丽拉从地窖朝圣回来时，安妮双手托着下巴，眼睛望着天空，再次陷入沉思。玛丽拉离开了她，直到早饭上桌。

paragraphs.en: "I suppose I can have the mare and buggy this afternoon, Matthew?" said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “我想今天下午我可以拥有母马和马车，马修？”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: Matthew nodded and looked wistfully at Anne. Marilla intercepted the look and said grimly:
paragraphs.zh: 马修点点头，若有所思地看着安妮。玛丽拉拦截了目光，阴沉地说道：

paragraphs.en: "I'm going to drive over to White Sands and settle this thing. I'll take Anne with me and Mrs. Spencer will probably make arrangements to send her back to Nova Scotia at once. I'll set your tea out for you and I'll be home in time to milk the cows."
paragraphs.zh: “我要开车去白沙解决这件事。我会带上安妮，斯宾塞夫人可能会立即安排将她送回新斯科舍。我会为你准备茶，然后及时回家挤奶。”

paragraphs.en: Still Matthew said nothing and Marilla had a sense of having wasted words and breath. There is nothing more aggravating than a man who won't talk back—unless it is a woman who won't.
paragraphs.zh: 马修仍然一言不发，玛丽拉有一种浪费言语和呼吸的感觉。没有什么比一个男人不顶嘴更让人恼火的了——除非女人不顶嘴。

paragraphs.en: Matthew hitched the sorrel into the buggy in due time and Marilla and Anne set off. Matthew opened the yard gate for them and as they drove slowly through, he said, to nobody in particular as it seemed:
paragraphs.zh: 马修及时把酢浆草套上马车，玛丽拉和安妮出发了。马修为他们打开院门，当他们缓缓驶过时，他对任何人说道：

paragraphs.en: "Little Jerry Buote from the Creek was here this morning, and I told him I guessed I'd hire him for the summer."
paragraphs.zh: “来自克里克的小杰里·博特今天早上来了，我告诉他我想我会雇用他过夏天。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla made no reply, but she hit the unlucky sorrel such a vicious clip with the whip that the fat mare, unused to such treatment, whizzed indignantly down the lane at an alarming pace. Marilla looked back once as the buggy bounced along and saw that aggravating Matthew leaning over the gate, looking wistfully after them.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉没有回答，但她用鞭子猛烈地抽打那匹不幸的栗色马，致使那匹不习惯这种待遇的肥母马愤怒地以惊人的速度沿着小路呼啸而去。当马车颠簸前行时，玛丽拉回头看了一眼，看到恼怒的马修靠在大门上，若有所思地看着他们。

chapters.title: CHAPTER V. Anne's History
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：安妮坎坷凄凉的身世

paragraphs.en: "Do you know," said Anne confidentially, "I've made up my mind to enjoy this drive. It's been my experience that you can nearly always enjoy things if you make up your mind firmly that you will. Of course, you must make it up FIRMLY. I am not going to think about going back to the asylum while we're having our drive. I'm just going to think about the drive. Oh, look, there's one little early wild rose out! Isn't it lovely? Don't you think it must be glad to be a rose? Wouldn't it be nice if roses could talk? I'm sure they could tell us such lovely things. And isn't pink the most bewitching color in the world? I love it, but I can't wear it. Redheaded people can't wear pink, not even in imagination. Did you ever know of anybody whose hair was red when she was young, but got to be another color when she grew up?"
paragraphs.zh: “你知道吗，”安妮秘密地说，“我已经下定决心要享受这次驾车的乐趣。根据我的经验，只要你下定决心，你几乎总是能享受到事情。当然，你必须下定决心。在我们驾车的时候，我不会考虑回精神病院。我只想考虑驾车的事情。哦，看，有一朵早开的野玫瑰开出来了！不是很可爱吗？不是吗？”你认为成为一朵玫瑰一定很高兴吗？我相信它们能告诉我们如此可爱的事情，难道粉色不是世界上最迷人的颜色吗？但我不能穿粉色，即使在想象中也不能。你知道有谁年轻时头发是红色的，但长大后却变成了另一种颜色吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No, I don't know as I ever did," said Marilla mercilessly, "and I shouldn't think it likely to happen in your case either."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不知道，就像我以前那样，”玛丽拉无情地说，“而且我认为这种情况也不会发生在你的身上。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "Well, that is another hope gone. 'My life is a perfect graveyard of buried hopes.' That's a sentence I read in a book once, and I say it over to comfort myself whenever I'm disappointed in anything."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，这又是一个破灭的希望。‘我的生活是一个埋藏着希望的完美坟墓。’”这是我在书上读过的一句话，每当我对任何事感到失望时，我都会念叨这句话来安慰自己。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't see where the comforting comes in myself," said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白我自己有什么安慰，”马里拉说。

paragraphs.en: "Why, because it sounds so nice and romantic, just as if I were a heroine in a book, you know. I am so fond of romantic things, and a graveyard full of buried hopes is about as romantic a thing as one can imagine isn't it? I'm rather glad I have one. Are we going across the Lake of Shining Waters today?"
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，因为这听起来如此美好和浪漫，就像我是一本书中的女主角一样，你知道。我很喜欢浪漫的东西，而充满埋藏希望的墓地是人们能想象到的最浪漫的事情，不是吗？我很高兴我有一个。今天我们要穿越闪亮水域湖吗？”

paragraphs.en: "We're not going over Barry's pond, if that's what you mean by your Lake of Shining Waters. We're going by the shore road."
paragraphs.zh: “我们不会越过巴里池塘，如果这就是你所说的光辉湖的意思的话。我们要沿着海岸路走。”

paragraphs.en: "Shore road sounds nice," said Anne dreamily. "Is it as nice as it sounds? Just when you said 'shore road' I saw it in a picture in my mind, as quick as that! And White Sands is a pretty name, too; but I don't like it as well as Avonlea. Avonlea is a lovely name. It just sounds like music. How far is it to White Sands?"
paragraphs.zh: “海岸路听起来不错，”安妮若有所思地说。 “它像听起来那么好听吗？当你说‘海岸路’时，我就在脑海中看到了它的画面，速度那么快！白沙也是一个漂亮的名字，但我不像埃文利那样喜欢它。埃文利是一个可爱的名字。它听起来像音乐。它到白沙有多远？”

paragraphs.en: "It's five miles; and as you're evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself."
paragraphs.zh: “有五英里；而且你显然一心想说话，所以不妨告诉我你对自己的了解，以达到某种目的。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, what I KNOW about myself isn't really worth telling," said Anne eagerly. "If you'll only let me tell you what I IMAGINE about myself you'll think it ever so much more interesting."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我所知道的关于我自己的事情并不值得讲述，”安妮急切地说。 “如果你让我告诉你我对自己的想象，你会觉得这更有趣。”

paragraphs.en: "No, I don't want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?"
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不需要你的任何想象。只要你坚持赤裸裸的事实。从头开始。你在哪里出生，多大了？”

paragraphs.en: "I was eleven last March," said Anne, resigning herself to bald facts with a little sigh. "And I was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia. My father's name was Walter Shirley, and he was a teacher in the Bolingbroke High School. My mother's name was Bertha Shirley. Aren't Walter and Bertha lovely names? I'm so glad my parents had nice names. It would be a real disgrace to have a father named—well, say Jedediah, wouldn't it?"
paragraphs.zh: “去年三月我十一岁了，”安妮轻轻叹了口气，接受了赤裸裸的事实。 “我出生在新斯科舍省的博林布鲁克。我父亲的名字叫沃尔特·雪利，他是博林布鲁克高中的一名老师。我母亲的名字叫伯莎·雪利。沃尔特和伯莎不是很可爱的名字吗？我很高兴我父母有好名字。如果有一个父亲的名字——好吧，杰迪戴亚，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I guess it doesn't matter what a person's name is as long as he behaves himself," said Marilla, feeling herself called upon to inculcate a good and useful moral.
paragraphs.zh: “我想一个人叫什么并不重要，只要他表现得好就行，”玛丽拉说，她觉得自己有责任灌输良好而有用的道德。

paragraphs.en: "Well, I don't know." Anne looked thoughtful. "I read in a book once that a rose by any other name would smell as sweet, but I've never been able to believe it. I don't believe a rose WOULD be as nice if it was called a thistle or a skunk cabbage. I suppose my father could have been a good man even if he had been called Jedediah; but I'm sure it would have been a cross. Well, my mother was a teacher in the High school, too, but when she married father she gave up teaching, of course. A husband was enough responsibility. Mrs. Thomas said that they were a pair of babies and as poor as church mice. They went to live in a weeny-teeny little yellow house in Bolingbroke. I've never seen that house, but I've imagined it thousands of times. I think it must have had honeysuckle over the parlor window and lilacs in the front yard and lilies of the valley just inside the gate. Yes, and muslin curtains in all the windows. Muslin curtains give a house such an air. I was born in that house. Mrs. Thomas said I was the homeliest baby she ever saw, I was so scrawny and tiny and nothing but eyes, but that mother thought I was perfectly beautiful. I should think a mother would be a better judge than a poor woman who came in to scrub, wouldn't you? I'm glad she was satisfied with me anyhow, I would feel so sad if I thought I was a disappointment to her—because she didn't live very long after that, you see. She died of fever when I was just three months old. I do wish she'd lived long enough for me to remember calling her mother. I think it would be so sweet to say 'mother,' don't you? And father died four days afterwards from fever too. That left me an orphan and folks were at their wits' end, so Mrs. Thomas said, what to do with me. You see, nobody wanted me even then. It seems to be my fate. Father and mother had both come from places far away and it was well known they hadn't any relatives living. Finally Mrs. Thomas said she'd take me, though she was poor and had a drunken husband. She brought me up by hand. Do you know if there is anything in being brought up by hand that ought to make people who are brought up that way better than other people? Because whenever I was naughty Mrs. Thomas would ask me how I could be such a bad girl when she had brought me up by hand—reproachful-like.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我不知道。”安妮看上去若有所思。 “我曾经在一本书上读到，任何其他名字的玫瑰闻起来都会一样香甜，但我从来不敢相信。我不相信玫瑰如果被称为蓟或臭甘蓝，就不会那么好。我想我的父亲即使被称为杰迪戴亚也可能是一个好人；但我确信这会是一个十字架。嗯，我的母亲也是一名高中老师，但当她嫁给父亲后，她放弃了教学，托马斯太太说，他们是一对婴儿，就像教堂里的老鼠一样，我从来没有见过那所房子，但我想它的客厅窗户上一定有金银花，大门内有铃兰，是的，所有的窗户都挂着铃兰。平纹细布窗帘给房子带来了这样的气氛。托马斯太太说我是她见过的最丑陋的孩子，我骨瘦如柴，身材娇小，除了眼睛之外一无所有，但我认为母亲比一个进来擦洗的可怜女人更能判断，不是吗？无论如何，我很高兴她对我感到失望，因为我活不了多久了。在那之后，我才三个月大，她就因发烧去世了。我想，我觉得叫她妈妈是一件很甜蜜的事，不是吗？四天后，我的父亲也因发烧去世了，所以托马斯太太说，我该怎么办？看来我的父亲和母亲都来自不同的地方。众所周知，他们没有任何亲戚居住。最后，托马斯夫人说她会带我，尽管她很穷，而且有一个酗酒的丈夫。她亲手抚养我长大，你知道有什么东西能让那些以这种方式长大的人比其他人更好吗？因为每当我淘气时，托马斯夫人就会问我，当她亲手抚养我时，我怎么会是一个坏女孩。

paragraphs.en: "Mr. and Mrs. Thomas moved away from Bolingbroke to Marysville, and I lived with them until I was eight years old. I helped look after the Thomas children—there were four of them younger than me—and I can tell you they took a lot of looking after. Then Mr. Thomas was killed falling under a train and his mother offered to take Mrs. Thomas and the children, but she didn't want me. Mrs. Thomas was at HER wits' end, so she said, what to do with me. Then Mrs. Hammond from up the river came down and said she'd take me, seeing I was handy with children, and I went up the river to live with her in a little clearing among the stumps. It was a very lonesome place. I'm sure I could never have lived there if I hadn't had an imagination. Mr. Hammond worked a little sawmill up there, and Mrs. Hammond had eight children. She had twins three times. I like babies in moderation, but twins three times in succession is TOO MUCH. I told Mrs. Hammond so firmly, when the last pair came. I used to get so dreadfully tired carrying them about.
paragraphs.zh: “托马斯先生和托马斯太太从博林布鲁克搬到了马里斯维尔，我和他们住在一起直到我八岁。我帮忙照顾托马斯的孩子们——其中有四个比我小——我可以告诉你，他们花了很多时间照顾。然后托马斯先生在火车下摔死了，他的母亲提出要带走托马斯太太和孩子们，但她不想要我。托马斯太太束手无策，所以她说，该怎么办然后，河上游的哈蒙德太太过来，说她会带我去，我就到河上游去，住在树桩间的一小块空地里。我确信，如果哈蒙德先生在那里经营一家小锯木厂，我绝对不可能住在那里，而哈蒙德太太有八个孩子，但我喜欢双胞胎。当最后一双来的时候，我已经累得要命了。

paragraphs.en: "I lived up river with Mrs. Hammond over two years, and then Mr. Hammond died and Mrs. Hammond broke up housekeeping. She divided her children among her relatives and went to the States. I had to go to the asylum at Hopeton, because nobody would take me. They didn't want me at the asylum, either; they said they were over-crowded as it was. But they had to take me and I was there four months until Mrs. Spencer came."
paragraphs.zh: “我和哈蒙德太太在河边住了两年多，然后哈蒙德先生去世了，哈蒙德太太也不再做家务了。她把孩子分给了她的亲戚，去了美国。我不得不去霍普顿的精神病院，因为没有人愿意收留我。他们也不想让我去精神病院；他们说那里已经人满为患了。但他们不得不收留我，我在那里呆了四个月，直到斯宾塞太太来。”

paragraphs.en: Anne finished up with another sigh, of relief this time. Evidently she did not like talking about her experiences in a world that had not wanted her.
paragraphs.zh: 说完，安妮又叹了口气，这一次她松了口气。显然，她不喜欢谈论她在一个不需要她的世界中的经历。

paragraphs.en: "Did you ever go to school?" demanded Marilla, turning the sorrel mare down the shore road.
paragraphs.zh: “你上过学吗？” “怎么了？”玛丽拉一边问道，一边把栗色母马调到了海岸路上。

paragraphs.en: "Not a great deal. I went a little the last year I stayed with Mrs. Thomas. When I went up river we were so far from a school that I couldn't walk it in winter and there was a vacation in summer, so I could only go in the spring and fall. But of course I went while I was at the asylum. I can read pretty well and I know ever so many pieces of poetry off by heart—'The Battle of Hohenlinden' and 'Edinburgh after Flodden,' and 'Bingen of the Rhine,' and most of the 'Lady of the Lake' and most of 'The Seasons' by James Thompson. Don't you just love poetry that gives you a crinkly feeling up and down your back? There is a piece in the Fifth Reader—'The Downfall of Poland'—that is just full of thrills. Of course, I wasn't in the Fifth Reader—I was only in the Fourth—but the big girls used to lend me theirs to read."
paragraphs.zh: “没什么。去年我和托马斯太太住在一起的时候，我去了一点。当我逆流而上时，我们离学校太远了，冬天没法走路，夏天有假期，所以我只能在春天和秋天去。当然，我在精神病院的时候去了。我读得很好，还背诵了很多诗篇——《霍恩林登之战》和《弗洛登之后的爱丁堡》， 《莱茵河的宾根》以及詹姆斯·汤普森的大部分《湖中女子》和《四季》，你难道不喜欢那些让你脊背发酸的诗歌吗？《第五读本》里有一首《波兰的没落》——当然，我没读过《第五读本》——我只读过《第四读本》——但大姑娘们常常把她们的诗借给我读。”

paragraphs.en: "Were those women—Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond—good to you?" asked Marilla, looking at Anne out of the corner of her eye.
paragraphs.zh: “那些女人——托马斯夫人和哈蒙德夫人——对你好吗？”玛丽拉用眼角的余光看着安妮问道。

paragraphs.en: "O-o-o-h," faltered Anne. Her sensitive little face suddenly flushed scarlet and embarrassment sat on her brow. "Oh, they MEANT to be—I know they meant to be just as good and kind as possible. And when people mean to be good to you, you don't mind very much when they're not quite—always. They had a good deal to worry them, you know. It's very trying to have a drunken husband, you see; and it must be very trying to have twins three times in succession, don't you think? But I feel sure they meant to be good to me."
paragraphs.zh: “噢——噢——噢，”安妮结结巴巴地说。她敏感的小脸顿时涨得通红，眉宇间满是尴尬。 “哦，他们的本意是——我知道他们本意是尽可能地善良和仁慈。当人们本意对你好时，如果他们不总是——你不会太介意。他们有很多事情让他们担心，你知道。有一个醉酒的丈夫是非常困难的，你看；而且连续生三个双胞胎一定很困难，你不觉得吗？但我确信他们是想对我好。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla asked no more questions. Anne gave herself up to a silent rapture over the shore road and Marilla guided the sorrel abstractedly while she pondered deeply. Pity was suddenly stirring in her heart for the child. What a starved, unloved life she had had—a life of drudgery and poverty and neglect; for Marilla was shrewd enough to read between the lines of Anne's history and divine the truth. No wonder she had been so delighted at the prospect of a real home. It was a pity she had to be sent back. What if she, Marilla, should indulge Matthew's unaccountable whim and let her stay? He was set on it; and the child seemed a nice, teachable little thing.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉没有再问什么。安妮默默地陶醉在海岸公路上，玛丽拉一边心不在焉地引导着栗色树，一边陷入沉思。她心中突然升起了对孩子的怜悯。她过着多么饥饿、不被爱的生活——苦差事、贫穷和被忽视的生活；因为玛丽拉足够精明，能够从安妮的历史字里行间看出真相。难怪她对拥有一个真正的家感到如此高兴。可惜她不得不被送回去。如果她，玛丽拉，纵容马修莫名其妙的突发奇想，让她留下来怎么办？他已经下定决心要这么做了。这孩子看上去是个可爱、好学的小东西。

paragraphs.en: "She's got too much to say," thought Marilla, "but she might be trained out of that. And there's nothing rude or slangy in what she does say. She's ladylike. It's likely her people were nice folks."
paragraphs.zh: “她有太多话要说，”玛丽拉想，“但她可能是受过训练而不会这样说的。而且她所说的话没有任何粗鲁或俚语。她很淑女。她的人很可能都是好人。”

paragraphs.en: The shore road was "woodsy and wild and lonesome." On the right hand, scrub firs, their spirits quite unbroken by long years of tussle with the gulf winds, grew thickly. On the left were the steep red sandstone cliffs, so near the track in places that a mare of less steadiness than the sorrel might have tried the nerves of the people behind her. Down at the base of the cliffs were heaps of surf-worn rocks or little sandy coves inlaid with pebbles as with ocean jewels; beyond lay the sea, shimmering and blue, and over it soared the gulls, their pinions flashing silvery in the sunlight.
paragraphs.zh: 岸边的道路“树木繁茂、荒野而孤独”。右手边，灌木丛冷杉长得茂密，它们的精神丝毫没有因为长年与海湾风的搏斗而受到摧残。左边是陡峭的红砂岩悬崖，有些地方离赛道很近，一匹比栗色稳定性差的母马可能会考验她后面的人的神经。悬崖底部有成堆的被海浪冲刷过的岩石，或者是镶嵌着海洋宝石般鹅卵石的小沙湾。远处是蔚蓝的大海，波光粼粼，海鸥在海面上翱翔，它们的翅膀在阳光下闪烁着银色的光芒。

paragraphs.en: "Isn't the sea wonderful?" said Anne, rousing from a long, wide-eyed silence. "Once, when I lived in Marysville, Mr. Thomas hired an express wagon and took us all to spend the day at the shore ten miles away. I enjoyed every moment of that day, even if I had to look after the children all the time. I lived it over in happy dreams for years. But this shore is nicer than the Marysville shore. Aren't those gulls splendid? Would you like to be a gull? I think I would—that is, if I couldn't be a human girl. Don't you think it would be nice to wake up at sunrise and swoop down over the water and away out over that lovely blue all day; and then at night to fly back to one's nest? Oh, I can just imagine myself doing it. What big house is that just ahead, please?"
paragraphs.zh: “大海不是很棒吗？”安妮从长时间的睁大眼睛的沉默中醒来。 “有一次，当我住在马里斯维尔时，托马斯先生租了一辆特快马车，带我们大家去十英里外的海岸度过一天。我很享受那天的每一刻，即使我必须一直照顾孩子们。我在幸福的梦中度过了很多年。但是这个海岸比马里斯维尔海岸更好。那些海鸥不是很漂亮吗？你想成为一只海鸥吗？我想我会的——也就是说，如果我你不觉得在日出时醒来，飞翔在水面上，然后在晚上飞回自己的巢穴吗？

paragraphs.en: "That's the White Sands Hotel. Mr. Kirke runs it, but the season hasn't begun yet. There are heaps of Americans come there for the summer. They think this shore is just about right."
paragraphs.zh: “那是白沙酒店。柯克先生经营着它，但季节还没有开始。有很多美国人来这里避暑。他们认为这个海岸正好合适。”

paragraphs.en: "I was afraid it might be Mrs. Spencer's place," said Anne mournfully. "I don't want to get there. Somehow, it will seem like the end of everything."
paragraphs.zh: “我担心这可能是斯宾塞夫人的住所，”安妮悲伤地说。 “我不想到达那里。不知何故，这似乎是一切的终结。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 6 章：玛丽拉下定决心收养

paragraphs.en: Get there they did, however, in due season. Mrs. Spencer lived in a big yellow house at White Sands Cove, and she came to the door with surprise and welcome mingled on her benevolent face.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，他们在适当的季节到达了那里。斯宾塞夫人住在白沙湾的一栋黄色大房子里，她来到门口时，慈祥的脸上夹杂着惊讶和欢迎。

paragraphs.en: "Dear, dear," she exclaimed, "you're the last folks I was looking for today, but I'm real glad to see you. You'll put your horse in? And how are you, Anne?"
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的，亲爱的，”她喊道，“你们是我今天最后找的人，但我真的很高兴见到你们。你会把你的马放进去吗？你好吗，安妮？”

paragraphs.en: "I'm as well as can be expected, thank you," said Anne smilelessly. A blight seemed to have descended on her.
paragraphs.zh: “我一切都很好，谢谢你。”安妮微笑着说道。一场灾难似乎降临在她身上。

paragraphs.en: "I suppose we'll stay a little while to rest the mare," said Marilla, "but I promised Matthew I'd be home early. The fact is, Mrs. Spencer, there's been a queer mistake somewhere, and I've come over to see where it is. We send word, Matthew and I, for you to bring us a boy from the asylum. We told your brother Robert to tell you we wanted a boy ten or eleven years old."
paragraphs.zh: “我想我们会留下来休息一会儿，让母马休息一下，”玛丽拉说，“但我答应过马修我会早点回家。事实是，斯宾塞夫人，某个地方出了一个奇怪的错误，我过来看看它在哪里。马修和我，我们派人传话，让你从精神病院给我们带来一个男孩。我们告诉你的兄弟罗伯特，告诉你我们想要一个十岁或十一岁的男孩。”

paragraphs.en: "Marilla Cuthbert, you don't say so!" said Mrs. Spencer in distress. "Why, Robert sent word down by his daughter Nancy and she said you wanted a girl—didn't she Flora Jane?" appealing to her daughter who had come out to the steps.
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉·库斯伯特，你别这么说！”斯宾塞夫人苦恼地说。 “为什么，罗伯特让他的女儿南希传话，她说你想要一个女孩——她不是弗洛拉·简吗？”向走到台阶上的女儿求助。

paragraphs.en: "She certainly did, Miss Cuthbert," corroborated Flora Jane earnestly.
paragraphs.zh: “她确实做到了，库斯伯特小姐，”弗洛拉·简认真地证实。

paragraphs.en: "I'm dreadful sorry," said Mrs. Spencer. "It's too bad; but it certainly wasn't my fault, you see, Miss Cuthbert. I did the best I could and I thought I was following your instructions. Nancy is a terrible flighty thing. I've often had to scold her well for her heedlessness."
paragraphs.zh: “我非常抱歉，”斯宾塞夫人说。 “这太糟糕了；但这当然不是我的错，你看，库斯伯特小姐。我已经尽力了，我以为我正在听从你的指示。南希是个可怕的轻浮的人。我经常不得不责备她的粗心大意。”

paragraphs.en: "It was our own fault," said Marilla resignedly. "We should have come to you ourselves and not left an important message to be passed along by word of mouth in that fashion. Anyhow, the mistake has been made and the only thing to do is to set it right. Can we send the child back to the asylum? I suppose they'll take her back, won't they?"
paragraphs.zh: “这是我们自己的错，”玛丽拉无奈地说。 “我们应该亲自来找你，而不是留下重要的信息，以这种方式通过口口相传。无论如何，错误已经犯了，唯一能做的就是纠正它。我们可以把孩子送回精神病院吗？我想他们会带她回去，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose so," said Mrs. Spencer thoughtfully, "but I don't think it will be necessary to send her back. Mrs. Peter Blewett was up here yesterday, and she was saying to me how much she wished she'd sent by me for a little girl to help her. Mrs. Peter has a large family, you know, and she finds it hard to get help. Anne will be the very girl for you. I call it positively providential."
paragraphs.zh: “我想是这样，”斯宾塞夫人若有所思地说，“但我认为没有必要把她送回去。彼得·布莱威特夫人昨天来过这里，她对我说，她多么希望我派一个小女孩来帮助她。彼得夫人有一个大家庭，你知道，她发现很难得到帮助。安妮将是最适合你的女孩。我称这真是天意。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla did not look as if she thought Providence had much to do with the matter. Here was an unexpectedly good chance to get this unwelcome orphan off her hands, and she did not even feel grateful for it.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看起来似乎并不认为普罗维登斯与这件事有多大关系。这是一个意想不到的好机会，可以让这个不受欢迎的孤儿摆脱她的手，而她甚至没有对此感到感激。

paragraphs.en: She knew Mrs. Peter Blewett only by sight as a small, shrewish-faced woman without an ounce of superfluous flesh on her bones. But she had heard of her. "A terrible worker and driver," Mrs. Peter was said to be; and discharged servant girls told fearsome tales of her temper and stinginess, and her family of pert, quarrelsome children. Marilla felt a qualm of conscience at the thought of handing Anne over to her tender mercies.
paragraphs.zh: 她只见过彼得·布卢伊特夫人，她身材娇小，面容泼辣，骨头上没有一丁点多余的肉。但她听说过她。据说彼得夫人是“一个糟糕的工人和司机”。被解雇的女仆讲述了她的脾气和吝啬的可怕故事，以及她的家庭中顽皮、爱吵架的孩子。一想到要把安妮交给她温柔的怜悯，马里拉就感到良心不安。

paragraphs.en: "Well, I'll go in and we'll talk the matter over," she said.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我进去，我们谈谈这件事，”她说。

paragraphs.en: "And if there isn't Mrs. Peter coming up the lane this blessed minute!" exclaimed Mrs. Spencer, bustling her guests through the hall into the parlor, where a deadly chill struck on them as if the air had been strained so long through dark green, closely drawn blinds that it had lost every particle of warmth it had ever possessed. "That is real lucky, for we can settle the matter right away. Take the armchair, Miss Cuthbert. Anne, you sit here on the ottoman and don't wiggle. Let me take your hats. Flora Jane, go out and put the kettle on. Good afternoon, Mrs. Blewett. We were just saying how fortunate it was you happened along. Let me introduce you two ladies. Mrs. Blewett, Miss Cuthbert. Please excuse me for just a moment. I forgot to tell Flora Jane to take the buns out of the oven."
paragraphs.zh: “如果这一刻没有彼得太太沿着小巷走来就好了！”斯宾塞夫人惊呼道，她催促着她的客人们穿过大厅进入客厅，一股致命的寒意向他们袭来，仿佛空气经过深绿色、紧闭的百叶窗过滤了太久，失去了曾经拥有的每一丝温暖。 “真是幸运，因为我们可以马上解决问题。拿把扶手椅，卡斯伯特小姐。安妮，你坐在脚凳上，别扭动。让我拿走你的帽子。弗洛拉·简，出去把水壶打开。下午好，布莱威特夫人。我们只是说你们碰巧在一起是多么幸运。让我向你们介绍两位女士。布莱威特夫人，卡斯伯特小姐。请稍等一下。我忘记告诉你了。”弗洛拉·简把面包从烤箱里拿出来。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer whisked away, after pulling up the blinds. Anne sitting mutely on the ottoman, with her hands clasped tightly in her lap, stared at Mrs Blewett as one fascinated. Was she to be given into the keeping of this sharp-faced, sharp-eyed woman? She felt a lump coming up in her throat and her eyes smarted painfully. She was beginning to be afraid she couldn't keep the tears back when Mrs. Spencer returned, flushed and beaming, quite capable of taking any and every difficulty, physical, mental or spiritual, into consideration and settling it out of hand.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞夫人拉上百叶窗后迅速离开。安妮默默地坐在脚凳上，双手紧紧地握在腿上，出神地盯着布卢伊特夫人。难道要交给这个脸尖眼尖的女人照顾吗？她感觉喉咙里有一个肿块，眼睛发痛。当斯宾塞夫人回来时，她开始担心自己无法忍住泪水，她满脸通红，笑容满面，非常有能力考虑到任何困难，无论是身体上的、精神上的还是精神上的，并立即解决它。

paragraphs.en: "It seems there's been a mistake about this little girl, Mrs. Blewett," she said. "I was under the impression that Mr. and Miss Cuthbert wanted a little girl to adopt. I was certainly told so. But it seems it was a boy they wanted. So if you're still of the same mind you were yesterday, I think she'll be just the thing for you."
paragraphs.zh: “布莱威特夫人，这个小女孩的事似乎有误，”她说。 “我的印象是卡斯伯特先生和小姐想要收养一个小女孩。当然有人告诉过我。但看来他们想要的是一个男孩。所以，如果你仍然和昨天一样，我想她会很适合你。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Blewett darted her eyes over Anne from head to foot.
paragraphs.zh: 布卢伊特夫人从头到脚地扫视着安妮。

paragraphs.en: "How old are you and what's your name?" she demanded.
paragraphs.zh: “你多大了，你叫什么名字？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley," faltered the shrinking child, not daring to make any stipulations regarding the spelling thereof, "and I'm eleven years old."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，”胆怯的孩子结结巴巴地说，不敢对拼写做出任何规定，“我十一岁了。”

paragraphs.en: "Humph! You don't look as if there was much to you. But you're wiry. I don't know but the wiry ones are the best after all. Well, if I take you you'll have to be a good girl, you know—good and smart and respectful. I'll expect you to earn your keep, and no mistake about that. Yes, I suppose I might as well take her off your hands, Miss Cuthbert. The baby's awful fractious, and I'm clean worn out attending to him. If you like I can take her right home now."
paragraphs.zh: “哼！你看起来似乎没什么出息。但你很瘦。我不知道，但瘦的毕竟是最好的。好吧，如果我收下你，你就必须是一个好女孩，你知道的——善良、聪明、有礼貌。我希望你能挣钱养活自己，这一点没错。是的，我想我最好把她从你手里夺走，库斯伯特小姐。这孩子太暴躁了，我如果你愿意的话，我现在就可以带她回家了。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla looked at Anne and softened at sight of the child's pale face with its look of mute misery—the misery of a helpless little creature who finds itself once more caught in the trap from which it had escaped. Marilla felt an uncomfortable conviction that, if she denied the appeal of that look, it would haunt her to her dying day. More-over, she did not fancy Mrs. Blewett. To hand a sensitive, "highstrung" child over to such a woman! No, she could not take the responsibility of doing that!
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看着安妮，看到孩子苍白的脸和无言的痛苦表情，她的心软化了——这是一个无助的小动物发现自己再次陷入了它逃脱的陷阱的痛苦。玛丽拉感到一种不安的信念，如果她否认这种外表的吸引力，它会一直困扰着她直到她临死为止。而且，她也不喜欢布卢伊特夫人。把一个敏感、“神经质”的孩子交给这样一个女人！不，她不能承担那样的责任！

paragraphs.en: "Well, I don't know," she said slowly. "I didn't say that Matthew and I had absolutely decided that we wouldn't keep her. In fact I may say that Matthew is disposed to keep her. I just came over to find out how the mistake had occurred. I think I'd better take her home again and talk it over with Matthew. I feel that I oughtn't to decide on anything without consulting him. If we make up our mind not to keep her we'll bring or send her over to you tomorrow night. If we don't you may know that she is going to stay with us. Will that suit you, Mrs. Blewett?"
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我不知道，”她慢慢地说。 “我并没有说马修和我绝对决定不留下她。事实上，我可以说马修打算留下她。我只是过来看看这个错误是怎么发生的。我想我最好再把她带回家，和马修商量一下。我觉得我不应该在没有咨询他的情况下做出任何决定。如果我们决定不留下她，我们明天晚上就会把她带来或送到你那里。如果我们不这样做，你可能会知道她你会和我们一起住吗，布卢伊特夫人？”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose it'll have to," said Mrs. Blewett ungraciously.
paragraphs.zh: “我想这是必须的，”布卢伊特夫人不客气地说。

paragraphs.en: During Marilla's speech a sunrise had been dawning on Anne's face. First the look of despair faded out; then came a faint flush of hope; her eyes grew deep and bright as morning stars. The child was quite transfigured; and, a moment later, when Mrs. Spencer and Mrs. Blewett went out in quest of a recipe the latter had come to borrow she sprang up and flew across the room to Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 在玛丽拉讲话的时候，安妮的脸上已经露出了日出的光芒。首先，绝望的表情消失了；随之而来的是一丝微弱的希望。她的眼睛变得深邃而明亮，像晨星一样。孩子整个人都变了。过了一会儿，当斯宾塞夫人和布卢伊特夫人出去寻找菜谱时，布卢伊特夫人来借菜谱，她跳了起来，飞过房间，飞到玛丽拉那里。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Miss Cuthbert, did you really say that perhaps you would let me stay at Green Gables?" she said, in a breathless whisper, as if speaking aloud might shatter the glorious possibility. "Did you really say it? Or did I only imagine that you did?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，卡斯伯特小姐，你真的说过也许你会让我留在绿山墙吗？”她气喘吁吁地低声说道，仿佛大声说话可能会破坏这个辉煌的可能性。 “你真的这么说吗？还是我只是想象你这么说？”

paragraphs.en: "I think you'd better learn to control that imagination of yours, Anne, if you can't distinguish between what is real and what isn't," said Marilla crossly. "Yes, you did hear me say just that and no more. It isn't decided yet and perhaps we will conclude to let Mrs. Blewett take you after all. She certainly needs you much more than I do."
paragraphs.zh: “我想你最好学会控制你的想象力，安妮，如果你无法区分什么是真实的，什么不是，”玛丽拉生气地说。 “是的，你确实听到我这么说了，仅此而已。现在还没有决定，也许我们最终会决定让布莱威特夫人带你去。她当然比我更需要你。”

paragraphs.en: "I'd rather go back to the asylum than go to live with her," said Anne passionately. "She looks exactly like a—like a gimlet."
paragraphs.zh: “我宁愿回到精神病院，也不愿和她一起住。”安妮热情地说。 “她看起来就像——就像一个钻头。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla smothered a smile under the conviction that Anne must be reproved for such a speech.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉强忍着笑容，她确信安妮的这种言论一定会受到谴责。

paragraphs.en: "A little girl like you should be ashamed of talking so about a lady and a stranger," she said severely. "Go back and sit down quietly and hold your tongue and behave as a good girl should."
paragraphs.zh: “像你这样的小女孩应该为谈论一位女士和一个陌生人而感到羞耻，”她严厉地说。 “回去安静地坐下来，闭嘴，表现得像一个好女孩应该的那样。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll try to do and be anything you want me, if you'll only keep me," said Anne, returning meekly to her ottoman.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你愿意留住我，我会尽力做你想要我做的任何事，”安妮说，温顺地回到她的脚凳上。

paragraphs.en: When they arrived back at Green Gables that evening Matthew met them in the lane. Marilla from afar had noted him prowling along it and guessed his motive. She was prepared for the relief she read in his face when he saw that she had at least brought back Anne back with her. But she said nothing, to him, relative to the affair, until they were both out in the yard behind the barn milking the cows. Then she briefly told him Anne's history and the result of the interview with Mrs. Spencer.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，当他们回到绿山墙时，马修在小巷里遇见了他们。玛丽拉远远地注意到他沿着这条路徘徊，并猜出了他的动机。当他看到她至少把安妮带回来时，她从他脸上看到的轻松感已经做好了准备。但她没有对他提及这件事，直到他们俩都到谷仓后面的院子里挤牛奶。然后她简单地向他讲述了安妮的历史以及采访斯宾塞夫人的结果。

paragraphs.en: "I wouldn't give a dog I liked to that Blewett woman," said Matthew with unusual vim.
paragraphs.zh: “我不会把我喜欢的狗送给那个布勒伊特女人，”马修异常生气地说。

paragraphs.en: "I don't fancy her style myself," admitted Marilla, "but it's that or keeping her ourselves, Matthew. And since you seem to want her, I suppose I'm willing—or have to be. I've been thinking over the idea until I've got kind of used to it. It seems a sort of duty. I've never brought up a child, especially a girl, and I dare say I'll make a terrible mess of it. But I'll do my best. So far as I'm concerned, Matthew, she may stay."
paragraphs.zh: “我自己也不喜欢她的风格，”玛丽拉承认道，“但就是这样，或者让她自己留着，马修。既然你似乎想要她，我想我愿意——或者必须如此。我一直在思考这个想法，直到我已经习惯了。这似乎是一种责任。我从来没有养育过一个孩子，尤其是一个女孩，我敢说我会把它搞得一团糟。但我会尽力而为。就我而言担心，马修，她可能会留下来。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew's shy face was a glow of delight.
paragraphs.zh: 马修害羞的脸上闪现出喜悦的光芒。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I reckoned you'd come to see it in that light, Marilla," he said. "She's such an interesting little thing."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我想你会从这个角度来看待它的，玛丽拉，”他说。 “她真是个有趣的小东西。”

paragraphs.en: "It'd be more to the point if you could say she was a useful little thing," retorted Marilla, "but I'll make it my business to see she's trained to be that. And mind, Matthew, you're not to go interfering with my methods. Perhaps an old maid doesn't know much about bringing up a child, but I guess she knows more than an old bachelor. So you just leave me to manage her. When I fail it'll be time enough to put your oar in."
paragraphs.zh: “如果你能说她是一个有用的小东西，那就更切中要害了，”玛丽拉反驳道，“但我会以看到她被训练成那样为我的事。注意，马修，你不要去干涉我的方法。也许一个老处女不知道如何抚养孩子，但我猜她比一个老单身汉懂得更多。所以你就让我来管理她吧。当我失败时，你就有足够的时间来划桨了。在。”

paragraphs.en: "There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way," said Matthew reassuringly. "Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she's one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you."
paragraphs.zh: “好了，好了，玛丽拉，你可以用你自己的方式，”马修安慰地说。 “只能对她好一点，不要宠坏她。我觉得她是那种你可以为她做任何事情的人，只要你让她爱你。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla sniffed, to express her contempt for Matthew's opinions concerning anything feminine, and walked off to the dairy with the pails.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉吸了吸鼻子，以表达她对马修关于任何女性化事物的看法的蔑视，然后提着桶朝牛奶店走去。

paragraphs.en: "I won't tell her tonight that she can stay," she reflected, as she strained the milk into the creamers. "She'd be so excited that she wouldn't sleep a wink. Marilla Cuthbert, you're fairly in for it. Did you ever suppose you'd see the day when you'd be adopting an orphan girl? It's surprising enough; but not so surprising as that Matthew should be at the bottom of it, him that always seemed to have such a mortal dread of little girls. Anyhow, we've decided on the experiment and goodness only knows what will come of it."
paragraphs.zh: “今晚我不会告诉她她可以留下来，”她边想边把牛奶滤入奶精中。 “她会兴奋得睡不着觉。玛丽拉·库斯伯特，你真是太有才了。你有没有想过有一天你会收养一个孤儿女孩？这已经够令人惊讶的了；但更令人惊讶的是，马修竟然是这件事的始作俑者，他似乎总是对小女孩怀有一种致命的恐惧。不管怎样，我们已经决定进行这个实验，只有天知道会发生什么。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：安妮的第一次祈祷

paragraphs.en: When Marilla took Anne up to bed that night she said stiffly:
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，当玛丽拉把安妮抱上床睡觉时，她生硬地说：

paragraphs.en: "Now, Anne, I noticed last night that you threw your clothes all about the floor when you took them off. That is a very untidy habit, and I can't allow it at all. As soon as you take off any article of clothing fold it neatly and place it on the chair. I haven't any use at all for little girls who aren't neat."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，安妮，我昨晚注意到你脱衣服的时候把衣服扔得满地都是。这是一个非常不整洁的习惯，我根本不允许。你一脱下任何一件衣服，就把它折叠整齐，放在椅子上。不整洁的小女孩对我来说根本没有任何用处。”

paragraphs.en: "I was so harrowed up in my mind last night that I didn't think about my clothes at all," said Anne. "I'll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I'd forget, I'd be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things."
paragraphs.zh: “昨晚我心里非常难过，根本没有想到我的衣服，”安妮说。 “今晚我会把它们叠好。在精神病院时，他们总是让我们这样做。不过，有一半的时间，我会忘记，我会匆忙地安静地躺在床上，想象一些事情。”

paragraphs.en: "You'll have to remember a little better if you stay here," admonished Marilla. "There, that looks something like. Say your prayers now and get into bed."
paragraphs.zh: “如果你留在这里，你就必须记住一点，”玛丽拉告诫道。 “好了，看起来就像是这样。现在祈祷一下，然后上床睡觉。”

paragraphs.en: "I never say any prayers," announced Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “我从不做任何祈祷，”安妮宣布。

paragraphs.en: Marilla looked horrified astonishment.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看上去惊恐万状。

paragraphs.en: "Why, Anne, what do you mean? Were you never taught to say your prayers? God always wants little girls to say their prayers. Don't you know who God is, Anne?"
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，安妮，你这是什么意思？你从来没有被教过祈祷吗？上帝总是希望小女孩们祈祷。难道你不知道上帝是谁吗，安妮？”

paragraphs.en: "'God is a spirit, infinite, eternal and unchangeable, in His being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth,'" responded Anne promptly and glibly.
paragraphs.zh: “‘上帝是一个灵，无限、永恒、不变，他的存在、智慧、力量、圣洁、正义、良善和真理，’”安妮迅速而流畅地回答道。

paragraphs.en: Marilla looked rather relieved.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看上去松了口气。

paragraphs.en: "So you do know something then, thank goodness! You're not quite a heathen. Where did you learn that?"
paragraphs.zh: “所以你确实知道一些事情，谢天谢地！你不完全是异教徒。你从哪里学到的？”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, at the asylum Sunday-school. They made us learn the whole catechism. I liked it pretty well. There's something splendid about some of the words. 'Infinite, eternal and unchangeable.' Isn't that grand? It has such a roll to it—just like a big organ playing. You couldn't quite call it poetry, I suppose, but it sounds a lot like it, doesn't it?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，在收容所的主日学校。他们让我们学习了整个教义问答。我非常喜欢它。有些词很精彩。‘无限、永恒和不变。’这不是很伟大吗？它的滚动感非常好——就像一架大风琴在演奏。我想你不能完全称其为诗，但听起来很像，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "We're not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don't you know it's a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I'm afraid you are a very bad little girl."
paragraphs.zh: “我们不是在谈论诗歌，安妮——我们是在谈论祈祷。你难道不知道每天晚上不祈祷是一件可怕的邪恶的事情吗？我担心你是一个非常坏的小女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "You'd find it easier to be bad than good if you had red hair," said Anne reproachfully. "People who haven't red hair don't know what trouble is. Mrs. Thomas told me that God made my hair red ON PURPOSE, and I've never cared about Him since. And anyhow I'd always be too tired at night to bother saying prayers. People who have to look after twins can't be expected to say their prayers. Now, do you honestly think they can?"
paragraphs.zh: “如果你有一头红头发，你会发现做坏事比做好事更容易。”安妮责备地说。 “没有红头发的人不知道什么是麻烦。托马斯夫人告诉我，上帝故意让我的头发变成红色，从那以后我再也没有关心过他。无论如何，我晚上总是太累，懒得去祈祷。不能指望那些必须照顾双胞胎的人会祈祷。现在，你真的认为他们可以吗？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla decided that Anne's religious training must be begun at once. Plainly there was no time to be lost.
paragraphs.zh: 马里拉决定必须立即开始安妮的宗教训练。显然，没有时间可以浪费了。

paragraphs.en: "You must say your prayers while you are under my roof, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “当你在我的屋檐下时，你必须祈祷，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "Why, of course, if you want me to," assented Anne cheerfully. "I'd do anything to oblige you. But you'll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I'll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it."
paragraphs.zh: “当然，如果你愿意的话，”安妮高兴地表示同意。 “我愿意做任何事来满足你。但是你必须告诉我这一次要说什么。我上床后，我会想象出一个真正美好的祈祷，永远要说。我相信，现在我想起来了，这会很有趣。”

paragraphs.en: "You must kneel down," said Marilla in embarrassment.
paragraphs.zh: “你必须跪下。”玛丽拉尴尬地说。

paragraphs.en: Anne knelt at Marilla's knee and looked up gravely.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮跪在玛丽拉的膝盖上，严肃地抬起头。

paragraphs.en: "Why must people kneel down to pray? If I really wanted to pray I'll tell you what I'd do. I'd go out into a great big field all alone or into the deep, deep, woods, and I'd look up into the sky—up—up—up—into that lovely blue sky that looks as if there was no end to its blueness. And then I'd just FEEL a prayer. Well, I'm ready. What am I to say?"
paragraphs.zh: “为什么人们必须跪下来祈祷？如果我真的想祈祷，我会告诉你我会做什么。我会独自走到一大片大田里，或者走进很深很深的树林，然后我抬头看看天空——向上——向上——向上——那可爱的蓝天，看起来好像没有尽头的蓝色。然后我就会感觉到祈祷。好吧，我准备好了。我该说什么？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla felt more embarrassed than ever. She had intended to teach Anne the childish classic, "Now I lay me down to sleep." But she had, as I have told you, the glimmerings of a sense of humor—which is simply another name for a sense of fitness of things; and it suddenly occurred to her that that simple little prayer, sacred to white-robed childhood lisping at motherly knees, was entirely unsuited to this freckled witch of a girl who knew and cared nothing about God's love, since she had never had it translated to her through the medium of human love.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉感到比以往任何时候都更尴尬。她本来打算教安妮一句幼稚的经典话：“现在我躺下睡觉了。”但正如我告诉过你的，她有一丝幽默感——这只是适应事物的感觉的另一个名字；她突然想到，这个简单的小祈祷，对白袍童年来说是神圣的，在母亲的膝盖上口齿不清，完全不适合这个长着雀斑的女巫，她对上帝的爱一无所知，也不关心，因为她从来没有通过人类的爱的媒介将它传达给她。

paragraphs.en: "You're old enough to pray for yourself, Anne," she said finally. "Just thank God for your blessings and ask Him humbly for the things you want."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你已经长大了，可以为自己祈祷了。”她最后说道。 “感谢上帝赐予你的祝福，并谦卑地向他祈求你想要的东西。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I'll do my best," promised Anne, burying her face in Marilla's lap. "Gracious heavenly Father—that's the way the ministers say it in church, so I suppose it's all right in private prayer, isn't it?" she interjected, lifting her head for a moment.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我会尽力的。”安妮把脸埋在玛丽拉的腿上，保证道。 “仁慈的天父——牧师在教堂里就是这么说的，所以我想在私下祈祷中也可以这样，不是吗？”她插话道，抬起头片刻。

paragraphs.en: "Gracious heavenly Father, I thank Thee for the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters and Bonny and the Snow Queen. I'm really extremely grateful for them. And that's all the blessings I can think of just now to thank Thee for. As for the things I want, they're so numerous that it would take a great deal of time to name them all so I will only mention the two most important. Please let me stay at Green Gables; and please let me be good-looking when I grow up.
paragraphs.zh: “仁慈的天父，我感谢你赐予我白色的欢乐之路、光辉之湖、邦尼和冰雪女王。我真的非常感激他们。这就是我现在能想到的所有祝福，要感谢你。至于我想要的东西太多了，要花很多时间才能说出它们，所以我只提最重要的两个。请让我留在绿山墙；请让我长得好看。”当我长大后。

paragraphs.en: I remain,
paragraphs.zh: 我留下来，

paragraphs.en: "Yours respectfully,
paragraphs.zh: “尊敬的您，

paragraphs.en: Anne Shirley.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮·雪莉.

paragraphs.en: "There, did I do all right?" she asked eagerly, getting up. "I could have made it much more flowery if I'd had a little more time to think it over."
paragraphs.zh: “怎么样，我做得还好吗？”她站起来，急切地问道。 “如果我有更多时间思考的话，我本可以把它做得更加华丽。”

paragraphs.en: Poor Marilla was only preserved from complete collapse by remembering that it was not irreverence, but simply spiritual ignorance on the part of Anne that was responsible for this extraordinary petition. She tucked the child up in bed, mentally vowing that she should be taught a prayer the very next day, and was leaving the room with the light when Anne called her back.
paragraphs.zh: 可怜的玛丽拉只有记住，安妮造成这一非同寻常的请愿并不是不敬，而是精神上的无知，才免于彻底崩溃。她把孩子盖在床上，心里发誓第二天就应该教她祈祷，当安妮叫她回来时，她正准备离开开着灯的房间。

paragraphs.en: "I've just thought of it now. I should have said, 'Amen' in place of 'yours respectfully,' shouldn't I?—the way the ministers do. I'd forgotten it, but I felt a prayer should be finished off in some way, so I put in the other. Do you suppose it will make any difference?"
paragraphs.zh: “我现在才想起来。我应该说‘阿门’来代替‘恭敬的’，不是吗？就像牧师们做的那样。我忘记了，但我觉得祈祷应该以某种方式结束，所以我加上了另一个。你认为这会有什么不同吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I—I don't suppose it will," said Marilla. "Go to sleep now like a good child. Good night."
paragraphs.zh: “我——我想不会的，”玛丽拉说。 “像个好孩子一样去睡觉吧。晚安。”

paragraphs.en: "I can only say good night tonight with a clear conscience," said Anne, cuddling luxuriously down among her pillows.
paragraphs.zh: “今晚我只能问心无愧地道晚安，”安妮舒适地依偎在枕头里说道。

paragraphs.en: Marilla retreated to the kitchen, set the candle firmly on the table, and glared at Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: 马瑞拉退到厨房，把蜡烛稳稳地放在桌子上，瞪着马修。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew Cuthbert, it's about time somebody adopted that child and taught her something. She's next door to a perfect heathen. Will you believe that she never said a prayer in her life till tonight? I'll send her to the manse tomorrow and borrow the Peep of the Day series, that's what I'll do. And she shall go to Sunday-school just as soon as I can get some suitable clothes made for her. I foresee that I shall have my hands full. Well, well, we can't get through this world without our share of trouble. I've had a pretty easy life of it so far, but my time has come at last and I suppose I'll just have to make the best of it."
paragraphs.zh: “马修·库斯伯特，是时候有人收养那个孩子并教她一些东西了。她是一个完美的异教徒的邻居。你相信她一生中直到今晚才祈祷过吗？明天我会把她送到豪宅并借用《每日一瞥》系列，这就是我要做的。一旦我能为她做一些合适的衣服，她就会去主日学校。我预见我会忙得不可开交。好吧，好吧，我们无法通过到目前为止，我在这个没有麻烦的世界里过着相当轻松的生活，但我的时代终于到来了，我想我必须充分利用它。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER VIII. Anne's Bringing-up Is Begun
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：安妮的教养生活开始了

paragraphs.en: For reasons best known to herself, Marilla did not tell Anne that she was to stay at Green Gables until the next afternoon. During the forenoon she kept the child busy with various tasks and watched over her with a keen eye while she did them. By noon she had concluded that Anne was smart and obedient, willing to work and quick to learn; her most serious shortcoming seemed to be a tendency to fall into daydreams in the middle of a task and forget all about it until such time as she was sharply recalled to earth by a reprimand or a catastrophe.
paragraphs.zh: 由于她自己最清楚的原因，玛丽拉没有告诉安妮她要在绿山墙呆到第二天下午。整个上午，她让孩子忙着做各种事情，并在她做这些事情时用敏锐的目光注视着她。到了中午，她得出结论，安妮聪明、听话、愿意工作、学得很快。她最严重的缺点似乎是在工作中容易陷入白日梦，然后忘记一切，直到受到斥责或灾难才将她拉回现实。

paragraphs.en: When Anne had finished washing the dinner dishes she suddenly confronted Marilla with the air and expression of one desperately determined to learn the worst. Her thin little body trembled from head to foot; her face flushed and her eyes dilated until they were almost black; she clasped her hands tightly and said in an imploring voice:
paragraphs.zh: 当安妮洗完晚餐的盘子后，她突然面对玛丽拉，脸上的表情和表情就像是一个拼命想知道最坏情况的人。她瘦小的身体从头到脚都在颤抖。她的脸涨得通红，眼睛睁大，几乎变成黑色。她紧紧地握着双手，用哀求的声音说道：

paragraphs.en: "Oh, please, Miss Cuthbert, won't you tell me if you are going to send me away or not? I've tried to be patient all the morning, but I really feel that I cannot bear not knowing any longer. It's a dreadful feeling. Please tell me."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，求你了，卡斯伯特小姐，你能不能告诉我你是否要送我走？整个早上我都在努力保持耐心，但我真的觉得我无法忍受再不知道了。这是一种可怕的感觉。请告诉我。”

paragraphs.en: "You haven't scalded the dishcloth in clean hot water as I told you to do," said Marilla immovably. "Just go and do it before you ask any more questions, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “你没有按照我告诉你的那样，用干净的热水烫洗抹布。”玛丽拉不动声色地说。 “在你问任何问题之前，先去做吧，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: Anne went and attended to the dishcloth. Then she returned to Marilla and fastened imploring eyes of the latter's face. "Well," said Marilla, unable to find any excuse for deferring her explanation longer, "I suppose I might as well tell you. Matthew and I have decided to keep you—that is, if you will try to be a good little girl and show yourself grateful. Why, child, whatever is the matter?"
paragraphs.zh: 安妮去收拾抹布。然后她回到马瑞拉身边，用恳求的目光注视着后者的脸。 “好吧，”玛丽拉找不到任何借口再拖延解释，“我想我还是告诉你吧。马修和我决定留下你——也就是说，如果你愿意努力做一个好小女孩并表现出感激之情。为什么，孩子，到底出了什么事？”

paragraphs.en: "I'm crying," said Anne in a tone of bewilderment. "I can't think why. I'm glad as glad can be. Oh, GLAD doesn't seem the right word at all. I was glad about the White Way and the cherry blossoms—but this! Oh, it's something more than glad. I'm so happy. I'll try to be so good. It will be uphill work, I expect, for Mrs. Thomas often told me I was desperately wicked. However, I'll do my very best. But can you tell me why I'm crying?"
paragraphs.zh: “我在哭。”安妮困惑地说。 “我想不出为什么。我很高兴，但很高兴。哦，高兴这个词根本不合适。我对白路和樱花感到高兴——但是这个！哦，这不仅仅是高兴。我太高兴了。我会努力变得很好。我预计这将是一项艰巨的工作，因为托马斯夫人经常告诉我，我非常邪恶。不过，我会尽力而为。但是你能告诉我为什么吗？我哭了？”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose it's because you're all excited and worked up," said Marilla disapprovingly. "Sit down on that chair and try to calm yourself. I'm afraid you both cry and laugh far too easily. Yes, you can stay here and we will try to do right by you. You must go to school; but it's only a fortnight till vacation so it isn't worth while for you to start before it opens again in September."
paragraphs.zh: “我想这是因为你太兴奋了，太激动了。”玛丽拉不以为然地说。 “坐到那张椅子上，试着让自己平静下来。恐怕你们都太容易哭和笑了。是的，你可以留在这里，我们会尽力为你做正确的事。你必须去学校；但距离假期只有两周了，所以在九月重新开学之前，你不值得开始。”

paragraphs.en: "What am I to call you?" asked Anne. "Shall I always say Miss Cuthbert? Can I call you Aunt Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “我该怎么称呼你呢？”安妮问。 “我应该一直叫卡斯伯特小姐吗？我可以叫你玛丽拉阿姨吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No; you'll call me just plain Marilla. I'm not used to being called Miss Cuthbert and it would make me nervous."
paragraphs.zh: “不；你会叫我普通的玛丽拉。我不习惯被称为卡斯伯特小姐，这会让我紧张。”

paragraphs.en: "It sounds awfully disrespectful to just say Marilla," protested Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “只说玛丽拉听起来非常不尊重，”安妮抗议道。

paragraphs.en: "I guess there'll be nothing disrespectful in it if you're careful to speak respectfully. Everybody, young and old, in Avonlea calls me Marilla except the minister. He says Miss Cuthbert—when he thinks of it."
paragraphs.zh: “我想，如果你小心地说话，尊重别人的话，这并没有什么不尊重的地方。埃文利的每个人，无论老少，都叫我玛丽拉，除了部长。他说是卡斯伯特小姐——当他想到这一点时。”

paragraphs.en: "I'd love to call you Aunt Marilla," said Anne wistfully. "I've never had an aunt or any relation at all—not even a grandmother. It would make me feel as if I really belonged to you. Can't I call you Aunt Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “我很想叫你玛丽拉阿姨，”安妮若有所思地说。 “我从来没有过阿姨或任何亲戚——甚至没有祖母。这会让我觉得我真的属于你。我不能叫你玛丽拉阿姨吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No. I'm not your aunt and I don't believe in calling people names that don't belong to them."
paragraphs.zh: “不。我不是你阿姨，我不喜欢用不属于他们的名字来称呼别人。”

paragraphs.en: "But we could imagine you were my aunt."
paragraphs.zh: “但我们可以想象你是我的阿姨。”

paragraphs.en: "I couldn't," said Marilla grimly.
paragraphs.zh: “我不能，”玛丽拉冷酷地说。

paragraphs.en: "Do you never imagine things different from what they really are?" asked Anne wide-eyed.
paragraphs.zh: “你从来没有想象过与实际情况不同的事情吗？”安妮睁大眼睛问道。

paragraphs.en: "No."
"Oh!" Anne drew a long breath. "Oh, Miss—Marilla, how much you miss!"
paragraphs.zh: “哦！”安妮长长地吸了一口气。 “哦，玛丽拉小姐，你多么想念啊！”

paragraphs.en: "I don't believe in imagining things different from what they really are," retorted Marilla. "When the Lord puts us in certain circumstances He doesn't mean for us to imagine them away. And that reminds me. Go into the sitting room, Anne—be sure your feet are clean and don't let any flies in—and bring me out the illustrated card that's on the mantelpiece. The Lord's Prayer is on it and you'll devote your spare time this afternoon to learning it off by heart. There's to be no more of such praying as I heard last night."
paragraphs.zh: “我不相信想象的事情与实际情况不同，”马里拉反驳道。 “当主把我们置于某些环境中时，他并不是要我们想象它们会消失。这提醒了我。安妮，到客厅去——确保你的脚干净，不要让苍蝇进来——然后把壁炉架上的带插图的卡片拿出来给我。上面有主祷文，你今天下午要花空闲时间背诵它。不要再像我昨晚听到的那样祈祷了。”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose I was very awkward," said Anne apologetically, "but then, you see, I'd never had any practice. You couldn't really expect a person to pray very well the first time she tried, could you? I thought out a splendid prayer after I went to bed, just as I promised you I would. It was nearly as long as a minister's and so poetical. But would you believe it? I couldn't remember one word when I woke up this morning. And I'm afraid I'll never be able to think out another one as good. Somehow, things never are so good when they're thought out a second time. Have you ever noticed that?"
paragraphs.zh: “我想我很尴尬，”安妮抱歉地说，“但是，你看，我从来没有进行过任何练习。你真的不能指望一个人第一次尝试就能很好地祈祷，不是吗？我上床睡觉后想出了一个精彩的祈祷文，就像我向你保证的那样。它几乎和牧师的祈祷文一样长，而且充满诗意。但是你相信吗？今天早上我醒来时，我一个字都不记得了。我害怕我永远无法再想出一个更好的东西。不知何故，当事情再想一遍时，它就不会那么好了，你有没有注意到这一点？”

paragraphs.en: "Here is something for you to notice, Anne. When I tell you to do a thing I want you to obey me at once and not stand stock-still and discourse about it. Just you go and do as I bid you."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，有件事你要注意。当我告诉你做一件事时，我希望你立即服从我，而不是站着不动，谈论它。你只要照我吩咐的去做就可以了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne promptly departed for the sitting-room across the hall; she failed to return; after waiting ten minutes Marilla laid down her knitting and marched after her with a grim expression. She found Anne standing motionless before a picture hanging on the wall between the two windows, with her eyes astar with dreams. The white and green light strained through apple trees and clustering vines outside fell over the rapt little figure with a half-unearthly radiance.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮立即走向大厅对面的客厅。她没能回来；等了十分钟后，玛丽拉放下手中的毛衣，表情严肃地跟在她后面走。她发现安妮一动不动地站在两扇窗户之间的墙上挂着的一幅画前，眼睛里充满了梦想。白色和绿色的光线透过外面的苹果树和丛生的藤蔓，落在这个全神贯注的小人物身上，散发出一种半神秘的光芒。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, whatever are you thinking of?" demanded Marilla sharply.
paragraphs.zh: “安安，你在想什么？”玛丽拉尖锐地问道。

paragraphs.en: Anne came back to earth with a start.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮一惊，回到了地面。

paragraphs.en: "That," she said, pointing to the picture—a rather vivid chromo entitled, "Christ Blessing Little Children"—"and I was just imagining I was one of them—that I was the little girl in the blue dress, standing off by herself in the corner as if she didn't belong to anybody, like me. She looks lonely and sad, don't you think? I guess she hadn't any father or mother of her own. But she wanted to be blessed, too, so she just crept shyly up on the outside of the crowd, hoping nobody would notice her—except Him. I'm sure I know just how she felt. Her heart must have beat and her hands must have got cold, like mine did when I asked you if I could stay. She was afraid He mightn't notice her. But it's likely He did, don't you think? I've been trying to imagine it all out—her edging a little nearer all the time until she was quite close to Him; and then He would look at her and put His hand on her hair and oh, such a thrill of joy as would run over her! But I wish the artist hadn't painted Him so sorrowful looking. All His pictures are like that, if you've noticed. But I don't believe He could really have looked so sad or the children would have been afraid of Him."
paragraphs.zh: “那个，”她指着那张相当生动的彩色照片，题为“基督祝福小孩子”，“我只是想象自己是其中之一，我是那个穿着蓝色裙子的小女孩，独自站在角落里，好像她不属于任何人，就像我一样。她看起来孤独而悲伤，你不觉得吗？我猜她没有自己的父亲或母亲。但她也想受到祝福，所以她就爬了过去害羞地站在人群外面，希望没人会注意到她——除了他，我确信她的感觉一定很强烈，就像我问你是否可以留下来时我的感觉一样。但你不觉得吗？我一直在努力想象这一切——直到她离他很近，然后他看着她；将他的手放在她的头发上，哦，她会感到如此的喜悦！但我希望艺术家没有把他画得那么悲伤，如果你注意到的话，但我不相信他真的看起来如此悲伤，否则孩子们会害怕他。”

paragraphs.en: "Anne," said Marilla, wondering why she had not broken into this speech long before, "you shouldn't talk that way. It's irreverent—positively irreverent."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”玛丽拉说，她想知道自己为什么没有早点插话，“你不应该那样说话。这是不敬的——绝对是不敬的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's eyes marveled.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的眼神里充满了惊叹。

paragraphs.en: "Why, I felt just as reverent as could be. I'm sure I didn't mean to be irreverent."
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，我感到尽可能的虔诚。我确信我并不是故意不敬的。”

paragraphs.en: "Well I don't suppose you did—but it doesn't sound right to talk so familiarly about such things. And another thing, Anne, when I send you after something you're to bring it at once and not fall into mooning and imagining before pictures. Remember that. Take that card and come right to the kitchen. Now, sit down in the corner and learn that prayer off by heart."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不认为你这么做了——但是这么熟悉地谈论这些事情听起来不太对。还有一件事，安妮，当我派你去寻找某样东西时，你要立即把它带来，不要在照片之前陷入沉思和想象。记住这一点。拿着那张卡片，径直来到厨房。现在，坐在角落里，背诵那个祈祷。”

paragraphs.en: Anne set the card up against the jugful of apple blossoms she had brought in to decorate the dinner-table—Marilla had eyed that decoration askance, but had said nothing—propped her chin on her hands, and fell to studying it intently for several silent minutes.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮把卡片放在她带来来装饰餐桌的一壶苹果花上——马里拉斜视着那装饰物，但什么也没说——用手撑着下巴，专心致志地研究了几分钟，沉默不语。

paragraphs.en: "I like this," she announced at length. "It's beautiful. I've heard it before—I heard the superintendent of the asylum Sunday school say it over once. But I didn't like it then. He had such a cracked voice and he prayed it so mournfully. I really felt sure he thought praying was a disagreeable duty. This isn't poetry, but it makes me feel just the same way poetry does. 'Our Father who art in heaven hallowed be Thy name.' That is just like a line of music. Oh, I'm so glad you thought of making me learn this, Miss—Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “我喜欢这个，”她最后宣布。 “太美了。我以前听过——我听收容所主日学的负责人说过一次。但当时我不喜欢。他的声音那么沙哑，祈祷得那么悲伤。我真的确信他认为祈祷是一件令人讨厌的事情。这不是诗歌，但它让我有同样的感觉。‘我们在天上的父亲愿人都尊你的名为圣。’这就像一行音乐。哦，我很高兴你想让我学习这个，玛丽拉小姐。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, learn it and hold your tongue," said Marilla shortly.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，学习一下，然后闭嘴，”玛丽拉简短地说。

paragraphs.en: Anne tipped the vase of apple blossoms near enough to bestow a soft kiss on a pink-cupped bud, and then studied diligently for some moments longer.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮把装着苹果花的花瓶倾斜得足够近，在粉色杯状花蕾上轻轻一吻，然后又勤奋地研究了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: "Marilla," she demanded presently, "do you think that I shall ever have a bosom friend in Avonlea?"
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，”她立刻问道，“你认为我在埃文利会有一个知音吗？”

paragraphs.en: "A—a what kind of friend?"
paragraphs.zh: “一个——什么样的朋友？”

paragraphs.en: "A bosom friend—an intimate friend, you know—a really kindred spirit to whom I can confide my inmost soul. I've dreamed of meeting her all my life. I never really supposed I would, but so many of my loveliest dreams have come true all at once that perhaps this one will, too. Do you think it's possible?"
paragraphs.zh: “一位知己——一位亲密的朋友，你知道——一位真正志同道合的人，我可以向她倾诉我内心深处的情感。我一生都梦想着见到她。我从来没有真正想过我会实现，但我的许多最可爱的梦想一下子实现了，也许这个也能实现。你认为这可能吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Diana Barry lives over at Orchard Slope and she's about your age. She's a very nice little girl, and perhaps she will be a playmate for you when she comes home. She's visiting her aunt over at Carmody just now. You'll have to be careful how you behave yourself, though. Mrs. Barry is a very particular woman. She won't let Diana play with any little girl who isn't nice and good."
paragraphs.zh: “戴安娜·巴里住在果园坡，她和你年纪相仿。她是一个非常好的小女孩，也许她回家后会成为你的玩伴。她刚才去卡莫迪看望她的姨妈。不过，你必须小心自己的举止。巴里夫人是个很特别的女人。她不会让戴安娜和任何不乖的小女孩一起玩。”

paragraphs.en: Anne looked at Marilla through the apple blossoms, her eyes aglow with interest.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮透过苹果花看着玛丽拉，她的眼睛充满了兴趣。

paragraphs.en: "What is Diana like? Her hair isn't red, is it? Oh, I hope not. It's bad enough to have red hair myself, but I positively couldn't endure it in a bosom friend."
paragraphs.zh: “戴安娜是什么样子？她的头发不是红的，是吗？哦，我希望不是。我自己有红头发就已经够糟糕了，但我绝对无法忍受在一个知己的身边。”

paragraphs.en: "Diana is a very pretty little girl. She has black eyes and hair and rosy cheeks. And she is good and smart, which is better than being pretty."
paragraphs.zh: “戴安娜是一个非常漂亮的小女孩。她有黑色的眼睛和头发，红润的脸颊。而且她很善良，很聪明，这比漂亮更重要。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla was as fond of morals as the Duchess in Wonderland, and was firmly convinced that one should be tacked on to every remark made to a child who was being brought up.
paragraphs.zh: 马里拉就像仙境中的公爵夫人一样热衷于道德，她坚信对正在长大的孩子所说的每一句话都应该受到重视。

paragraphs.en: But Anne waved the moral inconsequently aside and seized only on the delightful possibilities before it.
paragraphs.zh: 但安妮却把这个寓意抛在了一边，只抓住了眼前令人愉快的可能性。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm so glad she's pretty. Next to being beautiful oneself—and that's impossible in my case—it would be best to have a beautiful bosom friend. When I lived with Mrs. Thomas she had a bookcase in her sitting room with glass doors. There weren't any books in it; Mrs. Thomas kept her best china and her preserves there—when she had any preserves to keep. One of the doors was broken. Mr. Thomas smashed it one night when he was slightly intoxicated. But the other was whole and I used to pretend that my reflection in it was another little girl who lived in it. I called her Katie Maurice, and we were very intimate. I used to talk to her by the hour, especially on Sunday, and tell her everything. Katie was the comfort and consolation of my life. We used to pretend that the bookcase was enchanted and that if I only knew the spell I could open the door and step right into the room where Katie Maurice lived, instead of into Mrs. Thomas' shelves of preserves and china. And then Katie Maurice would have taken me by the hand and led me out into a wonderful place, all flowers and sunshine and fairies, and we would have lived there happy for ever after. When I went to live with Mrs. Hammond it just broke my heart to leave Katie Maurice. She felt it dreadfully, too, I know she did, for she was crying when she kissed me good-bye through the bookcase door. There was no bookcase at Mrs. Hammond's. But just up the river a little way from the house there was a long green little valley, and the loveliest echo lived there. It echoed back every word you said, even if you didn't talk a bit loud. So I imagined that it was a little girl called Violetta and we were great friends and I loved her almost as well as I loved Katie Maurice—not quite, but almost, you know. The night before I went to the asylum I said good-bye to Violetta, and oh, her good-bye came back to me in such sad, sad tones. I had become so attached to her that I hadn't the heart to imagine a bosom friend at the asylum, even if there had been any scope for imagination there."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我很高兴她漂亮。除了自己漂亮之外——这对我来说是不可能的——最好有一个漂亮的知己。当我和托马斯太太住在一起时，她的客厅里有一个带玻璃门的书柜。里面没有任何书；托马斯太太把她最好的瓷器和蜜饯放在那里——当她有蜜饯要保存时。其中一扇门坏了。有一天晚上，托马斯先生喝得有点醉，把它砸碎了。但另一个是完整的，我常常假装我的倒影是住在里面的另一个小女孩，我们非常亲密，我常常和她说话，尤其是在周日，并告诉她一切，凯蒂是我生活中的安慰和安慰，如果我知道这个咒语，我可以打开门，直接走进凯蒂·莫里斯住的房间，而不是进入托马斯夫人的房间。然后凯蒂·莫里斯会牵着我的手，带我去一个美妙的地方，那里充满了鲜花、阳光和仙女，当我去和哈蒙德太太住在一起时，离开凯蒂·莫里斯我也感到很伤心，因为她隔着书柜门吻别我时哭了。但就在河的上游，离房子不远的地方，有一个长长的绿色小山谷，即使你说话声音不大，它也会回响你所说的每一句话，所以我想象那是一个叫维奥莱塔的小女孩，我们是好朋友，我几乎像爱凯蒂·莫里斯一样爱她——不完全是，但几乎是，你知道的。哦，她的告别语气如此悲伤，我对她如此依恋，以至于我不忍心想象精神病院里有一个知音，即使那里有任何想象的空间。”

paragraphs.en: "I think it's just as well there wasn't," said Marilla drily. "I don't approve of such goings-on. You seem to half believe your own imaginations. It will be well for you to have a real live friend to put such nonsense out of your head. But don't let Mrs. Barry hear you talking about your Katie Maurices and your Violettas or she'll think you tell stories."
paragraphs.zh: “我想没有也好，”玛丽拉冷冷地说。 “我不赞成这样的事情。你似乎半信半疑。你最好有一个真正的活生生的朋友，让你把这些胡言乱语从你的脑海中赶走。但是别让巴里太太听到你谈论你的凯蒂·莫里斯和维奥莱塔，否则她会认为你在讲故事。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I won't. I couldn't talk of them to everybody—their memories are too sacred for that. But I thought I'd like to have you know about them. Oh, look, here's a big bee just tumbled out of an apple blossom. Just think what a lovely place to live—in an apple blossom! Fancy going to sleep in it when the wind was rocking it. If I wasn't a human girl I think I'd like to be a bee and live among the flowers."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我不会。我不能和每个人谈论他们——他们的记忆太神圣了。但我想我想让你了解他们。哦，看，这里有一只大蜜蜂刚刚从苹果花里掉下来。想想看，这是一个多么可爱的地方——在苹果花里！想象一下当风摇晃它的时候睡在里面吧。如果我不是一个人类女孩，我想我愿意成为一只蜜蜂，生活在苹果花中。花。”

paragraphs.en: "Yesterday you wanted to be a sea gull," sniffed Marilla. "I think you are very fickle minded. I told you to learn that prayer and not talk. But it seems impossible for you to stop talking if you've got anybody that will listen to you. So go up to your room and learn it."
paragraphs.zh: “昨天你想成为一只海鸥，”玛丽拉嗤之以鼻。 “我认为你的思想非常善变。我告诉过你要学会祈祷而不是说话。但如果有人愿意听你说话，你似乎不可能停止说话。所以到你的房间去学习它。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I know it pretty nearly all now—all but just the last line."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我现在几乎都知道了——除了最后一行。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, never mind, do as I tell you. Go to your room and finish learning it well, and stay there until I call you down to help me get tea."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，没关系，按我说的做，去你的房间好好学完，待在那里直到我叫你下去帮我倒茶。”

paragraphs.en: "Can I take the apple blossoms with me for company?" pleaded Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “我可以带着苹果花作伴吗？”安妮恳求道。

paragraphs.en: "No; you don't want your room cluttered up with flowers. You should have left them on the tree in the first place."
paragraphs.zh: “不；你不想让你的房间堆满鲜花。你一开始就应该把它们留在树上。”

paragraphs.en: "I did feel a little that way, too," said Anne. "I kind of felt I shouldn't shorten their lovely lives by picking them—I wouldn't want to be picked if I were an apple blossom. But the temptation was IRRESISTIBLE. What do you do when you meet with an irresistible temptation?"
paragraphs.zh: “我确实也有一点这样的感觉，”安妮说。 “我有点觉得我不应该因为采摘它们而缩短它们可爱的生命——如果我是一朵苹果花，我就不想被采摘。但诱惑是不可抗拒的。当你遇到不可抗拒的诱惑时，你会怎么做？”

paragraphs.en: "Anne, did you hear me tell you to go to your room?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你听到我叫你去房间了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed, retreated to the east gable, and sat down in a chair by the window.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，退到东山墙，在窗边的椅子上坐下。

paragraphs.en: "There—I know this prayer. I learned that last sentence coming upstairs. Now I'm going to imagine things into this room so that they'll always stay imagined. The floor is covered with a white velvet carpet with pink roses all over it and there are pink silk curtains at the windows. The walls are hung with gold and silver brocade tapestry. The furniture is mahogany. I never saw any mahogany, but it does sound SO luxurious. This is a couch all heaped with gorgeous silken cushions, pink and blue and crimson and gold, and I am reclining gracefully on it. I can see my reflection in that splendid big mirror hanging on the wall. I am tall and regal, clad in a gown of trailing white lace, with a pearl cross on my breast and pearls in my hair. My hair is of midnight darkness and my skin is a clear ivory pallor. My name is the Lady Cordelia Fitzgerald. No, it isn't—I can't make THAT seem real."
paragraphs.zh: “好了——我知道这个祷告了。我在楼上学到了最后一句话。现在我要想象这个房间里的东西，这样它们就永远停留在想象中。地板上铺着白色天鹅绒地毯，上面铺满了粉红色的玫瑰，窗户上挂着粉红色的丝绸窗帘。墙壁上挂着金银织锦挂毯。家具是桃花心木的。我从未见过任何桃花心木，但听起来确实很豪华。这是一张沙发，上面堆满了华丽的丝绸。粉色、蓝色、深红色和金色的靠垫，我优雅地靠在墙上那面华丽的大镜子上，我身材高大，穿着一件白色蕾丝长袍，胸前戴着珍珠十字架，头发上戴着珍珠，我的名字是科迪莉亚·菲茨杰拉德女士。这看起来是真的。”

paragraphs.en: She danced up to the little looking-glass and peered into it. Her pointed freckled face and solemn gray eyes peered back at her.
paragraphs.zh: 她跳到小镜子前，向里面凝视。她那张布满雀斑的尖脸和严肃的灰色眼睛凝视着她。

paragraphs.en: "You're only Anne of Green Gables," she said earnestly, "and I see you, just as you are looking now, whenever I try to imagine I'm the Lady Cordelia. But it's a million times nicer to be Anne of Green Gables than Anne of nowhere in particular, isn't it?"
paragraphs.zh: “你只是绿山墙的安妮，”她认真地说，“每当我试图想象自己是科迪莉亚夫人时，我就能看到你，就像你现在看到的那样。但是，成为绿山墙的安妮比成为一个无名小卒的安妮好一百万倍，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: She bent forward, kissed her reflection affectionately, and betook herself to the open window.
paragraphs.zh: 她向前倾身，深情地吻了吻自己的倒影，然后走到开着的窗户前。

paragraphs.en: "Dear Snow Queen, good afternoon. And good afternoon dear birches down in the hollow. And good afternoon, dear gray house up on the hill. I wonder if Diana is to be my bosom friend. I hope she will, and I shall love her very much. But I must never quite forget Katie Maurice and Violetta. They would feel so hurt if I did and I'd hate to hurt anybody's feelings, even a little bookcase girl's or a little echo girl's. I must be careful to remember them and send them a kiss every day."
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的雪之女王，下午好。下午好，山谷里亲爱的白桦树。下午好，山上亲爱的灰色房子。我想知道戴安娜是否会成为我的知心朋友。我希望她会，我会非常爱她。但我永远不能完全忘记凯蒂·莫里斯和维奥莱塔。如果我忘记了，他们会感到很受伤，我不想伤害任何人的感情，即使是一个小书柜女孩或一个小回声女孩的感情。我必须小心记住每天给他们一个吻。”

paragraphs.en: Anne blew a couple of airy kisses from her fingertips past the cherry blossoms and then, with her chin in her hands, drifted luxuriously out on a sea of daydreams.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮用指尖飞过樱花，轻轻地飞吻了几个，然后双手托着下巴，奢华地飘浮在白日梦的海洋中。

chapters.title: CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 9 章：雷切尔·林德太太惊呆了

paragraphs.en: Anne had been a fortnight at Green Gables before Mrs. Lynde arrived to inspect her. Mrs. Rachel, to do her justice, was not to blame for this. A severe and unseasonable attack of grippe had confined that good lady to her house ever since the occasion of her last visit to Green Gables. Mrs. Rachel was not often sick and had a well-defined contempt for people who were; but grippe, she asserted, was like no other illness on earth and could only be interpreted as one of the special visitations of Providence. As soon as her doctor allowed her to put her foot out-of-doors she hurried up to Green Gables, bursting with curiosity to see Matthew and Marilla's orphan, concerning whom all sorts of stories and suppositions had gone abroad in Avonlea.
paragraphs.zh: 林德夫人来检查安妮之前，她已经在绿山墙呆了两周了。公平地说，雷切尔夫人不应为此承担责任。自从上次访问绿山墙以来，一场严重的、不合时宜的流行性感冒发作，让这位好心的女士一直待在家里。雷切尔夫人并不经常生病，而且对生病的人怀有明显的蔑视。但她断言，流行性感冒与地球上任何其他疾病都不一样，只能被解释为上帝的特殊降临之一。医生一允许她走出家门，她就急忙赶到绿山墙，满怀好奇地想看看马修和玛丽拉的孤儿，关于他的各种故事和猜测已经在埃文利流传开来。

paragraphs.en: Anne had made good use of every waking moment of that fortnight. Already she was acquainted with every tree and shrub about the place. She had discovered that a lane opened out below the apple orchard and ran up through a belt of woodland; and she had explored it to its furthest end in all its delicious vagaries of brook and bridge, fir coppice and wild cherry arch, corners thick with fern, and branching byways of maple and mountain ash.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮充分利用了这两周的每一个醒着的时刻。她已经熟悉了这个地方的每一棵树和灌木。她发现苹果园下面有一条小路，穿过一片林地向上延伸。她已经探索到了它的最远的尽头，那里有小溪和桥梁、冷杉灌木丛和野樱桃拱门、长满蕨类植物的角落、枫树和山梣树的分支小道，所有奇妙的变幻莫测。

paragraphs.en: She had made friends with the spring down in the hollow—that wonderful deep, clear icy-cold spring; it was set about with smooth red sandstones and rimmed in by great palm-like clumps of water fern; and beyond it was a log bridge over the brook.
paragraphs.zh: 她和山谷里的泉水成了朋友——那美妙的深泉、清澈的冰冷泉水；它周围铺着光滑的红色砂岩，周围是大片棕榈状的水蕨丛。远处是小溪上的一座独木桥。

paragraphs.en: That bridge led Anne's dancing feet up over a wooded hill beyond, where perpetual twilight reigned under the straight, thick-growing firs and spruces; the only flowers there were myriads of delicate "June bells," those shyest and sweetest of woodland blooms, and a few pale, aerial starflowers, like the spirits of last year's blossoms. Gossamers glimmered like threads of silver among the trees and the fir boughs and tassels seemed to utter friendly speech.
paragraphs.zh: 那座桥引导着安妮舞动的双脚越过远处树木繁茂的小山，那里永远的暮色笼罩着笔直、茂密的冷杉和云杉。唯一的花朵是无数精致的“六月钟声”，那些最害羞、最甜美的林地花朵，还有一些苍白的空中星花，就像去年花朵的精灵。薄纱在树林中闪闪发光，像银丝一样，冷杉的树枝和流苏似乎在说着友好的话。

paragraphs.en: All these raptured voyages of exploration were made in the odd half hours which she was allowed for play, and Anne talked Matthew and Marilla half-deaf over her discoveries. Not that Matthew complained, to be sure; he listened to it all with a wordless smile of enjoyment on his face; Marilla permitted the "chatter" until she found herself becoming too interested in it, whereupon she always promptly quenched Anne by a curt command to hold her tongue.
paragraphs.zh: 所有这些令人兴奋的探索之旅都是在她被允许玩耍的零星半小时内完成的，安妮对她的发现半聋地与马修和玛丽拉交谈。可以肯定的是，马修并不是在抱怨。他听着这一切，脸上挂着无言的享受的微笑。玛丽拉允许她“喋喋不休”，直到她发现自己对此变得太感兴趣，于是她总是立即简短地命令安妮不要说话，从而让她安静下来。

paragraphs.en: Anne was out in the orchard when Mrs. Rachel came, wandering at her own sweet will through the lush, tremulous grasses splashed with ruddy evening sunshine; so that good lady had an excellent chance to talk her illness fully over, describing every ache and pulse beat with such evident enjoyment that Marilla thought even grippe must bring its compensations. When details were exhausted Mrs. Rachel introduced the real reason of her call.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔太太来时，安妮正在果园里，她随心所欲地在茂盛、颤动的草地上漫步，草地上洒满了红润的晚霞。这样，这位善良的女士就有了一个绝佳的机会来详细地谈论她的病情，用如此明显的乐趣描述每一次疼痛和脉搏，以至于玛丽拉认为即使是流行性感冒也必须带来它的补偿。当详细信息耗尽后，雷切尔夫人介绍了她打电话的真正原因。

paragraphs.en: "I've been hearing some surprising things about you and Matthew."
paragraphs.zh: “我听到了一些关于你和马修的令人惊讶的事情。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't suppose you are any more surprised than I am myself," said Marilla. "I'm getting over my surprise now."
paragraphs.zh: “我想你不会比我自己更惊讶，”玛丽拉说。 “我现在已经从惊讶中恢复过来了。”

paragraphs.en: "It was too bad there was such a mistake," said Mrs. Rachel sympathetically. "Couldn't you have sent her back?"
paragraphs.zh: “发生这样的错误真是太糟糕了，”雷切尔夫人同情地说。 “你就不能把她送回去吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose we could, but we decided not to. Matthew took a fancy to her. And I must say I like her myself—although I admit she has her faults. The house seems a different place already. She's a real bright little thing."
