paragraphs.zh: “我想我们可以，但我们决定不这样做。马修很喜欢她。我必须说我自己也喜欢她——尽管我承认她有缺点。房子看起来已经不一样了。她是一个真正聪明的小东西。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla said more than she had intended to say when she began, for she read disapproval in Mrs. Rachel's expression.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉说的比她开始时想说的要多，因为她从雷切尔夫人的表情中看出了不满。

paragraphs.en: "It's a great responsibility you've taken on yourself," said that lady gloomily, "especially when you've never had any experience with children. You don't know much about her or her real disposition, I suppose, and there's no guessing how a child like that will turn out. But I don't want to discourage you I'm sure, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “你为自己承担了很大的责任，”那位女士阴沉地说，“尤其是当你从未有过带孩子的经验时。我想你对她或她的真实性格了解不多，而且无法猜测像这样的孩子会变成什么样子。但我确信我不想让你灰心，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm not feeling discouraged," was Marilla's dry response, "when I make up my mind to do a thing it stays made up. I suppose you'd like to see Anne. I'll call her in."
paragraphs.zh: “我并没有感到灰心丧气，”玛丽拉干巴巴地回答，“当我下定决心要做一件事时，它就会一直下定决心。我想你想见见安妮。我会叫她进来的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne came running in presently, her face sparkling with the delight of her orchard rovings; but, abashed at finding the delight herself in the unexpected presence of a stranger, she halted confusedly inside the door. She certainly was an odd-looking little creature in the short tight wincey dress she had worn from the asylum, below which her thin legs seemed ungracefully long. Her freckles were more numerous and obtrusive than ever; the wind had ruffled her hatless hair into over-brilliant disorder; it had never looked redder than at that moment.
paragraphs.zh: 不久，安妮跑了进来，她的脸因果园漫游的喜悦而闪闪发光。但是，她为自己在陌生人的意外出现中找到乐趣而感到羞愧，困惑地在门内停了下来。穿着从疯人院出来时穿的紧身短裙，她确实是个看上去很奇怪的小东西，裙子下面她的细腿显得长得不雅观。她的雀斑比以往任何时候都更多、更引人注目。风把她没戴帽子的头发吹得乱七八糟。它从来没有比那一刻更红过。

paragraphs.en: "Well, they didn't pick you for your looks, that's sure and certain," was Mrs. Rachel Lynde's emphatic comment. Mrs. Rachel was one of those delightful and popular people who pride themselves on speaking their mind without fear or favor. "She's terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，他们并不是因为你的外表而选择你的，这是肯定的，”雷切尔·林德夫人强调道。雷切尔夫人是那些令人愉快、受欢迎的人之一，她以不畏惧、不偏袒地表达自己的想法而自豪。 “她骨瘦如柴，相貌平平，玛丽拉。过来吧，孩子，让我看看你。老实说，有人见过这样的雀斑吗？还有红得像胡萝卜的头发！过来吧，孩子，我说。”

paragraphs.en: Anne "came there," but not exactly as Mrs. Rachel expected. With one bound she crossed the kitchen floor and stood before Mrs. Rachel, her face scarlet with anger, her lips quivering, and her whole slender form trembling from head to foot.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮“来到了那里”，但并不完全像雷切尔夫人所期望的那样。她一跃穿过厨房的地板，站在雷切尔太太面前，她的脸气得通红，嘴唇颤抖，整个苗条的身躯从头到脚都在颤抖。

paragraphs.en: "I hate you," she cried in a choked voice, stamping her foot on the floor. "I hate you—I hate you—I hate you—" a louder stamp with each assertion of hatred. "How dare you call me skinny and ugly? How dare you say I'm freckled and redheaded? You are a rude, impolite, unfeeling woman!"
paragraphs.zh: “我恨你，”她用哽咽的声音喊道，脚跺在地板上。 “我恨你——我恨你——我恨你——”每一次表达仇恨，都会发出更大的声音。 “你竟敢说我又瘦又丑？你竟敢说我有雀斑、红发？你这个女人，粗鲁无礼，无情无义！”

paragraphs.en: "Anne!" exclaimed Marilla in consternation.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮！”玛丽拉惊愕地喊道。

paragraphs.en: But Anne continued to face Mrs. Rachel undauntedly, head up, eyes blazing, hands clenched, passionate indignation exhaling from her like an atmosphere.
paragraphs.zh: 但安妮依然毫不畏惧地面对着雷切尔夫人，昂首挺胸，目光炽热，双手紧握，一股浓浓的愤慨从她身上散发出来，如同大气一般。

paragraphs.en: "How dare you say such things about me?" she repeated vehemently. "How would you like to have such things said about you? How would you like to be told that you are fat and clumsy and probably hadn't a spark of imagination in you? I don't care if I do hurt your feelings by saying so! I hope I hurt them. You have hurt mine worse than they were ever hurt before even by Mrs. Thomas' intoxicated husband. And I'll NEVER forgive you for it, never, never!"
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么敢这么说我？”她激烈地重复道。 “你怎么愿意别人对你说这样的话？你怎么愿意别人告诉你你又胖又笨，而且可能没有一点想象力的火花？我不在乎我这样说是否伤害了你的感情！我希望我伤害了他们。你对我的伤害比他们以前对我的伤害还要严重，甚至比托马斯夫人醉酒的丈夫所伤害的还要严重。而且我永远不会原谅你，永远，永远！”

paragraphs.en: Stamp! Stamp!
paragraphs.zh: 邮票！邮票！

paragraphs.en: "Did anybody ever see such a temper!" exclaimed the horrified Mrs. Rachel.
paragraphs.zh: “谁见过这么脾气的！”惊恐的雷切尔夫人惊呼道。

paragraphs.en: "Anne go to your room and stay there until I come up," said Marilla, recovering her powers of speech with difficulty.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮去你的房间，呆在那里直到我上来。”玛丽拉艰难地恢复了说话的能力。

paragraphs.en: Anne, bursting into tears, rushed to the hall door, slammed it until the tins on the porch wall outside rattled in sympathy, and fled through the hall and up the stairs like a whirlwind. A subdued slam above told that the door of the east gable had been shut with equal vehemence.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮泪流满面，冲到大厅门口，关上门，直到外面门廊墙上的罐子发出同情的声音，然后像旋风一样逃离大厅，爬上楼梯。上方传来一声微弱的撞击声，表明东山墙的门也同样猛烈地关上了。

paragraphs.en: "Well, I don't envy you your job bringing THAT up, Marilla," said Mrs. Rachel with unspeakable solemnity.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我并不羡慕你提出这个问题的工作，玛丽拉，”雷切尔夫人带着难以言表的严肃说道。

paragraphs.en: Marilla opened her lips to say she knew not what of apology or deprecation. What she did say was a surprise to herself then and ever afterwards.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉张开双唇，表示她不知道该道歉还是不赞成。她所说的话让当时和以后的自己都感到惊讶。

paragraphs.en: "You shouldn't have twitted her about her looks, Rachel."
paragraphs.zh: “你不应该因为她的外表而取笑她，雷切尔。”

paragraphs.en: "Marilla Cuthbert, you don't mean to say that you are upholding her in such a terrible display of temper as we've just seen?" demanded Mrs. Rachel indignantly.
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉·库斯伯特，你不是说你在支持她，就像我们刚才看到的那样，表现出如此可怕的脾气吗？”雷切尔夫人愤怒地问道。

paragraphs.en: "No," said Marilla slowly, "I'm not trying to excuse her. She's been very naughty and I'll have to give her a talking to about it. But we must make allowances for her. She's never been taught what is right. And you WERE too hard on her, Rachel."
paragraphs.zh: “不，”玛丽拉慢慢地说，“我不是想原谅她。她太调皮了，我得跟她谈谈。但我们必须体谅她。她从来没有被教导过什么是正确的。而且你对她太严厉了，雷切尔。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla could not help tacking on that last sentence, although she was again surprised at herself for doing it. Mrs. Rachel got up with an air of offended dignity.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉忍不住补充了最后一句话，尽管她再次对自己这么做感到惊讶。雷切尔夫人站起身来，脸上带着一种被冒犯的尊严。

paragraphs.en: "Well, I see that I'll have to be very careful what I say after this, Marilla, since the fine feelings of orphans, brought from goodness knows where, have to be considered before anything else. Oh, no, I'm not vexed—don't worry yourself. I'm too sorry for you to leave any room for anger in my mind. You'll have your own troubles with that child. But if you'll take my advice—which I suppose you won't do, although I've brought up ten children and buried two—you'll do that 'talking to' you mention with a fair-sized birch switch. I should think THAT would be the most effective language for that kind of a child. Her temper matches her hair I guess. Well, good evening, Marilla. I hope you'll come down to see me often as usual. But you can't expect me to visit here again in a hurry, if I'm liable to be flown at and insulted in such a fashion. It's something new in MY experience."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我知道我以后说话必须非常小心，玛丽拉，因为孤儿的美好感情，天知道从哪里来的，必须首先考虑。哦，不，我不生气——你不用担心。我很抱歉你不能在我心里留下任何愤怒的余地。你会为那个孩子找到麻烦的。但如果你接受我的建议——我想你不会这么做，尽管我已经带来了十个孩子，埋葬两个——我想，对于那种孩子来说，这将是最有效的语言。好吧，晚安，玛丽拉，但如果我很容易受到这样的侮辱，你就不能指望我会匆忙地再次来到这里。我的经历。”

paragraphs.en: Whereat Mrs. Rachel swept out and away—if a fat woman who always waddled COULD be said to sweep away—and Marilla with a very solemn face betook herself to the east gable.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔太太大步走开——如果一个总是摇摇晃晃的胖女人也能说是大步走开的话——而玛丽拉则一脸严肃地走向东山墙。

paragraphs.en: On the way upstairs she pondered uneasily as to what she ought to do. She felt no little dismay over the scene that had just been enacted. How unfortunate that Anne should have displayed such temper before Mrs. Rachel Lynde, of all people! Then Marilla suddenly became aware of an uncomfortable and rebuking consciousness that she felt more humiliation over this than sorrow over the discovery of such a serious defect in Anne's disposition. And how was she to punish her? The amiable suggestion of the birch switch—to the efficiency of which all of Mrs. Rachel's own children could have borne smarting testimony—did not appeal to Marilla. She did not believe she could whip a child. No, some other method of punishment must be found to bring Anne to a proper realization of the enormity of her offense.
paragraphs.zh: 上楼的路上，她不安地思考着自己应该做什么。对于刚刚发生的一幕，她感到不小的沮丧。安妮在雷切尔·林德夫人面前表现出这样的脾气是多么不幸啊！然后玛丽拉突然意识到一种不舒服和责备的意识，她对此感到更多的是羞辱，而不是发现安妮性格中如此严重的缺陷的悲伤。而她该如何惩罚她呢？桦树开关的友善建议——雷切尔夫人自己的所有孩子都可以证明其有效性——并没有吸引玛丽拉。她不相信自己能鞭打一个孩子。不，必须找到其他惩罚方法，让安妮正确认识到她所犯下的罪行的严重性。

paragraphs.en: Marilla found Anne face downward on her bed, crying bitterly, quite oblivious of muddy boots on a clean counterpane.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉发现安妮脸朝下躺在床上，痛苦地哭泣，完全忘记了干净的床单上沾满泥的靴子。

paragraphs.en: "Anne," she said not ungently.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”她毫不客气地说。

paragraphs.en: No answer.
paragraphs.zh: 没有答案。

paragraphs.en: "Anne," with greater severity, "get off that bed this minute and listen to what I have to say to you."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”更加严厉地说道，“现在就起床，听听我要对你说的话。”

paragraphs.en: Anne squirmed off the bed and sat rigidly on a chair beside it, her face swollen and tear-stained and her eyes fixed stubbornly on the floor.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮从床上爬起来，僵硬地坐在床边的椅子上，脸肿胀，泪痕累累，眼睛死死地盯着地板。

paragraphs.en: "This is a nice way for you to behave. Anne! Aren't you ashamed of yourself?"
paragraphs.zh: “这对你来说是一个很好的行为方式。安妮！你不为自己感到羞耻吗？”

paragraphs.en: "She hadn't any right to call me ugly and redheaded," retorted Anne, evasive and defiant.
paragraphs.zh: “她没有权利说我丑陋和红发，”安妮反驳道，语气闪烁而挑衅。

paragraphs.en: "You hadn't any right to fly into such a fury and talk the way you did to her, Anne. I was ashamed of you—thoroughly ashamed of you. I wanted you to behave nicely to Mrs. Lynde, and instead of that you have disgraced me. I'm sure I don't know why you should lose your temper like that just because Mrs. Lynde said you were red-haired and homely. You say it yourself often enough."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你没有权利大发雷霆，用你对她的方式说话。我为你感到羞耻——彻底为你感到羞耻。我希望你对林德太太表现得友善，但你却让我蒙羞。我确信我不知道你为什么要这样发脾气，仅仅因为林德太太说你是红发的，相貌平平。你自己也经常这么说。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, but there's such a difference between saying a thing yourself and hearing other people say it," wailed Anne. "You may know a thing is so, but you can't help hoping other people don't quite think it is. I suppose you think I have an awful temper, but I couldn't help it. When she said those things something just rose right up in me and choked me. I HAD to fly out at her."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，但是你自己说的话和听别人说的话有很大的不同，”安妮哀叹道。 “你可能知道事情就是这样，但你情不自禁地希望别人不这么认为。我想你认为我脾气很糟糕，但我控制不住。当她说那些话时，有一种东西突然从我心里升起，让我窒息。我不得不向她飞去。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, you made a fine exhibition of yourself I must say. Mrs. Lynde will have a nice story to tell about you everywhere—and she'll tell it, too. It was a dreadful thing for you to lose your temper like that, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我必须说，你表现得很好。林德太太到处都会有一个关于你的好故事——她也会讲。安妮，你这样发脾气是一件可怕的事情。”

paragraphs.en: "Just imagine how you would feel if somebody told you to your face that you were skinny and ugly," pleaded Anne tearfully.
paragraphs.zh: “想象一下，如果有人当面告诉你，你又瘦又丑，你会有什么感觉，”安妮泪流满面地恳求道。

paragraphs.en: An old remembrance suddenly rose up before Marilla. She had been a very small child when she had heard one aunt say of her to another, "What a pity she is such a dark, homely little thing." Marilla was every day of fifty before the sting had gone out of that memory.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉的脑海中突然浮现出一段往事。当她还是个很小的孩子时，她听到一位阿姨对另一位阿姨说起她：“真遗憾，她是一个如此黑暗、相貌平庸的小东西。”玛丽拉每天都五十岁了，直到那段刺痛才从记忆中消失。

paragraphs.en: "I don't say that I think Mrs. Lynde was exactly right in saying what she did to you, Anne," she admitted in a softer tone. "Rachel is too outspoken. But that is no excuse for such behavior on your part. She was a stranger and an elderly person and my visitor—all three very good reasons why you should have been respectful to her. You were rude and saucy and"—Marilla had a saving inspiration of punishment—"you must go to her and tell her you are very sorry for your bad temper and ask her to forgive you."
paragraphs.zh: “我并不是说我认为林德夫人对你所做的事情是完全正确的，安妮，”她用更柔和的语气承认。 “雷切尔太直言不讳了。但这不是你做出这种行为的借口。她是一个陌生人，一个老人，也是我的访客——这三个都是你应该尊重她的充分理由。你粗鲁无礼，而且”——玛丽拉有了惩罚的拯救灵感——“你必须去找她，告诉她你对你的坏脾气感到非常抱歉，并请求她原谅你。”

paragraphs.en: "I can never do that," said Anne determinedly and darkly. "You can punish me in any way you like, Marilla. You can shut me up in a dark, damp dungeon inhabited by snakes and toads and feed me only on bread and water and I shall not complain. But I cannot ask Mrs. Lynde to forgive me."
paragraphs.zh: “我永远做不到。”安妮坚定而阴沉地说。 “你可以用任何你喜欢的方式惩罚我，玛丽拉。你可以把我关在一个黑暗、潮湿、蛇和蟾蜍居住的地牢里，只给我吃面包和水，我不会抱怨。但我不能请求林德夫人原谅我。”

paragraphs.en: "We're not in the habit of shutting people up in dark damp dungeons," said Marilla drily, "especially as they're rather scarce in Avonlea. But apologize to Mrs. Lynde you must and shall and you'll stay here in your room until you can tell me you're willing to do it."
paragraphs.zh: “我们没有把人关在又黑又湿的地牢里的习惯，”玛丽拉冷冷地说，“尤其是在埃文利，这种地牢相当稀少。不过，向林德夫人道歉，你必须而且应该这么做，而且你要待在你的房间里，直到你告诉我你愿意这样做。”

paragraphs.en: "I shall have to stay here forever then," said Anne mournfully, "because I can't tell Mrs. Lynde I'm sorry I said those things to her. How can I? I'm NOT sorry. I'm sorry I've vexed you; but I'm GLAD I told her just what I did. It was a great satisfaction. I can't say I'm sorry when I'm not, can I? I can't even IMAGINE I'm sorry."
paragraphs.zh: “那我就得永远留在这里了，”安妮悲伤地说，“因为我不能告诉林德太太，我很抱歉我对她说了这些话。我怎么能？我不抱歉。很抱歉我惹恼了你；但我很高兴我告诉了她我所做的事情。这是一种极大的满足。当我不道歉时，我不能说我很抱歉，不是吗？我什至无法想象我很抱歉。”

paragraphs.en: "Perhaps your imagination will be in better working order by the morning," said Marilla, rising to depart. "You'll have the night to think over your conduct in and come to a better frame of mind. You said you would try to be a very good girl if we kept you at Green Gables, but I must say it hasn't seemed very much like it this evening."
paragraphs.zh: “也许到早上你的想象力就会更好地发挥作用，”玛丽拉说，起身准备离开。 “你将有一个晚上的时间来思考你的行为，并获得更好的心态。你说过，如果我们把你留在绿山墙，你会努力成为一个非常好的女孩，但我必须说，今晚看起来不太像。”

paragraphs.en: Leaving this Parthian shaft to rankle in Anne's stormy bosom, Marilla descended to the kitchen, grievously troubled in mind and vexed in soul. She was as angry with herself as with Anne, because, whenever she recalled Mrs. Rachel's dumbfounded countenance her lips twitched with amusement and she felt a most reprehensible desire to laugh.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉把这根帕提亚式的竖井留在安妮暴风雨般的怀抱中，她下楼来到厨房，心里极度烦恼，灵魂烦恼。她对自己就像对安妮一样生气，因为每当她想起雷切尔夫人目瞪口呆的表情时，她的嘴唇都会因有趣而抽动，她感到一种最应受谴责的想笑的欲望。

chapters.title: CHAPTER X. Anne's Apology
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 10 章：安妮的赔礼道歉

paragraphs.en: Marilla said nothing to Matthew about the affair that evening; but when Anne proved still refractory the next morning an explanation had to be made to account for her absence from the breakfast table. Marilla told Matthew the whole story, taking pains to impress him with a due sense of the enormity of Anne's behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉没有向马修提及这件事。但第二天早上，当安妮仍然难以控制时，必须对她缺席早餐桌做出解释。玛丽拉向马修讲述了整个故事，并煞费苦心地让他对安妮行为的严重性产生应有的认识。

paragraphs.en: "It's a good thing Rachel Lynde got a calling down; she's a meddlesome old gossip," was Matthew's consolatory rejoinder.
paragraphs.zh: “雷切尔·林德接到电话是件好事；她是个爱管闲事的老八卦者，”马修安慰性地反驳道。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew Cuthbert, I'm astonished at you. You know that Anne's behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you'll be saying next thing that she oughtn't to be punished at all!"
paragraphs.zh: “马修·库斯伯特，我对你感到惊讶。你知道安妮的行为很可怕，但你却支持她！我想你接下来会说她根本不应该受到惩罚！”

paragraphs.en: "Well now—no—not exactly," said Matthew uneasily. "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don't be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn't ever had anyone to teach her right. You're—you're going to give her something to eat, aren't you?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧——不——不完全是，”马修不安地说。 “我认为她应该受到一点惩罚。但是别对她太严厉，玛丽拉。记住她从来没有人正确地教导过她。你——你会给她一些吃的，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "When did you ever hear of me starving people into good behavior?" demanded Marilla indignantly. "She'll have her meals regular, and I'll carry them up to her myself. But she'll stay up there until she's willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that's final, Matthew."
paragraphs.zh: “你什么时候听说过我让人们挨饿，让他们养成良好的行为？”玛丽拉愤怒地问道。 “她会定期吃饭，我会亲自给她送饭。但她会呆在那里，直到她愿意向林德夫人道歉，这是最后的决定，马修。”

paragraphs.en: Breakfast, dinner, and supper were very silent meals—for Anne still remained obdurate. After each meal Marilla carried a well-filled tray to the east gable and brought it down later on not noticeably depleted. Matthew eyed its last descent with a troubled eye. Had Anne eaten anything at all?
paragraphs.zh: 早餐、晚餐和晚饭都是非常安静的三餐——因为安妮仍然固执己见。每顿饭后，玛丽拉都会把一个装满食物的托盘带到东山墙，然后再把它拿下来，但托盘上的食物并没有明显耗尽。马修用不安的眼神看着它的最后一次下降。安妮到底吃过什么东西吗？

paragraphs.en: When Marilla went out that evening to bring the cows from the back pasture, Matthew, who had been hanging about the barns and watching, slipped into the house with the air of a burglar and crept upstairs. As a general thing Matthew gravitated between the kitchen and the little bedroom off the hall where he slept; once in a while he ventured uncomfortably into the parlor or sitting room when the minister came to tea. But he had never been upstairs in his own house since the spring he helped Marilla paper the spare bedroom, and that was four years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，当玛丽拉出去把奶牛从后面的牧场牵出来时，一直在谷仓周围观察的马修像窃贼一样溜进了房子，蹑手蹑脚地爬上了楼。一般来说，马修总是在厨房和他睡觉的大厅外的小卧室之间徘徊。偶尔，当部长来喝茶时，他会不舒服地冒险走进客厅或客厅。但自从四年前春天他帮助玛丽拉给空余的卧室贴上报纸以来，他就再也没有上过自己房子的楼上。

paragraphs.en: He tiptoed along the hall and stood for several minutes outside the door of the east gable before he summoned courage to tap on it with his fingers and then open the door to peep in.
paragraphs.zh: 他蹑手蹑脚地沿着大厅，在东山墙门外站了几分钟，才鼓起勇气用手指敲了敲门，然后打开门往里看。

paragraphs.en: Anne was sitting on the yellow chair by the window gazing mournfully out into the garden. Very small and unhappy she looked, and Matthew's heart smote him. He softly closed the door and tiptoed over to her.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮坐在窗边的黄色椅子上，悲伤地凝视着外面的花园。她看起来很小，而且很不高兴，马修的心猛地一跳。他轻轻关上门，蹑手蹑脚地走到她身边。

paragraphs.en: "Anne," he whispered, as if afraid of being overheard, "how are you making it, Anne?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”他低声说道，仿佛生怕被人听见，“安妮，你过得怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: Anne smiled wanly.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮苍白地笑了笑。

paragraphs.en: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it's rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."
paragraphs.zh: “还不错。我想了很多，这有助于打发时间。当然，这是相当孤独的。不过，我还是习惯一下吧。”

paragraphs.en: Anne smiled again, bravely facing the long years of solitary imprisonment before her.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮再次微笑，勇敢地面对眼前多年的孤独监禁。

paragraphs.en: Matthew recollected that he must say what he had come to say without loss of time, lest Marilla return prematurely. "Well now, Anne, don't you think you'd better do it and have it over with?" he whispered. "It'll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla's a dreadful deter-mined woman—dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over."
paragraphs.zh: 马修想起来，他必须抓紧时间说完自己要说的话，免得玛丽拉过早回来。 “好吧，安妮，你不认为你最好还是把这件事结束吧？”他低声说道。 “这件事迟早要完成，你知道，因为玛丽拉是个意志坚定得可怕的女人——意志坚定得可怕，安妮。我说，马上做，然后把它结束。”

paragraphs.en: "Do you mean apologize to Mrs. Lynde?"
paragraphs.zh: “你的意思是向林德夫人道歉吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes—apologize—that's the very word," said Matthew eagerly. "Just smooth it over so to speak. That's what I was trying to get at."
paragraphs.zh: “是的——道歉——就是这个词，”马修急切地说。 “可以这么说，把事情弄平。这就是我想要达到的目的。”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose I could do it to oblige you," said Anne thoughtfully. "It would be true enough to say I am sorry, because I AM sorry now. I wasn't a bit sorry last night. I was mad clear through, and I stayed mad all night. I know I did because I woke up three times and I was just furious every time. But this morning it was over. I wasn't in a temper anymore—and it left a dreadful sort of goneness, too. I felt so ashamed of myself. But I just couldn't think of going and telling Mrs. Lynde so. It would be so humiliating. I made up my mind I'd stay shut up here forever rather than do that. But still—I'd do anything for you—if you really want me to—"
paragraphs.zh: “我想我可以尽力满足你的要求，”安妮若有所思地说。 “说对不起是真的，因为我现在很抱歉。昨晚我一点也不后悔。我整个晚上都在生气。我知道我这么做了，因为我醒了三次，每次我都很生气。但是今天早上一切都结束了。我不再发脾气了——而且也留下了一种可怕的失落感。我为自己感到羞愧。但我就是想不起去告诉林德太太。所以，我决定永远关在这里，而不是那样做——但我愿意为你做任何事——如果你真的想要我——”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, of course I do. It's terrible lonesome downstairs without you. Just go and smooth things over—that's a good girl."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，我当然知道了。楼下没有你，太孤独了。去把事情搞平吧——这真是个好女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "Very well," said Anne resignedly. "I'll tell Marilla as soon as she comes in I've repented."
paragraphs.zh: “很好，”安妮无奈地说。 “玛丽拉一进来我就会告诉她我已经悔改了。”

paragraphs.en: "That's right—that's right, Anne. But don't tell Marilla I said anything about it. She might think I was putting my oar in and I promised not to do that."
paragraphs.zh: “没错——没错，安妮。但是别告诉玛丽拉我说过这件事。她可能会认为我在划桨，而我保证不会那样做。”

paragraphs.en: "Wild horses won't drag the secret from me," promised Anne solemnly. "How would wild horses drag a secret from a person anyhow?"
paragraphs.zh: “野马不会把这个秘密从我身边夺走。”安妮郑重地保证道。 “野马怎么可能从一个人身上夺走秘密呢？”

paragraphs.en: But Matthew was gone, scared at his own success. He fled hastily to the remotest corner of the horse pasture lest Marilla should suspect what he had been up to. Marilla herself, upon her return to the house, was agreeably surprised to hear a plaintive voice calling, "Marilla" over the banisters.
paragraphs.zh: 但马修却离开了，他对自己的成功感到害怕。他匆忙逃到马牧场最偏僻的角落，以免玛丽拉怀疑他的所作所为。玛丽拉回到家后，惊讶地听到栏杆上有一个悲伤的声音喊道：“玛丽拉”。

paragraphs.en: "Well?" she said, going into the hall.
paragraphs.zh: “出色地？”她一边说，一边走进大厅。

paragraphs.en: "I'm sorry I lost my temper and said rude things, and I'm willing to go and tell Mrs. Lynde so."
paragraphs.zh: “对不起，我发脾气了，说了粗鲁的话，我愿意去告诉林德太太。”

paragraphs.en: "Very well." Marilla's crispness gave no sign of her relief. She had been wondering what under the canopy she should do if Anne did not give in. "I'll take you down after milking."
paragraphs.zh: “很好。”玛丽拉的清脆心情并没有让她松一口气的迹象。她一直在想，如果安妮不屈服，她应该在天篷下做什么。“挤奶后我会把你带下去。”

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, after milking, behold Marilla and Anne walking down the lane, the former erect and triumphant, the latter drooping and dejected. But halfway down Anne's dejection vanished as if by enchantment. She lifted her head and stepped lightly along, her eyes fixed on the sunset sky and an air of subdued exhilaration about her. Marilla beheld the change disapprovingly. This was no meek penitent such as it behooved her to take into the presence of the offended Mrs. Lynde.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，挤完奶后，玛丽拉和安妮沿着小巷走去，前者昂首阔步，得意洋洋，后者垂头丧气，垂头丧气。但到了一半，安妮的沮丧仿佛着了魔一样消失了。她抬起头，迈着轻快的步伐，目光注视着夕阳的天空，浑身上下透着一股压抑的兴奋。玛丽拉不满地看着这一变化。这可不是温顺的忏悔，她应该在被冒犯的林德夫人面前接受这种忏悔。

paragraphs.en: "What are you thinking of, Anne?" she asked sharply.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你在想什么？”她尖锐地问道。

paragraphs.en: "I'm imagining out what I must say to Mrs. Lynde," answered Anne dreamily.
paragraphs.zh: “我正在想象我该对林德太太说些什么。”安妮若有所思地回答道。

paragraphs.en: This was satisfactory—or should have been so. But Marilla could not rid herself of the notion that something in her scheme of punishment was going askew. Anne had no business to look so rapt and radiant.
paragraphs.zh: 这是令人满意的——或者说应该如此。但玛丽拉无法摆脱这样的想法：她的惩罚计划中有些东西出了问题。安妮没必要显得如此全神贯注、容光焕发。

paragraphs.en: Rapt and radiant Anne continued until they were in the very presence of Mrs. Lynde, who was sitting knitting by her kitchen window. Then the radiance vanished. Mournful penitence appeared on every feature. Before a word was spoken Anne suddenly went down on her knees before the astonished Mrs. Rachel and held out her hands beseechingly.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮全神贯注、容光焕发地继续说着，直到林德太太出现在他们面前，林德太太正坐在厨房的窗边织毛衣。然后光芒消失了。每一个面容上都流露出悲痛的悔罪之情。还没等说话，安妮突然跪倒在惊讶的雷切尔夫人面前，恳求地伸出双手。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Mrs. Lynde, I am so extremely sorry," she said with a quiver in her voice. "I could never express all my sorrow, no, not if I used up a whole dictionary. You must just imagine it. I behaved terribly to you—and I've disgraced the dear friends, Matthew and Marilla, who have let me stay at Green Gables although I'm not a boy. I'm a dreadfully wicked and ungrateful girl, and I deserve to be punished and cast out by respectable people forever. It was very wicked of me to fly into a temper because you told me the truth. It WAS the truth; every word you said was true. My hair is red and I'm freckled and skinny and ugly. What I said to you was true, too, but I shouldn't have said it. Oh, Mrs. Lynde, please, please, forgive me. If you refuse it will be a lifelong sorrow on a poor little orphan girl, would you, even if she had a dreadful temper? Oh, I am sure you wouldn't. Please say you forgive me, Mrs. Lynde."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，林德夫人，我非常抱歉，”她声音颤抖地说。 “我永远无法表达我所有的悲伤，不，如果我用完了整本字典，我就永远无法表达我的悲伤。你必须想象一下。我对你的行为很糟糕——我让亲爱的朋友马修和玛丽拉蒙羞，他们让我留在绿山墙，尽管我不是一个男孩。我是一个非常邪恶和忘恩负义的女孩，我应该受到惩罚，并永远被可敬的人驱逐。我飞入一个脾气，因为你说的是实话；我的头发是红色的，我对你说的话也是真的，但我不应该说出来。哦，林德夫人，请原谅我。如果你拒绝，那将是一个可怜的小孤儿的一生的悲伤，哦，我相信你不会说。请原谅我，林德夫人。”

paragraphs.en: Anne clasped her hands together, bowed her head, and waited for the word of judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮双手合十，低下头，等待着判决的声音。

paragraphs.en: There was no mistaking her sincerity—it breathed in every tone of her voice. Both Marilla and Mrs. Lynde recognized its unmistakable ring. But the former under-stood in dismay that Anne was actually enjoying her valley of humiliation—was reveling in the thoroughness of her abasement. Where was the wholesome punishment upon which she, Marilla, had plumed herself? Anne had turned it into a species of positive pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 毫无疑问，她的真诚体现在她的每一个语气中。玛丽拉和林德夫人都认出了这枚毫无疑问的戒指。但前者沮丧地意识到，安妮实际上正在享受她的屈辱之谷——陶醉于她彻底的屈辱。她，玛丽拉，曾为自己引以为豪的有益健康的惩罚在哪里？安妮把它变成了一种积极的快乐。

paragraphs.en: Good Mrs. Lynde, not being overburdened with perception, did not see this. She only perceived that Anne had made a very thorough apology and all resentment vanished from her kindly, if somewhat officious, heart.
paragraphs.zh: 善良的林德夫人并没有被太多的感知所负担，她没有看到这一点。她只觉得安妮已经非常彻底地道歉了，所有的怨恨都从她那颗善良而又多管闲事的心里消失了。

paragraphs.en: "There, there, get up, child," she said heartily. "Of course I forgive you. I guess I was a little too hard on you, anyway. But I'm such an outspoken person. You just mustn't mind me, that's what. It can't be denied your hair is terrible red; but I knew a girl once—went to school with her, in fact—whose hair was every mite as red as yours when she was young, but when she grew up it darkened to a real handsome auburn. I wouldn't be a mite surprised if yours did, too—not a mite."
paragraphs.zh: “好了，好了，起来吧，孩子。”她由衷地说。 “我当然原谅你。无论如何，我想我对你有点太严厉了。但我是个直言不讳的人。你只是不能介意我，就是这样。不可否认，你的头发红得很厉害；但我曾经认识一个女孩——事实上，和她一起上学——她年轻时的头发和你的头发一样红，但长大后颜色变成了真正漂亮的赤褐色。如果你的也一样——一点也没有。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Mrs. Lynde!" Anne drew a long breath as she rose to her feet. "You have given me a hope. I shall always feel that you are a benefactor. Oh, I could endure anything if I only thought my hair would be a handsome auburn when I grew up. It would be so much easier to be good if one's hair was a handsome auburn, don't you think? And now may I go out into your garden and sit on that bench under the apple-trees while you and Marilla are talking? There is so much more scope for imagination out there."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，林德夫人！”安妮长长地吸了一口气，站了起来。 “你给了我希望。我会永远觉得你是一个恩人。哦，只要我长大后的头发是漂亮的赤褐色，我就可以忍受任何事情。如果一个人的头发是漂亮的赤褐色，那么做个好人会容易得多，你不觉得吗？现在我可以到你的花园去，坐在苹果树下的长凳上，而你和玛丽拉正在说话吗？那里有更多的想象空间。”

paragraphs.en: "Laws, yes, run along, child. And you can pick a bouquet of them white June lilies over in the corner if you like."
paragraphs.zh: “法律，是的，走吧，孩子。如果你愿意的话，你可以在角落里摘一束白色的六月百合。”

paragraphs.en: As the door closed behind Anne Mrs. Lynde got briskly up to light a lamp.
paragraphs.zh: 当安妮身后的门关上时，林德夫人轻快地起身点了一盏灯。

paragraphs.en: "She's a real odd little thing. Take this chair, Marilla; it's easier than the one you've got; I just keep that for the hired boy to sit on. Yes, she certainly is an odd child, but there is something kind of taking about her after all. I don't feel so surprised at you and Matthew keeping her as I did—nor so sorry for you, either. She may turn out all right. Of course, she has a queer way of expressing herself—a little too—well, too kind of forcible, you know; but she'll likely get over that now that she's come to live among civilized folks. And then, her temper's pretty quick, I guess; but there's one comfort, a child that has a quick temper, just blaze up and cool down, ain't never likely to be sly or deceitful. Preserve me from a sly child, that's what. On the whole, Marilla, I kind of like her."
paragraphs.zh: “她真是个奇怪的小东西。拿这把椅子吧，玛丽拉；它比你现有的容易一些；我只是把它留给雇来的男孩坐。是的，她确实是个奇怪的孩子，但毕竟她身上有某种东西。我对你和马修像我一样留着她并不感到惊讶——也不为你感到难过。她可能会没事。当然，她有一种奇怪的表达方式——有点太——呃，太善良了。”你知道，但既然她生活在文明人中间，她可能会克服这一点；但有一个安慰，一个脾气暴躁的孩子，永远不会狡猾或欺骗，这就是为什么，玛丽拉，我有点喜欢她。

paragraphs.en: When Marilla went home Anne came out of the fragrant twilight of the orchard with a sheaf of white narcissi in her hands.
paragraphs.zh: 当玛丽拉回家时，安妮从果园芬芳的暮色中走出来，手里拿着一束白色的水仙花。

paragraphs.en: "I apologized pretty well, didn't I?" she said proudly as they went down the lane. "I thought since I had to do it I might as well do it thoroughly."
paragraphs.zh: “我已经道歉得很好了，不是吗？”当他们沿着小巷走时，她自豪地说。 “我想既然非做不可，不如彻底做吧。”

paragraphs.en: "You did it thoroughly, all right enough," was Marilla's comment. Marilla was dismayed at finding herself inclined to laugh over the recollection. She had also an uneasy feeling that she ought to scold Anne for apologizing so well; but then, that was ridiculous! She compromised with her conscience by saying severely:
paragraphs.zh: “你做得很彻底，很好，”玛丽拉评论道。玛丽拉沮丧地发现自己很容易因为回忆而发笑。她还有一种不安的感觉，她应该责骂安妮道歉得这么好。但那时，这太荒谬了！她违背良心，严厉地说：

paragraphs.en: "I hope you won't have occasion to make many more such apologies. I hope you'll try to control your temper now, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你不会再有机会做出更多这样的道歉。我希望你现在能控制住自己的脾气，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "That wouldn't be so hard if people wouldn't twit me about my looks," said Anne with a sigh. "I don't get cross about other things; but I'm SO tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"
paragraphs.zh: “如果人们不因为我的外表而取笑我，那就不那么难了，”安妮叹了口气说。 “我不会对其他事情生气；但我厌倦了别人对我头发的嘲笑，这让我很生气。你认为我长大后的头发真的会变成漂亮的赤褐色吗？”

paragraphs.en: "You shouldn't think so much about your looks, Anne. I'm afraid you are a very vain little girl."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你不应该太在意自己的外表。我担心你是一个非常虚荣的小女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "How can I be vain when I know I'm homely?" protested Anne. "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn't pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn't beautiful."
paragraphs.zh: “既然我知道自己很相貌，怎么能虚荣呢？”安妮抗议道。 “我喜欢漂亮的东西；我讨厌在镜子里看到不漂亮的东西。这让我感到非常悲伤——就像我看到任何丑陋的东西时的感觉一样。我怜悯它，因为它不漂亮。”

paragraphs.en: "Handsome is as handsome does," quoted Marilla. "I've had that said to me before, but I have my doubts about it," remarked skeptical Anne, sniffing at her narcissi. "Oh, aren't these flowers sweet! It was lovely of Mrs. Lynde to give them to me. I have no hard feelings against Mrs. Lynde now. It gives you a lovely, comfortable feeling to apologize and be forgiven, doesn't it? Aren't the stars bright tonight? If you could live in a star, which one would you pick? I'd like that lovely clear big one away over there above that dark hill."
paragraphs.zh: “英俊就是英俊，”玛丽拉引用道。 “以前有人这样对我说过，但我对此表示怀疑，”持怀疑态度的安妮嗅着她的自恋，说道。 “噢，这些花不是很甜吗？林德夫人把它们送给我真是太可爱了。我现在对林德夫人没有任何怨恨了。道歉和被原谅会给你一种可爱、舒适的感觉，不是吗？今晚的星星不是很亮吗？如果你能生活在一颗星星里，你会选哪一颗？我想要在那座黑暗的山上那颗可爱的、清澈的大星星。”

paragraphs.en: "Anne, do hold your tongue," said Marilla, thoroughly worn out trying to follow the gyrations of Anne's thoughts.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，请闭嘴，”玛丽拉说，她在试图跟上安妮思绪的旋转时已经筋疲力尽了。

paragraphs.en: Anne said no more until they turned into their own lane. A little gypsy wind came down it to meet them, laden with the spicy perfume of young dew-wet ferns. Far up in the shadows a cheerful light gleamed out through the trees from the kitchen at Green Gables. Anne suddenly came close to Marilla and slipped her hand into the older woman's hard palm.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮没有再说什么，直到他们拐进自己的车道。一阵吉普赛风迎面而来，带着年轻的露水湿蕨类植物的辛辣香气。远处的阴影中，绿山墙厨房的树林里发出欢快的灯光。安妮突然靠近玛丽拉，把手伸进老妇人坚硬的手掌里。

paragraphs.en: "It's lovely to be going home and know it's home," she said. "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I'm so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."
paragraphs.zh: “回家并知道这是家真是太好了，”她说。 “我已经喜欢绿山墙了，以前我从来没有喜欢过任何地方。没有一个地方像家。哦，玛丽拉，我太高兴了。我现在就可以祈祷，不会觉得有点困难。”

paragraphs.en: Something warm and pleasant welled up in Marilla's heart at touch of that thin little hand in her own—a throb of the maternity she had missed, perhaps. Its very unaccustomedness and sweetness disturbed her. She hastened to restore her sensations to their normal calm by inculcating a moral.
paragraphs.zh: 当玛丽拉那只瘦弱的小手碰触到她的时候，一种温暖而愉快的感觉涌上心头——也许是她怀念的母性的悸动。这种不习惯和甜蜜让她不安。她赶紧通过灌输道德来使自己的感觉恢复正常的平静。

paragraphs.en: "If you'll be a good girl you'll always be happy, Anne. And you should never find it hard to say your prayers."
paragraphs.zh: “如果你是一个好女孩，你就会永远快乐，安妮。而且你永远不会觉得说出你的祈祷是困难的。”

paragraphs.en: "Saying one's prayers isn't exactly the same thing as praying," said Anne meditatively. "But I'm going to imagine that I'm the wind that is blowing up there in those tree tops. When I get tired of the trees I'll imagine I'm gently waving down here in the ferns—and then I'll fly over to Mrs. Lynde's garden and set the flowers dancing—and then I'll go with one great swoop over the clover field—and then I'll blow over the Lake of Shining Waters and ripple it all up into little sparkling waves. Oh, there's so much scope for imagination in a wind! So I'll not talk any more just now, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “祈祷和祈祷并不完全一样，”安妮若有所思地说。 “但我会想象自己是那些树顶上吹起的风。当我厌倦了树木时，我会想象自己在蕨类植物中轻轻地挥手——然后我会飞到林德夫人的花园，让花朵翩翩起舞——然后我会在三叶草田上猛扑一下——然后我会吹过光辉湖，把它荡漾成闪闪发光的小波浪。哦，风的想象空间真大啊，所以我现在不再说话了，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: "Thanks be to goodness for that," breathed Marilla in devout relief.
paragraphs.zh: “谢天谢地，”玛丽拉虔诚地松了口气。

chapters.title: CHAPTER XI. Anne's Impressions of Sunday-School
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 11 章：安妮的主日学印象

paragraphs.en: "Well, how do you like them?" said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，你觉得他们怎么样？”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: Anne was standing in the gable room, looking solemnly at three new dresses spread out on the bed. One was of snuffy colored gingham which Marilla had been tempted to buy from a peddler the preceding summer because it looked so serviceable; one was of black-and-white checkered sateen which she had picked up at a bargain counter in the winter; and one was a stiff print of an ugly blue shade which she had purchased that week at a Carmody store.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站在山墙房里，表情严肃地看着床上铺着的三件新衣服。其中一件是颜色鲜艳的格子布，去年夏天，玛丽拉很想从小贩那里买下来，因为它看起来很实用。一件是黑白格子棉缎，是她冬天在特价柜台买的；一件是她冬天在特价柜台买的。其中一张是一张丑陋的蓝色图案的硬板印刷品，是她那周在卡莫迪商店购买的。

paragraphs.en: She had made them up herself, and they were all made alike—plain skirts fulled tightly to plain waists, with sleeves as plain as waist and skirt and tight as sleeves could be.
paragraphs.zh: 都是她自己缝制的，而且都是一样的——朴素的裙子，紧紧地塞到朴素的腰部，袖子和腰身、裙子一样朴素，袖子也尽可能地紧。

paragraphs.en: "I'll imagine that I like them," said Anne soberly.
paragraphs.zh: “我会想象我喜欢它们，”安妮严肃地说。

paragraphs.en: "I don't want you to imagine it," said Marilla, offended. "Oh, I can see you don't like the dresses! What is the matter with them? Aren't they neat and clean and new?"
paragraphs.zh: “我不想让你想象，”玛丽拉生气地说。 “哦，我看得出来你不喜欢这些衣服！它们怎么了？它们不是很整洁、很新吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes."
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”

paragraphs.en: "Then why don't you like them?"
paragraphs.zh: “那你为什么不喜欢它们呢？”

paragraphs.en: "They're—they're not—pretty," said Anne reluctantly.
paragraphs.zh: “它们——它们——不——漂亮，”安妮不情愿地说。

paragraphs.en: "Pretty!" Marilla sniffed. "I didn't trouble my head about getting pretty dresses for you. I don't believe in pampering vanity, Anne, I'll tell you that right off. Those dresses are good, sensible, serviceable dresses, without any frills or furbelows about them, and they're all you'll get this summer. The brown gingham and the blue print will do you for school when you begin to go. The sateen is for church and Sunday school. I'll expect you to keep them neat and clean and not to tear them. I should think you'd be grateful to get most anything after those skimpy wincey things you've been wearing."
paragraphs.zh: “漂亮的！”玛丽拉吸了吸鼻子。 “我没有费尽心思为你买漂亮的衣服。我不相信虚荣心，安妮，我马上就告诉你。这些衣服很好，很实用，很实用，没有任何装饰或毛茸茸的东西，它们就是你今年夏天所能得到的。棕色格子布和蓝色印花可以让你开始上学时穿。缎子是教堂和主日学校穿的。我希望你保持它们整洁干净。我想，在你穿了那些破烂的衣服之后，你会很感激得到任何东西。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I AM grateful," protested Anne. "But I'd be ever so much gratefuller if—if you'd made just one of them with puffed sleeves. Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now. It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我很感激，”安妮抗议道。 “但如果——如果你只制作一件带有泡泡袖的衣服，我会非常感激。泡泡袖现在很流行。玛丽拉，只要穿一件泡泡袖连衣裙，我就会感到非常兴奋。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, you'll have to do without your thrill. I hadn't any material to waste on puffed sleeves. I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow. I prefer the plain, sensible ones."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你就得失去你的兴奋了。我没有任何材料可以浪费在泡泡袖上。无论如何，我认为它们看起来很可笑。我更喜欢朴素、明智的那些。”

paragraphs.en: "But I'd rather look ridiculous when everybody else does than plain and sensible all by myself," persisted Anne mournfully.
paragraphs.zh: “但我宁愿在其他人都这样做的时候显得可笑，也不愿自己一个人显得朴素而明智，”安妮悲伤地坚持道。

paragraphs.en: "Trust you for that! Well, hang those dresses carefully up in your closet, and then sit down and learn the Sunday school lesson. I got a quarterly from Mr. Bell for you and you'll go to Sunday school tomorrow," said Marilla, disappearing downstairs in high dudgeon.
paragraphs.zh: “相信你！好吧，把那些衣服小心地挂在你的衣柜里，然后坐下来学习主日学课程。我从贝尔先生那里给你买了一本季刊，你明天就可以去主日学了。”玛丽拉说着，一脸愤怒地消失在楼下。

paragraphs.en: Anne clasped her hands and looked at the dresses.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮握紧双手，看着裙子。

paragraphs.en: "I did hope there would be a white one with puffed sleeves," she whispered disconsolately. "I prayed for one, but I didn't much expect it on that account. I didn't suppose God would have time to bother about a little orphan girl's dress. I knew I'd just have to depend on Marilla for it. Well, fortunately I can imagine that one of them is of snow-white muslin with lovely lace frills and three-puffed sleeves."
paragraphs.zh: “我确实希望有一件白色的，泡泡袖的，”她沮丧地低声说道。 “我祈祷要一件，但我并没有抱太大的希望。我不认为上帝有时间关心一个小孤女的衣服。我知道我只能依靠玛丽拉来穿。好吧，幸运的是，我可以想象其中一件是雪白的平纹细布，上面有可爱的蕾丝褶边和三泡泡袖。”

paragraphs.en: The next morning warnings of a sick headache prevented Marilla from going to Sunday-school with Anne.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，玛丽拉因头痛而无法与安妮一起去主日学校。

paragraphs.en: "You'll have to go down and call for Mrs. Lynde, Anne," she said. "She'll see that you get into the right class. Now, mind you behave yourself properly. Stay to preaching afterwards and ask Mrs. Lynde to show you our pew. Here's a cent for collection. Don't stare at people and don't fidget. I shall expect you to tell me the text when you come home."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你得下去叫林德太太。”她说。 “她会确保你进入正确的班级。现在，请注意你的举止得体。之后继续讲道，请林德夫人带你看看我们的座位。这是收集的一分钱。不要盯着别人看，也不要坐立不安。我希望你回家后能告诉我课文。”

paragraphs.en: Anne started off irreproachable, arrayed in the stiff black-and-white sateen, which, while decent as regards length and certainly not open to the charge of skimpiness, contrived to emphasize every corner and angle of her thin figure. Her hat was a little, flat, glossy, new sailor, the extreme plainness of which had likewise much disappointed Anne, who had permitted herself secret visions of ribbon and flowers. The latter, however, were supplied before Anne reached the main road, for being confronted halfway down the lane with a golden frenzy of wind-stirred buttercups and a glory of wild roses, Anne promptly and liberally garlanded her hat with a heavy wreath of them. Whatever other people might have thought of the result it satisfied Anne, and she tripped gaily down the road, holding her ruddy head with its decoration of pink and yellow very proudly.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮一开始无可挑剔，穿着僵硬的黑白棉缎，虽然长度合适，当然不会被指责为短小，但她却设法强调了她瘦弱身材的每个角落和角度。她的帽子是一顶小而扁平、光滑的新水手帽，它的极其朴素同样让安妮非常失望，她允许自己秘密地想象丝带和花朵。然而，后者是在安妮到达主路之前提供的，因为在小巷的半路上，她遇到了风吹动的金色毛茛和绚丽的野玫瑰，安妮立即慷慨地在她的帽子上戴上一个沉重的花环。不管别人怎么想这个结果，安妮都满意了，她高兴地走在路上，自豪地抱着她红润的头，头上有粉红色和黄色的装饰。

paragraphs.en: When she had reached Mrs. Lynde's house she found that lady gone. Nothing daunted, Anne proceeded onward to the church alone. In the porch she found a crowd of little girls, all more or less gaily attired in whites and blues and pinks, and all staring with curious eyes at this stranger in their midst, with her extraordinary head adornment. Avonlea little girls had already heard queer stories about Anne. Mrs. Lynde said she had an awful temper; Jerry Buote, the hired boy at Green Gables, said she talked all the time to herself or to the trees and flowers like a crazy girl. They looked at her and whispered to each other behind their quarterlies. Nobody made any friendly advances, then or later on when the opening exercises were over and Anne found herself in Miss Rogerson's class.
paragraphs.zh: 当她到达林德太太家时，她发现那位女士已经不见了。安妮毫不畏惧，独自前往教堂。她在门廊里发现了一群小女孩，她们或多或少都穿着白色、蓝色和粉色的衣服，都用好奇的眼睛盯着她们中间这个戴着非凡头饰的陌生人。埃文利的小女孩们已经听说过有关安妮的奇怪故事。林德太太说她脾气很坏。杰瑞·博特（Jerry Buote）是绿山墙公园的雇工，他说她总是像个疯狂的女孩一样自言自语，或者对着树木和花朵说话。他们看着她，在季刊后面窃窃私语。无论是当时还是后来，当开场练习结束后，安妮发现自己在罗杰森小姐的课堂上时，都没有人做出任何友好的举动。

paragraphs.en: Miss Rogerson was a middle-aged lady who had taught a Sunday-school class for twenty years. Her method of teaching was to ask the printed questions from the quarterly and look sternly over its edge at the particular little girl she thought ought to answer the question. She looked very often at Anne, and Anne, thanks to Marilla's drilling, answered promptly; but it may be questioned if she understood very much about either question or answer.
paragraphs.zh: 罗杰森小姐是一位中年女士，在主日学校任教二十年。她的教学方法是问季刊上印刷的问题，并越过边缘严肃地看着她认为应该回答问题的小女孩。她经常看着安妮，而安妮在玛丽拉的训练下很快就做出了回答。但她是否非常理解问题或答案可能会受到质疑。

paragraphs.en: She did not think she liked Miss Rogerson, and she felt very miserable; every other little girl in the class had puffed sleeves. Anne felt that life was really not worth living without puffed sleeves.
paragraphs.zh: 她认为自己不喜欢罗杰森小姐，她感到非常痛苦。班上的其他小女孩都穿着泡泡袖。安妮觉得如果没有泡泡袖，生活真的不值得过。

paragraphs.en: "Well, how did you like Sunday school?" Marilla wanted to know when Anne came home. Her wreath having faded, Anne had discarded it in the lane, so Marilla was spared the knowledge of that for a time.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，你喜欢周日学校吗？”玛丽拉想知道安妮什么时候回家。她的花环褪色了，安妮把它扔在巷子里，所以玛丽拉暂时不知道这件事。

paragraphs.en: "I didn't like it a bit. It was horrid."
paragraphs.zh: “我有点不喜欢它。太可怕了。”

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley!" said Marilla rebukingly.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉！”玛丽拉责备地说。

paragraphs.en: Anne sat down on the rocker with a long sigh, kissed one of Bonny's leaves, and waved her hand to a blossoming fuchsia.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮长长地叹了一口气，坐在摇椅上，亲吻了邦尼的一片叶子，向一朵盛开的紫红色挥手。

paragraphs.en: "They might have been lonesome while I was away," she explained. "And now about the Sunday school. I behaved well, just as you told me. Mrs. Lynde was gone, but I went right on myself. I went into the church, with a lot of other little girls, and I sat in the corner of a pew by the window while the opening exercises went on. Mr. Bell made an awfully long prayer. I would have been dreadfully tired before he got through if I hadn't been sitting by that window. But it looked right out on the Lake of Shining Waters, so I just gazed at that and imagined all sorts of splendid things."
paragraphs.zh: “我不在的时候他们可能会感到孤独，”她解释道。 “现在关于主日学校。我表现得很好，正如你告诉我的。林德夫人走了，但我自己继续。我和许多其他小女孩一起走进教堂，当开场练习继续进行时，我坐在窗边长椅的角落里。贝尔先生做了一个非常长的祈祷。如果我没有坐在窗边，在他通过之前我会累得要命。但从窗户望出去，就是光辉湖，所以我只是凝视着它，想象着各种美妙的事情。”

paragraphs.en: "You shouldn't have done anything of the sort. You should have listened to Mr. Bell."
paragraphs.zh: “你不应该做这种事。你应该听贝尔先生的话。”

paragraphs.en: "But he wasn't talking to me," protested Anne. "He was talking to God and he didn't seem to be very much inter-ested in it, either. I think he thought God was too far off though. There was a long row of white birches hanging over the lake and the sunshine fell down through them, 'way, 'way down, deep into the water. Oh, Marilla, it was like a beautiful dream! It gave me a thrill and I just said, 'Thank you for it, God,' two or three times."
paragraphs.zh: “但他没有跟我说话，”安妮抗议道。 “他在和上帝说话，而且他似乎对此也不太感兴趣。不过我想他认为上帝离我们太远了。湖上悬挂着一长排白桦树，阳光穿过它们，‘一路、‘一路向下，深入水里。哦，玛丽拉，这就像一个美丽的梦！这让我兴奋不已，我只是说了两三遍‘谢谢你，上帝’。”

paragraphs.en: "Not out loud, I hope," said Marilla anxiously.
paragraphs.zh: “我希望不要大声说出来，”玛丽拉焦急地说。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, no, just under my breath. Well, Mr. Bell did get through at last and they told me to go into the classroom with Miss Rogerson's class. There were nine other girls in it. They all had puffed sleeves. I tried to imagine mine were puffed, too, but I couldn't. Why couldn't I? It was as easy as could be to imagine they were puffed when I was alone in the east gable, but it was awfully hard there among the others who had really truly puffs."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，不，就在我的呼吸声中。好吧，贝尔先生终于接通了，他们让我和罗杰森小姐的班级一起走进教室。教室里还有另外九个女孩。她们都穿着泡泡袖。我试图想象我的袖子也是泡泡袖的，但我不能。为什么我不能呢？当我独自一人在东山墙时，想象她们泡泡袖是很容易的，但在其他真正真正拥有泡泡袖的人中，这是非常困难的。泡芙。”

paragraphs.en: "You shouldn't have been thinking about your sleeves in Sunday school. You should have been attending to the lesson. I hope you knew it."
paragraphs.zh: “你不应该在主日学校里想着你的袖子。你应该去听课。我希望你知道这一点。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, yes; and I answered a lot of questions. Miss Rogerson asked ever so many. I don't think it was fair for her to do all the asking. There were lots I wanted to ask her, but I didn't like to because I didn't think she was a kindred spirit. Then all the other little girls recited a paraphrase. She asked me if I knew any. I told her I didn't, but I could recite, 'The Dog at His Master's Grave' if she liked. That's in the Third Royal Reader. It isn't a really truly religious piece of poetry, but it's so sad and melancholy that it might as well be. She said it wouldn't do and she told me to learn the nineteenth paraphrase for next Sunday. I read it over in church afterwards and it's splendid. There are two lines in particular that just thrill me.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，是的；我回答了很多问题。罗杰森小姐问了这么多。我觉得让她问所有的问题是不公平的。我有很多问题想问她，但我不想问，因为我认为她不是志同道合的人。然后所有其他小女孩都背诵了一段话。她问我是否知道。我告诉她我不知道，但我可以背诵，“狗在他主人的坟墓上”，如果她喜欢《第三皇家读者》中的那首诗，但它是如此悲伤和忧郁，所以她说那不行，她告诉我下周日我在教堂里读了它的第十九句，其中有两行特别让我兴奋。

paragraphs.en: "'Quick as the slaughtered squadrons fell
paragraphs.zh: “‘被屠杀的中队很快就倒下了

paragraphs.en: In Midian's evil day.'
paragraphs.zh: 在米甸邪恶的日子。

paragraphs.en: "I don't know what 'squadrons' means nor 'Midian,' either, but it sounds SO tragical. I can hardly wait until next Sunday to recite it. I'll practice it all the week. After Sunday school I asked Miss Rogerson—because Mrs. Lynde was too far away—to show me your pew. I sat just as still as I could and the text was Revelations, third chapter, second and third verses. It was a very long text. If I was a minister I'd pick the short, snappy ones. The sermon was awfully long, too. I suppose the minister had to match it to the text. I didn't think he was a bit interesting. The trouble with him seems to be that he hasn't enough imagination. I didn't listen to him very much. I just let my thoughts run and I thought of the most surprising things."
paragraphs.zh: “我也不知道‘中队’和‘米甸’是什么意思，但这听起来太悲惨了。我迫不及待地要等到下周日背诵它。我会练习一整周。周日学校放学后，我请罗杰森小姐——因为林德夫人太远了——让我看看你的座位。我尽量一动不动地坐着，课文是《启示录》，第三章，第二节和第三节。这是一篇很长的课文。如果我是我认为牧师的讲道也太长了，我觉得他不太有趣，因为我没有太多想象力，我只考虑了最令人惊讶的事情。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla felt helplessly that all this should be sternly reproved, but she was hampered by the undeniable fact that some of the things Anne had said, especially about the minister's sermons and Mr. Bell's prayers, were what she herself had really thought deep down in her heart for years, but had never given expression to. It almost seemed to her that those secret, unuttered, critical thoughts had suddenly taken visible and accusing shape and form in the person of this outspoken morsel of neglected humanity.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉无奈地觉得这一切都应该受到严厉的谴责，但她又被一个不可否认的事实所困扰，那就是安妮所说的一些话，尤其是牧师的布道和贝尔先生的祈祷，是她自己多年来内心深处所想却从未表达出来的。在她看来，那些秘密的、不言而喻的、批判性的想法突然在这个直言不讳、被忽视的人性身上变得可见和指责。

chapters.title: CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 12 章：庄严的誓言与承诺

paragraphs.en: It was not until the next Friday that Marilla heard the story of the flower-wreathed hat. She came home from Mrs. Lynde's and called Anne to account.
paragraphs.zh: 直到下周五，玛丽拉才听到了花环帽子的故事。她从林德太太家回到家，要求安妮负责。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, Mrs. Rachel says you went to church last Sunday with your hat rigged out ridiculous with roses and buttercups. What on earth put you up to such a caper? A pretty-looking object you must have been!"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，雷切尔太太说你上周日去了教堂，帽子上装饰着玫瑰和毛茛花，可笑了。到底是什么让你做出这样的举动？你一定是个漂亮的东西！”

paragraphs.en: "Oh. I know pink and yellow aren't becoming to me," began Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “哦。我知道粉色和黄色不适合我，”安妮开始说道。

paragraphs.en: "Becoming fiddlesticks! It was putting flowers on your hat at all, no matter what color they were, that was ridiculous. You are the most aggravating child!"
paragraphs.zh: “变成拉小提琴的人了！简直就是在帽子上插花，不管花什么颜色，太可笑了。你才是最可气的孩子！”

paragraphs.en: "I don't see why it's any more ridiculous to wear flowers on your hat than on your dress," protested Anne. "Lots of little girls there had bouquets pinned on their dresses. What's the difference?"
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白为什么在帽子上戴花比在衣服上戴花更可笑，”安妮抗议道。 “那里很多小女孩的衣服上都别着花束。有什么区别吗？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla was not to be drawn from the safe concrete into dubious paths of the abstract.
paragraphs.zh: 马里拉不会从安全的具体事物中被拉入可疑的抽象道路。

paragraphs.en: "Don't answer me back like that, Anne. It was very silly of you to do such a thing. Never let me catch you at such a trick again. Mrs. Rachel says she thought she would sink through the floor when she saw you come in all rigged out like that. She couldn't get near enough to tell you to take them off till it was too late. She says people talked about it something dreadful. Of course they would think I had no better sense than to let you go decked out like that."
paragraphs.zh: “别这样回答我，安妮。你做这样的事真是太愚蠢了。别再让我抓住你这样的把戏了。雷切尔太太说，当她看到你穿着这样的衣服进来时，她以为自己会从地板上沉下去。她无法走近让你把它们脱下来，直到为时已晚。她说人们谈论这件事很可怕。当然，他们会认为我没有比让你打扮成这样更好的明智之举。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm so sorry," said Anne, tears welling into her eyes. "I never thought you'd mind. The roses and buttercups were so sweet and pretty I thought they'd look lovely on my hat. Lots of the little girls had artificial flowers on their hats. I'm afraid I'm going to be a dreadful trial to you. Maybe you'd better send me back to the asylum. That would be terrible; I don't think I could endure it; most likely I would go into consumption; I'm so thin as it is, you see. But that would be better than being a trial to you."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我很抱歉，”安妮说，泪水涌入眼眶。 “我没想到你会介意。玫瑰和毛茛花又甜又漂亮，我以为它们戴在我的帽子上会很可爱。很多小女孩的帽子上都戴着人造花。我担心我对你来说会是一个可怕的考验。也许你最好把我送回疯人院。那太可怕了；我想我无法忍受；很可能我会得肺病；你看，我这么瘦。但那样的话比对你进行考验要好得多。”

paragraphs.en: "Nonsense," said Marilla, vexed at herself for having made the child cry. "I don't want to send you back to the asylum, I'm sure. All I want is that you should behave like other little girls and not make yourself ridiculous. Don't cry any more. I've got some news for you. Diana Barry came home this afternoon. I'm going up to see if I can borrow a skirt pattern from Mrs. Barry, and if you like you can come with me and get acquainted with Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道，”玛丽拉说，她为自己把孩子弄哭而懊恼。 “我不想把你送回精神病院，我确定。我只想让你表现得像其他小女孩一样，不要让自己变得可笑。别再哭了。我有一些消息要告诉你。戴安娜·巴里今天下午回家了。我要去看看是否可以向巴里夫人借一条裙子的图案，如果你愿意，可以跟我一起去认识一下戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: Anne rose to her feet, with clasped hands, the tears still glistening on her cheeks; the dish towel she had been hemming slipped unheeded to the floor.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站了起来，双手紧握，脸颊上仍然闪烁着泪水。她包边的洗碗巾不经意间滑落到了地板上。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, I'm frightened—now that it has come I'm actually frightened. What if she shouldn't like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，我很害怕——现在它来了，我真的很害怕。如果她不喜欢我怎么办！这将是我一生中最悲惨的失望。”

paragraphs.en: "Now, don't get into a fluster. And I do wish you wouldn't use such long words. It sounds so funny in a little girl. I guess Diana'll like you well enough. It's her mother you've got to reckon with. If she doesn't like you it won't matter how much Diana does. If she has heard about your outburst to Mrs. Lynde and going to church with buttercups round your hat I don't know what she'll think of you. You must be polite and well behaved, and don't make any of your startling speeches. For pity's sake, if the child isn't actually trembling!"
paragraphs.zh: “现在，别慌了。我真希望你不要用这么长的词。这对一个小女孩来说听起来很有趣。我想戴安娜会很喜欢你的。你必须考虑的是她的母亲。如果她不喜欢你，戴安娜有多喜欢也没关系。如果她听说你对林德夫人发脾气，并在帽子上戴着毛茛去教堂，我不知道她会怎么想你。你必须有礼貌，举止得体，如果孩子没有真正颤抖的话，不要发表任何令人震惊的言论。”

paragraphs.en: Anne WAS trembling. Her face was pale and tense.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮浑身发抖。她的脸色苍白而紧张。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, you'd be excited, too, if you were going to meet a little girl you hoped to be your bosom friend and whose mother mightn't like you," she said as she hastened to get her hat.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，如果你要见到一个小女孩，你希望成为你的知音，而她的妈妈可能不喜欢你，你也会很兴奋的，”她一边说，一边赶紧去拿帽子。

paragraphs.en: They went over to Orchard Slope by the short cut across the brook and up the firry hill grove. Mrs. Barry came to the kitchen door in answer to Marilla's knock. She was a tall black-eyed, black-haired woman, with a very resolute mouth. She had the reputation of being very strict with her children.
paragraphs.zh: 他们抄近路穿过小溪，爬上冷杉山林，来到了果园坡。听到玛丽拉的敲门声，巴里太太来到厨房门口。她是一个身材高挑、黑眼黑发的女人，嘴巴非常坚决。她以对孩子非常严格而闻名。

paragraphs.en: "How do you do, Marilla?" she said cordially. "Come in. And this is the little girl you have adopted, I suppose?"
paragraphs.zh: “你好吗，玛丽拉？”她亲切地说。 “进来吧。我想这就是你收养的小女孩吧？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, this is Anne Shirley," said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，这是安妮·雪莉，”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: "Spelled with an E," gasped Anne, who, tremulous and excited as she was, was determined there should be no misunderstanding on that important point.
paragraphs.zh: “拼写为 E，”安妮气喘吁吁地说，尽管她浑身颤抖又兴奋，但她决心在这一重要点上不应该有任何误解。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Barry, not hearing or not comprehending, merely shook hands and said kindly:
paragraphs.zh: 巴里夫人没有听见，也没有理解，只是握了握手，友善地说：

paragraphs.en: "How are you?"
paragraphs.zh: “你好吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I am well in body although considerable rumpled up in spirit, thank you ma'am," said Anne gravely. Then aside to Marilla in an audible whisper, "There wasn't anything startling in that, was there, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “我身体很好，虽然精神上有些不舒服，谢谢你，女士，”安妮严肃地说。然后用可听见的低语声对玛丽拉说道：“这没有什么令人吃惊的，不是吗，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: Diana was sitting on the sofa, reading a book which she dropped when the callers entered. She was a very pretty little girl, with her mother's black eyes and hair, and rosy cheeks, and the merry expression which was her inheritance from her father.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜坐在沙发上看一本书，当打电话的人进来时，她把书掉在了地上。她是一个非常漂亮的小女孩，有着她母亲的黑色眼睛和头发，红润的脸颊，还有她从父亲那里继承的快乐的表情。

paragraphs.en: "This is my little girl Diana," said Mrs. Barry. "Diana, you might take Anne out into the garden and show her your flowers. It will be better for you than straining your eyes over that book. She reads entirely too much—" this to Marilla as the little girls went out—"and I can't prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She's always poring over a book. I'm glad she has the prospect of a playmate—perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors."
paragraphs.zh: “这是我的小女儿戴安娜，”巴里夫人说。 “戴安娜，你可以带安妮去花园，给她看你的花。这对你来说比把眼睛盯着那本书更好。她读得太多了——”小女孩们出去时，这是对玛丽拉说的——“我无法阻止她，因为她父亲帮助和怂恿她。她总是埋头读书。我很高兴她有一个玩伴——也许这会让她更多地户外活动。”

paragraphs.en: Outside in the garden, which was full of mellow sunset light streaming through the dark old firs to the west of it, stood Anne and Diana, gazing bashfully at each other over a clump of gorgeous tiger lilies.
paragraphs.zh: 外面的花园里，柔和的夕阳透过西边深色的老冷杉洒下来，安妮和戴安娜站在花园里，在一丛华丽的虎百合面前羞涩地凝视着对方。

paragraphs.en: The Barry garden was a bowery wilderness of flowers which would have delighted Anne's heart at any time less fraught with destiny. It was encircled by huge old willows and tall firs, beneath which flourished flowers that loved the shade. Prim, right-angled paths neatly bordered with clamshells, intersected it like moist red ribbons and in the beds between old-fashioned flowers ran riot. There were rosy bleeding-hearts and great splendid crimson peonies; white, fragrant narcissi and thorny, sweet Scotch roses; pink and blue and white columbines and lilac-tinted Bouncing Bets; clumps of southernwood and ribbon grass and mint; purple Adam-and-Eve, daffodils, and masses of sweet clover white with its delicate, fragrant, feathery sprays; scarlet lightning that shot its fiery lances over prim white musk-flowers; a garden it was where sunshine lingered and bees hummed, and winds, beguiled into loitering, purred and rustled.
paragraphs.zh: 巴里花园是一片繁花似锦的绿荫荒野，只要不那么充满命运，安妮的心就会感到高兴。周围环绕着巨大的老柳树和高大的冷杉，树下开满了喜荫的花朵。整齐的直角小路整齐地用蛤壳镶边，像潮湿的红丝带一样将其交叉，老式花朵之间的花坛里乱七八糟。这里有玫瑰色的血心花和绚丽的深红色牡丹。白色芬芳的水仙花和带刺的甜美苏格兰玫瑰；粉色、蓝色和白色的耧斗菜和淡紫色的弹跳赌注；丛生的南方木、带状草和薄荷；紫色的亚当和夏娃、水仙花和一大片白色的甜三叶草，上面有精致、芬芳、羽毛状的花朵；猩红色的闪电将其炽热的长矛射向古板的白麝香花；这是一座花园，阳光灿烂，蜜蜂嗡嗡作响，风儿在花园中徘徊，发出咕噜声和沙沙声。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Diana," said Anne at last, clasping her hands and speaking almost in a whisper, "oh, do you think you can like me a little—enough to be my bosom friend?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，戴安娜，”安妮最后说道，她紧握双手，几乎是低声说道，“哦，你认为你能喜欢我一点点——足以成为我的知己吗？”

paragraphs.en: Diana laughed. Diana always laughed before she spoke.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜笑了。戴安娜说话前总是笑。

paragraphs.en: "Why, I guess so," she said frankly. "I'm awfully glad you've come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn't any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I've no sisters big enough."
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，我想是这样，”她坦白地说。 “我非常高兴你来到绿山墙住。能有人和你一起玩真是太高兴了。没有其他女孩住得足够近可以一起玩，而且我也没有足够大的姐妹。”

paragraphs.en: "Will you swear to be my friend forever and ever?" demanded Anne eagerly.
paragraphs.zh: “你愿意发誓永远做我的朋友吗？”安妮急切地问道。

paragraphs.en: Diana looked shocked.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜看上去很震惊。

paragraphs.en: "Why it's dreadfully wicked to swear," she said rebukingly.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么说脏话是极其邪恶的，”她斥责道。

paragraphs.en: "Oh no, not my kind of swearing. There are two kinds, you know."
paragraphs.zh: “哦不，不是我的那种咒骂。你知道，有两种咒骂。”

paragraphs.en: "I never heard of but one kind," said Diana doubtfully.
paragraphs.zh: “我只听说过一种。”戴安娜疑惑地说。

paragraphs.en: "There really is another. Oh, it isn't wicked at all. It just means vowing and promising solemnly."
paragraphs.zh: “还真有一个，哦，一点也不邪恶，只是郑重的发誓和承诺而已。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I don't mind doing that," agreed Diana, relieved. "How do you do it?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不介意这样做，”黛安娜同意道，松了口气。 “你是怎么做到的？”

paragraphs.en: "We must join hands—so," said Anne gravely. "It ought to be over running water. We'll just imagine this path is running water. I'll repeat the oath first. I solemnly swear to be faithful to my bosom friend, Diana Barry, as long as the sun and moon shall endure. Now you say it and put my name in."
paragraphs.zh: “我们必须携起手来——所以，”安妮严肃地说。 “应该是在流水之上。我们想象这条路是流水。我先重复一下誓言。我郑重宣誓，日月长存，忠于我的知己戴安娜·巴里。现在你说吧，把我的名字写进去。”

paragraphs.en: Diana repeated the "oath" with a laugh fore and aft. Then she said:
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜前后笑着重复了一遍“誓言”。然后她说：

paragraphs.en: "You're a queer girl, Anne. I heard before that you were queer. But I believe I'm going to like you real well."
paragraphs.zh: “你是个酷儿女孩，安妮。我以前听说你是个酷儿。但我相信我会非常喜欢你。”

paragraphs.en: When Marilla and Anne went home Diana went with them as far as the log bridge. The two little girls walked with their arms about each other. At the brook they parted with many promises to spend the next afternoon together.
paragraphs.zh: 当玛丽拉和安妮回家时，戴安娜和他们一起一直走到独木桥。两个小女孩互相搂着对方走路。在小溪边，他们告别时许下许多诺言，要一起度过第二天下午。

paragraphs.en: "Well, did you find Diana a kindred spirit?" asked Marilla as they went up through the garden of Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: “那么，你觉得戴安娜志趣相投吗？”当他们穿过绿山墙花园时，玛丽拉问道。

paragraphs.en: "Oh yes," sighed Anne, blissfully unconscious of any sarcasm on Marilla's part. "Oh Marilla, I'm the happiest girl on Prince Edward Island this very moment. I assure you I'll say my prayers with a right good-will tonight. Diana and I are going to build a playhouse in Mr. William Bell's birch grove tomorrow. Can I have those broken pieces of china that are out in the woodshed? Diana's birthday is in February and mine is in March. Don't you think that is a very strange coincidence? Diana is going to lend me a book to read. She says it's perfectly splendid and tremendously exciting. She's going to show me a place back in the woods where rice lilies grow. Don't you think Diana has got very soulful eyes? I wish I had soulful eyes. Diana is going to teach me to sing a song called 'Nelly in the Hazel Dell.' She's going to give me a picture to put up in my room; it's a perfectly beautiful picture, she says—a lovely lady in a pale blue silk dress. A sewing-machine agent gave it to her. I wish I had something to give Diana. I'm an inch taller than Diana, but she is ever so much fatter; she says she'd like to be thin because it's so much more graceful, but I'm afraid she only said it to soothe my feelings. We're going to the shore some day to gather shells. We have agreed to call the spring down by the log bridge the Dryad's Bubble. Isn't that a perfectly elegant name? I read a story once about a spring called that. A dryad is sort of a grown-up fairy, I think."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，是的，”安妮叹了口气，幸福地没有意识到玛丽拉的任何讽刺。 “哦，玛丽拉，此时此刻，我是爱德华王子岛最幸福的女孩。我向你保证，今晚我会怀着正确的善意进行祈祷。明天，戴安娜和我将在威廉·贝尔先生的白桦林里建造一座剧场。我可以要木棚里的那些碎瓷器吗？戴安娜的生日是二月，我的生日是三月。你不觉得这是一个非常奇怪的巧合吗？戴安娜要借给我一个她说这本书非常精彩，非常令人兴奋。你不觉得戴安娜有一双深情的眼睛吗？我希望戴安娜会教我唱一首叫做《榛树谷里的耐莉》的歌。她会给我一张照片挂在我的房间里；她说，这是一幅非常美丽的图画——一位穿着淡蓝色丝绸连衣裙的可爱女士。一位缝纫机代理商把它给了她。我希望我有东西可以送给戴安娜。我比戴安娜高一英寸，但她却胖得多；她说她想瘦一点，因为这样更优雅，但恐怕她这么说只是为了安抚我的感情。有一天我们要去岸边捡贝壳。我们同意将独木桥旁的泉水称为树妖泡泡。这不是一个非常优雅的名字吗？我曾经读过一个关于春天的故事。我认为树妖有点像成年的仙女。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, all I hope is you won't talk Diana to death," said Marilla. "But remember this in all your planning, Anne. You're not going to play all the time nor most of it. You'll have your work to do and it'll have to be done first."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我只希望你不要把戴安娜说死。”玛丽拉说。 “但是在你所有的计划中记住这一点，安妮。你不会一直玩，也不会玩大部分时间。你有你的工作要做，而且必须先完成。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's cup of happiness was full, and Matthew caused it to overflow. He had just got home from a trip to the store at Carmody, and he sheepishly produced a small parcel from his pocket and handed it to Anne, with a deprecatory look at Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的幸福之杯已经满了，马修让它溢出来。他刚刚逛完卡莫迪的商店回到家，羞涩地从口袋里掏出一个小包裹，递给安妮，脸上带着不屑的目光看着玛丽拉。

paragraphs.en: "I heard you say you liked chocolate sweeties, so I got you some," he said.
paragraphs.zh: “我听到你说你喜欢巧克力糖，所以我给你买了一些，”他说。

paragraphs.en: "Humph," sniffed Marilla. "It'll ruin her teeth and stomach. There, there, child, don't look so dismal. You can eat those, since Matthew has gone and got them. He'd better have brought you peppermints. They're wholesomer. Don't sicken yourself eating all them at once now."
paragraphs.zh: “哼，”玛丽拉吸了吸鼻子。 “这会毁了她的牙齿和胃。好了，好了，孩子，别显得这么沮丧。你可以吃那些，因为马修已经去拿了它们。他最好给你带来薄荷糖。它们更有益健康。现在不要一下子吃完它们而感到恶心。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, no, indeed, I won't," said Anne eagerly. "I'll just eat one tonight, Marilla. And I can give Diana half of them, can't I? The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her. It's delightful to think I have something to give her."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，不，确实，我不会，”安妮急切地说。 “今晚我就吃一个，玛丽拉。我可以给戴安娜一半，不是吗？如果我给她一些，另一半的味道会加倍甜。想到我有东西可以给她，我很高兴。”

paragraphs.en: "I will say it for the child," said Marilla when Anne had gone to her gable, "she isn't stingy. I'm glad, for of all faults I detest stinginess in a child. Dear me, it's only three weeks since she came, and it seems as if she'd been here always. I can't imagine the place without her. Now, don't be looking I told-you-so, Matthew. That's bad enough in a woman, but it isn't to be endured in a man. I'm perfectly willing to own up that I'm glad I consented to keep the child and that I'm getting fond of her, but don't you rub it in, Matthew Cuthbert."
paragraphs.zh: “我会为孩子说的，”安妮走到她的山墙边时，玛丽拉说，“她并不小气。我很高兴，因为我最讨厌孩子的小气。亲爱的我，她来才三个星期，而她似乎一直都在这里。我无法想象没有她的地方。现在，别看我告诉过你了，马修。这对一个女人来说已经够糟糕的了，但还不是我完全愿意承认我很高兴同意保留这个孩子，而且我越来越喜欢她了，但你别再强调了，马修·库斯伯特。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 13 章：期待的快乐

paragraphs.en: "It's time Anne was in to do her sewing," said Marilla, glancing at the clock and then out into the yellow August afternoon where everything drowsed in the heat. "She stayed playing with Diana more than half an hour more'n I gave her leave to; and now she's perched out there on the woodpile talking to Matthew, nineteen to the dozen, when she knows perfectly well she ought to be at her work. And of course he's listening to her like a perfect ninny. I never saw such an infatuated man. The more she talks and the odder the things she says, the more he's delighted evidently. Anne Shirley, you come right in here this minute, do you hear me!"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮该进去做针线活了。”玛丽拉说着，看了一眼时钟，然后走进了八月的黄色午后，一切都在炎热中昏昏欲睡。 “在我允许她离开的时候，她和戴安娜一起玩了半个多小时；现在她坐在柴堆上和马修聊天，十九到十几，当她完全知道她应该去工作时。当然，他像一个完美的傻瓜一样听她说话。我从未见过如此痴情的男人。她说得越多，说的事情越奇怪，他显然就越高兴。安妮·雪莉，你来了就在这儿，你听见我说话了吗！”

paragraphs.en: A series of staccato taps on the west window brought Anne flying in from the yard, eyes shining, cheeks faintly flushed with pink, unbraided hair streaming behind her in a torrent of brightness.
paragraphs.zh: 西窗上一连串断断续续的敲击声让安妮从院子里飞了进来，她的眼睛闪闪发亮，脸颊微微泛红，粉色的未编辫子的头发在她身后闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla," she exclaimed breathlessly, "there's going to be a Sunday-school picnic next week—in Mr. Harmon Andrews's field, right near the lake of Shining Waters. And Mrs. Superintendent Bell and Mrs. Rachel Lynde are going to make ice cream—think of it, Marilla—ICE CREAM! And, oh, Marilla, can I go to it?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，”她气喘吁吁地喊道，“下周主日学校将举行野餐会，地点是哈蒙·安德鲁斯先生的田地，就在闪亮水域湖附近。贝尔警监夫人和雷切尔·林德夫人要制作冰淇淋——玛丽拉，想想看——冰淇淋！还有，哦，玛丽拉，我可以去吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Just look at the clock, if you please, Anne. What time did I tell you to come in?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，请你看一下时钟。我叫你几点进来的？”

paragraphs.en: "Two o'clock—but isn't it splendid about the picnic, Marilla? Please can I go? Oh, I've never been to a picnic—I've dreamed of picnics, but I've never—"
paragraphs.zh: “两点了——但是野餐不是很棒吗，玛丽拉？我可以走了吗？哦，我从来没有去过野餐——我梦想着野餐，但我从来没有——”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I told you to come at two o'clock. And it's a quarter to three. I'd like to know why you didn't obey me, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我告诉你两点钟来。现在是三点一刻。我想知道你为什么不听我的话，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "Why, I meant to, Marilla, as much as could be. But you have no idea how fascinating Idlewild is. And then, of course, I had to tell Matthew about the picnic. Matthew is such a sympathetic listener. Please can I go?"
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，玛丽拉，我本想尽可能多的。但是你不知道艾德怀德有多么迷人。然后，当然，我必须告诉马修关于野餐的事情。马修是一位很有同情心的倾听者。我可以去吗？”

paragraphs.en: "You'll have to learn to resist the fascination of Idle-whatever-you-call-it. When I tell you to come in at a certain time I mean that time and not half an hour later. And you needn't stop to discourse with sympathetic listeners on your way, either. As for the picnic, of course you can go. You're a Sunday-school scholar, and it's not likely I'd refuse to let you go when all the other little girls are going."
paragraphs.zh: “你必须学会​​抵制‘无所事事’的魅力。当我告诉你在某个时间进来时，我指的是那个时间，而不是半小时后。而且你也不必在路上停下来与同情的听众交谈。至于野餐，你当然可以去。你是主日学校的学生，当其他小女孩都走了时，我不可能拒绝让你走。”

paragraphs.en: "But—but," faltered Anne, "Diana says that everybody must take a basket of things to eat. I can't cook, as you know, Marilla, and—and—I don't mind going to a picnic without puffed sleeves so much, but I'd feel terribly humiliated if I had to go without a basket. It's been preying on my mind ever since Diana told me."
paragraphs.zh: “但是——但是，”安妮结结巴巴地说，“戴安娜说每个人都必须带一篮子吃的东西。你知道，我不会做饭，玛丽拉，而且——而且——我不介意不带泡泡袖子去野餐，但如果我不得不不带篮子去野餐，我会感到非常羞辱。自从戴安娜告诉我以来，这一直在我的脑海中萦绕。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, it needn't prey any longer. I'll bake you a basket."
paragraphs.zh: “好了，它不用再捕食了，我给你烤一篮子。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, you dear good Marilla. Oh, you are so kind to me. Oh, I'm so much obliged to you."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，你亲爱的好玛丽拉。哦，你对我真好。哦，我非常感谢你。”

paragraphs.en: Getting through with her "ohs" Anne cast herself into Marilla's arms and rapturously kissed her sallow cheek. It was the first time in her whole life that childish lips had voluntarily touched Marilla's face. Again that sudden sensation of startling sweetness thrilled her. She was secretly vastly pleased at Anne's impulsive caress, which was probably the reason why she said brusquely:
paragraphs.zh: 安妮“哦”了一声，投入了玛丽拉的怀抱，欣喜若狂地亲吻了她蜡黄的脸颊。这是她一生中第一次，孩子气的嘴唇主动触碰玛丽拉的脸。那种突如其来的甜蜜感再次让她兴奋不已。她暗暗为安妮冲动的爱抚而欣喜不已，大概这就是她粗暴地说的原因：

paragraphs.en: "There, there, never mind your kissing nonsense. I'd sooner see you doing strictly as you're told. As for cooking, I mean to begin giving you lessons in that some of these days. But you're so featherbrained, Anne, I've been waiting to see if you'd sober down a little and learn to be steady before I begin. You've got to keep your wits about you in cooking and not stop in the middle of things to let your thoughts rove all over creation. Now, get out your patchwork and have your square done before teatime."
paragraphs.zh: “好了，好了，别介意你胡言乱语的接吻。我宁愿看到你严格按照吩咐去做。至于烹饪，我打算这几天开始给你上这方面的课。但是你太头脑简单了，安妮，我一直在等着看你是否能清醒一点，学会在我开始之前保持稳定。你必须在烹饪中保持头脑清醒，不要半途而废，让你的思想在创造物中徘徊。现在，拿出你的拼布作品，在下午茶时间之前把你的方块画好。”

paragraphs.en: "I do NOT like patchwork," said Anne dolefully, hunting out her workbasket and sitting down before a little heap of red and white diamonds with a sigh. "I think some kinds of sewing would be nice; but there's no scope for imagination in patchwork. It's just one little seam after another and you never seem to be getting anywhere. But of course I'd rather be Anne of Green Gables sewing patchwork than Anne of any other place with nothing to do but play. I wish time went as quick sewing patches as it does when I'm playing with Diana, though. Oh, we do have such elegant times, Marilla. I have to furnish most of the imagination, but I'm well able to do that. Diana is simply perfect in every other way. You know that little piece of land across the brook that runs up between our farm and Mr. Barry's. It belongs to Mr. William Bell, and right in the corner there is a little ring of white birch trees—the most romantic spot, Marilla. Diana and I have our playhouse there. We call it Idlewild. Isn't that a poetical name? I assure you it took me some time to think it out. I stayed awake nearly a whole night before I invented it. Then, just as I was dropping off to sleep, it came like an inspiration. Diana was ENRAPTURED when she heard it. We have got our house fixed up elegantly. You must come and see it, Marilla—won't you? We have great big stones, all covered with moss, for seats, and boards from tree to tree for shelves. And we have all our dishes on them. Of course, they're all broken but it's the easiest thing in the world to imagine that they are whole. There's a piece of a plate with a spray of red and yellow ivy on it that is especially beautiful. We keep it in the parlor and we have the fairy glass there, too. The fairy glass is as lovely as a dream. Diana found it out in the woods behind their chicken house. It's all full of rainbows—just little young rainbows that haven't grown big yet—and Diana's mother told her it was broken off a hanging lamp they once had. But it's nice to imagine the fairies lost it one night when they had a ball, so we call it the fairy glass. Matthew is going to make us a table. Oh, we have named that little round pool over in Mr. Barry's field Willowmere. I got that name out of the book Diana lent me. That was a thrilling book, Marilla. The heroine had five lovers. I'd be satisfied with one, wouldn't you? She was very handsome and she went through great tribulations. She could faint as easy as anything. I'd love to be able to faint, wouldn't you, Marilla? It's so romantic. But I'm really very healthy for all I'm so thin. I believe I'm getting fatter, though. Don't you think I am? I look at my elbows every morning when I get up to see if any dimples are coming. Diana is having a new dress made with elbow sleeves. She is going to wear it to the picnic. Oh, I do hope it will be fine next Wednesday. I don't feel that I could endure the disappointment if anything happened to prevent me from getting to the picnic. I suppose I'd live through it, but I'm certain it would be a lifelong sorrow. It wouldn't matter if I got to a hundred picnics in after years; they wouldn't make up for missing this one. They're going to have boats on the Lake of Shining Waters—and ice cream, as I told you. I have never tasted ice cream. Diana tried to explain what it was like, but I guess ice cream is one of those things that are beyond imagination."
paragraphs.zh: “我不喜欢拼凑而成的东西，”安妮悲伤地说，一边找出工作篮，一边叹了口气，坐在一小堆红白钻石前。 “我认为某些类型的缝纫会很好；但是拼接没有想象力的余地。这只是一个又一个的小接缝，你似乎永远不会有任何进展。但是，当然，我宁愿成为绿山墙的安妮缝制拼凑物，也不愿成为任何其他地方的安妮，除了玩耍之外无所事事。不过，我希望时间过得像我和戴安娜玩耍时缝纫补丁一样快。哦，我们确实有如此优雅的时光，玛丽拉。我必须提供大部分想象力，但是我完全可以做到这一点。你知道，我们农场和巴里先生家之间的那片小土地属于威廉·贝尔先生，拐角处有一小片白桦树——这是最浪漫的地方，玛丽拉，我们把它称为“艾德怀德”，我向你保证，这不是一个富有诗意的名字吗？在我发明它之前，我几乎整个晚上都睡不着。然后，当我快要入睡时，当她听到这个消息时，她感到很兴奋。你一定要来看看它，不是吗？我们有很大的石头，从树到树都有架子。当然，它们都坏了，但这是最容易的。我们把一块上面喷着红色和黄色常春藤的盘子放在客厅里，那里也有仙女玻璃，戴安娜在他们的鸡舍后面的树林里发现了它，里面全是彩虹，只是还没有长大的小彩虹，但黛安娜的母亲告诉她，它是从他们曾经拥有的一盏吊灯上折下来的。想象一下仙女们在舞会上丢失了它，所以我们把它称为仙女玻璃。哦，我们把巴里先生田里的那个小圆池命名为威洛米尔。那是一本令人兴奋的书，玛丽拉。我会很满意她有五个情人，不是吗？ She could faint as easy as anything. I'd love to be able to faint, wouldn't you, Marilla? It's so romantic. But I'm really very healthy for all I'm so thin. I believe I'm getting fatter, though. Don't you think I am? I look at my elbows every morning when I get up to see if any dimples are coming. Diana is having a new dress made with elbow sleeves. She is going to wear it to the picnic. Oh, I do hope it下周三就没事了。我想如果有什么事情阻止我去野餐的话，我肯定会感到遗憾，但我确信，即使我以后能参加一百次野餐，也不会弥补错过这次的机会——正如我告诉过你的，我从来没有吃过冰淇淋。试图解释它是什么样的，但我想冰淇淋是超乎想象的东西之一。”

paragraphs.en: "Anne, you have talked even on for ten minutes by the clock," said Marilla. "Now, just for curiosity's sake, see if you can hold your tongue for the same length of time."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，按时钟计算，你已经讲了十分钟了，”玛丽拉说。 “现在，出于好奇，看看你能否在同样的时间内保持沉默。”

paragraphs.en: Anne held her tongue as desired. But for the rest of the week she talked picnic and thought picnic and dreamed picnic. On Saturday it rained and she worked herself up into such a frantic state lest it should keep on raining until and over Wednesday that Marilla made her sew an extra patchwork square by way of steadying her nerves.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮按照自己的意愿闭嘴了。但在这一周剩下的时间里，她谈论着野餐，思考着野餐，梦想着野餐。周六下雨了，她把自己搞得焦躁不安，生怕雨一直下到周三，玛丽拉让她多缝了一块拼布方巾，以稳定她的神经。

paragraphs.en: On Sunday Anne confided to Marilla on the way home from church that she grew actually cold all over with excitement when the minister announced the picnic from the pulpit.
paragraphs.zh: 周日，安妮在从教堂回家的路上向玛丽拉透露，当牧师在讲坛上宣布野餐时，她兴奋得浑身发冷。

paragraphs.en: "Such a thrill as went up and down my back, Marilla! I don't think I'd ever really believed until then that there was honestly going to be a picnic. I couldn't help fearing I'd only imagined it. But when a minister says a thing in the pulpit you just have to believe it."
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，我的后背感到无比的激动！直到那时我才真正相信会有一场野餐。我不禁担心自己只是想象出来的。但是当一位牧师在讲坛上说某件事时，你就必须相信它。”

paragraphs.en: "You set your heart too much on things, Anne," said Marilla, with a sigh. "I'm afraid there'll be a great many disappointments in store for you through life."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你太在意事情了，”玛丽拉叹了口气说。 “我担心你一生中将会有很多失望。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, looking forward to things is half the pleasure of them," exclaimed Anne. "You mayn't get the things themselves; but nothing can prevent you from having the fun of looking forward to them. Mrs. Lynde says, 'Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.' But I think it would be worse to expect nothing than to be disappointed."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，期待事情是他们一半的快乐，”安妮惊呼道。 “你可能无法得到这些东西本身；但是没有什么可以阻止你享受期待它们的乐趣。林德夫人说，‘那些不抱任何期望的人是有福的，因为他们不会失望。’但我认为什么都不期待比失望更糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla wore her amethyst brooch to church that day as usual. Marilla always wore her amethyst brooch to church. She would have thought it rather sacrilegious to leave it off—as bad as forgetting her Bible or her collection dime. That amethyst brooch was Marilla's most treasured possession. A seafaring uncle had given it to her mother who in turn had bequeathed it to Marilla. It was an old-fashioned oval, containing a braid of her mother's hair, surrounded by a border of very fine amethysts. Marilla knew too little about precious stones to realize how fine the amethysts actually were; but she thought them very beautiful and was always pleasantly conscious of their violet shimmer at her throat, above her good brown satin dress, even although she could not see it.
paragraphs.zh: 那天，玛丽拉像往常一样戴着紫水晶胸针去教堂。玛丽拉总是戴着她的紫水晶胸针去教堂。她会认为把它留下来是相当亵渎的——就像忘记她的圣经或她的收藏一毛钱一样糟糕。那枚紫水晶胸针是玛丽拉最珍贵的财产。一位航海叔叔把它送给了她的母亲，而她的母亲又将它遗赠给了玛丽拉。这是一个老式的椭圆形，里面扎着她母亲的辫子，周围镶着一圈非常精美的紫水晶。玛丽拉对宝石知之甚少，无法意识到紫水晶实际上有多精美。但她认为它们非常美丽，并且总是愉快地意识到它们在她喉咙处、在她漂亮的棕色缎子连衣裙上方闪烁着紫罗兰色的光芒，尽管她看不到它。

paragraphs.en: Anne had been smitten with delighted admiration when she first saw that brooch.
paragraphs.zh: 当安妮第一次看到那枚胸针时，她就被欣喜若狂的钦佩所迷住了。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, it's a perfectly elegant brooch. I don't know how you can pay attention to the sermon or the prayers when you have it on. I couldn't, I know. I think amethysts are just sweet. They are what I used to think diamonds were like. Long ago, before I had ever seen a diamond, I read about them and I tried to imagine what they would be like. I thought they would be lovely glimmering purple stones. When I saw a real diamond in a lady's ring one day I was so disappointed I cried. Of course, it was very lovely but it wasn't my idea of a diamond. Will you let me hold the brooch for one minute, Marilla? Do you think amethysts can be the souls of good violets?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，这是一枚非常优雅的胸针。我不知道当你戴上它的时候，你如何能够关注布道或祈祷。我不能，我知道。我认为紫水晶很甜。它们就像我以前认为的钻石一样。很久以前，在我见过钻石之前，我读到过它们，并试图想象它们会是什么样子。我以为它们会是可爱的闪闪发光的紫色宝石。当我在一个钻石中看到一颗真正的钻石时，有一天，我非常失望地哭了。当然，它非常可爱，但这不是我想要的钻石，你能让我拿着这枚胸针一分钟吗，玛丽拉，你认为紫水晶可以成为好紫罗兰的灵魂吗？

chapters.title: CHAPTER XIV. Anne's Confession
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 14 章：安妮的坦白

paragraphs.en: On the Monday evening before the picnic Marilla came down from her room with a troubled face.
paragraphs.zh: 野餐前的周一晚上，玛丽拉从房间里走出来，一脸困惑。

paragraphs.en: "Anne," she said to that small personage, who was shelling peas by the spotless table and singing, "Nelly of the Hazel Dell" with a vigor and expression that did credit to Diana's teaching, "did you see anything of my amethyst brooch? I thought I stuck it in my pincushion when I came home from church yesterday evening, but I can't find it anywhere."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”她对那个在一尘不染的桌子旁剥豌豆、唱着《榛树谷的耐莉》的小人物说，她的活力和表情值得戴安娜的教导，“你看到我的紫水晶胸针了吗？我以为昨天晚上从教堂回家时我把它插在针垫里了，但我在任何地方都找不到它。”

paragraphs.en: "I—I saw it this afternoon when you were away at the Aid Society," said Anne, a little slowly. "I was passing your door when I saw it on the cushion, so I went in to look at it."
paragraphs.zh: “我——今天下午你去援助协会的时候我看到了。”安妮语气有点慢。 “我路过你家门口的时候，看到垫子上有这个，所以就进去看看。”

paragraphs.en: "Did you touch it?" said Marilla sternly.
paragraphs.zh: “你碰过它吗？”玛丽拉严厉地说。

paragraphs.en: "Y-e-e-s," admitted Anne, "I took it up and I pinned it on my breast just to see how it would look."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，是的，”安妮承认，“我把它拿起来，别在胸前，只是想看看它是什么样子。”

paragraphs.en: "You had no business to do anything of the sort. It's very wrong in a little girl to meddle. You shouldn't have gone into my room in the first place and you shouldn't have touched a brooch that didn't belong to you in the second. Where did you put it?"
paragraphs.zh: “你没有权利做这种事。一个小女孩多管闲事是非常错误的。你一开始就不应该进入我的房间，其次就不应该碰一枚不属于你的胸针。你把它放在哪里了？”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I put it back on the bureau. I hadn't it on a minute. Truly, I didn't mean to meddle, Marilla. I didn't think about its being wrong to go in and try on the brooch; but I see now that it was and I'll never do it again. That's one good thing about me. I never do the same naughty thing twice."
