paragraphs.zh: “哦，我把它放回梳妆台上。我一分钟就没有了。说实话，我不是有意多管闲事，玛丽拉。我并不认为进去试戴胸针是错误的；但我现在明白了，我再也不会这样做了。这是我的一件好事。我从来不会做同样顽皮的事情第二次。”

paragraphs.en: "You didn't put it back," said Marilla. "That brooch isn't anywhere on the bureau. You've taken it out or something, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “你没有把它放回去，”玛丽拉说。 “那枚胸针不在办公室的任何地方。你把它拿出来了，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "I did put it back," said Anne quickly—pertly, Marilla thought. "I don't just remember whether I stuck it on the pincushion or laid it in the china tray. But I'm perfectly certain I put it back."
paragraphs.zh: “我确实把它放回去了，”安妮很快地说——很得体，玛丽拉想。 “我不记得我是把它贴在针垫上还是放在瓷盘里。但我完全确定我把它放回去了。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll go and have another look," said Marilla, determining to be just. "If you put that brooch back it's there still. If it isn't I'll know you didn't, that's all!"
paragraphs.zh: “我再去看看。”玛丽拉说，决心要公正。 “如果你把那枚胸针放回去，它仍然在那里。如果没有，我就知道你没有，仅此而已！”

paragraphs.en: Marilla went to her room and made a thorough search, not only over the bureau but in every other place she thought the brooch might possibly be. It was not to be found and she returned to the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉走进自己的房间，彻底搜查了一遍，不仅搜遍了衣柜，还搜遍了她认为胸针可能存在的所有其他地方。没找到，她又回到了厨房。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, the brooch is gone. By your own admission you were the last person to handle it. Now, what have you done with it? Tell me the truth at once. Did you take it out and lose it?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，胸针不见了。据你自己承认，你是最后一个处理它的人。现在，你对它做了什么？立即告诉我真相。你是不是把它拿出来丢了？”

paragraphs.en: "No, I didn't," said Anne solemnly, meeting Marilla's angry gaze squarely. "I never took the brooch out of your room and that is the truth, if I was to be led to the block for it—although I'm not very certain what a block is. So there, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我没有，”安妮严肃地说，直视着玛丽拉愤怒的目光。 “我从来没有把胸针带出你的房间，这就是事实，如果我被带到街区去拿的话——尽管我不太确定街区是什么。所以，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's "so there" was only intended to emphasize her assertion, but Marilla took it as a display of defiance.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的“就在那里”只是为了强调她的主张，但玛丽拉认为这是一种蔑视的表现。

paragraphs.en: "I believe you are telling me a falsehood, Anne," she said sharply. "I know you are. There now, don't say anything more unless you are prepared to tell the whole truth. Go to your room and stay there until you are ready to confess."
paragraphs.zh: “我相信你在告诉我一个谎言，安妮，”她尖锐地说。 “我知道你是这样的。现在，除非你准备好说出全部真相，否则不要再说什么。回到你的房间，呆在那里，直到你准备好坦白为止。”

paragraphs.en: "Will I take the peas with me?" said Anne meekly.
paragraphs.zh: “我可以带走豌豆吗？”安妮温顺地说。

paragraphs.en: "No, I'll finish shelling them myself. Do as I bid you."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我会亲自去炮轰他们。按我吩咐的去做。”

paragraphs.en: When Anne had gone Marilla went about her evening tasks in a very disturbed state of mind. She was worried about her valuable brooch. What if Anne had lost it? And how wicked of the child to deny having taken it, when anybody could see she must have! With such an innocent face, too!
paragraphs.zh: 安妮走后，玛丽拉心神不安地继续做晚上的事。她担心她那枚珍贵的胸针。如果安妮丢了怎么办？当任何人都知道她一定是拿走了它的时候，这个孩子却否认自己拿走了它，这是多么邪恶啊！还长着一张无辜的脸呢！

paragraphs.en: "I don't know what I wouldn't sooner have had happen," thought Marilla, as she nervously shelled the peas. "Of course, I don't suppose she meant to steal it or anything like that. She's just taken it to play with or help along that imagination of hers. She must have taken it, that's clear, for there hasn't been a soul in that room since she was in it, by her own story, until I went up tonight. And the brooch is gone, there's nothing surer. I suppose she has lost it and is afraid to own up for fear she'll be punished. It's a dreadful thing to think she tells falsehoods. It's a far worse thing than her fit of temper. It's a fearful responsibility to have a child in your house you can't trust. Slyness and untruthfulness—that's what she has displayed. I declare I feel worse about that than about the brooch. If she'd only have told the truth about it I wouldn't mind so much."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道如果不早点发生什么，”马里拉一边紧张地剥豌豆壳一边想。 “当然，我不认为她打算偷它或类似的东西。她只是拿它来玩弄或帮助她的想象力。很明显，她肯定拿走了它，因为从她自己的故事来看，那个房间里自从她进来以来一直没有灵魂，直到我今晚上去。而胸针不见了，没有什么比这更确定的了。我想她已经把它弄丢了，并且不敢承认，因为担心会受到惩罚。这是一个认为她说谎是一件比她脾气暴躁更糟糕的事情，这是一种可怕的责任，她的狡猾和不诚实就是她所表现出来的，如果她只说实话，我不会那么介意。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla went to her room at intervals all through the evening and searched for the brooch, without finding it. A bedtime visit to the east gable produced no result. Anne persisted in denying that she knew anything about the brooch but Marilla was only the more firmly convinced that she did.
paragraphs.zh: 整个晚上，玛丽拉时不时地去她的房间寻找那枚胸针，但没有找到。睡前去东山墙拜访没有结果。安妮坚持否认她对这枚胸针一无所知，但玛丽拉更加坚信她知道。

paragraphs.en: She told Matthew the story the next morning. Matthew was confounded and puzzled; he could not so quickly lose faith in Anne but he had to admit that circumstances were against her.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，她把这个故事告诉了马修。马太感到困惑和困惑。他不能这么快就对安妮失去信心，但他不得不承认情况对她不利。

paragraphs.en: "You're sure it hasn't fell down behind the bureau?" was the only suggestion he could offer.
paragraphs.zh: “你确定它没有掉到办公室后面吗？”这是他能提供的唯一建议。

paragraphs.en: "I've moved the bureau and I've taken out the drawers and I've looked in every crack and cranny" was Marilla's positive answer. "The brooch is gone and that child has taken it and lied about it. That's the plain, ugly truth, Matthew Cuthbert, and we might as well look it in the face."
paragraphs.zh: “我已经把衣柜搬走了，抽屉也拿出来了，我检查了每一个缝隙”，玛丽拉肯定地回答。 “胸针不见了，那个孩子拿走了它，还撒了谎。马修·库斯伯特，这是显而易见的、丑陋的事实，我们不妨正视它。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, what are you going to do about it?" Matthew asked forlornly, feeling secretly thankful that Marilla and not he had to deal with the situation. He felt no desire to put his oar in this time.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，现在你打算怎么办？”马修凄凉地问道，暗自庆幸是玛丽拉而不是他来应对这种情况。这次他不想划桨了。

paragraphs.en: "She'll stay in her room until she confesses," said Marilla grimly, remembering the success of this method in the former case. "Then we'll see. Perhaps we'll be able to find the brooch if she'll only tell where she took it; but in any case she'll have to be severely punished, Matthew."
paragraphs.zh: “她会待在自己的房间里，直到她坦白为止。”玛丽拉冷酷地说，她想起了这种方法在前一个案件中的成功。 “那我们就拭目以待吧。也许只要她说出她在哪里拿到了胸针，我们就能找到它；但无论如何，她都必须受到严厉的惩罚，马修。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, you'll have to punish her," said Matthew, reaching for his hat. "I've nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，你必须惩罚她了，”马修说，伸手去拿帽子。 “记住，我与这件事无关。你自己警告过我。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla felt deserted by everyone. She could not even go to Mrs. Lynde for advice. She went up to the east gable with a very serious face and left it with a face more serious still. Anne steadfastly refused to confess. She persisted in asserting that she had not taken the brooch. The child had evidently been crying and Marilla felt a pang of pity which she sternly repressed. By night she was, as she expressed it, "beat out."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉感到被所有人抛弃了。她甚至无法向林德夫人寻求建议。她一脸严肃地上了东山墙，离开时又一脸严肃。安妮坚决不肯承认。她坚持坚称自己没有拿走胸针。孩子显然一直在哭，玛丽拉感到一阵怜悯，但她强忍住了。用她的话说，到了晚上，她“精疲力竭”。

paragraphs.en: "You'll stay in this room until you confess, Anne. You can make up your mind to that," she said firmly.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你会一直待在这个房间里，直到你坦白为止。你可以下定决心。”她坚定地说。

paragraphs.en: "But the picnic is tomorrow, Marilla," cried Anne. "You won't keep me from going to that, will you? You'll just let me out for the afternoon, won't you? Then I'll stay here as long as you like AFTERWARDS cheerfully. But I MUST go to the picnic."
paragraphs.zh: “但是野餐是明天，玛丽拉，”安妮喊道。 “你不会阻止我去那个地方，是吗？你会让我出去玩一个下午，不是吗？然后只要你愿意，我就会一直待在这儿。但我必须去野餐。”

paragraphs.en: "You'll not go to picnics nor anywhere else until you've confessed, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “在你坦白之前，你不能去野餐，也不能去其他任何地方，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla," gasped Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，”安妮喘着气说。

paragraphs.en: But Marilla had gone out and shut the door.
paragraphs.zh: 但玛丽拉已经出去并关上了门。

paragraphs.en: Wednesday morning dawned as bright and fair as if expressly made to order for the picnic. Birds sang around Green Gables; the Madonna lilies in the garden sent out whiffs of perfume that entered in on viewless winds at every door and window, and wandered through halls and rooms like spirits of benediction. The birches in the hollow waved joyful hands as if watching for Anne's usual morning greeting from the east gable. But Anne was not at her window. When Marilla took her breakfast up to her she found the child sitting primly on her bed, pale and resolute, with tight-shut lips and gleaming eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三的早晨，阳光明媚、晴朗，仿佛是专门为野餐定制的。鸟儿在绿山墙周围歌唱；花园里的圣母百合散发出阵阵香气，随着微风吹进每扇门窗，像祝福的精灵一样在大厅和房间里徘徊。空地里的白桦树快乐地挥舞着小手，仿佛在等待着安妮从东山墙传来的早晨问候。但安妮不在她的窗前。当玛丽拉把早餐端到她面前时，她发现孩子一本正经地坐在她的床上，脸色苍白，表情坚定，嘴唇紧闭，眼睛闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: "Marilla, I'm ready to confess."
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，我准备好坦白了。”

paragraphs.en: "Ah!" Marilla laid down her tray. Once again her method had succeeded; but her success was very bitter to her. "Let me hear what you have to say then, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “啊！”玛丽拉放下托盘。她的方法再一次成功了。但她的成功让她感到非常痛苦。 “那么让我听听你要说什么，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "I took the amethyst brooch," said Anne, as if repeating a lesson she had learned. "I took it just as you said. I didn't mean to take it when I went in. But it did look so beautiful, Marilla, when I pinned it on my breast that I was overcome by an irresistible temptation. I imagined how perfectly thrilling it would be to take it to Idlewild and play I was the Lady Cordelia Fitzgerald. It would be so much easier to imagine I was the Lady Cordelia if I had a real amethyst brooch on. Diana and I make necklaces of roseberries but what are roseberries compared to amethysts? So I took the brooch. I thought I could put it back before you came home. I went all the way around by the road to lengthen out the time. When I was going over the bridge across the Lake of Shining Waters I took the brooch off to have another look at it. Oh, how it did shine in the sunlight! And then, when I was leaning over the bridge, it just slipped through my fingers—so—and went down—down—down, all purply-sparkling, and sank forevermore beneath the Lake of Shining Waters. And that's the best I can do at confessing, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “我拿走了紫水晶胸针，”安妮说道，仿佛在重复她所学到的教训。 “我就像你说的那样把它拿走了。我进去的时候并不是故意要拿它的。但它看起来确实很漂亮，玛丽拉，当我把它别在胸前时，我被一种不可抗拒的诱惑所征服。我想象着把它带到艾德怀尔德玩会是多么令人兴奋。我是科迪莉亚·菲茨杰拉德夫人。如果我戴上一枚真正的紫水晶胸针，我会更容易想象我是科迪莉亚夫人。戴安娜和我制作玫瑰莓项链，但与紫水晶相比，我想在你回家之前把它放回去，以便延长时间。当我走过闪亮水域的桥时，我把胸针取下来再看看它，然后，当我俯身在桥上时，它就从我的手指间溜走了。往下——往下——往下，一切都闪闪发亮，永远沉入闪亮水域之下，这就是我能做的最好的忏悔了，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla felt hot anger surge up into her heart again. This child had taken and lost her treasured amethyst brooch and now sat there calmly reciting the details thereof without the least apparent compunction or repentance.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉感到火热的怒火再次涌上心头。这个孩子拿走了她珍爱的紫水晶胸针，现在又丢了，现在平静地坐在那里，背诵着其中的细节，没有丝毫内疚或悔恨。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, this is terrible," she said, trying to speak calmly. "You are the very wickedest girl I ever heard of."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，这太可怕了，”她试图平静地说。 “你是我听过的最邪恶的女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I suppose I am," agreed Anne tranquilly. "And I know I'll have to be punished. It'll be your duty to punish me, Marilla. Won't you please get it over right off because I'd like to go to the picnic with nothing on my mind."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我想是的。”安妮平静地表示同意。 “我知道我必须受到惩罚。惩罚我是你的责任，玛丽拉。你能不能马上结束这件事，因为我想心无旁骛地去野餐。”

paragraphs.en: "Picnic, indeed! You'll go to no picnic today, Anne Shirley. That shall be your punishment. And it isn't half severe enough either for what you've done!"
paragraphs.zh: “野餐，确实如此！你今天不能去野餐，安妮·雪莉。这将是对你的惩罚。而且对于你所做的事情来说，这还不够严厉！”

paragraphs.en: "Not go to the picnic!" Anne sprang to her feet and clutched Marilla's hand. "But you PROMISED me I might! Oh, Marilla, I must go to the picnic. That was why I confessed. Punish me any way you like but that. Oh, Marilla, please, please, let me go to the picnic. Think of the ice cream! For anything you know I may never have a chance to taste ice cream again."
paragraphs.zh: “不去野餐！”安妮跳了起来，抓住了玛丽拉的手。 “但是你答应过我我会去的！哦，玛丽拉，我必须去野餐。这就是我坦白的原因。除了那样，你可以用任何你喜欢的方式惩罚我。哦，玛丽拉，求你了，求你了，让我去野餐吧。想想冰淇淋吧！你知道的，我可能再也没有机会品尝冰淇淋了。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla disengaged Anne's clinging hands stonily.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉冷漠地松开安妮紧握的双手。

paragraphs.en: "You needn't plead, Anne. You are not going to the picnic and that's final. No, not a word."
paragraphs.zh: “你不必恳求，安妮。你不会去野餐，这是最后的决定。不，一个字都没有。”

paragraphs.en: Anne realized that Marilla was not to be moved. She clasped her hands together, gave a piercing shriek, and then flung herself face downward on the bed, crying and writhing in an utter abandonment of disappointment and despair.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮意识到玛丽拉不能被感动。她双手合十，发出一声刺耳的尖叫，然后脸朝下扑倒在床上，哭泣着，翻滚着，彻底放弃了失望和绝望。

paragraphs.en: "For the land's sake!" gasped Marilla, hastening from the room. "I believe the child is crazy. No child in her senses would behave as she does. If she isn't she's utterly bad. Oh dear, I'm afraid Rachel was right from the first. But I've put my hand to the plow and I won't look back."
paragraphs.zh: “为了土地！”玛丽拉喘着气说，赶紧离开房间。 “我相信这孩子疯了。任何有理智的孩子都不会像她那样行事。如果她不是，那她就彻底坏了。天哪，恐怕雷切尔从一开始就是对的。但我已经把手放在了犁上，我不会回头。”

paragraphs.en: That was a dismal morning. Marilla worked fiercely and scrubbed the porch floor and the dairy shelves when she could find nothing else to do. Neither the shelves nor the porch needed it—but Marilla did. Then she went out and raked the yard.
paragraphs.zh: 那是一个令人沮丧的早晨。当玛丽拉无事可做时，她就拼命工作，擦洗门廊的地板和乳品架。架子和门廊都不需要它——但玛丽拉需要。然后她出去清扫院子。

paragraphs.en: When dinner was ready she went to the stairs and called Anne. A tear-stained face appeared, looking tragically over the banisters.
paragraphs.zh: 晚餐准备好后，她走到楼梯上给安妮打电话。一张满是泪水的脸出现了，悲惨地看着栏杆。

paragraphs.en: "Come down to your dinner, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “下来吃晚饭吧，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't want any dinner, Marilla," said Anne, sobbingly. "I couldn't eat anything. My heart is broken. You'll feel remorse of conscience someday, I expect, for breaking it, Marilla, but I forgive you. Remember when the time comes that I forgive you. But please don't ask me to eat anything, especially boiled pork and greens. Boiled pork and greens are so unromantic when one is in affliction."
paragraphs.zh: “我不想吃晚饭，玛丽拉，”安妮抽泣着说。 “我什么都吃不了。我的心都碎了。我想，有一天你会因为打破了它而感到良心悔恨，玛丽拉，但我原谅你。记住，到时候我会原谅你。但请不要让我吃任何东西，尤其是煮猪肉和青菜。当一个人处于痛苦之中时，煮猪肉和青菜是那么不浪漫。”

paragraphs.en: Exasperated, Marilla returned to the kitchen and poured out her tale of woe to Matthew, who, between his sense of justice and his unlawful sympathy with Anne, was a miserable man.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉愤怒地回到厨房，向马修讲述了她的悲惨故事，马修既有正义感，又有对安妮非法的同情，是一个悲惨的人。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, she shouldn't have taken the brooch, Marilla, or told stories about it," he admitted, mournfully surveying his plateful of unromantic pork and greens as if he, like Anne, thought it a food unsuited to crises of feeling, "but she's such a little thing—such an interesting little thing. Don't you think it's pretty rough not to let her go to the picnic when she's so set on it?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，玛丽拉，她不应该拿走胸针，也不应该讲关于它的故事，”他承认道，悲伤地审视着他那盘不浪漫的猪肉和蔬菜，就好像他和安妮一样，认为这是一种不适合感情危机的食物，“但她是这么一个小东西——这么有趣的小东西。当她如此下定决心去野餐时，你不觉得不让她去野餐很粗鲁吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Matthew Cuthbert, I'm amazed at you. I think I've let her off entirely too easy. And she doesn't appear to realize how wicked she's been at all—that's what worries me most. If she'd really felt sorry it wouldn't be so bad. And you don't seem to realize it, neither; you're making excuses for her all the time to yourself—I can see that."
paragraphs.zh: “马修·库斯伯特，我对你感到惊讶。我想我太轻易地放过她了。而且她似乎根本没有意识到自己有多邪恶——这才是我最担心的。如果她真的感到抱歉，事情也不会那么糟糕。而你似乎也没有意识到这一点；你一直在给自己找借口——我看得出来。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, she's such a little thing," feebly reiterated Matthew. "And there should be allowances made, Marilla. You know she's never had any bringing up."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，她只是个小东西，”马修有气无力地重复道。 “而且应该给予宽容，玛丽拉。你知道她从来没有受过任何教育。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, she's having it now" retorted Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，她现在就这样了，”玛丽拉反驳道。

paragraphs.en: The retort silenced Matthew if it did not convince him. That dinner was a very dismal meal. The only cheerful thing about it was Jerry Buote, the hired boy, and Marilla resented his cheerfulness as a personal insult.
paragraphs.zh: 如果马修的反驳不能说服他的话，他就会闭嘴。那顿晚餐吃得非常惨淡。唯一令人高兴的是雇来的男孩杰里·博特，而玛丽拉则认为他的高兴是对他个人的侮辱。

paragraphs.en: When her dishes were washed and her bread sponge set and her hens fed Marilla remembered that she had noticed a small rent in her best black lace shawl when she had taken it off on Monday afternoon on returning from the Ladies' Aid.
paragraphs.zh: 当她洗完盘子，准备好面包海绵，喂母鸡后，玛丽拉想起，周一下午从妇女救助会回来后，她把最好的黑色蕾丝披肩取下来，发现它有一点小裂口。

paragraphs.en: She would go and mend it. The shawl was in a box in her trunk. As Marilla lifted it out, the sunlight, falling through the vines that clustered thickly about the window, struck upon something caught in the shawl—something that glittered and sparkled in facets of violet light. Marilla snatched at it with a gasp. It was the amethyst brooch, hanging to a thread of the lace by its catch!
paragraphs.zh: 她会去修补它。围巾放在她行李箱的一个盒子里。当玛丽拉把它拿出来时，阳光透过窗户周围密密麻麻的藤蔓照下来，照在披肩上的某个东西上——某个东西在紫罗兰色的光线中闪闪发光。玛丽拉气喘吁吁地一把抓住了它。那是紫水晶胸针，用扣子挂在蕾丝线上！

paragraphs.en: "Dear life and heart," said Marilla blankly, "what does this mean? Here's my brooch safe and sound that I thought was at the bottom of Barry's pond. Whatever did that girl mean by saying she took it and lost it? I declare I believe Green Gables is bewitched. I remember now that when I took off my shawl Monday afternoon I laid it on the bureau for a minute. I suppose the brooch got caught in it somehow. Well!"
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的生命和心灵，”玛丽拉茫然地说，“这是什么意思？这是我的胸针，安然无恙，我以为它在巴里的池塘底。那个女孩说她拿走了它，然后又把它弄丢了，这是什么意思？我声明我相信绿山墙被施了魔法。我现在记得，周一下午我脱下披肩时，我把它放在梳妆台上一分钟。我想胸针不知怎么被夹在里面了。好吧！”

paragraphs.en: Marilla betook herself to the east gable, brooch in hand. Anne had cried herself out and was sitting dejectedly by the window.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉手里拿着胸针，来到东山墙。安妮哭了出来，沮丧地坐在窗边。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley," said Marilla solemnly, "I've just found my brooch hanging to my black lace shawl. Now I want to know what that rigmarole you told me this morning meant."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，”玛丽拉严肃地说，“我刚刚发现我的胸针挂在我的黑色蕾丝披肩上。现在我想知道你今天早上告诉我的那句废话是什么意思。”

paragraphs.en: "Why, you said you'd keep me here until I confessed," returned Anne wearily, "and so I decided to confess because I was bound to get to the picnic. I thought out a confession last night after I went to bed and made it as interesting as I could. And I said it over and over so that I wouldn't forget it. But you wouldn't let me go to the picnic after all, so all my trouble was wasted."
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀，你说过要把我留在这里直到我坦白为止，”安妮疲倦地回答道，“所以我决定坦白，因为我必须要去野餐。昨晚我上床睡觉后就想好了一个坦白，并尽可能让它变得有趣。我一遍又一遍地说，这样我就不会忘记。但你终究不让我去野餐，所以我所有的麻烦都白费了。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla had to laugh in spite of herself. But her conscience pricked her.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉忍不住笑了起来。但她的良心却刺痛了她。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, you do beat all! But I was wrong—I see that now. I shouldn't have doubted your word when I'd never known you to tell a story. Of course, it wasn't right for you to confess to a thing you hadn't done—it was very wrong to do so. But I drove you to it. So if you'll forgive me, Anne, I'll forgive you and we'll start square again. And now get yourself ready for the picnic."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你确实打败了一切！但我错了——我现在明白了。当我从来不知道你会讲故事的时候，我不应该怀疑你的话。当然，你承认一件你没有做过的事情是不对的——这样做是非常错误的。但我驱使你这么做了。所以，如果你能原谅我，安妮，我会原谅你，我们会重新开始。现在准备好去野餐吧。”

paragraphs.en: Anne flew up like a rocket.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮像火箭一样飞了起来。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, isn't it too late?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，是不是太晚了？”

paragraphs.en: "No, it's only two o'clock. They won't be more than well gathered yet and it'll be an hour before they have tea. Wash your face and comb your hair and put on your gingham. I'll fill a basket for you. There's plenty of stuff baked in the house. And I'll get Jerry to hitch up the sorrel and drive you down to the picnic ground."
paragraphs.zh: “不，现在才两点。他们还没有集合好，再过一个小时就可以喝茶了。洗把脸，梳好头发，穿上格子布。我给你装一篮子。屋里有很多烤的东西。我会让杰里把酢浆草套上马车，开车送你去野餐地。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla," exclaimed Anne, flying to the washstand. "Five minutes ago I was so miserable I was wishing I'd never been born and now I wouldn't change places with an angel!"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，”安妮惊呼道，飞奔到盥洗台前。 “五分钟前我非常痛苦，我希望自己从未出生过，但现在我不会与天使交换位置！”

paragraphs.en: That night a thoroughly happy, completely tired-out Anne returned to Green Gables in a state of beatification impossible to describe.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，安妮非常高兴，但又疲惫不堪，带着一种无法形容的幸福状态回到了绿山墙。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, I've had a perfectly scrumptious time. Scrumptious is a new word I learned today. I heard Mary Alice Bell use it. Isn't it very expressive? Everything was lovely. We had a splendid tea and then Mr. Harmon Andrews took us all for a row on the Lake of Shining Waters—six of us at a time. And Jane Andrews nearly fell overboard. She was leaning out to pick water lilies and if Mr. Andrews hadn't caught her by her sash just in the nick of time she'd fallen in and prob'ly been drowned. I wish it had been me. It would have been such a romantic experience to have been nearly drowned. It would be such a thrilling tale to tell. And we had the ice cream. Words fail me to describe that ice cream. Marilla, I assure you it was sublime."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，我度过了一段完美的美味时光。美味是我今天学到的一个新词。我听到玛丽·爱丽丝·贝尔用了它。它不是很有表现力吗？一切都很可爱。我们喝了一杯美味的茶，然后哈蒙·安德鲁斯先生带我们大家在光辉湖上划船——一次我们六个人。简·安德鲁斯差点从船上掉下来。她正探身去采睡莲，如果安德鲁斯先生我真希望那是我，差点被淹死，这真是一个令人兴奋的故事，我无法用语言来形容那个冰淇淋。”

paragraphs.en: That evening Marilla told the whole story to Matthew over her stocking basket.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉通过她的购物篮向马修讲述了整个故事。

paragraphs.en: "I'm willing to own up that I made a mistake," she concluded candidly, "but I've learned a lesson. I have to laugh when I think of Anne's 'confession,' although I suppose I shouldn't for it really was a falsehood. But it doesn't seem as bad as the other would have been, somehow, and anyhow I'm responsible for it. That child is hard to understand in some respects. But I believe she'll turn out all right yet. And there's one thing certain, no house will ever be dull that she's in."
paragraphs.zh: “我愿意承认我犯了一个错误，”她坦率地总结道，“但我已经吸取了教训。当我想到安妮的‘坦白’时，我不得不笑，尽管我想我不应该笑，因为这确实是一个谎言。但不知何故，它似乎并不像另一个那样糟糕，无论如何，我对此负有责任。那个孩子在某些方面很难理解。但我相信她会好起来的。而且有一点是肯定的，有她在的房子永远不会沉闷。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 15 章：学校茶壶里的风暴

paragraphs.en: "What a splendid day!" said Anne, drawing a long breath. "Isn't it good just to be alive on a day like this? I pity the people who aren't born yet for missing it. They may have good days, of course, but they can never have this one. And it's splendider still to have such a lovely way to go to school by, isn't it?"
paragraphs.zh: “多么美好的一天啊！”安妮长长地吸了一口气说道。 “能活在这样的一天不是很好吗？我为那些还没有出生的人错过了这一天而感到遗憾。当然，他们可能有美好的日子，但他们永远不会拥有这样的日子。而且有这样可爱的方式上学，这仍然是很棒的，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: "It's a lot nicer than going round by the road; that is so dusty and hot," said Diana practically, peeping into her dinner basket and mentally calculating if the three juicy, toothsome, raspberry tarts reposing there were divided among ten girls how many bites each girl would have.
paragraphs.zh: “这比在路边绕来绕去好多了，又脏又热，”戴安娜一边说，一边偷偷地看着她的餐篮，心里盘算着如果把放在那里的三个多汁、美味的覆盆子馅饼分给十个女孩，每个女孩会咬多少口。

paragraphs.en: The little girls of Avonlea school always pooled their lunches, and to eat three raspberry tarts all alone or even to share them only with one's best chum would have forever and ever branded as "awful mean" the girl who did it. And yet, when the tarts were divided among ten girls you just got enough to tantalize you.
paragraphs.zh: 埃文利学校的小女孩们总是把午餐集中在一起，独自吃三个覆盆子馅饼，甚至只与最好的朋友分享，都会永远被认为做这件事的女孩“非常卑鄙”。然而，当馅饼分给十个女孩时，你得到的就足以让你着迷了。

paragraphs.en: The way Anne and Diana went to school WAS a pretty one. Anne thought those walks to and from school with Diana couldn't be improved upon even by imagination. Going around by the main road would have been so unromantic; but to go by Lover's Lane and Willowmere and Violet Vale and the Birch Path was romantic, if ever anything was.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮和戴安娜上学的方式很漂亮。安妮认为，与戴安娜一起步行上下学的路即使是想象也无法改善。沿着主干道绕行实在是太不浪漫了。但经过情人巷、威洛米尔、紫罗兰谷和白桦林路，如果有什么浪漫的话，那就很浪漫了。

paragraphs.en: Lover's Lane opened out below the orchard at Green Gables and stretched far up into the woods to the end of the Cuthbert farm. It was the way by which the cows were taken to the back pasture and the wood hauled home in winter. Anne had named it Lover's Lane before she had been a month at Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: 情人巷通向绿山墙果园下方，一直延伸到树林深处，一直延伸到卡斯伯特农场的尽头。这是在冬天把牛带到后面的牧场和把木头拖回家的方式。安妮在绿山墙呆了一个月之前，就把它命名为情人巷。

paragraphs.en: "Not that lovers ever really walk there," she explained to Marilla, "but Diana and I are reading a perfectly magnificent book and there's a Lover's Lane in it. So we want to have one, too. And it's a very pretty name, don't you think? So romantic! We can't imagine the lovers into it, you know. I like that lane because you can think out loud there without people calling you crazy."
paragraphs.zh: “并不是情侣们真的会走过那里，”她向玛丽拉解释道，“但戴安娜和我正在读一本非常精彩的书，里面有一条情人巷。所以我们也想拥有一个。这是一个非常漂亮的名字，你不觉得吗？太浪漫了！你知道，我们无法想象情人走进去。我喜欢那条巷子，因为你可以在那里大声思考，而不会被人说你疯了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne, starting out alone in the morning, went down Lover's Lane as far as the brook. Here Diana met her, and the two little girls went on up the lane under the leafy arch of maples—"maples are such sociable trees," said Anne; "they're always rustling and whispering to you"—until they came to a rustic bridge. Then they left the lane and walked through Mr. Barry's back field and past Willowmere. Beyond Willowmere came Violet Vale—a little green dimple in the shadow of Mr. Andrew Bell's big woods. "Of course there are no violets there now," Anne told Marilla, "but Diana says there are millions of them in spring. Oh, Marilla, can't you just imagine you see them? It actually takes away my breath. I named it Violet Vale. Diana says she never saw the beat of me for hitting on fancy names for places. It's nice to be clever at something, isn't it? But Diana named the Birch Path. She wanted to, so I let her; but I'm sure I could have found something more poetical than plain Birch Path. Anybody can think of a name like that. But the Birch Path is one of the prettiest places in the world, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮早上独自出发，沿着情人巷一直走到小溪边。在这里，黛安娜遇到了她，两个小女孩沿着小巷往前走，在枫叶茂密的拱门下——“枫树是一种善于交际的树，”安妮说；“枫树是一种非常善于交际的树。” “他们总是沙沙作响，对你窃窃私语”——直到他们来到一座质朴的桥上。然后他们离开小巷，穿过巴里先生的后场，经过威洛米尔。越过威洛米尔，来到了紫罗兰谷——安德鲁·贝尔先生的大树林阴影下的一个绿色小凹坑。 “当然，现在那里没有紫罗兰了，”安妮告诉玛丽拉，“但戴安娜说春天有数以百万计的紫罗兰。哦，玛丽拉，你不能想象一下你看到它们吗？它真的让我喘不过气来。我把它命名为紫罗兰谷。戴安娜说她从来没有见过我为地方起奇特名字的节奏。在某些事情上聪明是很好，不是吗？但是戴安娜命名了白桦林路。她想这么做，所以我让她了；但是我确信我可以找到比普通的白桦林更诗意的名字，但白桦林是世界上最美丽的地方之一，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: It was. Other people besides Anne thought so when they stumbled on it. It was a little narrow, twisting path, winding down over a long hill straight through Mr. Bell's woods, where the light came down sifted through so many emerald screens that it was as flawless as the heart of a diamond. It was fringed in all its length with slim young birches, white stemmed and lissom boughed; ferns and starflowers and wild lilies-of-the-valley and scarlet tufts of pigeonberries grew thickly along it; and always there was a delightful spiciness in the air and music of bird calls and the murmur and laugh of wood winds in the trees overhead. Now and then you might see a rabbit skipping across the road if you were quiet—which, with Anne and Diana, happened about once in a blue moon. Down in the valley the path came out to the main road and then it was just up the spruce hill to the school.
paragraphs.zh: 是的。除了安妮之外，其他人在偶然发现这一点时也是这么认为的。这是一条狭窄而曲折的小路，蜿蜒而下，越过一座长长的山丘，笔直穿过贝尔先生的树林，那里的光线透过许多翠绿的屏风照射下来，就像钻石的心脏一样完美无瑕。它的四周都长满了细长的白桦树，茎是白色的，枝条是柔软的。蕨类植物、星花、野铃兰和猩红色的鸽子丛沿着它茂密地生长。空气中总是弥漫着令人愉悦的辛香，鸟儿的鸣叫声和头顶上树林里的木风的低语和笑声。如果你安静的话，你有时可能会看到一只兔子跳过马路——这种情况对于安妮和戴安娜来说是千载难逢的。沿着山谷，小路通向主干道，然后沿着云杉山到达学校。

paragraphs.en: The Avonlea school was a whitewashed building, low in the eaves and wide in the windows, furnished inside with comfortable substantial old-fashioned desks that opened and shut, and were carved all over their lids with the initials and hieroglyphics of three generations of school children. The schoolhouse was set back from the road and behind it was a dusky fir wood and a brook where all the children put their bottles of milk in the morning to keep cool and sweet until dinner hour.
paragraphs.zh: 埃文利学校是一栋粉刷成白色的建筑，屋檐低矮，窗户宽阔，里面摆着舒适的、坚固的老式课桌，可以打开和关闭，课桌的盖子上刻满了三代学童的姓名首字母和象形文字。校舍远离道路，后面是一片昏暗的冷杉树林和一条小溪，所有的孩子早上都会把牛奶瓶放在小溪里，以保持凉爽和甜美，直到晚餐时间。

paragraphs.en: Marilla had seen Anne start off to school on the first day of September with many secret misgivings. Anne was such an odd girl. How would she get on with the other children? And how on earth would she ever manage to hold her tongue during school hours?
paragraphs.zh: 九月第一天，玛丽拉看到安妮带着许多秘密的疑虑开始上学。安妮真是个奇怪的女孩。她和其他孩子相处得怎么样？她究竟是如何在上课时间管住自己的嘴的呢？

paragraphs.en: Things went better than Marilla feared, however. Anne came home that evening in high spirits.
paragraphs.zh: 然而事情比玛丽拉担心的要好。那天晚上，安妮兴高采烈地回到家。

paragraphs.en: "I think I'm going to like school here," she announced. "I don't think much of the master, through. He's all the time curling his mustache and making eyes at Prissy Andrews. Prissy is grown up, you know. She's sixteen and she's studying for the entrance examination into Queen's Academy at Charlottetown next year. Tillie Boulter says the master is DEAD GONE on her. She's got a beautiful complexion and curly brown hair and she does it up so elegantly. She sits in the long seat at the back and he sits there, too, most of the time—to explain her lessons, he says. But Ruby Gillis says she saw him writing something on her slate and when Prissy read it she blushed as red as a beet and giggled; and Ruby Gillis says she doesn't believe it had anything to do with the lesson."
paragraphs.zh: “我想我会喜欢这里的学校，”她宣布。 “我对这位大师的评价并不高。他总是卷着小胡子，对着普里西·安德鲁斯眨眼。你知道，普里西已经长大了。她十六岁了，正在为明年夏洛特敦女王学院的入学考试而学习。蒂莉·博尔特说，大师对她已经死心了。她有着美丽的肤色和棕色的卷发，而且打扮得非常优雅。她坐在餐厅的长椅上。他说，大多数时候他也坐在那儿——解释她的课程，但鲁比·吉利斯说她看到他在她的石板上写了一些东西，当普里西读到它时，她脸红得像甜菜一样，咯咯地笑起来，鲁比·吉利斯说她不相信这与课程有任何关系。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, don't let me hear you talking about your teacher in that way again," said Marilla sharply. "You don't go to school to criticize the master. I guess he can teach YOU something, and it's your business to learn. And I want you to understand right off that you are not to come home telling tales about him. That is something I won't encourage. I hope you were a good girl."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，别让我听到你再用这种方式谈论你的老师。”玛丽拉严厉地说。 “你去学校不是为了批评老师的。我想他可以教你一些东西，而学习是你的事。我希望你立刻明白，你不能回家讲述他的故事。这是我不会鼓励的事情。我希望你是一个好女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "Indeed I was," said Anne comfortably. "It wasn't so hard as you might imagine, either. I sit with Diana. Our seat is right by the window and we can look down to the Lake of Shining Waters. There are a lot of nice girls in school and we had scrumptious fun playing at dinnertime. It's so nice to have a lot of little girls to play with. But of course I like Diana best and always will. I ADORE Diana. I'm dreadfully far behind the others. They're all in the fifth book and I'm only in the fourth. I feel that it's kind of a disgrace. But there's not one of them has such an imagination as I have and I soon found that out. We had reading and geography and Canadian history and dictation today. Mr. Phillips said my spelling was disgraceful and he held up my slate so that everybody could see it, all marked over. I felt so mortified, Marilla; he might have been politer to a stranger, I think. Ruby Gillis gave me an apple and Sophia Sloane lent me a lovely pink card with 'May I see you home?' on it. I'm to give it back to her tomorrow. And Tillie Boulter let me wear her bead ring all the afternoon. Can I have some of those pearl beads off the old pincushion in the garret to make myself a ring? And oh, Marilla, Jane Andrews told me that Minnie MacPherson told her that she heard Prissy Andrews tell Sara Gillis that I had a very pretty nose. Marilla, that is the first compliment I have ever had in my life and you can't imagine what a strange feeling it gave me. Marilla, have I really a pretty nose? I know you'll tell me the truth."
paragraphs.zh: “确实如此，”安妮轻松地说。 “这也没有你想象的那么难。我和戴安娜坐在一起。我们的座位就在窗户旁边，我们可以俯瞰闪亮水域湖。学校里有很多漂亮的女孩，我们在晚餐时玩得很开心。有很多小女孩一起玩真是太好了。但当然，我最喜欢戴安娜，而且永远都会。我喜欢戴安娜。我远远落后于其他人。他们都在第五本书中我觉得这是一种耻辱，但他们中没有人像我一样有这样的想象力，我很快就发现了这一点。菲利普斯先生今天说我的拼写很丢脸，他举起了我的石板，让每个人都可以看到它，我觉得很丢脸，玛丽拉；我想他可能对一个陌生人更礼貌。吉利斯给了我一个苹果，索菲亚·斯隆借给我一张可爱的粉色卡片，上面写着“我可以送你回家吗？”在它上面。我明天就还给她。蒂莉·博尔特让我整个下午都戴着她的串珠戒指。我可以从阁楼上的旧针垫上取下一些珍珠珠来给自己做一枚戒指吗？哦，玛丽拉，简·安德鲁斯告诉我，米妮·麦克弗森告诉她，她听到普里西·安德鲁斯告诉萨拉·吉利斯，我有一个非常漂亮的鼻子。玛丽拉，这是我一生中第一次得到的赞美，你无法想象它给我带来了多么奇怪的感觉。玛丽拉，我的鼻子真的漂亮吗？我知道你会告诉我真相。”

paragraphs.en: "Your nose is well enough," said Marilla shortly. Secretly she thought Anne's nose was a remarkable pretty one; but she had no intention of telling her so.
paragraphs.zh: “你的鼻子还不错。”玛丽拉简短地说。她私下里觉得安妮的鼻子非常漂亮。但她并没有打算告诉她这些。

paragraphs.en: That was three weeks ago and all had gone smoothly so far. And now, this crisp September morning, Anne and Diana were tripping blithely down the Birch Path, two of the happiest little girls in Avonlea.
paragraphs.zh: 那是三周前的事了，到目前为止一切都很顺利。现在，在这个清爽的九月早晨，安妮和戴安娜愉快地沿着白桦林小径漫步，她们是埃文利最快乐的两个小女孩。

paragraphs.en: "I guess Gilbert Blythe will be in school today," said Diana. "He's been visiting his cousins over in New Brunswick all summer and he only came home Saturday night. He's AW'FLY handsome, Anne. And he teases the girls something terrible. He just torments our lives out."
paragraphs.zh: “我猜吉尔伯特·布莱斯今天会去学校，”戴安娜说。 “整个夏天他都在新不伦瑞克省看望他的表兄弟，周六晚上才回家。他真是太帅了，安妮。他还用一些可怕的东西来戏弄女孩们。他只是折磨我们的生活。”

paragraphs.en: Diana's voice indicated that she rather liked having her life tormented out than not.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜的声音表明，她宁愿自己的生活被折磨也不愿忍受。

paragraphs.en: "Gilbert Blythe?" said Anne. "Isn't his name that's written up on the porch wall with Julia Bell's and a big 'Take Notice' over them?"
paragraphs.zh: “吉尔伯特·布莱斯？”安妮说。 “门廊墙上不是写着他的名字和朱莉娅·贝尔的名字，上面还写着一个大大的‘注意’吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes," said Diana, tossing her head, "but I'm sure he doesn't like Julia Bell so very much. I've heard him say he studied the multiplication table by her freckles."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”黛安娜摇着头说道，“但我确信他不太喜欢朱莉娅·贝尔。我听他说他是通过她的雀斑来研究乘法表的。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, don't speak about freckles to me," implored Anne. "It isn't delicate when I've got so many. But I do think that writing take-notices up on the wall about the boys and girls is the silliest ever. I should just like to see anybody dare to write my name up with a boy's. Not, of course," she hastened to add, "that anybody would."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，别跟我谈论雀斑，”安妮恳求道。 “我有这么多，这并不微妙。但我确实认为在墙上写关于男孩和女孩的注意事项是有史以来最愚蠢的。我只是希望看到有人敢于把我的名字和男孩的名字写在一起。当然，不是，”她赶紧补充道，“任何人都会这样做。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed. She didn't want her name written up. But it was a little humiliating to know that there was no danger of it.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气。她不想让自己的名字被写下来。但知道没有危险，还是有点羞辱。

paragraphs.en: "Nonsense," said Diana, whose black eyes and glossy tresses had played such havoc with the hearts of Avonlea schoolboys that her name figured on the porch walls in half a dozen take-notices. "It's only meant as a joke. And don't you be too sure your name won't ever be written up. Charlie Sloane is DEAD GONE on you. He told his mother—his MOTHER, mind you—that you were the smartest girl in school. That's better than being good looking."
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道，”戴安娜说，她的黑眼睛和光泽的头发对埃文利学童的心造成了如此大的破坏，以至于她的名字出现在六张注意事项的门廊墙上。 “这只是个玩笑。别太确定你的名字永远不会被写下来。查理·斯隆对你很着迷。他告诉他的母亲——他的母亲，请注意——你是学校里最聪明的女孩。这比长得漂亮更好。”

paragraphs.en: "No, it isn't," said Anne, feminine to the core. "I'd rather be pretty than clever. And I hate Charlie Sloane, I can't bear a boy with goggle eyes. If anyone wrote my name up with his I'd never GET over it, Diana Barry. But it IS nice to keep head of your class."
paragraphs.zh: “不，不是的，”安妮说道，语气里充满了女性气息。 “我宁愿漂亮，也不愿聪明。而且我讨厌查理·斯隆，我无法忍受一个长着护目镜的男孩。如果有人把我的名字和他的名字写在一起，我永远不会忘记，戴安娜·巴里。但在班上保持领先是很好的。”

paragraphs.en: "You'll have Gilbert in your class after this," said Diana, "and he's used to being head of his class, I can tell you. He's only in the fourth book although he's nearly fourteen. Four years ago his father was sick and had to go out to Alberta for his health and Gilbert went with him. They were there three years and Gil didn't go to school hardly any until they came back. You won't find it so easy to keep head after this, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “这之后你的班上就会有吉尔伯特了，”黛安娜说，“我可以告诉你，他已经习惯了当班长。虽然他已经快十四岁了，但他只上了第四本书。四年前，他的父亲生病了，不得不去阿尔伯塔养病，吉尔伯特就跟着他去了。他们在那里待了三年，吉尔伯特几乎没有上过学，直到他们回来。安妮，你会发现在这之后保持头脑没那么容易了。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm glad," said Anne quickly. "I couldn't really feel proud of keeping head of little boys and girls of just nine or ten. I got up yesterday spelling 'ebullition.' Josie Pye was head and, mind you, she peeped in her book. Mr. Phillips didn't see her—he was looking at Prissy Andrews—but I did. I just swept her a look of freezing scorn and she got as red as a beet and spelled it wrong after all."
paragraphs.zh: “我很高兴，”安妮赶紧说道。 “我真的不能因为保留了九岁或十岁的小男孩和女孩的头而感到自豪。昨天我起床拼写了‘ebulition’。乔西·派伊（Josie Pye）是负责人，请注意，她偷看了她的书。菲利普斯先生没有看到她——他看着普莉西·安德鲁斯——但我看到了。我只是用冰冷的蔑视目光扫了她一眼，她脸红得像甜菜一样，而且还是拼错了。”

paragraphs.en: "Those Pye girls are cheats all round," said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road. "Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don't speak to her now."
paragraphs.zh: “那些派伊女孩都是骗子，”当她们爬上主路的栅栏时，戴安娜愤怒地说。 “格蒂·派伊昨天确实去把她的奶瓶放在小溪里我的位置了。你有吗？我现在不跟她说话了。”

paragraphs.en: When Mr. Phillips was in the back of the room hearing Prissy Andrews's Latin, Diana whispered to Anne,
paragraphs.zh: 当菲利普斯先生在房间后面听到普里西·安德鲁斯的拉丁语时，戴安娜对安妮低声说：

paragraphs.en: "That's Gilbert Blythe sitting right across the aisle from you, Anne. Just look at him and see if you don't think he's handsome."
paragraphs.zh: “那是吉尔伯特·布莱斯，坐在你对面的过道上，安妮。看看他，看看你是否认为他英俊。”

paragraphs.en: Anne looked accordingly. She had a good chance to do so, for the said Gilbert Blythe was absorbed in stealthily pinning the long yellow braid of Ruby Gillis, who sat in front of him, to the back of her seat. He was a tall boy, with curly brown hair, roguish hazel eyes, and a mouth twisted into a teasing smile. Presently Ruby Gillis started up to take a sum to the master; she fell back into her seat with a little shriek, believing that her hair was pulled out by the roots. Everybody looked at her and Mr. Phillips glared so sternly that Ruby began to cry. Gilbert had whisked the pin out of sight and was studying his history with the soberest face in the world; but when the commotion subsided he looked at Anne and winked with inexpressible drollery.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮相应地看了看。她有一个很好的机会这样做，因为吉尔伯特·布莱斯正全神贯注地把坐在他前面的鲁比·吉利斯的黄色长辫子偷偷地别在座位后面。他是个高个子男孩，有一头棕色的卷发，一双调皮的淡褐色眼睛，嘴角扭曲着一抹戏谑的微笑。不久，鲁比·吉利斯开始向主人取一笔钱。她尖叫一声倒回座位上，她相信自己的头发被连根拔掉了。每个人都看着她，菲利普斯先生的目光如此严厉，以至于鲁比开始哭泣。吉尔伯特迅速将别针从视线中移开，正以世界上最清醒的表情研究着自己的历史。但当骚动平息后，他看着安妮，用难以形容的滑稽表情眨了眨眼睛。

paragraphs.en: "I think your Gilbert Blythe IS handsome," confided Anne to Diana, "but I think he's very bold. It isn't good manners to wink at a strange girl."
paragraphs.zh: “我觉得你们家的吉尔伯特·布莱斯确实挺帅的，”安妮悄悄对戴安娜说，“但他太轻浮了。对一个陌生女孩眨眼睛可不是有礼貌的行为。”

paragraphs.en: But it was not until the afternoon that things really began to happen.
paragraphs.zh: 但直到下午，事情才真正开始爆发。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips was back in the corner explaining a problem in algebra to Prissy Andrews and the rest of the scholars were doing pretty much as they pleased eating green apples, whispering, drawing pictures on their slates, and driving crickets harnessed to strings, up and down aisle. Gilbert Blythe was trying to make Anne Shirley look at him and failing utterly, because Anne was at that moment totally oblivious not only to the very existence of Gilbert Blythe, but of every other scholar in Avonlea school itself. With her chin propped on her hands and her eyes fixed on the blue glimpse of the Lake of Shining Waters that the west window afforded, she was far away in a gorgeous dreamland hearing and seeing nothing save her own wonderful visions.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生正在角落里给普里西·安德鲁斯讲解代数题，其他学生则随心所欲：吃青苹果、咬耳朵低语、在石板上画画，或者用线拴着蟋蟀在走道上来回游走。吉尔伯特·布莱斯试图让安妮·雪莉看他一眼，却彻底失败了，因为安妮那一刻不仅完全无视了吉尔伯特·布莱斯的存在，连阿文莉学校里的其他任何学生都被她忘得一干二净。她双手托着下巴，双眼紧盯着西窗外那一抹蔚蓝的闪光湖水，早已飘向了远方绚丽的梦境，除了自己奇妙的幻象外什么也听不见、看不见。

paragraphs.en: Gilbert Blythe wasn't used to putting himself out to make a girl look at him and meeting with failure. She SHOULD look at him, that red-haired Shirley girl with the little pointed chin and the big eyes that weren't like the eyes of any other girl in Avonlea school.
paragraphs.zh: 吉尔伯特·布莱斯可不习惯费尽心思让一个女孩看他却遭致失败。她应该看他，那个有着小尖下巴和大眼睛的红头发雪莉女孩，她的眼睛与阿文莉学校里其他任何女孩的眼睛都不一样。

paragraphs.en: Gilbert reached across the aisle, picked up the end of Anne's long red braid, held it out at arm's length and said in a piercing whisper:
paragraphs.zh: 吉尔伯特伸手穿过走道，揪住安妮那条长长的红辫子末端，拉得老长，用刺耳的低语喊道：

paragraphs.en: "Carrots! Carrots!"
paragraphs.zh: “胡萝卜！胡萝卜！”

paragraphs.en: Then Anne looked at him with a vengeance!
paragraphs.zh: 这下安妮终于看他了，带着一股复仇般的怒火！

paragraphs.en: She did more than look. She sprang to her feet, her bright fancies fallen into cureless ruin. She flashed one indignant glance at Gilbert from eyes whose angry sparkle was swiftly quenched in equally angry tears.
paragraphs.zh: 她做的不仅仅是看。她一跃而起，她美好的幻想化为无法挽回的泡影。她用那双怒火中烧的眼睛狠狠向吉尔伯特投去愤怒的一瞥，怒火瞬间被同样愤怒的眼泪所熄灭。

paragraphs.en: "You mean, hateful boy!" she exclaimed passionately. "How dare you!"
paragraphs.zh: “你是说，可恶的小子！”她热情地喊道。 “你怎么敢！”

paragraphs.en: And then—thwack! Anne had brought her slate down on Gilbert's head and cracked it—slate not head—clear across.
paragraphs.zh: 接着——啪！安妮把她的石板狠狠砸在吉尔伯特的头上，石板咔嚓一声从中间断成了两截。

paragraphs.en: Avonlea school always enjoyed a scene. This was an especially enjoyable one. Everybody said "Oh" in horrified delight. Diana gasped. Ruby Gillis, who was inclined to be hysterical, began to cry. Tommy Sloane let his team of crickets escape him altogether while he stared open-mouthed at the tableau.
paragraphs.zh: 阿文莉学校的学生总是喜欢看热闹。这一幕尤为刺激。每个人都发出了惊恐又兴奋的惊呼声。戴安娜倒吸一口凉气，情绪容易激动的鲁比·吉利斯哭了起来，汤米·斯隆嘴巴张得老大，连手里用线拴着的一队蟋蟀跑掉了都浑然不知。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips stalked down the aisle and laid his hand heavily on Anne's shoulder.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生大步走下走道，沉重地把手放在安妮的肩膀上。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, what does this mean?" he said angrily. Anne returned no answer. It was asking too much of flesh and blood to expect her to tell before the whole school that she had been called "carrots." Gilbert it was who spoke up stoutly.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，这是什么意思？”他生气地说。安妮没有回答。要她在全班同学面前说出自己被叫了“胡萝卜”，对一个女孩子来说实在太残忍了。倒是吉尔伯特勇敢地站了出来。

paragraphs.en: "It was my fault Mr. Phillips. I teased her."
paragraphs.zh: “是我的错，菲利普斯先生。是我先挑逗戏弄她的。”

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips paid no heed to Gilbert.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生压根没有理会吉尔伯特。

paragraphs.en: "I am sorry to see a pupil of mine displaying such a temper and such a vindictive spirit," he said in a solemn tone, as if the mere fact of being a pupil of his ought to root out all evil passions from the hearts of small imperfect mortals. "Anne, go and stand on the platform in front of the blackboard for the rest of the afternoon."
paragraphs.zh: “我很遗憾看到我的学生展现出如此暴躁的脾气和报复心理，”他用庄严的语气说。“安妮，在今天下午剩下的时间里，去站在黑板前的讲台上罚站。”

paragraphs.en: Anne would have infinitely preferred a whipping to this punishment under which her sensitive spirit quivered as from a whiplash. With a white, set face she obeyed. Mr. Phillips took a chalk crayon and wrote on the blackboard above her head.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮宁愿挨一顿抽，也不愿接受这种让她敏感自尊心备受摧残的羞辱惩罚。她脸色苍白、嘴唇紧闭地服从了。菲利普斯先生拿了一支粉笔，在她头顶上的黑板上写了起来。

paragraphs.en: "Ann Shirley has a very bad temper. Ann Shirley must learn to control her temper," and then read it out loud so that even the primer class, who couldn't read writing, should understand it.
paragraphs.zh: “安·雪莉的脾气很坏。安·雪莉必须学会控制自己的脾气。”然后大声念出来，这样即使是不会读写的初级班也能理解。

paragraphs.en: Anne stood there the rest of the afternoon with that legend above her. She did not cry or hang her head. Anger was still too hot in her heart for that and it sustained her amid all her agony of humiliation. With resentful eyes and passion-red cheeks she confronted alike Diana's sympathetic gaze and Charlie Sloane's indignant nods and Josie Pye's malicious smiles. As for Gilbert Blythe, she would not even look at him. She would NEVER look at him again! She would never speak to him!!
paragraphs.zh: 整个下午，安妮都站在那里，那个传说就在她的上方。她没有哭，也没有低下头。她心中的愤怒仍然太强烈，无法承受这种痛苦，这让她在羞辱的痛苦中支撑着她。她用怨恨的眼神和激情泛红的脸颊面对着戴安娜同情的目光、查理·斯隆愤怒的点头和乔西·派伊恶意的微笑。至于吉尔伯特·布莱斯，她连看都不看他一眼。她再也不会看他一眼！她绝对不会跟他说话！！

paragraphs.en: When school was dismissed Anne marched out with her red head held high. Gilbert Blythe tried to intercept her at the porch door.
paragraphs.zh: 放学时，安妮高举着红头走出去。吉尔伯特·布莱斯试图在门廊门口拦截她。

paragraphs.en: "I'm awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne," he whispered contritely. "Honest I am. Don't be mad for keeps, now."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，我很抱歉我取笑了你的头发。”他悔恨地低声说道。 “我是诚实的。现在别再生气了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne swept by disdainfully, without look or sign of hearing. "Oh how could you, Anne?" breathed Diana as they went down the road half reproachfully, half admiringly. Diana felt that SHE could never have resisted Gilbert's plea.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮轻蔑地掠过，看也不看，也没有听见。 “哦，安妮，你怎么能这样？”当他们走在路上时，戴安娜半是责备半是钦佩地喘着气。戴安娜觉得她永远无法拒绝吉尔伯特的恳求。

paragraphs.en: "I shall never forgive Gilbert Blythe," said Anne firmly. "And Mr. Phillips spelled my name without an e, too. The iron has entered into my soul, Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “我永远不会原谅吉尔伯特·布莱斯，”安妮坚定地说。 “菲利普斯先生也把我的名字拼写成没有e。铁已经进入了我的灵魂，戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: Diana hadn't the least idea what Anne meant but she understood it was something terrible.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜根本不明白安妮的意思，但她知道这是一件可怕的事情。

paragraphs.en: "You mustn't mind Gilbert making fun of your hair," she said soothingly. "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it's so black. He's called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."
paragraphs.zh: “你一定不要介意吉尔伯特取笑你的头发，”她安慰道。 “哎呀，他取笑所有的女孩。他嘲笑我的女孩，因为它太黑了。他已经骂我乌鸦十几次了；我以前也从未听他为任何事情道歉过。”

paragraphs.en: "There's a great deal of difference between being called a crow and being called carrots," said Anne with dignity. "Gilbert Blythe has hurt my feelings EXCRUCIATINGLY, Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “被称为乌鸦和被称为胡萝卜有很大的区别。”安妮一本正经地说。 “吉尔伯特·布莱斯极大地伤害了我的感情，戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: It is possible the matter might have blown over without more excruciation if nothing else had happened. But when things begin to happen they are apt to keep on.
paragraphs.zh: 如果没有发生其他事情的话，这件事可能会结束，而不会造成更多痛苦。但当事情开始发生时，它们很容易继续下去。

paragraphs.en: Avonlea scholars often spent noon hour picking gum in Mr. Bell's spruce grove over the hill and across his big pasture field. From there they could keep an eye on Eben Wright's house, where the master boarded. When they saw Mr. Phillips emerging therefrom they ran for the schoolhouse; but the distance being about three times longer than Mr. Wright's lane they were very apt to arrive there, breathless and gasping, some three minutes too late.
paragraphs.zh: 埃文利的学者们经常在中午的时间里在贝尔先生的云杉林里采摘口香糖，林中的云杉林位于山坡上，穿过他的大牧场。从那里他们可以监视埃本赖特的房子，主人就在那里登船。当他们看到菲利普斯先生从里面出来时，他们就跑向校舍。但距离比赖特先生的车道长大约三倍，他们很可能气喘吁吁地到达那里，大约晚了三分钟。

paragraphs.en: On the following day Mr. Phillips was seized with one of his spasmodic fits of reform and announced before going home to dinner, that he should expect to find all the scholars in their seats when he returned. Anyone who came in late would be punished.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，菲利普斯先生突然进行了一次改革，他在回家吃晚饭之前宣布，当他回来时，他应该会发现所有学者都坐在座位上。任何迟到的人都会受到惩罚。

paragraphs.en: All the boys and some of the girls went to Mr. Bell's spruce grove as usual, fully intending to stay only long enough to "pick a chew." But spruce groves are seductive and yellow nuts of gum beguiling; they picked and loitered and strayed; and as usual the first thing that recalled them to a sense of the flight of time was Jimmy Glover shouting from the top of a patriarchal old spruce "Master's coming."
paragraphs.zh: 所有的男孩和一些女孩都像往常一样去了贝尔先生的云杉林，完全打算只停留足够长的时间来“采摘”。但云杉林却很诱人，黄色的树胶坚果令人着迷。他们采摘、徘徊、迷失；和往常一样，首先让他们想起时间流逝的感觉的是吉米·格洛弗在一棵父权制老云杉树顶上喊道“主人来了”。

paragraphs.en: The girls who were on the ground, started first and managed to reach the schoolhouse in time but without a second to spare. The boys, who had to wriggle hastily down from the trees, were later; and Anne, who had not been picking gum at all but was wandering happily in the far end of the grove, waist deep among the bracken, singing softly to herself, with a wreath of rice lilies on her hair as if she were some wild divinity of the shadowy places, was latest of all. Anne could run like a deer, however; run she did with the impish result that she overtook the boys at the door and was swept into the schoolhouse among them just as Mr. Phillips was in the act of hanging up his hat.
paragraphs.zh: 地面上的女孩们首先出发，并设法及时到达校舍，但没有多余的时间。男孩们后来才到，他们不得不赶紧从树上爬下来。安妮是最后一个，她根本没有采过口香糖，而是在小树林的尽头快乐地漫步，在齐腰深的蕨菜丛中，轻声地自言自语，头发上戴着稻花花环，仿佛她是阴暗地方的野生神灵。然而，安妮却可以像鹿一样奔跑。她跑起来，结果顽皮地超过了门口的男孩们，并在菲利普斯先生正在挂帽子的时候被卷进校舍，和他们在一起。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips's brief reforming energy was over; he didn't want the bother of punishing a dozen pupils; but it was necessary to do something to save his word, so he looked about for a scapegoat and found it in Anne, who had dropped into her seat, gasping for breath, with a forgotten lily wreath hanging askew over one ear and giving her a particularly rakish and disheveled appearance.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生短暂的改革精力结束了。他不想费心去惩罚十几个学生；但他必须做点什么来兑现诺言，所以他四处寻找替罪羊，并在安妮身上找到了替罪羊。安妮跌坐在座位上，气喘吁吁，一只被遗忘的百合花环歪斜地挂在一只耳朵上，让她显得特别放荡和凌乱。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, since you seem to be so fond of the boys' company we shall indulge your taste for it this afternoon," he said sarcastically. "Take those flowers out of your hair and sit with Gilbert Blythe."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮雪莉，既然你看起来很喜欢男孩们的陪伴，我们今天下午就满足你的口味，”他讽刺地说。 “把你头发上的花摘下来，和吉尔伯特·布莱斯坐在一起。”

paragraphs.en: The other boys snickered. Diana, turning pale with pity, plucked the wreath from Anne's hair and squeezed her hand. Anne stared at the master as if turned to stone.
paragraphs.zh: 其他男孩窃笑起来。戴安娜怜悯地脸色苍白，从安妮的头发上摘下花环，握紧了她的手。安妮凝视着主人，仿佛变成了石头。

paragraphs.en: "Did you hear what I said, Anne?" queried Mr. Phillips sternly.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你听到我说的话了吗？”菲利普斯先生严厉地问道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, sir," said Anne slowly "but I didn't suppose you really meant it."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生，”安妮慢慢地说，“但我不认为你是真心的。”

paragraphs.en: "I assure you I did"—still with the sarcastic inflection which all the children, and Anne especially, hated. It flicked on the raw. "Obey me at once."
paragraphs.zh: “我向你保证，我做到了”——仍然带有所有孩子们，尤其是安妮所讨厌的讽刺语气。它在原料上弹动。 “立刻服从我。”

paragraphs.en: For a moment Anne looked as if she meant to disobey. Then, realizing that there was no help for it, she rose haughtily, stepped across the aisle, sat down beside Gilbert Blythe, and buried her face in her arms on the desk. Ruby Gillis, who got a glimpse of it as it went down, told the others going home from school that she'd "acksually never seen anything like it—it was so white, with awful little red spots in it."
paragraphs.zh: 有那么一会儿，安妮看上去似乎有意违抗。然后，意识到没有办法，她傲慢地站起来，跨过过道，在吉尔伯特·布莱斯身边坐下，把脸埋在桌子上的双臂里。鲁比·吉利斯（Ruby Gillis）在它落下时瞥见了它，她告诉其他放学回家的人，她“实际上从未见过这样的东西——它是如此的白色，里面有可怕的小红点。”

paragraphs.en: To Anne, this was as the end of all things. It was bad enough to be singled out for punishment from among a dozen equally guilty ones; it was worse still to be sent to sit with a boy, but that that boy should be Gilbert Blythe was heaping insult on injury to a degree utterly unbearable. Anne felt that she could not bear it and it would be of no use to try. Her whole being seethed with shame and anger and humiliation.
paragraphs.zh: 对于安妮来说，这就是一切的终结。从十几个同样有罪的人中挑出来接受惩罚，这已经够糟糕的了。更糟糕的是被派去和一个男孩坐在一起，但那个男孩应该是吉尔伯特·布莱斯，这简直是侮辱到了完全无法忍受的程度。安妮觉得自己无法忍受，尝试也没用。她的整个人都充满了羞耻、愤怒和屈辱。

paragraphs.en: At first the other scholars looked and whispered and giggled and nudged. But as Anne never lifted her head and as Gilbert worked fractions as if his whole soul was absorbed in them and them only, they soon returned to their own tasks and Anne was forgotten. When Mr. Phillips called the history class out Anne should have gone, but Anne did not move, and Mr. Phillips, who had been writing some verses "To Priscilla" before he called the class, was thinking about an obstinate rhyme still and never missed her. Once, when nobody was looking, Gilbert took from his desk a little pink candy heart with a gold motto on it, "You are sweet," and slipped it under the curve of Anne's arm. Whereupon Anne arose, took the pink heart gingerly between the tips of her fingers, dropped it on the floor, ground it to powder beneath her heel, and resumed her position without deigning to bestow a glance on Gilbert.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，其他学者看了看，窃窃私语，咯咯地笑着，用肘碰了碰。但由于安妮从来没有抬起过头，吉尔伯特在计算分数时就好像他的整个灵魂都被它们所吸引，而且只专注于它们，所以他们很快就回到了自己的任务中，安妮被遗忘了。当菲利普斯先生叫历史课下课的时候，安妮应该走了，但安妮没有动，而菲利普斯先生在叫同学们前已经在写几首《致普里西拉》的诗句了，他还在想一个顽固的押韵，从来没有错过过她。有一次，趁没人注意的时候，吉尔伯特从办公桌上拿出一颗粉红色的小心形糖果，上面写着金色的座右铭：“你真可爱”，然后把它塞到安妮的手臂曲线下。于是安妮站起来，小心翼翼地用指尖夹起粉红色的心，把它扔到地板上，用脚后跟把它磨成粉末，然后又恢复了原来的姿势，连看吉尔伯特一眼都没有。

paragraphs.en: When school went out Anne marched to her desk, ostentatiously took out everything therein, books and writing tablet, pen and ink, testament and arithmetic, and piled them neatly on her cracked slate.
paragraphs.zh: 放学的时候，安妮大步走向自己的课桌，招摇地拿出课桌上的所有东西，书本、写字板、钢笔、墨水、遗嘱和算术，整齐地堆放在她那块有裂缝的石板上。

paragraphs.en: "What are you taking all those things home for, Anne?" Diana wanted to know, as soon as they were out on the road. She had not dared to ask the question before.
paragraphs.zh: “你把这些东西带回家干什么，安妮？”他们一上路，戴安娜就想知道。之前她还不敢问这个问题。

paragraphs.en: "I am not coming back to school any more," said Anne. Diana gasped and stared at Anne to see if she meant it.
paragraphs.zh: “我不会再回学校了，”安妮说。戴安娜喘着气，盯着安妮看她是否是这个意思。

paragraphs.en: "Will Marilla let you stay home?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉会让你呆在家里吗？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: "She'll have to," said Anne. "I'll NEVER go to school to that man again."
paragraphs.zh: “她必须这样做，”安妮说。 “我再也不会去那个男人的学校了。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Anne!" Diana looked as if she were ready to cry. "I do think you're mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，安妮！”戴安娜看起来好像快要哭了。 “我确实认为你很卑鄙。我该怎么办？菲利普斯先生会让我和那个可怕的格蒂·派伊坐在一起——我知道他会的，因为她一个人坐着。一定要回来，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "I'd do almost anything in the world for you, Diana," said Anne sadly. "I'd let myself be torn limb from limb if it would do you any good. But I can't do this, so please don't ask it. You harrow up my very soul."
paragraphs.zh: “我愿意为你做任何事情，戴安娜，”安妮悲伤地说。 “如果这对你有什么好处的话，我愿意让自己被撕成碎片。但我做不到，所以请不要问这个。你把我的灵魂都掏空了。”

paragraphs.en: "Just think of all the fun you will miss," mourned Diana. "We are going to build the loveliest new house down by the brook; and we'll be playing ball next week and you've never played ball, Anne. It's tremendously exciting. And we're going to learn a new song—Jane Andrews is practicing it up now; and Alice Andrews is going to bring a new Pansy book next week and we're all going to read it out loud, chapter about, down by the brook. And you know you are so fond of reading out loud, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “想想你会错过的所有乐趣，”戴安娜哀悼道。 “我们要在小溪边建造最可爱的新房子；下周我们要打球，而你从来没有打过球，安妮。这太令人兴奋了。我们要学一首新歌——简·安德鲁斯现在正在练习；爱丽丝·安德鲁斯下周将带来一本新的三色堇书，我们都会在小溪边大声朗读它，章节有关。你知道你很喜欢大声朗读，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: Nothing moved Anne in the least. Her mind was made up. She would not go to school to Mr. Phillips again; she told Marilla so when she got home.
paragraphs.zh: 没有什么能打动安妮。她已经下定决心了。她不会再去菲利普斯先生的学校了；当玛丽拉回到家时，她就这样告诉了她。

paragraphs.en: "Nonsense," said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “胡说，”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: "It isn't nonsense at all," said Anne, gazing at Marilla with solemn, reproachful eyes. "Don't you understand, Marilla? I've been insulted."
paragraphs.zh: “这根本不是废话，”安妮说道，用严肃而责备的眼神看着玛丽拉。 “你不明白吗，玛丽拉？我受到了侮辱。”

paragraphs.en: "Insulted fiddlesticks! You'll go to school tomorrow as usual."
paragraphs.zh: “被侮辱的胡言乱语！明天你照常去学校。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, no." Anne shook her head gently. "I'm not going back, Marilla. I'll learn my lessons at home and I'll be as good as I can be and hold my tongue all the time if it's possible at all. But I will not go back to school, I assure you."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，不。”安妮轻轻摇了摇头。 “我不会回去，玛丽拉。我会在家里学习我的功课，我会尽我所能，如果可能的话，一直保持沉默。但我向你保证，我不会回到学校。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla saw something remarkably like unyielding stubbornness looking out of Anne's small face. She understood that she would have trouble in overcoming it; but she re-solved wisely to say nothing more just then. "I'll run down and see Rachel about it this evening," she thought. "There's no use reasoning with Anne now. She's too worked up and I've an idea she can be awful stubborn if she takes the notion. Far as I can make out from her story, Mr. Phillips has been carrying matters with a rather high hand. But it would never do to say so to her. I'll just talk it over with Rachel. She's sent ten children to school and she ought to know something about it. She'll have heard the whole story, too, by this time."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉从安妮的小脸上看到了一种异常不屈的固执。她知道自己很难克服这个困难；但她明智地决定不再多说什么。 “今晚我会跑去见瑞秋，讨论这件事，”她想。 “现在跟安妮讲道理是没有用的。她太激动了，我觉得如果她接受了这个想法，她会非常固执。据我所知，菲利普斯先生在处理事情上一直居高临下。但对她这么说是不行的。我会和雷切尔讨论一下。她送了十个孩子上学，她应该对此有所了解。她也应该听到整个故事，通过这个时间。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla found Mrs. Lynde knitting quilts as industriously and cheerfully as usual.
paragraphs.zh: 马里拉发现林德太太像往常一样勤奋、愉快地织被子。

paragraphs.en: "I suppose you know what I've come about," she said, a little shamefacedly.
paragraphs.zh: “我想你知道我是怎么来的，”她有点羞愧地说。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel nodded.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人点点头。

paragraphs.en: "About Anne's fuss in school, I reckon," she said. "Tillie Boulter was in on her way home from school and told me about it." "I don't know what to do with her," said Marilla. "She declares she won't go back to school. I never saw a child so worked up. I've been expecting trouble ever since she started to school. I knew things were going too smooth to last. She's so high strung. What would you advise, Rachel?"
paragraphs.zh: “我想是安妮在学校里大惊小怪的原因，”她说。 “蒂莉·博尔特在放学回家的路上告诉了我这件事。” “我不知道该怎么处置她，”玛丽拉说。 “她宣称她不会再回学校了。我从来没有见过一个孩子这么激动。自从她开始上学以来，我就一直期待着会有麻烦。我知道事情进展得太顺利，不会持续太久。她太紧张了。你有什么建议，雷切尔？”

paragraphs.en: "Well, since you've asked my advice, Marilla," said Mrs. Lynde amiably—Mrs. Lynde dearly loved to be asked for advice—"I'd just humor her a little at first, that's what I'd do. It's my belief that Mr. Phillips was in the wrong. Of course, it doesn't do to say so to the children, you know. And of course he did right to punish her yesterday for giving way to temper. But today it was different. The others who were late should have been punished as well as Anne, that's what. And I don't believe in making the girls sit with the boys for punishment. It isn't modest. Tillie Boulter was real indignant. She took Anne's part right through and said all the scholars did too. Anne seems real popular among them, somehow. I never thought she'd take with them so well."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，既然你征求了我的意见，玛丽拉，”林德太太和蔼可亲地说。林德非常喜欢别人征求意见——“一开始我只是迁就她一点，这就是我会做的。我相信菲利普斯先生错了。当然，对孩子们这么说是不行的，你知道。当然，他昨天因为她发脾气而惩罚她是对的。但今天不同了。其他迟到的人应该像安妮一样受到惩罚，就是这样。我不相信让女孩们和男孩们坐在一起接受惩罚，蒂莉·博尔特真的很愤怒，她说安妮似乎也很受他们欢迎，不知怎的，我没想到她会这么好。”

paragraphs.en: "Then you really think I'd better let her stay home," said Marilla in amazement.
paragraphs.zh: “那你真的认为我最好让她呆在家里，”玛丽拉惊讶地说。

paragraphs.en: "Yes. That is I wouldn't say school to her again until she said it herself. Depend upon it, Marilla, she'll cool off in a week or so and be ready enough to go back of her own accord, that's what, while, if you were to make her go back right off, dear knows what freak or tantrum she'd take next and make more trouble than ever. The less fuss made the better, in my opinion. She won't miss much by not going to school, as far as THAT goes. Mr. Phillips isn't any good at all as a teacher. The order he keeps is scandalous, that's what, and he neglects the young fry and puts all his time on those big scholars he's getting ready for Queen's. He'd never have got the school for another year if his uncle hadn't been a trustee—THE trustee, for he just leads the other two around by the nose, that's what. I declare, I don't know what education in this Island is coming to."
paragraphs.zh: “是的。就是说，除非她自己说出来，否则我不会再对她说上学了。靠吧，玛丽拉，一周左右她就会冷静下来，准备好自己回去，就是这样，而如果你让她马上回去，亲爱的知道她接下来会发什么脾气或发脾气，并制造出比以前更多的麻烦。在我看来，越少大惊小怪越好。只要她不去上学，她就不会错过太多。菲利普斯先生作为一名老师，他所遵守的秩序是可耻的，就是这样，他忽视了年轻的鱼儿，把所有的时间都花在了那些为进入女王大学做准备的大学者身上，如果他的叔叔不是受托人——受托人，他就不可能再上这所学校了，因为他只是牵着另外两个人的鼻子走，这就是我声明的，我不知道这个岛上的教育将会发生什么。到。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Rachel shook her head, as much as to say if she were only at the head of the educational system of the Province things would be much better managed.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔夫人摇摇头，似乎在说，如果她只是省教育系统的负责人，事情会管理得更好。

paragraphs.en: Marilla took Mrs. Rachel's advice and not another word was said to Anne about going back to school. She learned her lessons at home, did her chores, and played with Diana in the chilly purple autumn twilights; but when she met Gilbert Blythe on the road or encountered him in Sunday school she passed him by with an icy contempt that was no whit thawed by his evident desire to appease her. Even Diana's efforts as a peacemaker were of no avail. Anne had evidently made up her mind to hate Gilbert Blythe to the end of life.
paragraphs.zh: 马里拉采纳了雷切尔夫人的建议，没有再对安妮说要回学校。她在家学习功课，做家务，并在寒冷的紫色秋暮中与戴安娜一起玩耍。但当她在路上遇到吉尔伯特·布莱斯或在主日学校遇到他时，她带着冰冷的蔑视从他身边走过，但他显然想安抚她，这种蔑视丝毫没有融化。就连戴安娜作为和事佬的努力也无济于事。安妮显然已经下定决心要恨吉尔伯特·布莱斯直至生命的尽头。

paragraphs.en: As much as she hated Gilbert, however, did she love Diana, with all the love of her passionate little heart, equally intense in its likes and dislikes. One evening Marilla, coming in from the orchard with a basket of apples, found Anne sitting along by the east window in the twilight, crying bitterly.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，尽管她恨吉尔伯特，但她也爱戴安娜，用她那颗充满激情的小心来爱她，爱和不爱同样强烈。一天晚上，玛丽拉提着一篮子苹果从果园回来，发现安妮在暮色中坐在东窗边痛哭。

paragraphs.en: "Whatever's the matter now, Anne?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “现在怎么样了，安妮？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: "It's about Diana," sobbed Anne luxuriously. "I love Diana so, Marilla. I cannot ever live without her. But I know very well when we grow up that Diana will get married and go away and leave me. And oh, what shall I do? I hate her husband—I just hate him furiously. I've been imagining it all out—the wedding and everything—Diana dressed in snowy garments, with a veil, and looking as beautiful and regal as a queen; and me the bridesmaid, with a lovely dress too, and puffed sleeves, but with a breaking heart hid beneath my smiling face. And then bidding Diana goodbye-e-e—" Here Anne broke down entirely and wept with increasing bitterness.
paragraphs.zh: “是关于戴安娜的事，”安妮奢华地抽泣着。 “我非常爱戴安娜，玛丽拉。没有她我就活不下去。但我很清楚，当我们长大后，戴安娜就会结婚，离开我，离开我。哦，我该怎么办？我恨她的丈夫——我简直是恨得要命。我一直在想象这一切——婚礼和一切——戴安娜穿着雪白的衣服，戴着面纱，看起来像女王一样美丽而高贵；而我是伴娘，也穿着漂亮的衣服，袖子鼓起，但在我的笑脸下隐藏着一颗破碎的心，然后向戴安娜告别——”说到这里，安妮完全崩溃了，哭得越来越痛苦。

paragraphs.en: Marilla turned quickly away to hide her twitching face; but it was no use; she collapsed on the nearest chair and burst into such a hearty and unusual peal of laughter that Matthew, crossing the yard outside, halted in amazement. When had he heard Marilla laugh like that before?
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉迅速转过身来隐藏她抽搐的脸。但没有用；她倒在最近的一张椅子上，爆发出一阵热烈而不同寻常的笑声，马修穿过外面的院子，惊讶地停了下来。他什么时候听过玛丽拉这样笑过？

paragraphs.en: "Well, Anne Shirley," said Marilla as soon as she could speak, "if you must borrow trouble, for pity's sake borrow it handier home. I should think you had an imagination, sure enough."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，安妮·雪莉，”玛丽拉一会说话就说道，“如果你一定要借麻烦的话，看在怜悯的份上，借个方便一点的回家吧。我想你肯定有想象力。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XVI. Diana Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 16 章：戴安娜受邀喝茶的悲剧

paragraphs.en: October was a beautiful month at Green Gables, when the birches in the hollow turned as golden as sunshine and the maples behind the orchard were royal crimson and the wild cherry trees along the lane put on the loveliest shades of dark red and bronzy green, while the fields sunned themselves in aftermaths.
paragraphs.zh: 十月对绿山墙来说是一个美丽的月份，山谷中的白桦树变成了阳光般的金色，果园后面的枫树呈现出高贵的深红色，小巷两旁的野樱桃树呈现出最可爱的深红色和青铜绿色，而田野则在余波中晒着太阳。

paragraphs.en: Anne reveled in the world of color about her.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮陶醉于她周围的色彩世界。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla," she exclaimed one Saturday morning, coming dancing in with her arms full of gorgeous boughs, "I'm so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers. It would be terrible if we just skipped from September to November, wouldn't it? Look at these maple branches. Don't they give you a thrill—several thrills? I'm going to decorate my room with them."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，”一个星期六的早晨，她抱着满是美丽树枝的舞蹈走进来，大声说道，“我很高兴我生活在一个有十月的世界。如果我们直接从九月跳到十一月，那就太可怕了，不是吗？看看这些枫树枝。它们难道不会给你带来刺激吗？我要用它们来装饰我的房间。”

paragraphs.en: "Messy things," said Marilla, whose aesthetic sense was not noticeably developed. "You clutter up your room entirely too much with out-of-doors stuff, Anne. Bedrooms were made to sleep in."
paragraphs.zh: “乱七八糟的东西，”玛丽拉说，她的审美意识还没有明显发展。 “安妮，你把你的房间弄得太多户外用品了。卧室是用来睡觉的。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, and dream in too, Marilla. And you know one can dream so much better in a room where there are pretty things. I'm going to put these boughs in the old blue jug and set them on my table."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，还有梦想，玛丽拉。你知道，在一个有漂亮东西的房间里，一个人可以做更好的梦。我要把这些树枝放在旧的蓝色罐子里，然后把它们放在我的桌子上。”

paragraphs.en: "Mind you don't drop leaves all over the stairs then. I'm going on a meeting of the Aid Society at Carmody this afternoon, Anne, and I won't likely be home before dark. You'll have to get Matthew and Jerry their supper, so mind you don't forget to put the tea to draw until you sit down at the table as you did last time."
paragraphs.zh: “那你要小心，不要把树叶掉在楼梯上。安妮，今天下午我要去卡莫迪参加一个援助协会的会议，天黑之前我不太可能回家。你得给马修和杰瑞准备晚饭，所以请注意，在你坐到桌边之前，不要忘记把茶倒好，就像上次那样。”

paragraphs.en: "It was dreadful of me to forget," said Anne apologetically, "but that was the afternoon I was trying to think of a name for Violet Vale and it crowded other things out. Matthew was so good. He never scolded a bit. He put the tea down himself and said we could wait awhile as well as not. And I told him a lovely fairy story while we were waiting, so he didn't find the time long at all. It was a beautiful fairy story, Marilla. I forgot the end of it, so I made up an end for it myself and Matthew said he couldn't tell where the join came in."
paragraphs.zh: “我很害怕忘记，”安妮抱歉地说，“但那天下午，我正想给紫罗兰谷起个名字，结果把其他事情都排挤掉了。马修太棒了。他从来不骂人。他自己把茶放下，说我们可以等一会儿，也可以不等。在我们等待的时候，我给他讲了一个可爱的童话故事，所以他根本没有花很长时间。这是一个美丽的童话故事，玛丽拉。我忘了。”结束了，所以我自己给它做了一个结束，马修说他不知道连接是从哪里来的。”

paragraphs.en: "Matthew would think it all right, Anne, if you took a notion to get up and have dinner in the middle of the night. But you keep your wits about you this time. And—I don't really know if I'm doing right—it may make you more addlepated than ever—but you can ask Diana to come over and spend the afternoon with you and have tea here."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，如果你想在半夜起床吃晚饭的话，马修会认为没问题。不过这次你要保持理智。而且——我真的不知道我做得对不对——这可能会让你比以前更迷糊——不过你可以请戴安娜过来和你一起度过一个下午，在这里喝茶。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla!" Anne clasped her hands. "How perfectly lovely! You ARE able to imagine things after all or else you'd never have understood how I've longed for that very thing. It will seem so nice and grown-uppish. No fear of my forgetting to put the tea to draw when I have company. Oh, Marilla, can I use the rosebud spray tea set?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉！”安妮双手合十。 “太可爱了！你毕竟能够想象事情，否则你永远不会明白我是多么渴望那件事。它会显得那么美好，那么成熟。不用担心我在有人陪伴的时候忘记放茶来泡。哦，玛丽拉，我可以使用玫瑰花蕾喷雾茶具吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No, indeed! The rosebud tea set! Well, what next? You know I never use that except for the minister or the Aids. You'll put down the old brown tea set. But you can open the little yellow crock of cherry preserves. It's time it was being used anyhow—I believe it's beginning to work. And you can cut some fruit cake and have some of the cookies and snaps."
paragraphs.zh: “不，确实如此！玫瑰花蕾茶具！好吧，接下来怎么办？你知道，除了牧师或艾滋，我从来不使用它。你会放下旧的棕色茶具。但是你可以打开装樱桃蜜饯的黄色小罐子。无论如何，现在是时候使用它了——我相信它开始起作用了。你可以切一些水果蛋糕，吃一些饼干和脆饼。”

paragraphs.en: "I can just imagine myself sitting down at the head of the table and pouring out the tea," said Anne, shutting her eyes ecstatically. "And asking Diana if she takes sugar! I know she doesn't but of course I'll ask her just as if I didn't know. And then pressing her to take another piece of fruit cake and another helping of preserves. Oh, Marilla, it's a wonderful sensation just to think of it. Can I take her into the spare room to lay off her hat when she comes? And then into the parlor to sit?"
paragraphs.zh: “我可以想象自己坐在桌首，倒茶，”安妮欣喜若狂地闭上眼睛说道。 “然后问戴安娜是否吃糖！我知道她不吃，但我当然会问她，就好像我不知道一样。然后催促她再拿一块水果蛋糕和一份蜜饯。哦，玛丽拉，光是想想就感觉棒极了。当她来的时候，我可以带她到空房间脱掉帽子吗？然后到客厅坐下？”

paragraphs.en: "No. The sitting room will do for you and your company. But there's a bottle half full of raspberry cordial that was left over from the church social the other night. It's on the second shelf of the sitting-room closet and you and Diana can have it if you like, and a cooky to eat with it along in the afternoon, for I daresay Matthew'll be late coming in to tea since he's hauling potatoes to the vessel."
paragraphs.zh: “不。客厅对你和你的公司来说就足够了。但是有一瓶半满的覆盆子甜酒，是那天晚上教堂社交活动留下的。它在客厅壁橱的第二个架子上，如果你愿意的话，你和戴安娜可以拿走它，还有下午可以一起吃的饼干，因为我敢说马修会迟到，因为他正在把土豆拖到船上。”

paragraphs.en: Anne flew down to the hollow, past the Dryad's Bubble and up the spruce path to Orchard Slope, to ask Diana to tea. As a result just after Marilla had driven off to Carmody, Diana came over, dressed in HER second-best dress and looking exactly as it is proper to look when asked out to tea. At other times she was wont to run into the kitchen without knocking; but now she knocked primly at the front door. And when Anne, dressed in her second best, as primly opened it, both little girls shook hands as gravely as if they had never met before. This unnatural solemnity lasted until after Diana had been taken to the east gable to lay off her hat and then had sat for ten minutes in the sitting room, toes in position.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮飞下山谷，经过树妖泡泡，沿着云杉小径来到果园坡，请戴安娜喝茶。结果，就在玛丽拉开车去卡莫迪之后，戴安娜就过来了，她穿着她第二好的衣服，看起来就像被邀请出去喝茶时的样子一样。其他时候，她习惯不敲门就跑进厨房。但现在她一本正经地敲了敲前门。当安妮穿着她第二好的衣服，一本正经地打开门时，两个小女孩严肃地握手，就好像她们以前从未见过面一样。这种不自然的庄严一直持续到戴安娜被带到东山墙脱下帽子，然后在客厅里坐了十分钟，脚趾就位。

paragraphs.en: "How is your mother?" inquired Anne politely, just as if she had not seen Mrs. Barry picking apples that morning in excellent health and spirits.
paragraphs.zh: “你妈妈好吗？”安妮礼貌地问道，就好像她没有看到巴里夫人那天早上摘苹果时身体健康、精神抖擞一样。

paragraphs.en: "She is very well, thank you. I suppose Mr. Cuthbert is hauling potatoes to the LILY SANDS this afternoon, is he?" said Diana, who had ridden down to Mr. Harmon Andrews's that morning in Matthew's cart.
paragraphs.zh: “她很好，谢谢你。我想库斯伯特先生今天下午正在把土豆拖到百合沙滩上，是吗？”戴安娜说，她那天早上坐着马修的马车去了哈蒙·安德鲁斯先生家。

paragraphs.en: "Yes. Our potato crop is very good this year. I hope your father's crop is good too."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，今年我们的土豆收成很好。希望你父亲的收成也很好。”

paragraphs.en: "It is fairly good, thank you. Have you picked many of your apples yet?"
paragraphs.zh: “还不错，谢谢。你的苹果摘完了吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, ever so many," said Anne forgetting to be dignified and jumping up quickly. "Let's go out to the orchard and get some of the Red Sweetings, Diana. Marilla says we can have all that are left on the tree. Marilla is a very generous woman. She said we could have fruit cake and cherry preserves for tea. But it isn't good manners to tell your company what you are going to give them to eat, so I won't tell you what she said we could have to drink. Only it begins with an R and a C and it's bright red color. I love bright red drinks, don't you? They taste twice as good as any other color."
paragraphs.zh: “噢，这么多。”安妮忘记了尊严，飞快地跳了起来。 “戴安娜，我们去果园买一些红色糖果。玛丽拉说我们可以吃掉树上剩下的所有东西。玛丽拉是个非常慷慨的女人。她说我们可以吃水果蛋糕和樱桃蜜饯当茶。但是告诉你的公司你要给他们吃什么是不礼貌的，所以我不会告诉你她说我们可以喝什么。只是它以 R 和 C 开头，而且是鲜红色的。我你喜欢鲜红色的饮料，不是吗？它们的味道是其他颜色的两倍。”

paragraphs.en: The orchard, with its great sweeping boughs that bent to the ground with fruit, proved so delightful that the little girls spent most of the afternoon in it, sitting in a grassy corner where the frost had spared the green and the mellow autumn sunshine lingered warmly, eating apples and talking as hard as they could. Diana had much to tell Anne of what went on in school. She had to sit with Gertie Pye and she hated it; Gertie squeaked her pencil all the time and it just made her—Diana's—blood run cold; Ruby Gillis had charmed all her warts away, true's you live, with a magic pebble that old Mary Joe from the Creek gave her. You had to rub the warts with the pebble and then throw it away over your left shoulder at the time of the new moon and the warts would all go. Charlie Sloane's name was written up with Em White's on the porch wall and Em White was AWFUL MAD about it; Sam Boulter had "sassed" Mr. Phillips in class and Mr. Phillips whipped him and Sam's father came down to the school and dared Mr. Phillips to lay a hand on one of his children again; and Mattie Andrews had a new red hood and a blue crossover with tassels on it and the airs she put on about it were perfectly sickening; and Lizzie Wright didn't speak to Mamie Wilson because Mamie Wilson's grown-up sister had cut out Lizzie Wright's grown-up sister with her beau; and everybody missed Anne so and wished she's come to school again; and Gilbert Blythe—
paragraphs.zh: 果园里硕大的树枝垂到地上，结满了果实，果园里的果园非常令人愉快，小女孩们整个下午的大部分时间都在里面度过，她们坐在草地的一角，霜冻没有绿意，柔和的秋日阳光温暖地萦绕着，一边吃着苹果，一边使劲地说话。戴安娜有很多事情要告诉安妮学校里发生的事情。她不得不和格蒂·派伊坐在一起，但她讨厌这样。格蒂的铅笔总是发出吱吱的声音，这让她——戴安娜——浑身发冷。鲁比·吉利斯用来自小溪的老玛丽·乔送给她的一块神奇的鹅卵石，把她所有的疣都祛除了，你还活着。你必须用鹅卵石擦疣，然后在新月的时候把它扔到左肩上，疣就会消失。查理·斯隆的名字和艾姆·怀特的名字一起写在门廊的墙上，艾姆·怀特对此非常生气；萨姆·博尔特在课堂上“辱骂”了菲利普斯先生，菲利普斯先生鞭打了他，萨姆的父亲来到学校，挑衅菲利普斯先生再次对他的一个孩子下手；玛蒂·安德鲁斯 (Mattie Andrews) 戴着一顶新的红色兜帽，穿着一件带有流苏的蓝色交叉背心，她的神态非常令人作呕。莉齐·赖特（Lizzie Wright）没有和玛米·威尔逊（Mamie Wilson）说话，因为玛米·威尔逊（Mamie Wilson）成年的姐姐已经把莉齐·赖特（Lizzie Wright）成年的妹妹和她的男友分开了；每个人都非常想念安妮，并希望她能再次回到学校；和吉尔伯特·布莱斯——

paragraphs.en: But Anne didn't want to hear about Gilbert Blythe. She jumped up hurriedly and said suppose they go in and have some raspberry cordial.
paragraphs.zh: 但安妮不想听到吉尔伯特·布莱斯的事。她急忙跳起来说，咱们进去喝点覆盆子甜酒吧。

paragraphs.en: Anne looked on the second shelf of the room pantry but there was no bottle of raspberry cordial there. Search revealed it away back on the top shelf. Anne put it on a tray and set it on the table with a tumbler.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮查看了房间食品储藏室的第二个架子，但那里没有一瓶覆盆子甜酒。搜索后发现它又回到了最上面的架子上。安妮把它放在托盘上，然后用玻璃杯放在桌子上。

paragraphs.en: "Now, please help yourself, Diana," she said politely. "I don't believe I'll have any just now. I don't feel as if I wanted any after all those apples."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，请自助，戴安娜，”她礼貌地说。 “我不相信我现在会得到任何东西。在那么多苹果之后，我觉得我不再想要任何东西了。”

paragraphs.en: Diana poured herself out a tumblerful, looked at its bright-red hue admiringly, and then sipped it daintily.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜给自己倒了一杯，钦佩地看着它鲜红的颜色，然后优雅地抿了一口。

paragraphs.en: "That's awfully nice raspberry cordial, Anne," she said. "I didn't know raspberry cordial was so nice."
paragraphs.zh: “这是非常好的覆盆子甜酒，安妮，”她说。 “我不知道覆盆子甜酒这么好喝。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm real glad you like it. Take as much as you want. I'm going to run out and stir the fire up. There are so many responsibilities on a person's mind when they're keeping house, isn't there?"
paragraphs.zh: “我很高兴你喜欢它。你想要多少就拿多少。我要跑出去把火煽起来。一个人在看家的时候，心里有很多责任，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: When Anne came back from the kitchen Diana was drinking her second glassful of cordial; and, being entreated thereto by Anne, she offered no particular objection to the drinking of a third. The tumblerfuls were generous ones and the raspberry cordial was certainly very nice.
paragraphs.zh: 当安妮从厨房回来时，戴安娜正在喝第二杯甜酒。在安妮的恳求下，她并没有特别反对第三个人喝酒。玻璃杯的量很大，覆盆子甜酒确实非常好喝。

paragraphs.en: "The nicest I ever drank," said Diana. "It's ever so much nicer than Mrs. Lynde's, although she brags of hers so much. It doesn't taste a bit like hers."
paragraphs.zh: “这是我喝过的最好喝的，”戴安娜说。 “它比林德太太的好吃多了，尽管她总是吹嘘自己的。味道一点也不像她的。”

paragraphs.en: "I should think Marilla's raspberry cordial would prob'ly be much nicer than Mrs. Lynde's," said Anne loyally. "Marilla is a famous cook. She is trying to teach me to cook but I assure you, Diana, it is uphill work. There's so little scope for imagination in cookery. You just have to go by rules. The last time I made a cake I forgot to put the flour in. I was thinking the loveliest story about you and me, Diana. I thought you were desperately ill with smallpox and everybody deserted you, but I went boldly to your bedside and nursed you back to life; and then I took the smallpox and died and I was buried under those poplar trees in the graveyard and you planted a rosebush by my grave and watered it with your tears; and you never, never forgot the friend of your youth who sacrificed her life for you. Oh, it was such a pathetic tale, Diana. The tears just rained down over my cheeks while I mixed the cake. But I forgot the flour and the cake was a dismal failure. Flour is so essential to cakes, you know. Marilla was very cross and I don't wonder. I'm a great trial to her. She was terribly mortified about the pudding sauce last week. We had a plum pudding for dinner on Tuesday and there was half the pudding and a pitcherful of sauce left over. Marilla said there was enough for another dinner and told me to set it on the pantry shelf and cover it. I meant to cover it just as much as could be, Diana, but when I carried it in I was imagining I was a nun—of course I'm a Protestant but I imagined I was a Catholic—taking the veil to bury a broken heart in cloistered seclusion; and I forgot all about covering the pudding sauce. I thought of it next morning and ran to the pantry. Diana, fancy if you can my extreme horror at finding a mouse drowned in that pudding sauce! I lifted the mouse out with a spoon and threw it out in the yard and then I washed the spoon in three waters. Marilla was out milking and I fully intended to ask her when she came in if I'd give the sauce to the pigs; but when she did come in I was imagining that I was a frost fairy going through the woods turning the trees red and yellow, whichever they wanted to be, so I never thought about the pudding sauce again and Marilla sent me out to pick apples. Well, Mr. and Mrs. Chester Ross from Spencervale came here that morning. You know they are very stylish people, especially Mrs. Chester Ross. When Marilla called me in dinner was all ready and everybody was at the table. I tried to be as polite and dignified as I could be, for I wanted Mrs. Chester Ross to think I was a ladylike little girl even if I wasn't pretty. Everything went right until I saw Marilla coming with the plum pudding in one hand and the pitcher of pudding sauce WARMED UP, in the other. Diana, that was a terrible moment. I remembered everything and I just stood up in my place and shrieked out 'Marilla, you mustn't use that pudding sauce. There was a mouse drowned in it. I forgot to tell you before.' Oh, Diana, I shall never forget that awful moment if I live to be a hundred. Mrs. Chester Ross just LOOKED at me and I thought I would sink through the floor with mortification. She is such a perfect housekeeper and fancy what she must have thought of us. Marilla turned red as fire but she never said a word—then. She just carried that sauce and pudding out and brought in some strawberry preserves. She even offered me some, but I couldn't swallow a mouthful. It was like heaping coals of fire on my head. After Mrs. Chester Ross went away, Marilla gave me a dreadful scolding. Why, Diana, what is the matter?"
paragraphs.zh: “我想玛丽拉的覆盆子甜酒可能比林德夫人的好得多，”安妮忠诚地说。 “玛丽拉是一位著名的厨师。她想教我做饭，但我向你保证，戴安娜，这是一项艰巨的工作。烹饪方面的想象力太小了。你只需要遵守规则。上次我做蛋糕时，我忘了放面粉。我在想关于你和我的最可爱的故事，戴安娜。我以为你得了天花，每个人都抛弃了你，但我大胆地走到你的床边，护理你，让你起死回生；然后我得了天花，死了，被埋在墓地的白杨树下，你在我的坟墓旁种了一棵玫瑰花，并用你的眼泪浇灌它；哦，这真是一个可悲的故事，戴安娜，当我搅拌蛋糕时，我忘记了面粉，而面粉对蛋糕来说是非常重要的。我很生气，我不奇怪她对布丁酱感到非常羞愧，我们周二的晚餐有一半的布丁和一壶酱，玛丽拉说还剩下足够的东西，并告诉我把它放在食品储藏室的架子上并盖上它，戴安娜。我是一名修女——当然我是一名新教徒，但我想象自己是一名天主教徒——带着面纱将一颗破碎的心埋葬在与世隔绝的地方；第二天早上我忘记了盖上布丁酱，你能想象一下，我发现一只老鼠淹死在布丁酱里，我感到非常恐惧！出去挤奶时，我完全想问她，当她进来时，我是否愿意把酱汁给猪吃；但当她进来时，我想象着我是一位霜仙子，将树木变成红色和黄色，无论他们想要什么，所以我再也没有想过布丁酱，玛丽拉派我出去摘苹果。切斯特·罗斯叫我去吃晚饭时，我尽量保持礼貌和端庄，因为我想让切斯特·罗斯夫人认为我是一个淑女般的小女孩，即使我不漂亮。我的住处尖叫道：“玛丽拉，你不能用那个布丁酱。我之前忘了告诉你，里面淹死了一只老鼠。”哦，戴安娜，如果我活到一百岁，我永远不会忘记那个可怕的时刻。切斯特·罗斯夫人只是看着我，我想我会羞愧地沉入地板。她是一位完美的管家，她一定对我们有什么看法。玛丽拉的脸涨得通红，但她什么也没说——然后。她只是把酱汁和布丁搬了出去，还带了一些草莓蜜饯进来。她甚至给了我一些，但我一口都咽不下去。这就像把炭堆堆在我的头上。切斯特·罗斯夫人走后，玛丽拉狠狠地责骂了我一顿。为什么，黛安娜，出什么事了？”

paragraphs.en: Diana had stood up very unsteadily; then she sat down again, putting her hands to her head.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜站起来时摇摇晃晃。然后她又坐下来，双手捂着头。
