paragraphs.en: "I'm—I'm awful sick," she said, a little thickly. "I—I—must go right home."
paragraphs.zh: “我——我病得很厉害，”她声音有点粗哑地说。 “我——我——必须马上回家。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, you mustn't dream of going home without your tea," cried Anne in distress. "I'll get it right off—I'll go and put the tea down this very minute."
paragraphs.zh: “噢，你别想不喝茶就回家。”安妮痛苦地喊道。 “我马上去拿——我马上就去把茶放下。”

paragraphs.en: "I must go home," repeated Diana, stupidly but determinedly.
paragraphs.zh: “我必须回家，”戴安娜重复道，愚蠢但坚定。

paragraphs.en: "Let me get you a lunch anyhow," implored Anne. "Let me give you a bit of fruit cake and some of the cherry preserves. Lie down on the sofa for a little while and you'll be better. Where do you feel bad?"
paragraphs.zh: “无论如何，让我给你弄一顿午餐吧。”安妮恳求道。 “给你吃点水果蛋糕和一些樱桃蜜饯吧，在沙发上躺一会儿就会好一些了，你哪里不舒服了？”

paragraphs.en: "I must go home," said Diana, and that was all she would say. In vain Anne pleaded.
paragraphs.zh: “我必须回家了，”戴安娜说，这就是她只会说的话。安妮徒劳地恳求。

paragraphs.en: "I never heard of company going home without tea," she mourned. "Oh, Diana, do you suppose that it's possible you're really taking the smallpox? If you are I'll go and nurse you, you can depend on that. I'll never forsake you. But I do wish you'd stay till after tea. Where do you feel bad?"
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有听说过有人不喝茶就回家，”她哀悼道。 “哦，黛安娜，你认为你真的可能得了天花吗？如果是的话，我会去护理你，你可以放心。我永远不会抛弃你。但我真希望你能留下来，直到喝完茶后。你哪里不舒服吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I'm awful dizzy," said Diana.
paragraphs.zh: “我头晕得很厉害，”戴安娜说。

paragraphs.en: And indeed, she walked very dizzily. Anne, with tears of disappointment in her eyes, got Diana's hat and went with her as far as the Barry yard fence. Then she wept all the way back to Green Gables, where she sorrowfully put the remainder of the raspberry cordial back into the pantry and got tea ready for Matthew and Jerry, with all the zest gone out of the performance.
paragraphs.zh: 确实，她走得非常头晕。安妮眼里含着失望的泪水，拿起戴安娜的帽子，跟着她一直走到巴里院子的栅栏前。然后她一路哭着回到绿山墙，悲伤地把剩下的覆盆子甜酒放回食品储藏室，为马修和杰瑞准备茶，表演的所有热情都消失了。

paragraphs.en: The next day was Sunday and as the rain poured down in torrents from dawn till dusk Anne did not stir abroad from Green Gables. Monday afternoon Marilla sent her down to Mrs. Lynde's on an errand. In a very short space of time Anne came flying back up the lane with tears rolling down her cheeks. Into the kitchen she dashed and flung herself face downward on the sofa in an agony.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天是星期天，从黎明到黄昏，倾盆大雨倾盆而下，安妮在绿山墙外一动不动。星期一下午，玛丽拉派她去林德太太家办事。不久之后，安妮飞快地飞回小巷，泪水从她的脸颊上滚落下来。她冲进厨房，痛苦地脸朝下倒在沙发上。

paragraphs.en: "Whatever has gone wrong now, Anne?" queried Marilla in doubt and dismay. "I do hope you haven't gone and been saucy to Mrs. Lynde again."
paragraphs.zh: “现在出了什么问题吗，安妮？”玛丽拉疑惑而沮丧地问道。 “我真希望你没有再去对林德太太调皮了。”

paragraphs.en: No answer from Anne save more tears and stormier sobs!
paragraphs.zh: 安妮没有回答，除了更多的眼泪和更大的抽泣！

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, when I ask you a question I want to be answered. Sit right up this very minute and tell me what you are crying about."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，当我问你一个问题时，我希望得到答案。现在就坐起来，告诉我你在哭什么。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sat up, tragedy personified.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮坐了起来，一副悲剧的化身。

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Lynde was up to see Mrs. Barry today and Mrs. Barry was in an awful state," she wailed. "She says that I set Diana DRUNK Saturday and sent her home in a disgraceful condition. And she says I must be a thoroughly bad, wicked little girl and she's never, never going to let Diana play with me again. Oh, Marilla, I'm just overcome with woe."
paragraphs.zh: “林德夫人今天去看望巴里夫人，巴里夫人的情况很糟糕，”她哭着说。 “她说我星期六让戴安娜喝醉了，然后让她在可耻的情况下回家。她说我一定是一个彻底坏、邪恶的小女孩，她永远不会再让戴安娜和我一起玩了。哦，玛丽拉，我只是被悲伤压倒了。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla stared in blank amazement.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉茫然地惊讶地看着。

paragraphs.en: "Set Diana drunk!" she said when she found her voice. "Anne are you or Mrs. Barry crazy? What on earth did you give her?"
paragraphs.zh: “让戴安娜喝醉！”当她找到自己的声音时，她说道。 “安妮，你还是巴里夫人疯了？你到底给了她什么？”

paragraphs.en: "Not a thing but raspberry cordial," sobbed Anne. "I never thought raspberry cordial would set people drunk, Marilla—not even if they drank three big tumblerfuls as Diana did. Oh, it sounds so—so—like Mrs. Thomas's husband! But I didn't mean to set her drunk."
paragraphs.zh: “什么都不是，只是覆盆子甜酒。”安妮抽泣着说。 “我从来没想过覆盆子甜酒会让人们喝醉，玛丽拉——即使他们像戴安娜那样喝了三大杯也不会。哦，听起来很——很——像托马斯夫人的丈夫！但我不是故意让她喝醉的。”

paragraphs.en: "Drunk fiddlesticks!" said Marilla, marching to the sitting room pantry. There on the shelf was a bottle which she at once recognized as one containing some of her three-year-old homemade currant wine for which she was celebrated in Avonlea, although certain of the stricter sort, Mrs. Barry among them, disapproved strongly of it. And at the same time Marilla recollected that she had put the bottle of raspberry cordial down in the cellar instead of in the pantry as she had told Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “喝醉了的小提琴手！”玛丽拉一边说着，一边朝客厅的食品储藏室走去。架子上有一瓶她立刻认出，里面装着她三年前自制的醋栗酒，她因此而在埃文利闻名，尽管巴里夫人等某些更严格的人强烈反对这种酒。与此同时，玛丽拉想起她把那瓶覆盆子甜酒放在地窖里，而不是像她告诉安妮的那样放在食品储藏室里。

paragraphs.en: She went back to the kitchen with the wine bottle in her hand. Her face was twitching in spite of herself.
paragraphs.zh: 她手里拿着酒瓶，回到了厨房。她的脸不由自主地抽搐起来。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, you certainly have a genius for getting into trouble. You went and gave Diana currant wine instead of raspberry cordial. Didn't you know the difference yourself?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你真是个惹麻烦的天才。你给戴安娜喝的是醋栗酒，而不是覆盆子甜酒。你自己不知道其中的区别吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I never tasted it," said Anne. "I thought it was the cordial. I meant to be so—so—hospitable. Diana got awfully sick and had to go home. Mrs. Barry told Mrs. Lynde she was simply dead drunk. She just laughed silly-like when her mother asked her what was the matter and went to sleep and slept for hours. Her mother smelled her breath and knew she was drunk. She had a fearful headache all day yesterday. Mrs. Barry is so indignant. She will never believe but what I did it on purpose."
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有尝过，”安妮说。 “我以为是甜酒。我本想如此——如此——热情好客。戴安娜病得很重，不得不回家。巴里夫人告诉林德夫人，她简直喝醉了。当她母亲问她怎么了时，她只是傻笑，然后就睡着了，睡了几个小时。她母亲闻到她的呼吸味，知道她喝醉了。昨天她头痛得厉害。巴里夫人非常愤怒。她永远不会相信但我是故意这么做的。”

paragraphs.en: "I should think she would better punish Diana for being so greedy as to drink three glassfuls of anything," said Marilla shortly. "Why, three of those big glasses would have made her sick even if it had only been cordial. Well, this story will be a nice handle for those folks who are so down on me for making currant wine, although I haven't made any for three years ever since I found out that the minister didn't approve. I just kept that bottle for sickness. There, there, child, don't cry. I can't see as you were to blame although I'm sorry it happened so."
paragraphs.zh: “我认为她最好惩罚戴安娜，因为她贪得无厌，什么都喝了三杯，”玛丽拉简短地说。 “哎呀，即使只是热情的酒，三个大玻璃杯也会让她恶心。好吧，这个故事对于那些因为我酿造醋栗酒而对我如此失望的人来说将是一个很好的句柄，尽管自从我发现部长不批准以来，我已经三年没有酿造过醋栗酒了。我只是为了生病而保留了那瓶酒。好了，好了，孩子，别哭。我不明白你应该受到责备，尽管我很抱歉发生了这样的事情。”

paragraphs.en: "I must cry," said Anne. "My heart is broken. The stars in their courses fight against me, Marilla. Diana and I are parted forever. Oh, Marilla, I little dreamed of this when first we swore our vows of friendship."
paragraphs.zh: “我必须哭，”安妮说。 “我的心都碎了。玛丽拉，星星在他们的道路上与我作斗争。戴安娜和我永远分开了。哦，玛丽拉，当我们第一次宣誓友谊时，我几乎没有想到这一点。”

paragraphs.en: "Don't be foolish, Anne. Mrs. Barry will think better of it when she finds you're not to blame. I suppose she thinks you've done it for a silly joke or something of that sort. You'd best go up this evening and tell her how it was."
paragraphs.zh: “别犯傻了，安妮。当巴里太太发现你不应该受到责备时，她会想得更好。我想她认为你这样做是为了一个愚蠢的笑话或类似的事情。你最好今天晚上上去告诉她是怎么回事。”

paragraphs.en: "My courage fails me at the thought of facing Diana's injured mother," sighed Anne. "I wish you'd go, Marilla. You're so much more dignified than I am. Likely she'd listen to you quicker than to me."
paragraphs.zh: “一想到要面对戴安娜受伤的母亲，我就失去了勇气，”安妮叹了口气。 “我希望你能走，玛丽拉。你比我有尊严得多。她可能会比我更快地听你的。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I will," said Marilla, reflecting that it would probably be the wiser course. "Don't cry any more, Anne. It will be all right."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我会的，”玛丽拉说，她认为这可能是更明智的做法。 “别再哭了，安妮。不会有事的。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla had changed her mind about it being all right by the time she got back from Orchard Slope. Anne was watching for her coming and flew to the porch door to meet her.
paragraphs.zh: 当玛丽拉从果园坡回来时，她改变了主意，认为一切都好。安妮正在等待她的到来，飞奔到门廊门口迎接她。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, I know by your face that it's been no use," she said sorrowfully. "Mrs. Barry won't forgive me?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，从你的表情我就知道这没有用，”她悲伤地说。 “巴里夫人不会原谅我吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Barry indeed!" snapped Marilla. "Of all the unreasonable women I ever saw she's the worst. I told her it was all a mistake and you weren't to blame, but she just simply didn't believe me. And she rubbed it well in about my currant wine and how I'd always said it couldn't have the least effect on anybody. I just told her plainly that currant wine wasn't meant to be drunk three tumblerfuls at a time and that if a child I had to do with was so greedy I'd sober her up with a right good spanking."
paragraphs.zh: “确实是巴里夫人！”玛丽拉厉声说道。 “在我见过的所有不可理喻的女人中，她是最糟糕的。我告诉她这都是个错误，你不应该受到责备，但她就是不相信我。她反复强调了我的醋栗酒，以及我总是说它不会对任何人产生丝毫影响。我只是明确地告诉她，醋栗酒不应该一次喝三杯，如果我养的一个孩子那么贪婪的话我会狠狠地打她屁股，让她清醒过来。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla whisked into the kitchen, grievously disturbed, leaving a very much distracted little soul in the porch behind her. Presently Anne stepped out bareheaded into the chill autumn dusk; very determinedly and steadily she took her way down through the sere clover field over the log bridge and up through the spruce grove, lighted by a pale little moon hanging low over the western woods. Mrs. Barry, coming to the door in answer to a timid knock, found a white-lipped eager-eyed suppliant on the doorstep.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉迅速走进厨房，心神不安，留下一个心烦意乱的小灵魂留在她身后的门廊上。不久，安妮光着头走进寒冷的秋日黄昏。她坚定而坚定地向下走，穿过荒凉的三叶草田，越过独木桥，向上穿过云杉林，一轮苍​​白的小月亮低悬在西边的树林上空，照亮了云杉林。巴里夫人来到门口，听见有人胆怯地敲门，她发现门阶上站着一个白唇、眼神热切的恳求者。

paragraphs.en: Her face hardened. Mrs. Barry was a woman of strong prejudices and dislikes, and her anger was of the cold, sullen sort which is always hardest to overcome. To do her justice, she really believed Anne had made Diana drunk out of sheer malice prepense, and she was honestly anxious to preserve her little daughter from the contamination of further intimacy with such a child.
paragraphs.zh: 她的脸色变得严肃起来。巴里夫人是一个有着强烈偏见和厌恶的女人，她的愤怒是冷酷、阴沉的，总是最难克服的。公平地说，她真的相信安妮让戴安娜喝醉是出于纯粹的恶意预谋，而且她真诚地渴望保护她的小女儿免受与这样一个孩子进一步亲密接触的污染。

paragraphs.en: "What do you want?" she said stiffly.
paragraphs.zh: “你想要什么？”她生硬地说。

paragraphs.en: Anne clasped her hands.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮双手合十。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Mrs. Barry, please forgive me. I did not mean to—to—intoxicate Diana. How could I? Just imagine if you were a poor little orphan girl that kind people had adopted and you had just one bosom friend in all the world. Do you think you would intoxicate her on purpose? I thought it was only raspberry cordial. I was firmly convinced it was raspberry cordial. Oh, please don't say that you won't let Diana play with me any more. If you do you will cover my life with a dark cloud of woe."
paragraphs.zh: “噢，巴里夫人，请原谅我。我不是故意……要……让戴安娜中毒的。我怎么可能？试想一下，如果你是一个被好心人收养的可怜的小孤女，全世界只有一个知音，你以为你会故意让她中毒吗？我以为那只是覆盆子甜酒，我坚信那是覆盆子甜酒。哦，请不要说你不会再让戴安娜和我玩了。如果你这样做，就会给我的生活蒙上一层悲伤的乌云。”

paragraphs.en: This speech which would have softened good Mrs. Lynde's heart in a twinkling, had no effect on Mrs. Barry except to irritate her still more. She was suspicious of Anne's big words and dramatic gestures and imagined that the child was making fun of her. So she said, coldly and cruelly:
paragraphs.zh: 这番话本来可以瞬间软化善良的林德夫人的心，但对巴里夫人却没有任何作用，只是让她更加恼火。她对安妮的豪言壮语和戏剧性的动作表示怀疑，并认为这个孩子是在取笑她。于是她冷酷而残忍地说：

paragraphs.en: "I don't think you are a fit little girl for Diana to associate with. You'd better go home and behave yourself."
paragraphs.zh: “我觉得你不适合戴安娜交往。你最好回家规矩点。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's lips quivered.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的嘴唇颤抖着。

paragraphs.en: "Won't you let me see Diana just once to say farewell?" she implored.
paragraphs.zh: “你不让我见戴安娜一次并告别吗？”她恳求道。

paragraphs.en: "Diana has gone over to Carmody with her father," said Mrs. Barry, going in and shutting the door.
paragraphs.zh: “戴安娜已经和她父亲一起去了卡莫迪，”巴里夫人说着走进去，关上了门。

paragraphs.en: Anne went back to Green Gables calm with despair.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮带着绝望平静地回到了绿山墙。

paragraphs.en: "My last hope is gone," she told Marilla. "I went up and saw Mrs. Barry myself and she treated me very insultingly. Marilla, I do NOT think she is a well-bred woman. There is nothing more to do except to pray and I haven't much hope that that'll do much good because, Marilla, I do not believe that God Himself can do very much with such an obstinate person as Mrs. Barry."
paragraphs.zh: “我最后的希望破灭了，”她告诉玛丽拉。 “我亲自去见了巴里夫人，她对我非常侮辱。玛丽拉，我不认为她是一个有教养的女人。除了祈祷之外，没有什么可做的，我不希望这会有多大好处，因为，玛丽拉，我不相信上帝自己能对像巴里夫人这样固执的人做很多事情。”

paragraphs.en: "Anne, you shouldn't say such things" rebuked Marilla, striving to overcome that unholy tendency to laughter which she was dismayed to find growing upon her. And indeed, when she told the whole story to Matthew that night, she did laugh heartily over Anne's tribulations.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你不应该说这样的话。”玛丽拉责备道，努力克服那种邪恶的笑倾向，她沮丧地发现这种倾向在她身上不断增长。事实上，那天晚上，当她向马修讲述整个故事时，她确实为安妮的磨难而开怀大笑。

paragraphs.en: But when she slipped into the east gable before going to bed and found that Anne had cried herself to sleep an unaccustomed softness crept into her face.
paragraphs.zh: 但当她在睡觉前溜进东山墙时，发现安妮已经哭着睡着了，一种不寻常的温柔爬上了她的脸。

paragraphs.en: "Poor little soul," she murmured, lifting a loose curl of hair from the child's tear-stained face. Then she bent down and kissed the flushed cheek on the pillow.
paragraphs.zh: “可怜的小灵魂，”她低声说道，从孩子泪流满面的脸上撩起一卷松散的头发。然后她弯下腰，吻了吻枕头上泛红的脸颊。

chapters.title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 17 章：生活中的新兴趣

paragraphs.en: The next afternoon Anne, bending over her patchwork at the kitchen window, happened to glance out and beheld Diana down by the Dryad's Bubble beckoning mysteriously. In a trice Anne was out of the house and flying down to the hollow, astonishment and hope struggling in her expressive eyes. But the hope faded when she saw Diana's dejected countenance.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天下午，安妮在厨房的窗户前弯下腰，看着她的拼布作品，碰巧向外瞥了一眼，看到戴安娜在树妖的泡泡旁边神秘地招手。刹那间，安妮走出了房子，飞向了空地，她那双富有​​表情的眼睛里充满了惊讶和希望。但当她看到戴安娜沮丧的表情时，希望破灭了。

paragraphs.en: "Your mother hasn't relented?" she gasped.
paragraphs.zh: “你妈妈还没有松口吗？”她喘着气。

paragraphs.en: Diana shook her head mournfully.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜悲伤地摇摇头。

paragraphs.en: "No; and oh, Anne, she says I'm never to play with you again. I've cried and cried and I told her it wasn't your fault, but it wasn't any use. I had ever such a time coaxing her to let me come down and say good-bye to you. She said I was only to stay ten minutes and she's timing me by the clock."
paragraphs.zh: “不；哦，安妮，她说我再也不会和你一起玩了。我哭了又哭，告诉她这不是你的错，但这没有任何用处。我曾经有过这样的一次，哄她让我下来和你告别。她说我只待十分钟，她按照时钟给我计时。”

paragraphs.en: "Ten minutes isn't very long to say an eternal farewell in," said Anne tearfully. "Oh, Diana, will you promise faithfully never to forget me, the friend of your youth, no matter what dearer friends may caress thee?"
paragraphs.zh: “对于永远的告别来说，十分钟并不算长。”安妮泪流满面地说。 “哦，戴安娜，你能忠实地保证永远不会忘记我，你年轻时的朋友，无论亲爱的朋友如何爱抚你吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Indeed I will," sobbed Diana, "and I'll never have another bosom friend—I don't want to have. I couldn't love anybody as I love you."
paragraphs.zh: “我确实会的，”黛安娜抽泣着，“我再也不会有另一个知心朋友了——我不想有。我不能像爱你那样爱任何人。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Diana," cried Anne, clasping her hands, "do you LOVE me?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，戴安娜，”安妮双手合十喊道，“你爱我吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Why, of course I do. Didn't you know that?"
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，我当然知道。你不知道吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No." Anne drew a long breath. "I thought you LIKED me of course but I never hoped you LOVED me. Why, Diana, I didn't think anybody could love me. Nobody ever has loved me since I can remember. Oh, this is wonderful! It's a ray of light which will forever shine on the darkness of a path severed from thee, Diana. Oh, just say it once again."
paragraphs.zh: “不。”安妮长长地吸了一口气。 “我当然以为你喜欢我，但我从来不希望你爱我。为什么，戴安娜，我不认为有人会爱我。自从我记事起，就没有人爱过我。哦，这太棒了！它就像一束光，将永远照耀在与你隔绝的道路上，戴安娜。哦，再说一遍。”

paragraphs.en: "I love you devotedly, Anne," said Diana stanchly, "and I always will, you may be sure of that."
paragraphs.zh: “我全心全意地爱你，安妮，”戴安娜坚定地说，“我永远都会爱你，你可以确信这一点。”

paragraphs.en: "And I will always love thee, Diana," said Anne, solemnly extending her hand. "In the years to come thy memory will shine like a star over my lonely life, as that last story we read together says. Diana, wilt thou give me a lock of thy jet-black tresses in parting to treasure forevermore?"
paragraphs.zh: “我将永远爱你，戴安娜，”安妮庄严地伸出手说道。 “在未来的岁月里，你的记忆将像星星一样闪耀在我孤独的生活中，正如我们一起读的最后一个故事所说的那样。戴安娜，你愿意在离别时送给我一绺乌黑的长发，让我永远珍藏吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Have you got anything to cut it with?" queried Diana, wiping away the tears which Anne's affecting accents had caused to flow afresh, and returning to practicalities.
paragraphs.zh: “你有什么东西可以用来切它吗？”黛安娜一边问道，一边擦掉因安妮动人的口音而再次流下的泪水，然后回到实际问题上来。

paragraphs.en: "Yes. I've got my patchwork scissors in my apron pocket fortunately," said Anne. She solemnly clipped one of Diana's curls. "Fare thee well, my beloved friend. Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side. But my heart will ever be faithful to thee."
paragraphs.zh: “是的。幸运的是，我的围裙口袋里有我的拼布剪刀，”安妮说。她郑重地剪掉了戴安娜的一头卷发。 “再见了，我亲爱的朋友。从此我们虽然毗邻而居，却像陌生人一样。但我的心永远忠于你。”

paragraphs.en: Anne stood and watched Diana out of sight, mournfully waving her hand to the latter whenever she turned to look back. Then she returned to the house, not a little consoled for the time being by this romantic parting.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站在那里，看着戴安娜消失在视线中，每当她回头看时，她都会悲伤地向后者挥手。然后她回到了家，暂时没有因为这次浪漫的离别而感到一点安慰。

paragraphs.en: "It is all over," she informed Marilla. "I shall never have another friend. I'm really worse off than ever before, for I haven't Katie Maurice and Violetta now. And even if I had it wouldn't be the same. Somehow, little dream girls are not satisfying after a real friend. Diana and I had such an affecting farewell down by the spring. It will be sacred in my memory forever. I used the most pathetic language I could think of and said 'thou' and 'thee.' 'Thou' and 'thee' seem so much more romantic than 'you.' Diana gave me a lock of her hair and I'm going to sew it up in a little bag and wear it around my neck all my life. Please see that it is buried with me, for I don't believe I'll live very long. Perhaps when she sees me lying cold and dead before her Mrs. Barry may feel remorse for what she has done and will let Diana come to my funeral."
paragraphs.zh: “一切都结束了，”她告诉玛丽拉。 “我再也不会有另一个朋友了。我的处境比以前更糟，因为我现在没有了凯蒂·莫里斯和维奥莱塔。即使我有，情况也不会一样。不知何故，梦想中的小女孩在拥有真正的朋友后并不满足。春天的时候，戴安娜和我进行了一场感人至深的告别。这将永远在我的记忆中神圣。我用了我能想到的最可怜的语言，说‘你’和‘你’。 “你”和“你”似乎比“你”浪漫得多。戴安娜给了我一绺头发，我要把它缝在一个小袋子里，一辈子戴在脖子上。请把它和我一起埋葬，因为我不相信我会活很久。也许当她看到我冰冷地死在她面前时，巴里夫人可能会为自己的所作所为感到悔恨，并会让戴安娜参加我的葬礼。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't think there is much fear of your dying of grief as long as you can talk, Anne," said Marilla unsympathetically.
paragraphs.zh: “我认为，只要你能说话，安妮，就不用担心你会因悲伤而死。”玛丽拉冷漠地说。

paragraphs.en: The following Monday Anne surprised Marilla by coming down from her room with her basket of books on her arm and hip and her lips primmed up into a line of determination.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来的星期一，安妮从房间下来，胳膊和臀部挎着一篮子书，嘴唇抿成一条坚定的线，这让玛丽拉大吃一惊。

paragraphs.en: "I'm going back to school," she announced. "That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me. In school I can look at her and muse over days departed."
paragraphs.zh: “我要回学校了，”她宣布。 “既然我的朋友被无情地从我身边夺走，这就是我生命中剩下的一切。在学校里，我可以看着她，沉思着逝去的日子。”

paragraphs.en: "You'd better muse over your lessons and sums," said Marilla, concealing her delight at this development of the situation. "If you're going back to school I hope we'll hear no more of breaking slates over people's heads and such carryings on. Behave yourself and do just what your teacher tells you."
paragraphs.zh: “你最好沉思一下你的教训和总结，”玛丽拉说，隐藏着她对事态发展的喜悦。 “如果你要回到学校，我希望我们不会再听到有人在人们头上打碎石板和类似的事情。表现得好，按照老师告诉你的去做。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll try to be a model pupil," agreed Anne dolefully. "There won't be much fun in it, I expect. Mr. Phillips said Minnie Andrews was a model pupil and there isn't a spark of imagination or life in her. She is just dull and poky and never seems to have a good time. But I feel so depressed that perhaps it will come easy to me now. I'm going round by the road. I couldn't bear to go by the Birch Path all alone. I should weep bitter tears if I did."
paragraphs.zh: “我会努力成为一名模范学生。”安妮悲伤地同意道。 “我想这不会有太多乐趣。菲利普斯先生说米妮·安德鲁斯是个模范学生，她身上没有一丝想象力和生命力。她只是迟钝、迟钝，似乎从来没有过快乐的时光。但我感到很沮丧，也许现在对我来说会很容易。我正在路边转。我不忍心独自走在桦树小路上。如果我这样做了，我应该流下痛苦的眼泪。”

paragraphs.en: Anne was welcomed back to school with open arms. Her imagination had been sorely missed in games, her voice in the singing and her dramatic ability in the perusal aloud of books at dinner hour. Ruby Gillis smuggled three blue plums over to her during testament reading; Ella May MacPherson gave her an enormous yellow pansy cut from the covers of a floral catalogue—a species of desk decoration much prized in Avonlea school. Sophia Sloane offered to teach her a perfectly elegant new pattern of knit lace, so nice for trimming aprons. Katie Boulter gave her a perfume bottle to keep slate water in, and Julia Bell copied carefully on a piece of pale pink paper scalloped on the edges the following effusion:
paragraphs.zh: 安妮张开双臂欢迎回到学校。她在游戏中的想象力、她在歌唱中的声音以及她在晚餐时间大声朗读书籍时的戏剧能力都被严重怀念了。鲁比·吉利斯（Ruby Gillis）在宣读遗嘱时偷偷地将三颗蓝李子送给了她；艾拉·梅·麦克弗森送给她一朵巨大的黄色三色堇，是从花卉目录的封面上剪下来的——这是埃文利学校非常珍贵的一种课桌装饰品。索菲亚·斯隆主动提出教她一种完美优雅的新针织蕾丝图案，非常适合修剪围裙。凯蒂·博尔特给了她一个香水瓶，用来盛石板水，朱莉娅·贝尔在一张边缘有扇形的淡粉色纸上仔细地抄写了以下流出物：

paragraphs.en: When twilight drops her curtain down
paragraphs.zh: 当暮色拉下帷幕时

paragraphs.en: And pins it with a star
paragraphs.zh: 并用星星钉住它

paragraphs.en: Remember that you have a friend
paragraphs.zh: 记住你有一个朋友

paragraphs.en: Though she may wander far.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管她可能会流浪很远。

paragraphs.en: "It's so nice to be appreciated," sighed Anne rapturously to Marilla that night.
paragraphs.zh: “被人欣赏真是太好了，”那天晚上，安妮兴高采烈地对玛丽拉叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: The girls were not the only scholars who "appreciated" her. When Anne went to her seat after dinner hour—she had been told by Mr. Phillips to sit with the model Minnie Andrews—she found on her desk a big luscious "strawberry apple." Anne caught it up all ready to take a bite when she remembered that the only place in Avonlea where strawberry apples grew was in the old Blythe orchard on the other side of the Lake of Shining Waters. Anne dropped the apple as if it were a red-hot coal and ostentatiously wiped her fingers on her handkerchief. The apple lay untouched on her desk until the next morning, when little Timothy Andrews, who swept the school and kindled the fire, annexed it as one of his perquisites. Charlie Sloane's slate pencil, gorgeously bedizened with striped red and yellow paper, costing two cents where ordinary pencils cost only one, which he sent up to her after dinner hour, met with a more favorable reception. Anne was graciously pleased to accept it and rewarded the donor with a smile which exalted that infatuated youth straightway into the seventh heaven of delight and caused him to make such fearful errors in his dictation that Mr. Phillips kept him in after school to rewrite it.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们并不是唯一“欣赏”她的学者。当安妮在晚餐时间回到座位上时——菲利普斯先生让她和模特米妮·安德鲁斯坐在一起——她发现桌子上有一个又大又香甜的“草莓苹果”。安妮把一切都抓起来，准备咬一口，这时她想起埃文利唯一种植草莓苹果的地方是闪亮水域湖对岸的老布莱斯果园。安妮像扔一块烧红的煤炭一样扔下了苹果，并夸张地用手帕擦了擦手指。苹果原封不动地放在她的桌子上，直到第二天早上，小蒂莫西·安德鲁斯打扫了学校并点燃了火，将它作为他的额外津贴之一并入。查理·斯隆的石板铅笔，上面铺着华丽的红黄条纹纸，售价两美分，而普通铅笔只需一分钱，他在晚饭后送给她，受到了更好评。安妮很高兴地接受了它，并以微笑奖励了捐赠者，这使这个痴情的年轻人立即升入了快乐的第七层天堂，并导致他在听写中犯了如此可怕的错误，以至于菲利普斯先生在放学后让他重写了它。

paragraphs.en: But as,
paragraphs.zh: 但作为，

paragraphs.en: The Caesar's pageant shorn of Brutus' bust
paragraphs.zh: 凯撒的盛会被布鲁图斯的半身像剪掉了

paragraphs.en: Did but of Rome's best son remind her more,
paragraphs.zh: 但罗马最好的儿子是否更让她想起，

paragraphs.en: so the marked absence of any tribute or recognition from Diana Barry who was sitting with Gertie Pye embittered Anne's little triumph.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，与格蒂·派伊坐在一起的戴安娜·巴里明显没有表示任何敬意或认可，这让安妮的小胜利感到痛苦。

paragraphs.en: "Diana might just have smiled at me once, I think," she mourned to Marilla that night. But the next morning a note most fearfully and wonderfully twisted and folded, and a small parcel were passed across to Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “我想，戴安娜可能只是对我微笑过一次，”那天晚上她向玛丽拉哀悼。但第二天早上，一张纸条被极其可怕地、奇妙地扭曲和折叠，还有一个小包裹被传递给了安妮。

paragraphs.en: Dear Anne (ran the former)
paragraphs.zh: 亲爱的安妮（前者）

paragraphs.en: Mother says I'm not to play with you or talk to you even in school. It isn't my fault and don't be cross at me, because I love you as much as ever. I miss you awfully to tell all my secrets to and I don't like Gertie Pye one bit. I made you one of the new bookmarkers out of red tissue paper. They are awfully fashionable now and only three girls in school know how to make them. When you look at it remember
paragraphs.zh: 妈妈说即使在学校我也不能和你一起玩或说话。这不是我的错，不要生我的气，因为我一如既往地爱你。我非常想念你告诉我所有的秘密，而且我一点也不喜欢格蒂·派伊。我用红色薄纸给你做了一个新书签。它们现在非常流行，学校里只有三个女孩知道如何制作它们。当你看到它的时候记得

paragraphs.en: Your true friend
paragraphs.zh: 你真正的朋友

paragraphs.en: Diana Barry.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜·巴里.

paragraphs.en: Anne read the note, kissed the bookmark, and dispatched a prompt reply back to the other side of the school.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮读了纸条，亲吻了书签，然后迅速回复学校的另一边。

paragraphs.en: My own darling Diana:—
paragraphs.zh: 我亲爱的戴安娜：——

paragraphs.en: Of course I am not cross at you because you have to obey your mother. Our spirits can commune. I shall keep your lovely present forever. Minnie Andrews is a very nice little girl—although she has no imagination—but after having been Diana's busum friend I cannot be Minnie's. Please excuse mistakes because my spelling isn't very good yet, although much improoved.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，我不会生你的气，因为你必须服从你的母亲。我们的精神可以交流。我会永远保留你可爱的礼物。米妮·安德鲁斯是一个非常好的小女孩——虽然她没有想象力——但在成为戴安娜的布苏姆朋友之后，我就不能成为米妮的了。请原谅错误，因为我的拼写还不是很好，尽管已经进步了很多。

paragraphs.en: Yours until death us do part
paragraphs.zh: 你的直到死亡我们分开

paragraphs.en: Anne or Cordelia Shirley.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮或科迪莉亚雪莉。

paragraphs.en: P.S. I shall sleep with your letter under my pillow tonight. A. OR C.S.
paragraphs.zh: 附：今晚我会把你的信放在枕头下睡觉。 A. 或 C.S.

paragraphs.en: Marilla pessimistically expected more trouble since Anne had again begun to go to school. But none developed. Perhaps Anne caught something of the "model" spirit from Minnie Andrews; at least she got on very well with Mr. Phillips thenceforth. She flung herself into her studies heart and soul, determined not to be outdone in any class by Gilbert Blythe. The rivalry between them was soon apparent; it was entirely good natured on Gilbert's side; but it is much to be feared that the same thing cannot be said of Anne, who had certainly an unpraiseworthy tenacity for holding grudges. She was as intense in her hatreds as in her loves. She would not stoop to admit that she meant to rival Gilbert in schoolwork, because that would have been to acknowledge his existence which Anne persistently ignored; but the rivalry was there and honors fluctuated between them. Now Gilbert was head of the spelling class; now Anne, with a toss of her long red braids, spelled him down. One morning Gilbert had all his sums done correctly and had his name written on the blackboard on the roll of honor; the next morning Anne, having wrestled wildly with decimals the entire evening before, would be first. One awful day they were ties and their names were written up together. It was almost as bad as a take-notice and Anne's mortification was as evident as Gilbert's satisfaction. When the written examinations at the end of each month were held the suspense was terrible. The first month Gilbert came out three marks ahead. The second Anne beat him by five. But her triumph was marred by the fact that Gilbert congratulated her heartily before the whole school. It would have been ever so much sweeter to her if he had felt the sting of his defeat.
paragraphs.zh: 自从安妮重新开始上学以来，玛丽拉悲观地预计会有更多麻烦。但没有一个发展起来。也许安妮从米妮·安德鲁斯身上学到了一些“模范”精神。至少从那以后她和菲利普斯先生相处得很好。她全心全意地投入学习，决心在任何一堂课上都不会被吉尔伯特·布莱斯超越。他们之间的竞争很快就显现出来了。吉尔伯特这边完全是出于善意。但令人担心的是，安妮却不能说同样的事情，她的记仇固执程度确实值得称赞。她的仇恨和她的爱一样强烈。她不会屈尊承认自己想在功课上与吉尔伯特竞争，因为那样就等于承认他的存在，而安妮却一直忽视这一点。但竞争是存在的，他们之间的荣誉也时有时无。现在吉尔伯特是拼写班的班主任。现在，安妮一甩她长长的红色辫子，把他打倒了。一天早上，吉尔伯特正确地算出了所有的数字，并把他的名字写在了黑板上的荣誉榜上。第二天早上，安妮将是第一个，她前一晚都在与小数进行了疯狂的斗争。可怕的一天，他们成了领带，他们的名字写在一起。这几乎和注意到一样糟糕，安妮的屈辱和吉尔伯特的满意一样明显。每个月底进行笔试时，悬念都是可怕的。第一个月，吉尔伯特领先三分。第二局安妮以五分优势击败了他。但吉尔伯特在全校面前衷心祝贺她，这损害了她的胜利。如果他能感受到失败的刺痛，那对她来说会更加甜蜜。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips might not be a very good teacher; but a pupil so inflexibly determined on learning as Anne was could hardly escape making progress under any kind of teacher. By the end of the term Anne and Gilbert were both promoted into the fifth class and allowed to begin studying the elements of "the branches"—by which Latin, geometry, French, and algebra were meant. In geometry Anne met her Waterloo.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生可能不是一个很好的老师；但是像安妮这样顽固地学习的学生在任何类型的老师的指导下都很难逃脱进步。学期结束时，安妮和吉尔伯特都升入五年级，并被允许开始学习“分支”的元素——“分支”指的是拉丁语、几何、法语和代数。在几何学中，安妮遇到了她的滑铁卢。

paragraphs.en: "It's perfectly awful stuff, Marilla," she groaned. "I'm sure I'll never be able to make head or tail of it. There is no scope for imagination in it at all. Mr. Phillips says I'm the worst dunce he ever saw at it. And Gil—I mean some of the others are so smart at it. It is extremely mortifying, Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “这真是太糟糕了，玛丽拉，”她抱怨道。 “我确信我永远无法搞清楚这件事。这根本没有想象的余地。菲利普斯先生说我是他见过的最糟糕的笨蛋。还有吉尔——我的意思是其他一些人在这方面非常聪明。这真是太丢脸了，玛丽拉。

paragraphs.en: "Even Diana gets along better than I do. But I don't mind being beaten by Diana. Even although we meet as strangers now I still love her with an INEXTINGUISHABLE love. It makes me very sad at times to think about her. But really, Marilla, one can't stay sad very long in such an interesting world, can one?"
paragraphs.zh: “即使是戴安娜也比我相处得好。但我不介意被戴安娜殴打。即使我们现在以陌生人的身份见面，我仍然以一种无法熄灭的爱来爱她。有时想到她我会感到非常悲伤。但说实话，玛丽拉，在这样一个有趣的世界里，一个人不能长时间悲伤，不是吗？”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 18 章：安妮挺身救人

paragraphs.en: All things great are wound up with all things little. At first glance it might not seem that the decision of a certain Canadian Premier to include Prince Edward Island in a political tour could have much or anything to do with the fortunes of little Anne Shirley at Green Gables. But it had.
paragraphs.zh: 一切伟大的事情都与一切小事缠绕在一起。乍一看，加拿大某位总理将爱德华王子岛纳入政治访问的决定似乎与绿山墙小安妮·雪莉的命运没有多大关系。但确实如此。

paragraphs.en: It was a January the Premier came, to address his loyal supporters and such of his nonsupporters as chose to be present at the monster mass meeting held in Charlottetown. Most of the Avonlea people were on Premier's side of politics; hence on the night of the meeting nearly all the men and a goodly proportion of the women had gone to town thirty miles away. Mrs. Rachel Lynde had gone too. Mrs. Rachel Lynde was a red-hot politician and couldn't have believed that the political rally could be carried through without her, although she was on the opposite side of politics. So she went to town and took her husband—Thomas would be useful in looking after the horse—and Marilla Cuthbert with her. Marilla had a sneaking interest in politics herself, and as she thought it might be her only chance to see a real live Premier, she promptly took it, leaving Anne and Matthew to keep house until her return the following day.
paragraphs.zh: 那是一月，总理来到这里，向他的忠实支持者和那些选择出席在夏洛特敦举行的大规模群众大会的非支持者发表讲话。大多数埃文利人在政治上都站在总理一边。因此，在会议当晚，几乎所有的男人和相当一部分女人都去了三十英里外的城镇。雷切尔·林德夫人也走了。雷切尔·林德夫人是一位炙手可热的政治家，尽管她站在政治的对立面，但她无法相信没有她，政治集会也能顺利进行。于是她带着她的丈夫（托马斯会帮忙照看马）和玛丽拉·卡斯伯特一起进城。玛丽拉自己对政治也有一种潜在的兴趣，因为她认为这可能是她见到真正的总理的唯一机会，所以她立即抓住了这个机会，留下安妮和马修留在家里，直到她第二天回来。

paragraphs.en: Hence, while Marilla and Mrs. Rachel were enjoying themselves hugely at the mass meeting, Anne and Matthew had the cheerful kitchen at Green Gables all to themselves. A bright fire was glowing in the old-fashioned Waterloo stove and blue-white frost crystals were shining on the windowpanes. Matthew nodded over a FARMERS' ADVOCATE on the sofa and Anne at the table studied her lessons with grim determination, despite sundry wistful glances at the clock shelf, where lay a new book that Jane Andrews had lent her that day. Jane had assured her that it was warranted to produce any number of thrills, or words to that effect, and Anne's fingers tingled to reach out for it. But that would mean Gilbert Blythe's triumph on the morrow. Anne turned her back on the clock shelf and tried to imagine it wasn't there.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，当玛丽拉和雷切尔夫人在群众大会上玩得很开心的时候，安妮和马修却独享了绿山墙令人愉悦的厨房。老式滑铁卢炉子里熊熊燃烧着明亮的火，窗玻璃上闪烁着蓝白色的霜晶。马修对着沙发上的农民律师点了点头，而坐在桌边的安妮则以坚定的决心学习着她的课程，尽管她不断地向钟架上投去渴望的目光，钟架上放着简·安德鲁斯那天借给她的一本新书。简向她保证，它一定会产生任何数量的刺激，或者类似的言语，而安妮伸手去拿它的手指感到刺痛。但这意味着吉尔伯特·布莱斯明天就会取得胜利。安妮转过身背对着钟架，试图想象它不在那儿。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew, did you ever study geometry when you went to school?"
paragraphs.zh: “马修，你上学的时候学过几何吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, no, I didn't," said Matthew, coming out of his doze with a start.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，不，我没有，”马修从睡梦中惊醒过来说道。

paragraphs.en: "I wish you had," sighed Anne, "because then you'd be able to sympathize with me. You can't sympathize properly if you've never studied it. It is casting a cloud over my whole life. I'm such a dunce at it, Matthew."
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你这么做了，”安妮叹了口气，“因为这样你就能同情我了。如果你从来没有研究过它，你就不可能真正地同情我。它给我的一生蒙上了一层阴影。我在这方面真是个笨蛋，马修。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno," said Matthew soothingly. "I guess you're all right at anything. Mr. Phillips told me last week in Blair's store at Carmody that you was the smartest scholar in school and was making rapid progress. 'Rapid progress' was his very words. There's them as runs down Teddy Phillips and says he ain't much of a teacher, but I guess he's all right."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道，”马修安慰地说。 “我想你什么都好。上周，菲利普斯先生在卡莫迪的布莱尔店里告诉我，你是学校里最聪明的学者，而且进步很快。‘进步很快’就是他的原话。有人责骂泰迪·菲利普斯，说他不太称职，但我想他还不错。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew would have thought anyone who praised Anne was "all right."
paragraphs.zh: 马修会认为任何赞扬安妮的人都“没问题”。

paragraphs.en: "I'm sure I'd get on better with geometry if only he wouldn't change the letters," complained Anne. "I learn the proposition off by heart and then he draws it on the blackboard and puts different letters from what are in the book and I get all mixed up. I don't think a teacher should take such a mean advantage, do you? We're studying agriculture now and I've found out at last what makes the roads red. It's a great comfort. I wonder how Marilla and Mrs. Lynde are enjoying themselves. Mrs. Lynde says Canada is going to the dogs the way things are being run at Ottawa and that it's an awful warning to the electors. She says if women were allowed to vote we would soon see a blessed change. What way do you vote, Matthew?"
paragraphs.zh: “我相信只要他不改变字母，我的几何学就会学得更好，”安妮抱怨道。 “我把这个命题背下来，然后他把它画在黑板上，并把书上的不同字母写下来，我就搞混了。我认为老师不应该利用这么卑鄙的优势，不是吗？我们现在正在研究农业，我终于找到了道路变红的原因。这是一个很大的安慰。我不知道玛丽拉和林德夫人玩得怎么样。林德夫人说加拿大正在走向狗，就像事情的运行方式一样。渥太华，这对选民来说是一个可怕的警告，她说，如果允许女性投票，我们很快就会看到一个幸运的改变，马修？”

paragraphs.en: "Conservative," said Matthew promptly. To vote Conservative was part of Matthew's religion.
paragraphs.zh: “保守，”马修立即说道。投票给保守党是马修信仰的一部分。

paragraphs.en: "Then I'm Conservative too," said Anne decidedly. "I'm glad because Gil—because some of the boys in school are Grits. I guess Mr. Phillips is a Grit too because Prissy Andrews's father is one, and Ruby Gillis says that when a man is courting he always has to agree with the girl's mother in religion and her father in politics. Is that true, Matthew?"
paragraphs.zh: “那我也是保守派，”安妮斩钉截铁地说。 “我很高兴，因为吉尔——因为学校里的一些男孩都是勇敢的人。我猜菲利普斯先生也是一个勇敢的人，因为普里西·安德鲁斯的父亲就是其中之一，而鲁比·吉利斯说，当一个男人在求爱时，他总是必须在宗教上同意女孩的母亲，在政治上同意她的父亲。是这样吗，马修？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno," said Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道，”马修说。

paragraphs.en: "Did you ever go courting, Matthew?"
paragraphs.zh: “你谈过恋爱吗，马修？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, no, I dunno's I ever did," said Matthew, who had certainly never thought of such a thing in his whole existence.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，不，我不知道我曾经做过什么，”马修说，他一生中肯定从未想过这样的事情。

paragraphs.en: Anne reflected with her chin in her hands.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮双手托着下巴思考着。

paragraphs.en: "It must be rather interesting, don't you think, Matthew? Ruby Gillis says when she grows up she's going to have ever so many beaus on the string and have them all crazy about her; but I think that would be too exciting. I'd rather have just one in his right mind. But Ruby Gillis knows a great deal about such matters because she has so many big sisters, and Mrs. Lynde says the Gillis girls have gone off like hot cakes. Mr. Phillips goes up to see Prissy Andrews nearly every evening. He says it is to help her with her lessons but Miranda Sloane is studying for Queen's too, and I should think she needed help a lot more than Prissy because she's ever so much stupider, but he never goes to help her in the evenings at all. There are a great many things in this world that I can't understand very well, Matthew."
paragraphs.zh: “这一定很有趣，马修，你不觉得吗？鲁比·吉利斯说，等她长大后，她会有那么多的男友，他们都为她疯狂；但我觉得那太令人兴奋了。我宁愿他脑子里只有一个。但是鲁比·吉利斯对这些事情了解很多，因为她有很多姐姐，林德太太说吉利斯家的女孩们都快走红了。”菲利普斯几乎每天晚上都会去看望普莉西·安德鲁斯，他说这是为了帮助她学习，但米兰达·斯隆也在为女王大学学习，我认为她比普莉西更需要帮助，因为她比普莉西笨得多，但他从来没有在晚上帮助她，这个世界上有很多事情我不太明白，马修。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno as I comprehend them all myself," acknowledged Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道，因为我自己理解它们，”马修承认。

paragraphs.en: "Well, I suppose I must finish up my lessons. I won't allow myself to open that new book Jane lent me until I'm through. But it's a terrible temptation, Matthew. Even when I turn my back on it I can see it there just as plain. Jane said she cried herself sick over it. I love a book that makes me cry. But I think I'll carry that book into the sitting room and lock it in the jam closet and give you the key. And you must NOT give it to me, Matthew, until my lessons are done, not even if I implore you on my bended knees. It's all very well to say resist temptation, but it's ever so much easier to resist it if you can't get the key. And then shall I run down the cellar and get some russets, Matthew? Wouldn't you like some russets?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我想我必须完成我的课程。在我读完之前，我不会允许自己打开简借给我的那本新书。但这是一个可怕的诱惑，马修。即使我背对着它，我也能清楚地看到它在那里。简说她为此哭得很厉害。我喜欢一本让我哭泣的书。但我想我会把那本书带到客厅，把它锁在果酱柜里，然后给你钥匙。你不可以把它给我，马修，在我的课结束之前，即使我跪着恳求你，说抵制诱惑也很好，但如果你拿不到钥匙，那么抵制它会容易得多，马修，你不想要一些赤褐色吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno but what I would," said Matthew, who never ate russets but knew Anne's weakness for them.
paragraphs.zh: “Well now, I dunno but what I would, said Matthew, who never ate russets but knew Annes weakness for them.。”

paragraphs.en: Just as Anne emerged triumphantly from the cellar with her plateful of russets came the sound of flying footsteps on the icy board walk outside and the next moment the kitchen door was flung open and in rushed Diana Barry, white faced and breathless, with a shawl wrapped hastily around her head. Anne promptly let go of her candle and plate in her surprise, and plate, candle, and apples crashed together down the cellar ladder and were found at the bottom embedded in melted grease, the next day, by Marilla, who gathered them up and thanked mercy the house hadn't been set on fire.
paragraphs.zh: Just as Anne emerged triumphantly from the cellar with her plateful of russets came the sound of flying footsteps on the icy board walk outside and the next moment the kitchen door was flung open and in rushed Diana Barry, white faced and breathless, with a shawl wrapped hastily around her head. Anne promptly let go of her candle and plate in her surprise, and plate, candle, and apples crashed together down the cellar ladder and were found at the bottom embedded in melted grease, the next day, by Marilla, who gathered them up and thanked mercy the house hadnt been set on fire.。

paragraphs.en: "Whatever is the matter, Diana?" cried Anne. "Has your mother relented at last?"
paragraphs.zh: “Whatever is the matter, Diana? cried Anne. Has your mother relented at last?。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Anne, do come quick," implored Diana nervously. "Minnie May is awful sick—she's got croup. Young Mary Joe says—and Father and Mother are away to town and there's nobody to go for the doctor. Minnie May is awful bad and Young Mary Joe doesn't know what to do—and oh, Anne, I'm so scared!"
paragraphs.zh: “Oh, Anne, do come quick, implored Diana nervously. Minnie May is awful sick—shes got croup. Young Mary Joe says—and Father and Mother are away to town and theres nobody to go for the doctor. Minnie May is awful bad and Young Mary Joe doesnt know what to do—and oh, Anne, Im so scared!。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew, without a word, reached out for cap and coat, slipped past Diana and away into the darkness of the yard.
paragraphs.zh: Matthew, without a word, reached out for cap and coat, slipped past Diana and away into the darkness of the yard.。

paragraphs.en: "He's gone to harness the sorrel mare to go to Carmody for the doctor," said Anne, who was hurrying on hood and jacket. "I know it as well as if he'd said so. Matthew and I are such kindred spirits I can read his thoughts without words at all."
paragraphs.zh: “Hes gone to harness the sorrel mare to go to Carmody for the doctor, said Anne, who was hurrying on hood and jacket. I know it as well as if hed said so. Matthew and I are such kindred spirits I can read his thoughts without words at all.。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't believe he'll find the doctor at Carmody," sobbed Diana. "I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!"
paragraphs.zh: “I dont believe hell find the doctor at Carmody, sobbed Diana. I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!。”

paragraphs.en: "Don't cry, Di," said Anne cheerily. "I know exactly what to do for croup. You forget that Mrs. Hammond had twins three times. When you look after three pairs of twins you naturally get a lot of experience. They all had croup regularly. Just wait till I get the ipecac bottle—you mayn't have any at your house. Come on now."
paragraphs.zh: “Dont cry, Di, said Anne cheerily. I know exactly what to do for croup. You forget that Mrs. Hammond had twins three times. When you look after three pairs of twins you naturally get a lot of experience. They all had croup regularly. Just wait till I get the ipecac bottle—you maynt have any at your house. Come on now.。”

paragraphs.en: The two little girls hastened out hand in hand and hurried through Lover's Lane and across the crusted field beyond, for the snow was too deep to go by the shorter wood way. Anne, although sincerely sorry for Minnie May, was far from being insensible to the romance of the situation and to the sweetness of once more sharing that romance with a kindred spirit.
paragraphs.zh: The two little girls hastened out hand in hand and hurried through Lovers Lane and across the crusted field beyond, for the snow was too deep to go by the shorter wood way. Anne, although sincerely sorry for Minnie May, was far from being insensible to the romance of the situation and to the sweetness of once more sharing that romance with a kindred spirit.。

paragraphs.en: The night was clear and frosty, all ebony of shadow and silver of snowy slope; big stars were shining over the silent fields; here and there the dark pointed firs stood up with snow powdering their branches and the wind whistling through them. Anne thought it was truly delightful to go skimming through all this mystery and loveliness with your bosom friend who had been so long estranged.
paragraphs.zh: The night was clear and frosty, all ebony of shadow and silver of snowy slope; big stars were shining over the silent fields; here and there the dark pointed firs stood up with snow powdering their branches and the wind whistling through them. Anne thought it was truly delightful to go skimming through all this mystery and loveliness with your bosom friend who had been so long estranged.。

paragraphs.en: Minnie May, aged three, was really very sick. She lay on the kitchen sofa feverish and restless, while her hoarse breathing could be heard all over the house. Young Mary Joe, a buxom, broad-faced French girl from the creek, whom Mrs. Barry had engaged to stay with the children during her absence, was helpless and bewildered, quite incapable of thinking what to do, or doing it if she thought of it.
paragraphs.zh: Minnie May, aged three, was really very sick. She lay on the kitchen sofa feverish and restless, while her hoarse breathing could be heard all over the house. Young Mary Joe, a buxom, broad-faced French girl from the creek, whom Mrs. Barry had engaged to stay with the children during her absence, was helpless and bewildered, quite incapable of thinking what to do, or doing it if she thought of it.。

paragraphs.en: Anne went to work with skill and promptness.
paragraphs.zh: Anne went to work with skill and promptness.。

paragraphs.en: "Minnie May has croup all right; she's pretty bad, but I've seen them worse. First we must have lots of hot water. I declare, Diana, there isn't more than a cupful in the kettle! There, I've filled it up, and, Mary Joe, you may put some wood in the stove. I don't want to hurt your feelings but it seems to me you might have thought of this before if you'd any imagination. Now, I'll undress Minnie May and put her to bed and you try to find some soft flannel cloths, Diana. I'm going to give her a dose of ipecac first of all."
paragraphs.zh: “Minnie May has croup all right; shes pretty bad, but Ive seen them worse. First we must have lots of hot water. I declare, Diana, there isnt more than a cupful in the kettle! There, Ive filled it up, and, Mary Joe, you may put some wood in the stove. I dont want to hurt your feelings but it seems to me you might have thought of this before if youd any imagination. Now, Ill undress Minnie May and put her to bed and you try to find some soft flannel cloths, Diana. Im going to give her a dose of ipecac first of all.。”

paragraphs.en: Minnie May did not take kindly to the ipecac but Anne had not brought up three pairs of twins for nothing. Down that ipecac went, not only once, but many times during the long, anxious night when the two little girls worked patiently over the suffering Minnie May, and Young Mary Joe, honestly anxious to do all she could, kept up a roaring fire and heated more water than would have been needed for a hospital of croupy babies.
paragraphs.zh: 米妮·梅对吐根并没有好感，但安妮也没有白养育三对双胞胎。在那个漫长而焦虑的夜晚，吐根不仅掉了一次，而且掉了很多次。两个小女孩耐心地照顾受苦受难的明妮·梅，年轻的玛丽·乔真诚地渴望尽她所能，一直生着熊熊的火，加热的水比医院里治疗哮吼婴儿所需的水还要多。

paragraphs.en: It was three o'clock when Matthew came with a doctor, for he had been obliged to go all the way to Spencervale for one. But the pressing need for assistance was past. Minnie May was much better and was sleeping soundly.
paragraphs.zh: 当马修带着一位医生来时，已经是下午三点了，因为他不得不千里迢迢去斯宾塞维尔看医生。但对援助的迫切需求已经成为过去。米妮·梅好多了，睡得很香。

paragraphs.en: "I was awfully near giving up in despair," explained Anne. "She got worse and worse until she was sicker than ever the Hammond twins were, even the last pair. I actually thought she was going to choke to death. I gave her every drop of ipecac in that bottle and when the last dose went down I said to myself—not to Diana or Young Mary Joe, because I didn't want to worry them any more than they were worried, but I had to say it to myself just to relieve my feelings—'This is the last lingering hope and I fear, tis a vain one.' But in about three minutes she coughed up the phlegm and began to get better right away. You must just imagine my relief, doctor, because I can't express it in words. You know there are some things that cannot be expressed in words."
paragraphs.zh: “我绝望得几乎要放弃了，”安妮解释道。 “她的病情越来越严重，直到她的病情比哈蒙德双胞胎甚至最后一对都更加严重。我真的以为她会窒息而死。我给了她瓶子里的每一滴吐根，当最后一剂喝完时，我对自己说——不是对戴安娜或年轻的玛丽·乔，因为我不想让他们比他们更担心，但我不得不对自己说，只是为了缓解我的感情——‘这是最后的希望，我担心，这是一个徒劳的人。但大约三分钟后，她咳出了痰，并立即开始好转。你一定想象一下我的解脱，医生，因为我无法用语言表达它。你知道，有些事情是无法用言语表达的。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I know," nodded the doctor. He looked at Anne as if he were thinking some things about her that couldn't be expressed in words. Later on, however, he expressed them to Mr. and Mrs. Barry.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我知道。”医生点点头。他看着安妮，似乎在思考一些无法用言语表达的事情。然而，后来他向巴里夫妇表达了这些想法。

paragraphs.en: "That little redheaded girl they have over at Cuthbert's is as smart as they make 'em. I tell you she saved that baby's life, for it would have been too late by the time I got there. She seems to have a skill and presence of mind perfectly wonderful in a child of her age. I never saw anything like the eyes of her when she was explaining the case to me."
paragraphs.zh: “卡斯伯特家的那个红发小女孩和他们想象的一样聪明。我告诉你，她救了那个婴儿的命，因为当我到达那里时已经太晚了。她似乎拥有她这个年纪的孩子中完美的技巧和冷静。当她向我解释案件时，我从未见过她的眼睛。”

paragraphs.en: Anne had gone home in the wonderful, white-frosted winter morning, heavy eyed from loss of sleep, but still talking unweariedly to Matthew as they crossed the long white field and walked under the glittering fairy arch of the Lover's Lane maples.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在一个美好的、白霜的冬日早晨回家了，她因失眠而双目沉重，但当他们穿过长长的白色田野，走在情人巷枫树闪闪发光的仙女拱门下时，安妮仍然不知疲倦地和马修说话。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Matthew, isn't it a wonderful morning? The world looks like something God had just imagined for His own pleasure, doesn't it? Those trees look as if I could blow them away with a breath—pouf! I'm so glad I live in a world where there are white frosts, aren't you? And I'm so glad Mrs. Hammond had three pairs of twins after all. If she hadn't I mightn't have known what to do for Minnie May. I'm real sorry I was ever cross with Mrs. Hammond for having twins. But, oh, Matthew, I'm so sleepy. I can't go to school. I just know I couldn't keep my eyes open and I'd be so stupid. But I hate to stay home, for Gil—some of the others will get head of the class, and it's so hard to get up again—although of course the harder it is the more satisfaction you have when you do get up, haven't you?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，马修，这不是一个美妙的早晨吗？这个世界看起来就像上帝为了自己的快乐而想象的那样，不是吗？那些树看起来好像我可以一口气把它们吹走——噗！我很高兴我生活在一个有白霜的世界，不是吗？而且我很高兴哈蒙德太太毕竟有了三对双胞胎。如果她没有，我可能不知道该怎么为米妮·梅做。我是真的抱歉，我因为生了双胞胎而生了哈蒙德太太的气，但是，哦，马修，我太困了，我只知道我无法睁开眼睛，我会变得很愚蠢，但我不想呆在家里，因为吉尔——其他一些人会成为班长，而且很难再起床——当然，当你起床时，你会感到越满足，不是吗？

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I guess you'll manage all right," said Matthew, looking at Anne's white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes. "You just go right to bed and have a good sleep. I'll do all the chores."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我想你会处理得很好，”马修看着安妮苍白的小脸和她眼睛下面的黑眼圈说道。 “你直接去床上睡个好觉吧。我会做所有的家务。”

paragraphs.en: Anne accordingly went to bed and slept so long and soundly that it was well on in the white and rosy winter afternoon when she awoke and descended to the kitchen where Marilla, who had arrived home in the meantime, was sitting knitting.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，安妮上床睡觉，睡得又长又香，当她醒来时，已经是一个白里透红的冬日午后了，下楼来到厨房，玛丽拉此时也到家了，正坐在厨房里织毛衣。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, did you see the Premier?" exclaimed Anne at once. "What did he look like Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，你见到总理了吗？”安妮立刻惊呼道。 “他长得像玛丽拉吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Well, he never got to be Premier on account of his looks," said Marilla. "Such a nose as that man had! But he can speak. I was proud of being a Conservative. Rachel Lynde, of course, being a Liberal, had no use for him. Your dinner is in the oven, Anne, and you can get yourself some blue plum preserve out of the pantry. I guess you're hungry. Matthew has been telling me about last night. I must say it was fortunate you knew what to do. I wouldn't have had any idea myself, for I never saw a case of croup. There now, never mind talking till you've had your dinner. I can tell by the look of you that you're just full up with speeches, but they'll keep."
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，他从来没有因为他的外表而成为总理，”马里拉说。 “那个人有这样的鼻子！但他会说话。我为自己是一名保守党人而感到自豪。雷切尔·林德，当然，作为一名自由党人，对他没有用处。你的晚餐在烤箱里，安妮，你可以从食品储藏室给自己买一些蓝李子蜜饯。我猜你饿了。马修一直在告诉我昨晚的事。我必须说，幸运的是你知道该怎么做。我自己也不知道，因为我从来没有见过一例好了，吃完晚饭之前别介意说话，从你的表情来看，你已经讲完了，但他们会继续讲下去的。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla had something to tell Anne, but she did not tell it just then for she knew if she did Anne's consequent excitement would lift her clear out of the region of such material matters as appetite or dinner. Not until Anne had finished her saucer of blue plums did Marilla say:
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉有话要告诉安妮，但她当时没有说出来，因为她知道如果她这样做，安妮随之而来的兴奋会让她摆脱食欲或晚餐等物质问题的困扰。直到安妮吃完她那碟蓝色李子，玛丽拉才说道：

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Barry was here this afternoon, Anne. She wanted to see you, but I wouldn't wake you up. She says you saved Minnie May's life, and she is very sorry she acted as she did in that affair of the currant wine. She says she knows now you didn't mean to set Diana drunk, and she hopes you'll forgive her and be good friends with Diana again. You're to go over this evening if you like for Diana can't stir outside the door on account of a bad cold she caught last night. Now, Anne Shirley, for pity's sake don't fly up into the air."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，巴里太太今天下午来过这里。她想见你，但我不会叫醒你。她说你救了明妮·梅的命，她对自己在醋栗酒事件中的所作所为感到非常抱歉。她说她现在知道你不是故意让戴安娜喝醉的，她希望你能原谅她，并再次与戴安娜成为好朋友。如果你愿意的话，你今晚就可以过去，因为戴安娜因为一件事而不能在门外动弹。她昨晚得了重感冒，现在，安妮·雪莉，看在怜悯的份上，别飞到空中了。”

paragraphs.en: The warning seemed not unnecessary, so uplifted and aerial was Anne's expression and attitude as she sprang to her feet, her face irradiated with the flame of her spirit.
paragraphs.zh: 这个警告似乎并非没有必要，当安妮跳起身来时，她的表情和态度都是如此振奋和昂扬，她的脸闪耀着她的精神之火。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, can I go right now—without washing my dishes? I'll wash them when I come back, but I cannot tie myself down to anything so unromantic as dishwashing at this thrilling moment."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，我现在可以走了吗——不洗碗？我回来后会洗的，但在这个激动人心的时刻，我不能把自己束缚在洗碗这样不浪漫的事情上。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, yes, run along," said Marilla indulgently. "Anne Shirley—are you crazy? Come back this instant and put something on you. I might as well call to the wind. She's gone without a cap or wrap. Look at her tearing through the orchard with her hair streaming. It'll be a mercy if she doesn't catch her death of cold."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，是的，一起跑吧。”玛丽拉宽容地说。 “安妮·雪莉——你疯了吗？赶紧回来，给你穿上点东西。我还不如呼唤风呢。她没有戴帽子，也没有围巾。看看她在果园里奔跑，头发流淌。如果她没有被冻死，那就太好了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne came dancing home in the purple winter twilight across the snowy places. Afar in the southwest was the great shimmering, pearl-like sparkle of an evening star in a sky that was pale golden and ethereal rose over gleaming white spaces and dark glens of spruce. The tinkles of sleigh bells among the snowy hills came like elfin chimes through the frosty air, but their music was not sweeter than the song in Anne's heart and on her lips.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在紫色的冬日暮色中穿过雪地跳舞回家。西南方向远处，一颗夜星闪烁着珍珠般的光芒，天空呈淡金色，空灵的玫瑰色笼罩着闪闪发光的白色空间和暗淡的云杉峡谷。雪山间雪橇铃的叮当声在寒冷的空气中响起，就像精灵的钟声，但它们的音乐并不比安妮心里和嘴唇上的歌更甜美。

paragraphs.en: "You see before you a perfectly happy person, Marilla," she announced. "I'm perfectly happy—yes, in spite of my red hair. Just at present I have a soul above red hair. Mrs. Barry kissed me and cried and said she was so sorry and she could never repay me. I felt fearfully embarrassed, Marilla, but I just said as politely as I could, 'I have no hard feelings for you, Mrs. Barry. I assure you once for all that I did not mean to intoxicate Diana and henceforth I shall cover the past with the mantle of oblivion.' That was a pretty dignified way of speaking wasn't it, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “You see before you a perfectly happy person, Marilla, she announced. Im perfectly happy—yes, in spite of my red hair. Just at present I have a soul above red hair. Mrs. Barry kissed me and cried and said she was so sorry and she could never repay me. I felt fearfully embarrassed, Marilla, but I just said as politely as I could, I have no hard feelings for you, Mrs. Barry. I assure you once for all that I did not mean to intoxicate Diana and henceforth I shall cover the past with the mantle of oblivion. That was a pretty dignified way of speaking wasnt it, Marilla?。”

paragraphs.en: "I felt that I was heaping coals of fire on Mrs. Barry's head. And Diana and I had a lovely afternoon. Diana showed me a new fancy crochet stitch her aunt over at Carmody taught her. Not a soul in Avonlea knows it but us, and we pledged a solemn vow never to reveal it to anyone else. Diana gave me a beautiful card with a wreath of roses on it and a verse of poetry:
paragraphs.zh: “我觉得我在巴里夫人的头上堆了一堆火炭。戴安娜和我度过了一个愉快的下午。戴安娜向我展示了她姨妈在卡莫迪教给她的一种新的花哨钩针。除了我们之外，埃文利没有一个人知道它，我们发誓永远不会向任何人透露它。戴安娜给了我一张漂亮的卡片，上面有玫瑰花环和一首诗：

paragraphs.en: "If you love me as I love you
paragraphs.zh: “如果你爱我就像我爱你一样

paragraphs.en: Nothing but death can part us two.
paragraphs.zh: 除了死亡，没有什么能把我们两个分开。

paragraphs.en: "And that is true, Marilla. We're going to ask Mr. Phillips to let us sit together in school again, and Gertie Pye can go with Minnie Andrews. We had an elegant tea. Mrs. Barry had the very best china set out, Marilla, just as if I was real company. I can't tell you what a thrill it gave me. Nobody ever used their very best china on my account before. And we had fruit cake and pound cake and doughnuts and two kinds of preserves, Marilla. And Mrs. Barry asked me if I took tea and said 'Pa, why don't you pass the biscuits to Anne?' It must be lovely to be grown up, Marilla, when just being treated as if you were is so nice."
paragraphs.zh: “确实如此，玛丽拉。我们要请求菲利普斯先生让我们再次在学校坐在一起，格蒂·派伊可以和米妮·安德鲁斯一起去。我们喝了一顿优雅的茶。巴里夫人准备了最好的瓷器，玛丽拉，就好像我是真正的陪伴一样。我无法告诉你这给了我多大的兴奋。以前从来没有人用过他们最好的瓷器在我的帐户上。我们有水果蛋糕、磅蛋糕、甜甜圈和两种玛丽拉，巴里太太问我是否喝茶，并说：“爸，你为什么不把饼干递给安妮呢？”玛丽拉，长大了一定很美好，只要像你一样被人对待就太好了。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't know about that," said Marilla, with a brief sigh.
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”玛丽拉简短地叹了口气说。

paragraphs.en: "Well, anyway, when I am grown up," said Anne decidedly, "I'm always going to talk to little girls as if they were too, and I'll never laugh when they use big words. I know from sorrowful experience how that hurts one's feelings. After tea Diana and I made taffy. The taffy wasn't very good, I suppose because neither Diana nor I had ever made any before. Diana left me to stir it while she buttered the plates and I forgot and let it burn; and then when we set it out on the platform to cool the cat walked over one plate and that had to be thrown away. But the making of it was splendid fun. Then when I came home Mrs. Barry asked me to come over as often as I could and Diana stood at the window and threw kisses to me all the way down to Lover's Lane. I assure you, Marilla, that I feel like praying tonight and I'm going to think out a special brand-new prayer in honor of the occasion."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，无论如何，等我长大了，”安妮坚决地说，“我总是会和小女孩说话，就好像她们也是一样，当她们用大词时，我永远不会笑。我从悲伤的经历中知道，这会伤害一个人的感情。喝完茶后，戴安娜和我做了太妃糖。我想太妃糖不太好，因为戴安娜和我以前都没有做过太妃糖。戴安娜让我搅拌，而她在盘子上涂黄油，我忘了，就让它了。然后，当我们把它放在平台上冷却时，猫走过了一个盘子，但它的制作非常有趣。然后，当我回到家时，巴里夫人让我尽可能多地过来，戴安娜站在窗前，一路吻着我，玛丽拉，我今晚想祈祷，我会想出一个特别的全新祈祷来纪念。场合。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XIX. A Concert a Catastrophe and a Confession
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 19 章：音乐会、灾难与坦白

paragraphs.en: "Marilla, can I go over to see Diana just for a minute?" asked Anne, running breathlessly down from the east gable one February evening.
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，我可以过去看看戴安娜吗？”二月的一个晚上，安妮气喘吁吁地从东山墙跑下来，问道。

paragraphs.en: "I don't see what you want to be traipsing about after dark for," said Marilla shortly. "You and Diana walked home from school together and then stood down there in the snow for half an hour more, your tongues going the whole blessed time, clickety-clack. So I don't think you're very badly off to see her again."
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白你想在天黑后到处闲逛做什么，”玛丽拉简短地说。 “你和戴安娜一起从学校走回家，然后在雪地里又站了半个小时，你们的舌头在整个幸福的时光里都在吱吱作响。所以我认为你再次见到她不会太糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: "But she wants to see me," pleaded Anne. "She has something very important to tell me."
paragraphs.zh: “但她想见我，”安妮恳求道。 “她有很重要的事情要告诉我。”

paragraphs.en: "How do you know she has?"
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么知道她有？”

paragraphs.en: "Because she just signaled to me from her window. We have arranged a way to signal with our candles and cardboard. We set the candle on the window sill and make flashes by passing the cardboard back and forth. So many flashes mean a certain thing. It was my idea, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “因为她刚刚从她的窗户向我发出信号。我们安排了一种用蜡烛和纸板发出信号的方式。我们把蜡烛放在窗台上，并通过来回传递纸板来发出闪光。这么多的闪光意味着某种事情。这是我的主意，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll warrant you it was," said Marilla emphatically. "And the next thing you'll be setting fire to the curtains with your signaling nonsense."
paragraphs.zh: “我向你保证，确实如此。”玛丽拉强调道。 “接下来你就会用你的无意义信号点燃窗帘。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, we're very careful, Marilla. And it's so interesting. Two flashes mean, 'Are you there?' Three mean 'yes' and four 'no.' Five mean, 'Come over as soon as possible, because I have something important to reveal.' Diana has just signaled five flashes, and I'm really suffering to know what it is."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我们非常小心，玛丽拉。这很有趣。两次闪光意味着，‘你在吗？’三个表示“是”，四个表示“否”。五的意思是，“尽快过来，因为我有重要的事情要透露。”戴安娜刚刚发出了五次闪光信号，我真的很难知道那是什么。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, you needn't suffer any longer," said Marilla sarcastically. "You can go, but you're to be back here in just ten minutes, remember that."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你不必再受苦了，”玛丽拉讽刺地说。 “你可以走了，但是你要在十分钟内回到这里，记住这一点。”

paragraphs.en: Anne did remember it and was back in the stipulated time, although probably no mortal will ever know just what it cost her to confine the discussion of Diana's important communication within the limits of ten minutes. But at least she had made good use of them.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮确实记得这件事，并在规定的时间内回来了，尽管可能没有人知道她将戴安娜重要通讯的讨论限制在十分钟之内要付出什么代价。但至少她充分利用了它们。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, what do you think? You know tomorrow is Diana's birthday. Well, her mother told her she could ask me to go home with her from school and stay all night with her. And her cousins are coming over from Newbridge in a big pung sleigh to go to the Debating Club concert at the hall tomorrow night. And they are going to take Diana and me to the concert—if you'll let me go, that is. You will, won't you, Marilla? Oh, I feel so excited."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，你觉得怎么样？你知道明天是戴安娜的生日。好吧，她妈妈告诉她，她可以请我和她一起放学回家，并在她身边过夜。她的表兄弟姐妹们将从纽布里奇乘坐大彭雪橇赶来，明天晚上去大厅参加辩论俱乐部音乐会。他们将带戴安娜和我去听音乐会——如果你让我去的话。你会的，不是吗，玛丽拉？哦，我感觉很兴奋。”

paragraphs.en: "You can calm down then, because you're not going. You're better at home in your own bed, and as for that club concert, it's all nonsense, and little girls should not be allowed to go out to such places at all."
paragraphs.zh: “那你就冷静点，因为你不去，你在家里自己床上比较好，至于那场俱乐部音乐会，那都是废话，根本不应该允许小女孩出去这种地方。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm sure the Debating Club is a most respectable affair," pleaded Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “我确信辩论俱乐部是一项最受人尊敬的活动，”安妮恳求道。

paragraphs.en: "I'm not saying it isn't. But you're not going to begin gadding about to concerts and staying out all hours of the night. Pretty doings for children. I'm surprised at Mrs. Barry's letting Diana go."
paragraphs.zh: “我并不是说它不是。但是你不会开始去听音乐会并整夜待在外面。这对孩子们来说是很好的行为。我对巴里夫人让戴安娜离开感到惊讶。”

paragraphs.en: "But it's such a very special occasion," mourned Anne, on the verge of tears. "Diana has only one birthday in a year. It isn't as if birthdays were common things, Marilla. Prissy Andrews is going to recite 'Curfew Must Not Ring Tonight.' That is such a good moral piece, Marilla, I'm sure it would do me lots of good to hear it. And the choir are going to sing four lovely pathetic songs that are pretty near as good as hymns. And oh, Marilla, the minister is going to take part; yes, indeed, he is; he's going to give an address. That will be just about the same thing as a sermon. Please, mayn't I go, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “但这是一个非常特殊的时刻，”安妮哀悼道，她快要哭了。 “戴安娜一年只有一次生日。玛丽拉，生日并不是一件常见的事情。普里西·安德鲁斯将背诵‘今晚宵禁不得敲响’。”这是一篇很好的道德文章，玛丽拉，我相信听到它会对我有很多好处。合唱团将演唱四首可爱而可怜的歌曲，它们几乎和赞美诗一样好。哦，玛丽拉，部长要参加；是的，确实如此；他会给出一个地址。这与布道几乎是一样的。拜托，我可以走了吗，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: "You heard what I said, Anne, didn't you? Take off your boots now and go to bed. It's past eight."
paragraphs.zh: “你听到我说的话了，安妮，不是吗？现在脱掉靴子去睡觉吧。已经八点多了。”

paragraphs.en: "There's just one more thing, Marilla," said Anne, with the air of producing the last shot in her locker. "Mrs. Barry told Diana that we might sleep in the spare-room bed. Think of the honor of your little Anne being put in the spare-room bed."
paragraphs.zh: “还有一件事，玛丽拉，”安妮说道，神情像是在储物柜里打出最后一枪。 “巴里夫人告诉戴安娜，我们可以睡在备用房间的床上。想想你的小安妮被放在备用房间的床上是多么荣幸。”

paragraphs.en: "It's an honor you'll have to get along without. Go to bed, Anne, and don't let me hear another word out of you."
paragraphs.zh: “这是一种荣誉，你必须在没有它的情况下相处。去睡觉吧，安妮，别让我听到你再说一个字。”

paragraphs.en: When Anne, with tears rolling over her cheeks, had gone sorrowfully upstairs, Matthew, who had been apparently sound asleep on the lounge during the whole dialogue, opened his eyes and said decidedly:
paragraphs.zh: 当安妮泪流满面，悲伤地上楼时，整个对话过程中一直在休息室熟睡的马修睁开了眼睛，斩钉截铁地说：

paragraphs.en: "Well now, Marilla, I think you ought to let Anne go."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，玛丽拉，我认为你应该让安妮走。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't then," retorted Marilla. "Who's bringing this child up, Matthew, you or me?"
paragraphs.zh: “那么我不知道，”玛丽拉反驳道。 “谁抚养这个孩子，马修，你还是我？”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, you," admitted Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你，”马修承认道。

paragraphs.en: "Don't interfere then."
paragraphs.zh: “那就别插手了。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I ain't interfering. It ain't interfering to have your own opinion. And my opinion is that you ought to let Anne go."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不会干涉。你有自己的意见也不会干涉。我的意见是你应该让安妮走。”

paragraphs.en: "You'd think I ought to let Anne go to the moon if she took the notion, I've no doubt" was Marilla's amiable rejoinder. "I might have let her spend the night with Diana, if that was all. But I don't approve of this concert plan. She'd go there and catch cold like as not, and have her head filled up with nonsense and excitement. It would unsettle her for a week. I understand that child's disposition and what's good for it better than you, Matthew."
paragraphs.zh: “如果安妮接受这个想法，你会认为我应该让她去月球，我毫不怀疑”，马里拉和蔼可亲地反驳道。 “如果仅此而已，我可能会让她和戴安娜一起过夜。但我不赞成这个音乐会计划。她去那里会像不感冒一样，脑子里充满了胡言乱语和兴奋。这会让她不安一个星期。我比你更了解那个孩子的性格和好处，马修。”

paragraphs.en: "I think you ought to let Anne go," repeated Matthew firmly. Argument was not his strong point, but holding fast to his opinion certainly was. Marilla gave a gasp of helplessness and took refuge in silence. The next morning, when Anne was washing the breakfast dishes in the pantry, Matthew paused on his way out to the barn to say to Marilla again:
paragraphs.zh: “我认为你应该让安妮走。”马修坚定地重复道。争论不是他的强项，但坚持自己的观点无疑是他的强项。玛丽拉无奈地叹了口气，默默地躲了起来。第二天早上，当安妮在食品储藏室洗早餐盘子时，马修在去谷仓的路上停下来再次对玛丽拉说：

paragraphs.en: "I think you ought to let Anne go, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “我认为你应该让安妮走，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: For a moment Marilla looked things not lawful to be uttered. Then she yielded to the inevitable and said tartly:
paragraphs.zh: 一时之间，玛丽拉似乎有些话不该说出口。然后她就屈服了，尖酸刻薄地说：

paragraphs.en: "Very well, she can go, since nothing else'll please you."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，她可以走了，因为没有什么能让你高兴了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne flew out of the pantry, dripping dishcloth in hand.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮飞出了食品储藏室，手里拿着滴着水的抹布。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, Marilla, say those blessed words again."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，玛丽拉，再说一遍那些神圣的话语。”

paragraphs.en: "I guess once is enough to say them. This is Matthew's doings and I wash my hands of it. If you catch pneumonia sleeping in a strange bed or coming out of that hot hall in the middle of the night, don't blame me, blame Matthew. Anne Shirley, you're dripping greasy water all over the floor. I never saw such a careless child."
paragraphs.zh: “我想说一次就够了。这是马修的所作所为，我不会这么做。如果你睡在陌生的床上或者半夜从那个炎热的大厅里出来得了肺炎，别怪我，怪马修。安妮·雪莉，你把油腻的水滴了一地。我从来没有见过这么粗心的孩子。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I know I'm a great trial to you, Marilla," said Anne repentantly. "I make so many mistakes. But then just think of all the mistakes I don't make, although I might. I'll get some sand and scrub up the spots before I go to school. Oh, Marilla, my heart was just set on going to that concert. I never was to a concert in my life, and when the other girls talk about them in school I feel so out of it. You didn't know just how I felt about it, but you see Matthew did. Matthew understands me, and it's so nice to be understood, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我知道我对你来说是一个很大的考验，玛丽拉，”安妮悔恨地说。 “我犯了很多错误。但想想我不会犯的所有错误，尽管我可能会犯。在上学之前，我会拿一些沙子擦掉那些地方。哦，玛丽拉，我的心就是要去那场音乐会。我一生中从未听过音乐会，当其他女孩在学校谈论这些错误时，我感到很不舒服。你不知道我对此有何感受，但你看到马修做到了。马修理解我，很高兴理解吧，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: Anne was too excited to do herself justice as to lessons that morning in school. Gilbert Blythe spelled her down in class and left her clear out of sight in mental arithmetic. Anne's consequent humiliation was less than it might have been, however, in view of the concert and the spare-room bed. She and Diana talked so constantly about it all day that with a stricter teacher than Mr. Phillips dire disgrace must inevitably have been their portion.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮太兴奋了，无法公正地对待那天早上在学校的课程。吉尔伯特·布莱斯（Gilbert Blythe）在课堂上拼出了她的名字，并在心算中让她远离了视线。然而，考虑到音乐会和空余的床位，安妮因此受到的羞辱并没有想象中那么严重。她和戴安娜整天不停地谈论这件事，如果老师比菲利普斯先生更严格，他们必然会遭受可怕的耻辱。

paragraphs.en: Anne felt that she could not have borne it if she had not been going to the concert, for nothing else was discussed that day in school. The Avonlea Debating Club, which met fortnightly all winter, had had several smaller free entertainments; but this was to be a big affair, admission ten cents, in aid of the library. The Avonlea young people had been practicing for weeks, and all the scholars were especially interested in it by reason of older brothers and sisters who were going to take part. Everybody in school over nine years of age expected to go, except Carrie Sloane, whose father shared Marilla's opinions about small girls going out to night concerts. Carrie Sloane cried into her grammar all the afternoon and felt that life was not worth living.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮觉得如果她不去听音乐会她就无法忍受，因为那天学校里没有讨论任何其他事情。埃文利辩论俱乐部整个冬天每两周举行一次聚会，有几场规模较小的免费娱乐活动。但这是一件大事，入场费十美分，以资助图书馆。埃文利的年轻人已经练习了几个星期了，所有的学者都因为要参加的哥哥姐姐们而特别感兴趣。学校里九岁以上的每个人都希望去，除了凯丽·斯隆，她的父亲同意玛丽拉关于小女孩出去参加夜间音乐会的看法。凯莉·斯隆整个下午都在为她的语法哭泣，觉得生活不值得过。

paragraphs.en: For Anne the real excitement began with the dismissal of school and increased therefrom in crescendo until it reached to a crash of positive ecstasy in the concert itself. They had a "perfectly elegant tea;" and then came the delicious occupation of dressing in Diana's little room upstairs. Diana did Anne's front hair in the new pompadour style and Anne tied Diana's bows with the especial knack she possessed; and they experimented with at least half a dozen different ways of arranging their back hair. At last they were ready, cheeks scarlet and eyes glowing with excitement.
paragraphs.zh: 对于安妮来说，真正的兴奋始于学校放学，然后逐渐增强，直到音乐会本身达到了彻底的狂喜。他们喝了“非常优雅的茶”；然后就是在戴安娜楼上的小房间里穿衣服的美妙时光。戴安娜将安妮的前面的头发梳成了新的蓬巴杜风格，安妮则用她所拥有的特殊技巧为戴安娜打上了蝴蝶结。他们尝试了至少六种不同的方式来整理后背的头发。他们终于准备好了，脸颊猩红，眼睛里闪烁着兴奋的光芒。

paragraphs.en: True, Anne could not help a little pang when she contrasted her plain black tam and shapeless, tight-sleeved, homemade gray-cloth coat with Diana's jaunty fur cap and smart little jacket. But she remembered in time that she had an imagination and could use it.
paragraphs.zh: 确实，当安妮将她朴素的黑色Tam和不成形的紧身袖自制灰布外套与戴安娜活泼的毛皮帽和漂亮的小夹克形成鲜明对比时，她不禁感到有点痛苦。但她及时想起自己有想象力并且可以运用它。

paragraphs.en: Then Diana's cousins, the Murrays from Newbridge, came; they all crowded into the big pung sleigh, among straw and furry robes. Anne reveled in the drive to the hall, slipping along over the satin-smooth roads with the snow crisping under the runners. There was a magnificent sunset, and the snowy hills and deep-blue water of the St. Lawrence Gulf seemed to rim in the splendor like a huge bowl of pearl and sapphire brimmed with wine and fire. Tinkles of sleigh bells and distant laughter, that seemed like the mirth of wood elves, came from every quarter.
paragraphs.zh: 然后戴安娜的表兄弟，来自纽布里奇的默里一家也来了。他们全都挤进大彭雪橇，穿着稻草和毛茸茸的长袍。安妮陶醉在开车去大厅的路上，在光滑的道路上滑行，雪在跑步者的脚下嘎吱作响。夕阳西下，白雪皑皑的山峦和圣劳伦斯湾深蓝色的海水，仿佛盛满了酒和火的珍珠和蓝宝石的大碗，周围金碧辉煌。雪橇铃的叮当声和远处的笑声，仿佛木精灵的欢笑，从四面八方传来。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Diana," breathed Anne, squeezing Diana's mittened hand under the fur robe, "isn't it all like a beautiful dream? Do I really look the same as usual? I feel so different that it seems to me it must show in my looks."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，戴安娜，”安妮喘着气，将戴安娜戴手套的手捏在毛皮长袍下，“这一切不是像一场美丽的梦吗？我看起来真的和平常一样吗？我感觉如此不同，在我看来，这必须表现在我的外表上。”

paragraphs.en: "You look awfully nice," said Diana, who having just received a compliment from one of her cousins, felt that she ought to pass it on. "You've got the loveliest color."
paragraphs.zh: “你看起来非常好，”戴安娜说，她刚刚收到了她的一个表兄弟的赞美，觉得她应该把它传递下去。 “你有最可爱的颜色。”

paragraphs.en: The program that night was a series of "thrills" for at least one listener in the audience, and, as Anne assured Diana, every succeeding thrill was thrillier than the last. When Prissy Andrews, attired in a new pink-silk waist with a string of pearls about her smooth white throat and real carnations in her hair—rumor whispered that the master had sent all the way to town for them for her—"climbed the slimy ladder, dark without one ray of light," Anne shivered in luxurious sympathy; when the choir sang "Far Above the Gentle Daisies" Anne gazed at the ceiling as if it were frescoed with angels; when Sam Sloane proceeded to explain and illustrate "How Sockery Set a Hen" Anne laughed until people sitting near her laughed too, more out of sympathy with her than with amusement at a selection that was rather threadbare even in Avonlea; and when Mr. Phillips gave Mark Antony's oration over the dead body of Caesar in the most heart-stirring tones—looking at Prissy Andrews at the end of every sentence—Anne felt that she could rise and mutiny on the spot if but one Roman citizen led the way.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上的节目对观众中的至少一位听众来说是一系列的“刺激”，而且正如安妮向戴安娜保证的那样，每一次后续的刺激都比上一次更刺激。当普莉西·安德鲁斯穿着新的粉红色丝绸腰装，光滑白皙的喉咙上挂着一串珍珠，头发上插着真正的康乃馨时——有传言说主人派了千里迢迢到城里来接她——“爬上那条黏糊糊的梯子，漆黑一片，没有一丝光亮”，安妮在奢华的同情中颤抖着；当唱诗班唱起《远在温柔的雏菊之上》时，安妮凝视着天花板，仿佛天花板上画着天使。当萨姆·斯隆开始解释和说明“袜子如何养母鸡”时，安妮笑了，直到坐在她旁边的人也笑了，更多的是出于对她的同情，而不是对即使在埃文利也相当陈旧的选择感到高兴；当菲利普斯先生用最激动人心的语气向马克·安东尼发表关于凯撒尸体的演说时——每句话末尾都看着普里西·安德鲁斯——安妮觉得，只要有一个罗马公民带路，她就可以当场起义叛变。

paragraphs.en: Only one number on the program failed to interest her. When Gilbert Blythe recited "Bingen on the Rhine" Anne picked up Rhoda Murray's library book and read it until he had finished, when she sat rigidly stiff and motionless while Diana clapped her hands until they tingled.
paragraphs.zh: 节目中只有一个数字未能引起她的兴趣。当吉尔伯特·布莱斯背诵《莱茵河畔的宾根》时，安妮拿起罗达·默里在图书馆的书，读完，直到他读完，她僵硬地坐着，一动不动，而戴安娜则拍着手，直到感到刺痛。

paragraphs.en: It was eleven when they got home, sated with dissipation, but with the exceeding sweet pleasure of talking it all over still to come. Everybody seemed asleep and the house was dark and silent. Anne and Diana tiptoed into the parlor, a long narrow room out of which the spare room opened. It was pleasantly warm and dimly lighted by the embers of a fire in the grate.
paragraphs.zh: 他们回到家时已是十一点了，他们已经满足了放纵的心情，但还有一种无比甜蜜的快乐，那就是谈论这一切。每个人似乎都睡着了，房子里漆黑一片，一片寂静。安妮和戴安娜蹑手蹑脚地走进客厅，这是一间狭长的房间，空房间通向客厅。炉排里的余烬照亮了房间，温暖宜人。

paragraphs.en: "Let's undress here," said Diana. "It's so nice and warm."
paragraphs.zh: “我们在这里脱衣服吧，”戴安娜说。 “真是太好了，太温暖了。”

paragraphs.en: "Hasn't it been a delightful time?" sighed Anne rapturously. "It must be splendid to get up and recite there. Do you suppose we will ever be asked to do it, Diana?"
paragraphs.zh: “这不是一段愉快的时光吗？”安妮欣喜若狂地叹了口气。 “站起来在那里朗诵一定很棒。你认为我们会被要求这样做吗，戴安娜？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, of course, someday. They're always wanting the big scholars to recite. Gilbert Blythe does often and he's only two years older than us. Oh, Anne, how could you pretend not to listen to him? When he came to the line,
paragraphs.zh: “是的，当然，有一天。他们总是想让大学者背诵。吉尔伯特·布莱斯经常背诵，而且他只比我们大两岁。哦，安妮，你怎么能假装不听他呢？当他来到队列时，

paragraphs.en: "There'S ANOTHER, not A SISTER,
paragraphs.zh: “还有另一个，不是姐妹，

paragraphs.en: he looked right down at you."
paragraphs.zh: 他正低头看着你。”

paragraphs.en: "Diana," said Anne with dignity, "you are my bosom friend, but I cannot allow even you to speak to me of that person. Are you ready for bed? Let's run a race and see who'll get to the bed first."
paragraphs.zh: “戴安娜，”安妮尊严地说，“你是我的知心朋友，但我连你都不允许跟我谈论那个人。你准备好睡觉了吗？我们来赛跑，看看谁先上床。”

paragraphs.en: The suggestion appealed to Diana. The two little white-clad figures flew down the long room, through the spare-room door, and bounded on the bed at the same moment. And then—something—moved beneath them, there was a gasp and a cry—and somebody said in muffled accents:
paragraphs.zh: 这个建议对戴安娜很有吸引力。两个白衣小人飞下长长的房间，穿过空房间的门，同时跳到了床上。然后——有什么东西——在他们下面移动，传来一声喘息和一声叫喊——有人用低沉的口音说道：

paragraphs.en: "Merciful goodness!"
paragraphs.zh: “仁慈的善良！”

paragraphs.en: Anne and Diana were never able to tell just how they got off that bed and out of the room. They only knew that after one frantic rush they found themselves tiptoeing shiveringly upstairs.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮和戴安娜始终无法说出她们是如何从床上下来并走出房间的。他们只知道，一阵疯狂的冲刺之后，他们发现自己颤抖着蹑手蹑脚地上了楼。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, who was it—WHAT was it?" whispered Anne, her teeth chattering with cold and fright.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，那是谁——那是什么？”安妮小声说道，她的牙齿因寒冷和恐惧而打颤。

paragraphs.en: "It was Aunt Josephine," said Diana, gasping with laughter. "Oh, Anne, it was Aunt Josephine, however she came to be there. Oh, and I know she will be furious. It's dreadful—it's really dreadful—but did you ever know anything so funny, Anne?"
paragraphs.zh: “是约瑟芬姨妈，”戴安娜说，笑得气喘吁吁。 “哦，安妮，那是约瑟芬姨妈，不管她是怎么来的。哦，我知道她会生气的。这太可怕了——真的太可怕了——但是你知道有什么这么有趣的事吗，安妮？”

paragraphs.en: "Who is your Aunt Josephine?"
paragraphs.zh: “你的约瑟芬姨妈是谁？”

paragraphs.en: "She's father's aunt and she lives in Charlottetown. She's awfully old—seventy anyhow—and I don't believe she was EVER a little girl. We were expecting her out for a visit, but not so soon. She's awfully prim and proper and she'll scold dreadfully about this, I know. Well, we'll have to sleep with Minnie May—and you can't think how she kicks."
paragraphs.zh: “她是父亲的姨妈，住在夏洛特敦。她已经很老了——反正七十岁了——而且我不相信她曾经是个小女孩。我们本来期待她出来拜访，但不会这么快。她非常拘谨和得体，我知道她会为此骂得很厉害。好吧，我们得和米妮·梅一起睡觉——你无法想象她踢得怎么样。”

paragraphs.en: Miss Josephine Barry did not appear at the early breakfast the next morning. Mrs. Barry smiled kindly at the two little girls.
paragraphs.zh: 约瑟芬·巴里小姐没有出现在第二天早上的早餐会上。巴里夫人对两个小女孩和蔼地微笑。

paragraphs.en: "Did you have a good time last night? I tried to stay awake until you came home, for I wanted to tell you Aunt Josephine had come and that you would have to go upstairs after all, but I was so tired I fell asleep. I hope you didn't disturb your aunt, Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “你昨晚玩得开心吗？我试着保持清醒直到你回家，因为我想告诉你约瑟芬姨妈来了，你毕竟得上楼了，但我太累了，睡着了。我希望你不要打扰你的姨妈戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: Diana preserved a discreet silence, but she and Anne exchanged furtive smiles of guilty amusement across the table. Anne hurried home after breakfast and so remained in blissful ignorance of the disturbance which presently resulted in the Barry household until the late afternoon, when she went down to Mrs. Lynde's on an errand for Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜保持着谨慎的沉默，但她和安妮隔着桌子偷偷地交换了一个内疚的微笑。安妮吃完早饭就匆匆回家，一直幸福地对巴里家不久前发生的骚乱一无所知，直到下午晚些时候，她才去林德太太家为马里拉办事。

paragraphs.en: "So you and Diana nearly frightened poor old Miss Barry to death last night?" said Mrs. Lynde severely, but with a twinkle in her eye. "Mrs. Barry was here a few minutes ago on her way to Carmody. She's feeling real worried over it. Old Miss Barry was in a terrible temper when she got up this morning—and Josephine Barry's temper is no joke, I can tell you that. She wouldn't speak to Diana at all."
paragraphs.zh: “所以昨晚你和戴安娜差点把可怜的老巴里小姐吓死了？”林德太太严厉地说，但眼睛里闪烁着光芒。 “巴里夫人几分钟前在去卡莫迪的路上来过这里。她对此感到非常担心。老巴里小姐今天早上起床时脾气很糟糕——我可以告诉你，约瑟芬·巴里的脾气可不是开玩笑。她根本不和戴安娜说话。”

paragraphs.en: "It wasn't Diana's fault," said Anne contritely. "It was mine. I suggested racing to see who would get into bed first."
paragraphs.zh: “这不是戴安娜的错，”安妮懊悔地说。 “是我的。我建议比赛看谁先上床睡觉。”

paragraphs.en: "I knew it!" said Mrs. Lynde, with the exultation of a correct guesser. "I knew that idea came out of your head. Well, it's made a nice lot of trouble, that's what. Old Miss Barry came out to stay for a month, but she declares she won't stay another day and is going right back to town tomorrow, Sunday and all as it is. She'd have gone today if they could have taken her. She had promised to pay for a quarter's music lessons for Diana, but now she is determined to do nothing at all for such a tomboy. Oh, I guess they had a lively time of it there this morning. The Barrys must feel cut up. Old Miss Barry is rich and they'd like to keep on the good side of her.
