Of course, Mrs. Barry didn't say just that to me, but I'm a pretty good judge of human nature, that's what."
paragraphs.zh: “我就知道！”林德太太兴奋地说，就像猜对了一样。 “我知道这个想法是从你脑子里冒出来的。好吧，这惹了很多麻烦，就是这样。老巴里小姐出来要住一个月，但她说她不会再呆一天了，明天周日就回城了。如果他们能带她去的话，她今天就走了。她本来答应为戴安娜支付四分之一的音乐课费用，但现在她决定不为这样一个假小子做任何事。哦，我想今天早上他们在那里度过了一段愉快的时光，老巴里小姐一定很富有，他们想继续对她好的一面。当然，巴里夫人没有对我这么说，但我对人性有很好的判断力，就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm such an unlucky girl," mourned Anne. "I'm always getting into scrapes myself and getting my best friends—people I'd shed my heart's blood for—into them too. Can you tell me why it is so, Mrs. Lynde?"
paragraphs.zh: “我真是个不幸的女孩，”安妮哀悼道。 “我自己总是陷入困境，也让我最好的朋友——那些我为之流血的人——也陷入困境。林德夫人，你能告诉我为什么会这样吗？”

paragraphs.en: "It's because you're too heedless and impulsive, child, that's what. You never stop to think—whatever comes into your head to say or do you say or do it without a moment's reflection."
paragraphs.zh: “Its because youre too heedless and impulsive, child, thats what. You never stop to think—whatever comes into your head to say or do you say or do it without a moments reflection.。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, but that's the best of it," protested Anne. "Something just flashes into your mind, so exciting, and you must out with it. If you stop to think it over you spoil it all. Haven't you never felt that yourself, Mrs. Lynde?"
paragraphs.zh: “Oh, but thats the best of it, protested Anne. Something just flashes into your mind, so exciting, and you must out with it. If you stop to think it over you spoil it all. Havent you never felt that yourself, Mrs. Lynde?。”

paragraphs.en: No, Mrs. Lynde had not. She shook her head sagely.
paragraphs.zh: No, Mrs. Lynde had not. She shook her head sagely.。

paragraphs.en: "You must learn to think a little, Anne, that's what. The proverb you need to go by is 'Look before you leap'—especially into spare-room beds."
paragraphs.zh: “You must learn to think a little, Anne, thats what. The proverb you need to go by is Look before you leap—especially into spare-room beds.。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Lynde laughed comfortably over her mild joke, but Anne remained pensive. She saw nothing to laugh at in the situation, which to her eyes appeared very serious. When she left Mrs. Lynde's she took her way across the crusted fields to Orchard Slope. Diana met her at the kitchen door.
paragraphs.zh: Mrs. Lynde laughed comfortably over her mild joke, but Anne remained pensive. She saw nothing to laugh at in the situation, which to her eyes appeared very serious. When she left Mrs. Lyndes she took her way across the crusted fields to Orchard Slope. Diana met her at the kitchen door.。

paragraphs.en: "Your Aunt Josephine was very cross about it, wasn't she?" whispered Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “Your Aunt Josephine was very cross about it, wasnt she? whispered Anne.。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes," answered Diana, stifling a giggle with an apprehensive glance over her shoulder at the closed sitting-room door. "She was fairly dancing with rage, Anne. Oh, how she scolded. She said I was the worst-behaved girl she ever saw and that my parents ought to be ashamed of the way they had brought me up. She says she won't stay and I'm sure I don't care. But Father and Mother do."
paragraphs.zh: “Yes, answered Diana, stifling a giggle with an apprehensive glance over her shoulder at the closed sitting-room door. She was fairly dancing with rage, Anne. Oh, how she scolded. She said I was the worst-behaved girl she ever saw and that my parents ought to be ashamed of the way they had brought me up. She says she wont stay and Im sure I dont care. But Father and Mother do.。”

paragraphs.en: "Why didn't you tell them it was my fault?" demanded Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “Why didnt you tell them it was my fault? demanded Anne.。”

paragraphs.en: "It's likely I'd do such a thing, isn't it?" said Diana with just scorn. "I'm no telltale, Anne Shirley, and anyhow I was just as much to blame as you."
paragraphs.zh: “Its likely Id do such a thing, isnt it? said Diana with just scorn. Im no telltale, Anne Shirley, and anyhow I was just as much to blame as you.。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I'm going in to tell her myself," said Anne resolutely.
paragraphs.zh: “Well, Im going in to tell her myself, said Anne resolutely.。”

paragraphs.en: Diana stared.
paragraphs.zh: Diana stared.。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, you'd never! why—she'll eat you alive!"
paragraphs.zh: “Anne Shirley, youd never! why—shell eat you alive!。”

paragraphs.en: "Don't frighten me any more than I am frightened," implored Anne. "I'd rather walk up to a cannon's mouth. But I've got to do it, Diana. It was my fault and I've got to confess. I've had practice in confessing, fortunately."
paragraphs.zh: “Dont frighten me any more than I am frightened, implored Anne. Id rather walk up to a cannons mouth. But Ive got to do it, Diana. It was my fault and Ive got to confess. Ive had practice in confessing, fortunately.。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, she's in the room," said Diana. "You can go in if you want to. I wouldn't dare. And I don't believe you'll do a bit of good."
paragraphs.zh: “Well, shes in the room, said Diana. You can go in if you want to. I wouldnt dare. And I dont believe youll do a bit of good.。”

paragraphs.en: With this encouragement Anne bearded the lion in its den—that is to say, walked resolutely up to the sitting-room door and knocked faintly. A sharp "Come in" followed.
paragraphs.zh: With this encouragement Anne bearded the lion in its den—that is to say, walked resolutely up to the sitting-room door and knocked faintly. A sharp Come in followed.。

paragraphs.en: Miss Josephine Barry, thin, prim, and rigid, was knitting fiercely by the fire, her wrath quite unappeased and her eyes snapping through her gold-rimmed glasses. She wheeled around in her chair, expecting to see Diana, and beheld a white-faced girl whose great eyes were brimmed up with a mixture of desperate courage and shrinking terror.
paragraphs.zh: Miss Josephine Barry, thin, prim, and rigid, was knitting fiercely by the fire, her wrath quite unappeased and her eyes snapping through her gold-rimmed glasses. She wheeled around in her chair, expecting to see Diana, and beheld a white-faced girl whose great eyes were brimmed up with a mixture of desperate courage and shrinking terror.。

paragraphs.en: "Who are you?" demanded Miss Josephine Barry, without ceremony.
paragraphs.zh: “Who are you? demanded Miss Josephine Barry, without ceremony.。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm Anne of Green Gables," said the small visitor tremulously, clasping her hands with her characteristic gesture, "and I've come to confess, if you please."
paragraphs.zh: “Im Anne of Green Gables, said the small visitor tremulously, clasping her hands with her characteristic gesture, and Ive come to confess, if you please.。”

paragraphs.en: "Confess what?"
paragraphs.zh: “Confess what?。”

paragraphs.en: "That it was all my fault about jumping into bed on you last night. I suggested it. Diana would never have thought of such a thing, I am sure. Diana is a very ladylike girl, Miss Barry. So you must see how unjust it is to blame her."
paragraphs.zh: “That it was all my fault about jumping into bed on you last night. I suggested it. Diana would never have thought of such a thing, I am sure. Diana is a very ladylike girl, Miss Barry. So you must see how unjust it is to blame her.。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"
paragraphs.zh: “Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!。”

paragraphs.en: "But we were only in fun," persisted Anne. "I think you ought to forgive us, Miss Barry, now that we've apologized. And anyhow, please forgive Diana and let her have her music lessons. Diana's heart is set on her music lessons, Miss Barry, and I know too well what it is to set your heart on a thing and not get it. If you must be cross with anyone, be cross with me. I've been so used in my early days to having people cross at me that I can endure it much better than Diana can."
paragraphs.zh: “但我们只是为了好玩，”安妮坚持说。 “巴里小姐，既然我们已经道歉了，我想你应该原谅我们，巴里小姐。不管怎样，请原谅戴安娜，让她上音乐课。戴安娜全心全意地上音乐课，巴里小姐，我太清楚什么是一心一意却得不到它。如果你一定要生谁的气，那就生我的气吧。我早年已经习惯了别人对我发脾气，所以我比戴安娜更能忍受。”

paragraphs.en: Much of the snap had gone out of the old lady's eyes by this time and was replaced by a twinkle of amused interest. But she still said severely:
paragraphs.zh: 这时，老太太眼中的怒气已经消失了，取而代之的是一抹有趣的兴趣。但她还是严肃地说：

paragraphs.en: "I don't think it is any excuse for you that you were only in fun. Little girls never indulged in that kind of fun when I was young. You don't know what it is to be awakened out of a sound sleep, after a long and arduous journey, by two great girls coming bounce down on you."
paragraphs.zh: “我不认为你只是为了好玩而成为你的借口。我年轻的时候，小女孩从来没有沉迷于这种乐趣。你不知道在经过漫长而艰辛的旅程后，被两个伟大的女孩扑向你，从熟睡中惊醒是什么感觉。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't KNOW, but I can IMAGINE," said Anne eagerly. "I'm sure it must have been very disturbing. But then, there is our side of it too. Have you any imagination, Miss Barry? If you have, just put yourself in our place. We didn't know there was anybody in that bed and you nearly scared us to death. It was simply awful the way we felt. And then we couldn't sleep in the spare room after being promised. I suppose you are used to sleeping in spare rooms. But just imagine what you would feel like if you were a little orphan girl who had never had such an honor."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，但我可以想象，”安妮急切地说。 “我确信这一定非常令人不安。但是，这也有我们的一面。你有想象力吗，巴里小姐？如果你有的话，就把你自己放在我们的位置上。我们不知道那张床上有人，你几乎把我们吓死了。我们的感觉简直太糟糕了。然后我们在得到承诺后就不能睡在空房间里了。我想你已经习惯了睡在空房间里。但是想象一下，如果你是一个从来没有睡过的小孤儿，你会感觉怎么样？有这样的荣幸。”

paragraphs.en: All the snap had gone by this time. Miss Barry actually laughed—a sound which caused Diana, waiting in speechless anxiety in the kitchen outside, to give a great gasp of relief.
paragraphs.zh: 此时所有的快照都已经消失了。巴里小姐真的笑了——这声音让黛安娜在外面厨房里焦急得说不出话来，这才松了一口气。

paragraphs.en: "I'm afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it's so long since I used it," she said. "I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself."
paragraphs.zh: “恐怕我的想象力有点生锈了——我已经很久没有使用它了，”她说。 “我敢说你的同情心和我的一样强烈。这完全取决于我们看待它的方式。坐下来告诉我你自己。”

paragraphs.en: "I am very sorry I can't," said Anne firmly. "I would like to, because you seem like an interesting lady, and you might even be a kindred spirit although you don't look very much like it. But it is my duty to go home to Miss Marilla Cuthbert. Miss Marilla Cuthbert is a very kind lady who has taken me to bring up properly. She is doing her best, but it is very discouraging work. You must not blame her because I jumped on the bed. But before I go I do wish you would tell me if you will forgive Diana and stay just as long as you meant to in Avonlea."
paragraphs.zh: “很抱歉我不能，”安妮坚定地说。 “我愿意，因为你看上去是一位有趣的女士，而且你们甚至可能是志同道合的人，尽管你们看起来不太像。但我有责任回家见玛丽拉·卡斯伯特小姐。玛丽拉·卡斯伯特小姐是一位非常善良的女士，她把我好好地抚养长大。她正在尽力而为，但这真是令人沮丧的工作。你不能因为我跳到床上而责怪她。但在我走之前，我真希望你能告诉我你是否会原谅戴安娜并留下来。只要你想在埃文利就可以。”

paragraphs.en: "I think perhaps I will if you will come over and talk to me occasionally," said Miss Barry.
paragraphs.zh: “我想也许我会的，如果你偶尔过来跟我说话的话，”巴里小姐说。

paragraphs.en: That evening Miss Barry gave Diana a silver bangle bracelet and told the senior members of the household that she had unpacked her valise.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，巴里小姐送给戴安娜一条银手镯，并告诉家里的高级成员，她已经打开了她的手提箱。

paragraphs.en: "I've made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl," she said frankly. "She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity."
paragraphs.zh: “我决定留下来，只是为了能更好地了解那个安妮姑娘。”她坦言。 “她让我很有趣，在我这个年纪，有趣的人是很少见的。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla's only comment when she heard the story was, "I told you so." This was for Matthew's benefit.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉听到这个故事时唯一的评论是：“我告诉过你了。”这是为了马太的利益。

paragraphs.en: Miss Barry stayed her month out and over. She was a more agreeable guest than usual, for Anne kept her in good humor. They became firm friends.
paragraphs.zh: 巴里小姐一连住了一个月。她是一位比平时更讨人喜欢的客人，因为安妮让她保持着良好的幽默感。他们成了坚定的朋友。

paragraphs.en: When Miss Barry went away she said:
paragraphs.zh: 巴里小姐走后她说：

paragraphs.en: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you're to visit me and I'll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."
paragraphs.zh: “记住，你这个安妮女孩，当你来到城里时，你要来看我，我会把你放在我最宽敞的备用床上睡觉。”

paragraphs.en: "Miss Barry was a kindred spirit, after all," Anne confided to Marilla. "You wouldn't think so to look at her, but she is. You don't find it right out at first, as in Matthew's case, but after a while you come to see it. Kindred spirits are not so scarce as I used to think. It's splendid to find out there are so many of them in the world."
paragraphs.zh: “毕竟，巴里小姐是志同道合的人，”安妮向玛丽拉吐露心声。 “看着她你不会这么认为，但她确实如此。你一开始并没有像马修那样立即发现这一点，但过了一段时间你就会发现这一点。志同道合的人并不像我以前想象的那么稀缺。发现世界上有这么多这样的人真是太棒了。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 20 章：走入歧途的丰富想象力

paragraphs.en: Spring had come once more to Green Gables—the beautiful capricious, reluctant Canadian spring, lingering along through April and May in a succession of sweet, fresh, chilly days, with pink sunsets and miracles of resurrection and growth. The maples in Lover's Lane were red budded and little curly ferns pushed up around the Dryad's Bubble. Away up in the barrens, behind Mr. Silas Sloane's place, the Mayflowers blossomed out, pink and white stars of sweetness under their brown leaves. All the school girls and boys had one golden afternoon gathering them, coming home in the clear, echoing twilight with arms and baskets full of flowery spoil.
paragraphs.zh: 春天再次来到了绿山墙——美丽的、反复无常的、不情愿的加拿大春天，在四月和五月中持续存在，伴随着一系列甜蜜、新鲜、寒冷的日子，伴随着粉红色的日落和复活和生长的奇迹。情人巷里的枫树已经发出了红色的芽，树妖泡泡周围长满了卷曲的小蕨类植物。远处的荒原上，在塞拉斯·斯隆先生住处的后面，五月花绽放了，棕色的叶子下绽放着粉色和白色的甜蜜星星。所有的男女学生都度过了一个金色的下午，他们在晴朗的暮色中带着手臂和装满鲜花的篮子回家。

paragraphs.en: "I'm so sorry for people who live in lands where there are no Mayflowers," said Anne. "Diana says perhaps they have something better, but there couldn't be anything better than Mayflowers, could there, Marilla? And Diana says if they don't know what they are like they don't miss them. But I think that is the saddest thing of all. I think it would be TRAGIC, Marilla, not to know what Mayflowers are like and NOT to miss them. Do you know what I think Mayflowers are, Marilla? I think they must be the souls of the flowers that died last summer and this is their heaven. But we had a splendid time today, Marilla. We had our lunch down in a big mossy hollow by an old well—such a ROMANTIC spot. Charlie Sloane dared Arty Gillis to jump over it, and Arty did because he wouldn't take a dare. Nobody would in school. It is very FASHIONABLE to dare. Mr. Phillips gave all the Mayflowers he found to Prissy Andrews and I heard him to say 'sweets to the sweet.' He got that out of a book, I know; but it shows he has some imagination. I was offered some Mayflowers too, but I rejected them with scorn. I can't tell you the person's name because I have vowed never to let it cross my lips. We made wreaths of the Mayflowers and put them on our hats; and when the time came to go home we marched in procession down the road, two by two, with our bouquets and wreaths, singing 'My Home on the Hill.' Oh, it was so thrilling, Marilla. All Mr. Silas Sloane's folks rushed out to see us and everybody we met on the road stopped and stared after us. We made a real sensation."
paragraphs.zh: “我对生活在没有五月花号的土地上的人们感到非常抱歉，”安妮说。 “戴安娜说也许他们有更好的东西，但没有比五月花更好的东西了，不是吗，玛丽拉？戴安娜说，如果他们不知道自己是什么样子，就不会想念他们。但我认为这是最悲伤的事情。我认为，玛丽拉，如果不知道五月花是什么样子，也不怀念它们，那将是悲剧。你知道我认为五月花是什么吗，玛丽拉？我认为它们一定是那些死去的花朵的灵魂。去年夏天，这里是他们的天堂。玛丽拉，我们在一个长满青苔的大洼地里吃午饭，查理·斯隆向阿蒂·吉利斯提出了挑战，因为他在学校里不敢这么做。菲利普斯先生把他找到的所有五月花都送给了普里西·安德鲁斯，这真是太时髦了。 “甜到甜。”我知道，他是从书里学来的；但这表明他有一定的想象力。有人还向我提供了一些五月花，但我轻蔑地拒绝了。我不能告诉你这个人的名字，因为我发誓永远不会让这个名字出现在我的嘴边。我们用五月花制作了花环，把它们戴在帽子上；回家的时间到了，我们带着花束和花圈，两个两个地沿着路游行，唱着“我的山上的家”。哦，太令人兴奋了，玛丽拉。塞拉斯·斯隆先生的所有家人都冲出来看我们，我们在路上遇到的每个人都停下来盯着我们看。我们确实引起了轰动。”

paragraphs.en: "Not much wonder! Such silly doings!" was Marilla's response.
paragraphs.zh: “不足为奇！如此愚蠢的行为！”这是玛丽拉的回应。

paragraphs.en: After the Mayflowers came the violets, and Violet Vale was empurpled with them. Anne walked through it on her way to school with reverent steps and worshiping eyes, as if she trod on holy ground.
paragraphs.zh: 继五月花之后，又迎来了紫罗兰，整个紫罗兰谷都被它们染上了紫色。安妮在上学的路上迈着虔诚的步伐和崇拜的目光走过这里，仿佛踏在圣地上。

paragraphs.en: "Somehow," she told Diana, "when I'm going through here I don't really care whether Gil—whether anybody gets ahead of me in class or not. But when I'm up in school it's all different and I care as much as ever. There's such a lot of different Annes in me. I sometimes think that is why I'm such a troublesome person. If I was just the one Anne it would be ever so much more comfortable, but then it wouldn't be half so interesting."
paragraphs.zh: “不知何故，”她告诉戴安娜，“当我经过这里时，我并不真正关心吉尔是否在课堂上领先于我。但当我上学时，一切都不同了，我一如既往地关心。我身上有很多不同的安妮。有时我想这就是为什么我是一个如此麻烦的人。如果我只是一个安妮，那就会舒服得多，但那就不会那么有趣了。”

paragraphs.en: One June evening, when the orchards were pink blossomed again, when the frogs were singing silverly sweet in the marshes about the head of the Lake of Shining Waters, and the air was full of the savor of clover fields and balsamic fir woods, Anne was sitting by her gable window. She had been studying her lessons, but it had grown too dark to see the book, so she had fallen into wide-eyed reverie, looking out past the boughs of the Snow Queen, once more bestarred with its tufts of blossom.
paragraphs.zh: 六月的一个傍晚，当果园再次绽放粉红色的花朵，当青蛙在闪亮湖畔的沼泽地里唱着银铃般甜美的歌声，空气中充满了三叶草田和香脂冷杉林的香味时，安妮正坐在她的山墙窗边。她一直在学习功课，但天色太暗了，看不清书本，所以她陷入了睁大眼睛的沉思，眺望着冰雪女王的树枝，那里再次布满了一簇簇花朵。

paragraphs.en: In all essential respects the little gable chamber was unchanged. The walls were as white, the pincushion as hard, the chairs as stiffly and yellowly upright as ever. Yet the whole character of the room was altered. It was full of a new vital, pulsing personality that seemed to pervade it and to be quite independent of schoolgirl books and dresses and ribbons, and even of the cracked blue jug full of apple blossoms on the table. It was as if all the dreams, sleeping and waking, of its vivid occupant had taken a visible although unmaterial form and had tapestried the bare room with splendid filmy tissues of rainbow and moonshine. Presently Marilla came briskly in with some of Anne's freshly ironed school aprons. She hung them over a chair and sat down with a short sigh. She had had one of her headaches that afternoon, and although the pain had gone she felt weak and "tuckered out," as she expressed it. Anne looked at her with eyes limpid with sympathy.
paragraphs.zh: 小山墙室在所有重要方面都没有改变。墙壁一如既往地洁白，针垫一如既往地坚硬，椅子也一如既往地僵硬、呈黄色。然而房间的整体特征却发生了改变。它充满了一种新的、充满活力、脉动的个性，似乎弥漫在其中，完全独立于女学生的书籍、裙子和丝带，甚至独立于桌子上装满苹果花的蓝色裂罐。就好像它生动的居住者的所有梦境，无论是睡着的还是醒着的，都采取了一种可见但非物质的形式，并用彩虹和月光的绚丽的薄薄的薄纸挂满了这个空荡荡的房间。不久，玛丽拉拿着安妮刚熨好的学校围裙快步走了进来。她把它们挂在椅子上，然后短促地叹了口气坐下。那天下午，她出现了一次头痛，虽然疼痛已经消失，但正如她所说，她感到虚弱，“精神不振”。安妮看着她，眼神清澈，充满同情。

paragraphs.en: "I do truly wish I could have had the headache in your place, Marilla. I would have endured it joyfully for your sake."
paragraphs.zh: “我真的希望我能代替你承受头痛，玛丽拉。为了你，我会愉快地忍受它。”

paragraphs.en: "I guess you did your part in attending to the work and letting me rest," said Marilla. "You seem to have got on fairly well and made fewer mistakes than usual. Of course it wasn't exactly necessary to starch Matthew's handkerchiefs! And most people when they put a pie in the oven to warm up for dinner take it out and eat it when it gets hot instead of leaving it to be burned to a crisp. But that doesn't seem to be your way evidently."
paragraphs.zh: “我想你尽了自己的一份力，专注于工作并让我休息，”马里拉说。 “你似乎相处得很好，犯的错误也比平时少了。当然，没有必要给马修的手帕上浆！而且大多数人在把馅饼放进烤箱加热准备晚餐时，都会在热的时候拿出来吃，而不是让它被烧焦。但这显然不是你的方式。”

paragraphs.en: Headaches always left Marilla somewhat sarcastic.
paragraphs.zh: 头痛总是让玛丽拉有些讽刺。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm so sorry," said Anne penitently. "I never thought about that pie from the moment I put it in the oven till now, although I felt INSTINCTIVELY that there was something missing on the dinner table. I was firmly resolved, when you left me in charge this morning, not to imagine anything, but keep my thoughts on facts. I did pretty well until I put the pie in, and then an irresistible temptation came to me to imagine I was an enchanted princess shut up in a lonely tower with a handsome knight riding to my rescue on a coal-black steed. So that is how I came to forget the pie. I didn't know I starched the handkerchiefs. All the time I was ironing I was trying to think of a name for a new island Diana and I have discovered up the brook. It's the most ravishing spot, Marilla. There are two maple trees on it and the brook flows right around it. At last it struck me that it would be splendid to call it Victoria Island because we found it on the Queen's birthday. Both Diana and I are very loyal. But I'm sorry about that pie and the handkerchiefs. I wanted to be extra good today because it's an anniversary. Do you remember what happened this day last year, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我很抱歉，”安妮悔恨地说。 “从我把馅饼放进烤箱的那一刻起，直到现在，我从来没有想过那个馅饼，尽管我本能地感觉到餐桌上缺少了一些东西。今天早上，当你让我负责的时候，我下定决心，不要想象任何事情，而要把我的想法放在事实上。我做得很好，直到我把馅饼放进去，然后一种不可抗拒的诱惑向我袭来，想象我是一位被施了魔法的公主，被关在一座孤独的塔楼里，有一位英俊的骑士骑着一辆煤黑色的车来营救我。就这样，我忘记了我在熨烫手帕的过程中，一直在想一个新的岛屿的名字：黛安娜，我发现这是最迷人的地方，玛丽拉，上面有两棵枫树，溪流就在它周围。戴安娜和我都很忠诚，但我对今天的馅饼和手帕感到很抱歉，因为这是周年纪念日。”

paragraphs.en: "No, I can't think of anything special."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我想不出有什么特别的。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, it was the day I came to Green Gables. I shall never forget it. It was the turning point in my life. Of course it wouldn't seem so important to you. I've been here for a year and I've been so happy. Of course, I've had my troubles, but one can live down troubles. Are you sorry you kept me, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，那是我来到绿山墙的那一天。我永远不会忘记它。那是我人生的转折点。当然，这对你来说似乎不那么重要。我在这里已经一年了，我很高兴。当然，我也有过烦恼，但人可以忍受烦恼。你为留下我而感到遗憾吗，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: "No, I can't say I'm sorry," said Marilla, who sometimes wondered how she could have lived before Anne came to Green Gables, "no, not exactly sorry. If you've finished your lessons, Anne, I want you to run over and ask Mrs. Barry if she'll lend me Diana's apron pattern."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不能说对不起，”马里拉说，她有时会想，在安妮来到绿山墙之前她该如何生活，“不，不完全是对不起。如果你完成了课程，安妮，我希望你跑过去问巴里太太是否愿意借给我戴安娜的围裙图案。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh—it's—it's too dark," cried Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “哦——这——太黑了，”安妮叫道。

paragraphs.en: "Too dark? Why, it's only twilight. And goodness knows you've gone over often enough after dark."
paragraphs.zh: “太黑了？哎呀，这只是黄昏。天知道你已经经常在天黑后走过来了。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll go over early in the morning," said Anne eagerly. "I'll get up at sunrise and go over, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “我一早就过去。”安妮急切地说。 “我会在日出时起床过去，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: "What has got into your head now, Anne Shirley? I want that pattern to cut out your new apron this evening. Go at once and be smart too."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，你现在脑子里在想什么？今晚我想用这个图案剪出你的新围裙。马上去，也聪明点。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll have to go around by the road, then," said Anne, taking up her hat reluctantly.
paragraphs.zh: “那我就得绕路走了。”安妮不情愿地拿起帽子说道。

paragraphs.en: "Go by the road and waste half an hour! I'd like to catch you!"
paragraphs.zh: “沿着路走，浪费半个小时！我想抓住你！”

paragraphs.en: "I can't go through the Haunted Wood, Marilla," cried Anne desperately.
paragraphs.zh: “我不能穿过鬼林，玛丽拉，”安妮绝望地喊道。

paragraphs.en: Marilla stared.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉凝视着。

paragraphs.en: "The Haunted Wood! Are you crazy? What under the canopy is the Haunted Wood?"
paragraphs.zh: “鬼林！你疯了吗？天篷下面是什么鬼林？”

paragraphs.en: "The spruce wood over the brook," said Anne in a whisper.
paragraphs.zh: “小溪那边的云杉林，”安妮低声说道。

paragraphs.en: "Fiddlesticks! There is no such thing as a haunted wood anywhere. Who has been telling you such stuff?"
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道！世界上根本就没有闹鬼的森林这回事。谁告诉你这些事的？”

paragraphs.en: "Nobody," confessed Anne. "Diana and I just imagined the wood was haunted. All the places around here are so—so—COMMONPLACE. We just got this up for our own amusement. We began it in April. A haunted wood is so very romantic, Marilla. We chose the spruce grove because it's so gloomy. Oh, we have imagined the most harrowing things. There's a white lady walks along the brook just about this time of the night and wrings her hands and utters wailing cries. She appears when there is to be a death in the family. And the ghost of a little murdered child haunts the corner up by Idlewild; it creeps up behind you and lays its cold fingers on your hand—so. Oh, Marilla, it gives me a shudder to think of it. And there's a headless man stalks up and down the path and skeletons glower at you between the boughs. Oh, Marilla, I wouldn't go through the Haunted Wood after dark now for anything. I'd be sure that white things would reach out from behind the trees and grab me."
paragraphs.zh: “没有人，”安妮承认道。 “戴安娜和我只是想象这片树林闹鬼。这里周围的所有地方都那么——那么——平常。我们只是为了自己的娱乐而设计这个。我们从四月开始。闹鬼的树林非常浪漫，玛丽拉。我们选择云杉林，因为它太阴暗了。哦，我们想象了最痛苦的事情。大约在晚上的这个时候，有一位白人女士沿着小溪散步，扭着双手，当家里有人要死的时候，她就会出现，一个被谋杀的小孩子的鬼魂会在你身后悄悄出现，用冰冷的手指放在你的手上——所以，哦，玛丽拉，一想到这个，我就感到不寒而栗，还有一个无头男人在树枝间怒视着你。天黑后穿过闹鬼森林，我确信白色的东西会从树后伸出来抓住我。”

paragraphs.en: "Did ever anyone hear the like!" ejaculated Marilla, who had listened in dumb amazement. "Anne Shirley, do you mean to tell me you believe all that wicked nonsense of your own imagination?"
paragraphs.zh: “有没有人听过类似的话！”玛丽拉惊呼道，她听得目瞪口呆。 “安妮·雪莉，你的意思是告诉我你相信你自己想象的那些邪恶的废话吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Not believe EXACTLY," faltered Anne. "At least, I don't believe it in daylight. But after dark, Marilla, it's different. That is when ghosts walk."
paragraphs.zh: “不太相信，”安妮结结巴巴地说。 “至少，白天我不相信。但是天黑后，玛丽拉，情况就不同了。那是鬼魂行走的时候。”

paragraphs.en: "There are no such things as ghosts, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “世界上不存在鬼魂这样的东西，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, but there are, Marilla," cried Anne eagerly. "I know people who have seen them. And they are respectable people. Charlie Sloane says that his grandmother saw his grandfather driving home the cows one night after he'd been buried for a year. You know Charlie Sloane's grandmother wouldn't tell a story for anything. She's a very religious woman. And Mrs. Thomas's father was pursued home one night by a lamb of fire with its head cut off hanging by a strip of skin. He said he knew it was the spirit of his brother and that it was a warning he would die within nine days. He didn't, but he died two years after, so you see it was really true. And Ruby Gillis says—"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，但是有，玛丽拉，”安妮急切地喊道。 “我认识一些见过它们的人。他们都是受人尊敬的人。查理·斯隆说，他的祖母在他被埋葬一年后，有一天晚上看到他的祖父赶着牛回家。你知道查理·斯隆的祖母不会讲任何故事。她是一个非常虔诚的女人。托马斯夫人的父亲有一天晚上被一只火焰羔羊追赶回家，它的头被一条皮割下来。他说他知道那是他哥哥的灵魂，那是一个警告他会在九天内死去，但他没有，但两年后他就去世了，所以你看，这确实是真的，鲁比·吉利斯说——”

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley," interrupted Marilla firmly, "I never want to hear you talking in this fashion again. I've had my doubts about that imagination of yours right along, and if this is going to be the outcome of it, I won't countenance any such doings. You'll go right over to Barry's, and you'll go through that spruce grove, just for a lesson and a warning to you. And never let me hear a word out of your head about haunted woods again."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，”玛丽拉坚决地打断道，“我再也不想听到你用这种方式说话了。我一直对你的想象力表示怀疑，如果结果是这样的话，我不会支持任何这样的行为。你会直接去巴里家，你会穿过那片云杉林，只是为了给你一个教训和警告。永远不要让我听到你脑子里冒出来的任何一个字又是闹鬼的树林了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne might plead and cry as she liked—and did, for her terror was very real. Her imagination had run away with her and she held the spruce grove in mortal dread after nightfall. But Marilla was inexorable. She marched the shrinking ghost-seer down to the spring and ordered her to proceed straightaway over the bridge and into the dusky retreats of wailing ladies and headless specters beyond.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮可以随心所欲地恳求和哭泣——她确实这么做了，因为她的恐惧是非常真实的。她的想象力已经消失，夜幕降临后，她对云杉林抱有致命的恐惧。但玛丽拉却毫不留情。她把这个畏缩的幽灵先知带到了泉水边，命令她直接过桥，进入远处哭泣的女士和无头幽灵的昏暗隐居处。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, how can you be so cruel?" sobbed Anne. "What would you feel like if a white thing did snatch me up and carry me off?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，你怎么可以这么残忍？”安妮抽泣着。 “如果有一个白色的东西把我抓起来并带走，你会有什么感觉？”

paragraphs.en: "I'll risk it," said Marilla unfeelingly. "You know I always mean what I say. I'll cure you of imagining ghosts into places. March, now."
paragraphs.zh: “我愿意冒这个险。”玛丽拉冷酷地说。 “你知道我总是说到做到。我会治愈你想象鬼魂到某个地方的毛病。现在就进军吧。”

paragraphs.en: Anne marched. That is, she stumbled over the bridge and went shuddering up the horrible dim path beyond. Anne never forgot that walk. Bitterly did she repent the license she had given to her imagination. The goblins of her fancy lurked in every shadow about her, reaching out their cold, fleshless hands to grasp the terrified small girl who had called them into being. A white strip of birch bark blowing up from the hollow over the brown floor of the grove made her heart stand still. The long-drawn wail of two old boughs rubbing against each other brought out the perspiration in beads on her forehead. The swoop of bats in the darkness over her was as the wings of unearthly creatures. When she reached Mr. William Bell's field she fled across it as if pursued by an army of white things, and arrived at the Barry kitchen door so out of breath that she could hardly gasp out her request for the apron pattern. Diana was away so that she had no excuse to linger. The dreadful return journey had to be faced. Anne went back over it with shut eyes, preferring to take the risk of dashing her brains out among the boughs to that of seeing a white thing. When she finally stumbled over the log bridge she drew one long shivering breath of relief.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮游行。也就是说，她跌跌撞撞地跨过桥，颤抖着沿着远处可怕的昏暗小路走去。安妮永远不会忘记那次散步。她痛苦地后悔自己放纵了自己的想象力。她想象中的妖精潜伏在她周围的每一个阴影中，伸出冰冷、毫无血肉的手，抓住那个召唤它们的恐惧的小女孩。一条白色的白桦树皮从树林棕色地面上的空洞中吹起，让她的心停止了跳动。两根老树枝相互摩擦发出的长长的哀嚎声，衬托出了她额头上的汗珠。黑暗中，蝙蝠在她上方俯冲，就像超凡脱俗的生物的翅膀。当她到达威廉·贝尔先生的田地时，她像被一群白色的东西追赶一样穿过田地，来到巴里厨房门口时，气喘吁吁，几乎无法说出要围裙图案的要求。戴安娜不在，所以她没有借口逗留。必须面对可怕的回程。安妮闭上眼睛重新审视它，宁愿冒把脑袋撞到树枝上的风险，也不愿看到一个白色的东西。当她终于跌跌撞撞地走上独木桥时，她颤抖着长长地松了一口气。

paragraphs.en: "Well, so nothing caught you?" said Marilla unsympathetically.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，所以什么也没抓到你？”玛丽拉毫无同情心地说。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Mar—Marilla," chattered Anne, "I'll b-b-be contt-tented with c-c-commonplace places after this."
paragraphs.zh: “噢，玛——玛瑞拉，”安妮喋喋不休地说，“这之后我就满足于平庸的地方了。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 21 章：调味料的新风波

paragraphs.en: "Dear me, there is nothing but meetings and partings in this world, as Mrs. Lynde says," remarked Anne plaintively, putting her slate and books down on the kitchen table on the last day of June and wiping her red eyes with a very damp handkerchief. "Wasn't it fortunate, Marilla, that I took an extra handkerchief to school today? I had a presentiment that it would be needed."
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的我，正如林德夫人所说，这个世界上只有相遇和离别，”安妮哀怨地说，在六月的最后一天，她把石板和书放在厨房的桌子上，用一块湿漉漉的手帕擦着红红的眼睛。 “玛丽拉，我今天带了一块额外的手帕去学校，这不是很幸运吗？我预感到会需要它。”

paragraphs.en: "I never thought you were so fond of Mr. Phillips that you'd require two handkerchiefs to dry your tears just because he was going away," said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “我没想到你这么喜欢菲利普斯先生，只因为他要走了，你就需要两块手帕来擦干眼泪，”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: "I don't think I was crying because I was really so very fond of him," reflected Anne. "I just cried because all the others did. It was Ruby Gillis started it. Ruby Gillis has always declared she hated Mr. Phillips, but just as soon as he got up to make his farewell speech she burst into tears. Then all the girls began to cry, one after the other. I tried to hold out, Marilla. I tried to remember the time Mr. Phillips made me sit with Gil—with a, boy; and the time he spelled my name without an e on the blackboard; and how he said I was the worst dunce he ever saw at geometry and laughed at my spelling; and all the times he had been so horrid and sarcastic; but somehow I couldn't, Marilla, and I just had to cry too. Jane Andrews has been talking for a month about how glad she'd be when Mr. Phillips went away and she declared she'd never shed a tear. Well, she was worse than any of us and had to borrow a handkerchief from her brother—of course the boys didn't cry—because she hadn't brought one of her own, not expecting to need it. Oh, Marilla, it was heartrending. Mr. Phillips made such a beautiful farewell speech beginning, 'The time has come for us to part.' It was very affecting. And he had tears in his eyes too, Marilla. Oh, I felt dreadfully sorry and remorseful for all the times I'd talked in school and drawn pictures of him on my slate and made fun of him and Prissy. I can tell you I wished I'd been a model pupil like Minnie Andrews. She hadn't anything on her conscience. The girls cried all the way home from school. Carrie Sloane kept saying every few minutes, 'The time has come for us to part,' and that would start us off again whenever we were in any danger of cheering up. I do feel dreadfully sad, Marilla. But one can't feel quite in the depths of despair with two months' vacation before them, can they, Marilla? And besides, we met the new minister and his wife coming from the station. For all I was feeling so bad about Mr. Phillips going away I couldn't help taking a little interest in a new minister, could I? His wife is very pretty. Not exactly regally lovely, of course—it wouldn't do, I suppose, for a minister to have a regally lovely wife, because it might set a bad example. Mrs. Lynde says the minister's wife over at Newbridge sets a very bad example because she dresses so fashionably. Our new minister's wife was dressed in blue muslin with lovely puffed sleeves and a hat trimmed with roses. Jane Andrews said she thought puffed sleeves were too worldly for a minister's wife, but I didn't make any such uncharitable remark, Marilla, because I know what it is to long for puffed sleeves. Besides, she's only been a minister's wife for a little while, so one should make allowances, shouldn't they? They are going to board with Mrs. Lynde until the manse is ready."
paragraphs.zh: “我不认为我哭是因为我真的非常喜欢他，”安妮反映道。 “我只是哭了，因为其他人都哭了。是鲁比·吉利斯先开始的。鲁比·吉利斯一直宣称她讨厌菲利普斯先生，但他一站起来发表告别演说，她就哭了起来。然后所有的女孩都开始哭了，一个接一个。我试图忍住，玛丽拉。我试图回忆起菲利普斯先生让我和吉尔坐在一起的那次——和一个男孩；还有他在黑板上拼写我的名字时没有e的那一次；他说我是他所见过的最糟糕的几何笨蛋，还嘲笑我的拼写；但不知何故，我不能，玛丽拉，我也不得不哭了一个月，当菲利普斯先生离开时，她说她从未流过一滴眼泪。没有哭——因为她没有带自己的，没想到会需要它，菲利普斯先生做了一场如此美丽的告别演讲，“我们分手的时候到了。”这非常有影响力。他的眼里也含着泪水，玛丽拉。哦，我对自己在学校里说话、在石板上画他的照片、取笑他和普莉西的所有时间感到非常抱歉和悔恨。我可以告诉你，我希望自己能成为像米妮·安德鲁斯那样的模范学生。她没有任何良心上的事情。女孩们放学回家一路哭着。凯莉·斯隆每隔几分钟就不断地说：“我们分手的时间到了”，每当我们面临振作起来的危险时，这就会让我们重新出发。我确实感到非常悲伤，玛丽拉。但是，还有两个月的假期，人们不能感到极度绝望，不是吗，玛丽拉？此外，我们还见到了从车站过来的新部长和他的妻子。尽管我对菲利普斯先生的离开感到非常难过，但我还是忍不住对一位新部长产生了一点兴趣，可以吗？他的妻子非常漂亮。当然，这并不完全是帝王般的可爱——我想，对于一个牧师来说，拥有一个帝王般可爱的妻子是不行的，因为这可能会树立一个坏榜样。林德夫人说，新桥的牧师妻子树立了一个非常坏的榜样，因为她穿得太时尚了。我们的新部长的妻子穿着蓝色平纹细布，有可爱的泡泡袖，戴着一顶饰有玫瑰的帽子。简·安德鲁斯说她认为泡泡袖对于牧师的妻子来说太世俗了，但我没有发表任何这样无情的话，玛丽拉，因为我知道渴望泡泡袖是什么感觉。再说了，她才当部长夫人不久，应该体谅一下不是吗？他们将和林德夫人一起登机，直到宅邸准备好为止。”

paragraphs.en: If Marilla, in going down to Mrs. Lynde's that evening, was actuated by any motive save her avowed one of returning the quilting frames she had borrowed the preceding winter, it was an amiable weakness shared by most of the Avonlea people. Many a thing Mrs. Lynde had lent, sometimes never expecting to see it again, came home that night in charge of the borrowers thereof. A new minister, and moreover a minister with a wife, was a lawful object of curiosity in a quiet little country settlement where sensations were few and far between.
paragraphs.zh: 如果说那天晚上马里拉去林德太太家的动机除了她声称要归还去年冬天借的绗缝架之外，那么这就是大多数埃文利人共有的一个和蔼可亲的弱点。林德夫人借出的许多东西，有时根本没想到会再次见到，当天晚上就归来，由借款人负责。在一个安静的小乡村定居点，一位新部长，而且是一位有妻子的部长，是合法的好奇对象，那里的轰动事件很少。

paragraphs.en: Old Mr. Bentley, the minister whom Anne had found lacking in imagination, had been pastor of Avonlea for eighteen years. He was a widower when he came, and a widower he remained, despite the fact that gossip regularly married him to this, that, or the other one, every year of his sojourn. In the preceding February he had resigned his charge and departed amid the regrets of his people, most of whom had the affection born of long intercourse for their good old minister in spite of his shortcomings as an orator. Since then the Avonlea church had enjoyed a variety of religious dissipation in listening to the many and various candidates and "supplies" who came Sunday after Sunday to preach on trial. These stood or fell by the judgment of the fathers and mothers in Israel; but a certain small, red-haired girl who sat meekly in the corner of the old Cuthbert pew also had her opinions about them and discussed the same in full with Matthew, Marilla always declining from principle to criticize ministers in any shape or form.
paragraphs.zh: 老本特利先生是安妮认为缺乏想象力的牧师，他已经担任埃文利牧师十八年了。他来的时候是个鳏夫，现在仍然是个鳏夫，尽管事实上，在他逗留期间的每一年，流言经常把他与这个、那个或另一个结婚。去年二月，他在人民的遗憾中辞去了职务并离开了，尽管他作为演说家有缺点，但大多数人民对他们的好老部长长期交往产生了感情。从那时起，埃文利教会就享受着各种各样的宗教消遣，倾听着众多不同的候选人和“补给品”，他们周日又一个周日地在审判中宣讲。这些人的存亡取决于以色列父母的判断。但是，一个温顺地坐在老卡斯伯特长椅角落里的红发小女孩也对他们有自己的看法，并与马修充分讨论了同样的问题，玛丽拉总是从原则上拒绝以任何形式批评部长。

paragraphs.en: "I don't think Mr. Smith would have done, Matthew" was Anne's final summing up. "Mrs. Lynde says his delivery was so poor, but I think his worst fault was just like Mr. Bentley's—he had no imagination. And Mr. Terry had too much; he let it run away with him just as I did mine in the matter of the Haunted Wood. Besides, Mrs. Lynde says his theology wasn't sound. Mr. Gresham was a very good man and a very religious man, but he told too many funny stories and made the people laugh in church; he was undignified, and you must have some dignity about a minister, mustn't you, Matthew? I thought Mr. Marshall was decidedly attractive; but Mrs. Lynde says he isn't married, or even engaged, because she made special inquiries about him, and she says it would never do to have a young unmarried minister in Avonlea, because he might marry in the congregation and that would make trouble. Mrs. Lynde is a very farseeing woman, isn't she, Matthew? I'm very glad they've called Mr. Allan. I liked him because his sermon was interesting and he prayed as if he meant it and not just as if he did it because he was in the habit of it. Mrs. Lynde says he isn't perfect, but she says she supposes we couldn't expect a perfect minister for seven hundred and fifty dollars a year, and anyhow his theology is sound because she questioned him thoroughly on all the points of doctrine. And she knows his wife's people and they are most respectable and the women are all good housekeepers. Mrs. Lynde says that sound doctrine in the man and good housekeeping in the woman make an ideal combination for a minister's family."
paragraphs.zh: “我认为史密斯先生不会这么做，马修”是安妮最后的总结。 “林德夫人说他的表达很糟糕，但我认为他最大的缺点就像本特利先生一样——他没有想象力。特里先生太多了；他让它随他而去，就像我在闹鬼森林的问题上所做的那样。此外，林德夫人说他的神学不健全。格雷沙姆先生是一个非常好的人，一个非常虔诚的人，但他讲了太多有趣的故事，让教堂里的人们发笑；他马歇尔，你对牧师一定有一些尊严，不是吗？我认为马歇尔先生绝对有吸引力；但是林德夫人说他没有结婚，甚至没有订婚，因为她对他进行了特别询问，她说埃文利永远不会有一个年轻的未婚牧师，因为他可能会在会众中结婚，这会带来麻烦，不是吗，马修？我很高兴他们打电话给艾伦先生，因为他的布道很有趣，他的祷告好像是认真的，而不是因为他习惯了这样做，但她说她认为我们不能指望每年七百五十美元的完美牧师，无论如何，他的神学是正确的，因为她对他妻子的所有教义问题都进行了彻底的质疑。林德夫人说，男人的健全教义和女人的良好家务是牧师家庭的理想组合。

paragraphs.en: The new minister and his wife were a young, pleasant-faced couple, still on their honeymoon, and full of all good and beautiful enthusiasms for their chosen lifework. Avonlea opened its heart to them from the start. Old and young liked the frank, cheerful young man with his high ideals, and the bright, gentle little lady who assumed the mistress-ship of the manse. With Mrs. Allan Anne fell promptly and wholeheartedly in love. She had discovered another kindred spirit.
paragraphs.zh: 新牧师和他的妻子是一对年轻、面容愉快的夫妇，他们还在度蜜月，对他们所选择的毕生工作充满了美好而美好的热情。 Avonlea 从一开始就向他们敞开心扉。老老少少都喜欢这位坦率、开朗、有远大理想的年轻人，也喜欢这位开朗、温柔、当家作主的小女人。安妮很快就全心全意地爱上了艾伦夫人。她发现了另一个志趣相投的人。

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Allan is perfectly lovely," she announced one Sunday afternoon. "She's taken our class and she's a splendid teacher. She said right away she didn't think it was fair for the teacher to ask all the questions, and you know, Marilla, that is exactly what I've always thought. She said we could ask her any question we liked and I asked ever so many. I'm good at asking questions, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “艾伦夫人非常可爱，”一个周日下午她宣布。 "She's taken our class and she's a splendid teacher. She said right away she didn't think it was fair for the teacher to ask all the questions, and you know, Marilla, that is exactly what I've always thought. She said we could ask her any question we liked and I asked ever so many. I'm good at asking questions, Marilla."

paragraphs.en: "I believe you" was Marilla's emphatic comment.
paragraphs.zh: “我相信你”是玛丽拉强调的评论。

paragraphs.en: "Nobody else asked any except Ruby Gillis, and she asked if there was to be a Sunday-school picnic this summer. I didn't think that was a very proper question to ask because it hadn't any connection with the lesson—the lesson was about Daniel in the lions' den—but Mrs. Allan just smiled and said she thought there would be. Mrs. Allan has a lovely smile; she has such EXQUISITE dimples in her cheeks. I wish I had dimples in my cheeks, Marilla. I'm not half so skinny as I was when I came here, but I have no dimples yet. If I had perhaps I could influence people for good. Mrs. Allan said we ought always to try to influence other people for good. She talked so nice about everything. I never knew before that religion was such a cheerful thing. I always thought it was kind of melancholy, but Mrs. Allan's isn't, and I'd like to be a Christian if I could be one like her. I wouldn't want to be one like Mr. Superintendent Bell."
paragraphs.zh: “除了鲁比·吉利斯之外，没有人问过这个问题，她问今年夏天主日学校是否要举行野餐。我认为这个问题问得不太恰当，因为它与课程没有任何关系——课程是关于狮子窝里的丹尼尔——但艾伦夫人只是微笑着说她认为会有。艾伦夫人的笑容很可爱；她的脸颊上有如此精致的酒窝。我希望我的脸上也有酒窝。”玛丽拉，我的脸颊已经没有我来时那么瘦了，但如果我有的话，也许我可以永远影响别人。她以前从来不知道宗教是一件令人忧郁的事情，但艾伦夫人的却不是，如果我可以的话，我想成为一名基督徒。我不想成为像她一样的人。”

paragraphs.en: "It's very naughty of you to speak so about Mr. Bell," said Marilla severely. "Mr. Bell is a real good man."
paragraphs.zh: “你这样谈论贝尔先生，真是太顽皮了。”玛丽拉严肃地说。 “贝尔先生真是个好人。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, of course he's good," agreed Anne, "but he doesn't seem to get any comfort out of it. If I could be good I'd dance and sing all day because I was glad of it. I suppose Mrs. Allan is too old to dance and sing and of course it wouldn't be dignified in a minister's wife. But I can just feel she's glad she's a Christian and that she'd be one even if she could get to heaven without it."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，他当然很好，”安妮同意，“但他似乎并没有从中得到任何安慰。如果我能表现得好，我会整天唱歌跳舞，因为我很高兴。我想艾伦夫人太老了，不能跳舞唱歌，当然，这对牧师的妻子来说是不体面的。但我能感觉到她很高兴自己是一名基督徒，即使没有基督徒她也能上天堂，她也会成为一名基督徒。”

paragraphs.en: "I suppose we must have Mr. and Mrs. Allan up to tea someday soon," said Marilla reflectively. "They've been most everywhere but here. Let me see. Next Wednesday would be a good time to have them. But don't say a word to Matthew about it, for if he knew they were coming he'd find some excuse to be away that day. He'd got so used to Mr. Bentley he didn't mind him, but he's going to find it hard to get acquainted with a new minister, and a new minister's wife will frighten him to death."
paragraphs.zh: “我想我们很快就会邀请艾伦先生和夫人一起喝茶。”马里拉若有所思地说。 “他们到处都是，除了这里。让我想想。下周三是接待他们的好时机。不过，别对马修说这件事，因为如果他知道他们要来，那天他就会找借口离开。他已经习惯了本特利先生，不介意他，但他会发现很难认识一个新牧师，而新牧师的妻子会把他吓死的。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll be as secret as the dead," assured Anne. "But oh, Marilla, will you let me make a cake for the occasion? I'd love to do something for Mrs. Allan, and you know I can make a pretty good cake by this time."
paragraphs.zh: “我会像死人一样保密，”安妮保证道。 “但是哦，玛丽拉，你能让我为这个场合做一个蛋糕吗？我很乐意为艾伦夫人做点什么，你知道我这次可以做一个非常好的蛋糕。”

paragraphs.en: "You can make a layer cake," promised Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “你可以做一个夹心蛋糕，”玛丽拉答应道。

paragraphs.en: Monday and Tuesday great preparations went on at Green Gables. Having the minister and his wife to tea was a serious and important undertaking, and Marilla was determined not to be eclipsed by any of the Avonlea housekeepers. Anne was wild with excitement and delight. She talked it all over with Diana Tuesday night in the twilight, as they sat on the big red stones by the Dryad's Bubble and made rainbows in the water with little twigs dipped in fir balsam.
paragraphs.zh: 周一和周二，绿山墙球场进行了精彩的准备工作。请部长和他的妻子喝茶是一项严肃而重要的任务，玛丽拉决心不让任何埃文利管家黯然失色。安妮兴奋又高兴。周二晚上的暮色中，她和戴安娜谈了这一切，当时他们坐在树精泡泡旁的红色大石头上，用浸有冷杉香脂的小树枝在水中制造出彩虹。

paragraphs.en: "Everything is ready, Diana, except my cake which I'm to make in the morning, and the baking-powder biscuits which Marilla will make just before teatime. I assure you, Diana, that Marilla and I have had a busy two days of it. It's such a responsibility having a minister's family to tea. I never went through such an experience before. You should just see our pantry. It's a sight to behold. We're going to have jellied chicken and cold tongue. We're to have two kinds of jelly, red and yellow, and whipped cream and lemon pie, and cherry pie, and three kinds of cookies, and fruit cake, and Marilla's famous yellow plum preserves that she keeps especially for ministers, and pound cake and layer cake, and biscuits as aforesaid; and new bread and old both, in case the minister is dyspeptic and can't eat new. Mrs. Lynde says ministers are dyspeptic, but I don't think Mr. Allan has been a minister long enough for it to have had a bad effect on him. I just grow cold when I think of my layer cake. Oh, Diana, what if it shouldn't be good! I dreamed last night that I was chased all around by a fearful goblin with a big layer cake for a head."
paragraphs.zh: “一切都准备好了，戴安娜，除了我早上要做的蛋糕，还有玛丽拉在下午茶时间之前做的发酵粉饼干。我向你保证，戴安娜，我和玛丽拉已经忙了两天了。请牧师的家人喝茶真是一种责任。我以前从来没有经历过这样的经历。你应该看看我们的食品储藏室。这是一个值得一看的景象。我们要吃鸡肉冻和冷饮。我们要吃两种果冻，红色和黄色，鲜奶油和柠檬派，樱桃派，三种饼干，水果蛋糕，还有玛丽拉专门为部长们保留的著名的黄李子蜜饯，还有前面提到的磅蛋糕和千层蛋糕，还有新面包和旧面包，以防部长消化不良，林德夫人说部长消化不良，但我不吃。艾伦先生当牧师已经够久了，这对他产生了不好的影响，哦，戴安娜，如果它不好吃怎么办？昨晚我梦见我被一个头戴大蛋糕的可怕妖精追赶。”

paragraphs.en: "It'll be good, all right," assured Diana, who was a very comfortable sort of friend. "I'm sure that piece of the one you made that we had for lunch in Idlewild two weeks ago was perfectly elegant."
paragraphs.zh: “一切都会好起来的，好吧，”戴安娜保证道，她是一位非常令人舒服的朋友。 “我确信两周前我们在艾德维尔德吃午餐时你做的那件非常优雅。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes; but cakes have such a terrible habit of turning out bad just when you especially want them to be good," sighed Anne, setting a particularly well-balsamed twig afloat. "However, I suppose I shall just have to trust to Providence and be careful to put in the flour. Oh, look, Diana, what a lovely rainbow! Do you suppose the dryad will come out after we go away and take it for a scarf?"
paragraphs.zh: “是的；但是蛋糕有一个可怕的习惯，就是当你特别希望它们好吃的时候，它就会变质。”安妮叹了口气，把一根特别香脂的树枝浮在水面上。 “不过，我想我只能相信上帝，小心地把面粉放进去。哦，看，黛安娜，多可爱的彩虹啊！你认为我们走后树精会出来把它当围巾吗？”

paragraphs.en: "You know there is no such thing as a dryad," said Diana. Diana's mother had found out about the Haunted Wood and had been decidedly angry over it. As a result Diana had abstained from any further imitative flights of imagination and did not think it prudent to cultivate a spirit of belief even in harmless dryads.
paragraphs.zh: “你知道没有树妖这样的东西，”戴安娜说。戴安娜的母亲发现了闹鬼森​​林的事，并且对此非常生气。结果，戴安娜放弃了任何进一步的模仿想象，并且认为即使在无害的树精中培养信仰精神也是不明智的。

paragraphs.en: "But it's so easy to imagine there is," said Anne. "Every night before I go to bed, I look out of my window and wonder if the dryad is really sitting here, combing her locks with the spring for a mirror. Sometimes I look for her footprints in the dew in the morning. Oh, Diana, don't give up your faith in the dryad!"
paragraphs.zh: “但很容易想象有这样的存在，”安妮说。 “每天晚上睡觉前，我都会向窗外望去，想知道树精是否真的坐在这里，用弹簧梳理她的头发当镜子。有时我会在早晨的露水中寻找她的脚印。哦，戴安娜，不要放弃对树精的信心！”

paragraphs.en: Wednesday morning came. Anne got up at sunrise because she was too excited to sleep. She had caught a severe cold in the head by reason of her dabbling in the spring on the preceding evening; but nothing short of absolute pneumonia could have quenched her interest in culinary matters that morning. After breakfast she proceeded to make her cake. When she finally shut the oven door upon it she drew a long breath.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三早上到了。安妮在日出时起床，因为她太兴奋而睡不着。她因前一天晚上泡泉水而得了重感冒。但那天早上，除了绝对的肺炎之外，没有什么能够浇灭她对烹饪的兴趣。早餐后，她开始做蛋糕。当她最终关上烤箱门时，她长长地吸了一口气。

paragraphs.en: "I'm sure I haven't forgotten anything this time, Marilla. But do you think it will rise? Just suppose perhaps the baking powder isn't good? I used it out of the new can. And Mrs. Lynde says you can never be sure of getting good baking powder nowadays when everything is so adulterated. Mrs. Lynde says the Government ought to take the matter up, but she says we'll never see the day when a Tory Government will do it. Marilla, what if that cake doesn't rise?"
paragraphs.zh: “我确信这次我没有忘记任何东西，玛丽拉。但是你认为它会上升吗？假设泡打粉不好？我用的是新罐子里的泡打粉。林德夫人说，现在一切都如此掺假，你永远无法确定能买到好的泡打粉。林德夫人说政府应该解决这个问题，但她说我们永远不会看到保守党政府会这样做的一天。玛丽拉，如果那个蛋糕不这样做怎么办？起来？”

paragraphs.en: "We'll have plenty without it" was Marilla's unimpassioned way of looking at the subject.
paragraphs.zh: “没有它我们也会有很多”，马里拉冷静地看待这个话题。

paragraphs.en: The cake did rise, however, and came out of the oven as light and feathery as golden foam. Anne, flushed with delight, clapped it together with layers of ruby jelly and, in imagination, saw Mrs. Allan eating it and possibly asking for another piece!
paragraphs.zh: 然而，蛋糕确实膨胀了，从烤箱里出来时，它像金色的泡沫一样轻盈、羽毛状。安妮高兴得满脸通红，她把它和一层层的红宝石果冻拍在一起，在想象中，她看到艾伦太太吃了它，可能还要求再吃一块！

paragraphs.en: "You'll be using the best tea set, of course, Marilla," she said. "Can I fix the table with ferns and wild roses?"
paragraphs.zh: “当然，你会使用最好的茶具，玛丽拉，”她说。 “我可以用蕨类植物和野玫瑰来装饰桌子吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I think that's all nonsense," sniffed Marilla. "In my opinion it's the eatables that matter and not flummery decorations."
paragraphs.zh: “我认为这都是无稽之谈，”玛丽拉嗤之以鼻。 “在我看来，重要的是可食用的东西，而不是廉价的装饰品。”

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Barry had HER table decorated," said Anne, who was not entirely guiltless of the wisdom of the serpent, "and the minister paid her an elegant compliment. He said it was a feast for the eye as well as the palate."
paragraphs.zh: “巴里夫人布置了她的桌子，”安妮说道，她对蛇的智慧也并非完全没有愧疚，“牧师对她表示了优雅的赞美。他说这是一场视觉和味觉的盛宴。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, do as you like," said Marilla, who was quite determined not to be surpassed by Mrs. Barry or anybody else. "Only mind you leave enough room for the dishes and the food."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你想怎么办就怎么办吧，”玛丽拉说，她决心不让巴里夫人或其他任何人超越。 “请注意，为餐具和食物留出足够的空间。”

paragraphs.en: Anne laid herself out to decorate in a manner and after a fashion that should leave Mrs. Barry's nowhere. Having abundance of roses and ferns and a very artistic taste of her own, she made that tea table such a thing of beauty that when the minister and his wife sat down to it they exclaimed in chorus over it loveliness.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮以一种不会让巴里夫人无处可去的方式和时尚来装饰自己。她拥有丰富的玫瑰和蕨类植物，加上她自己的艺术品味，她把那张茶几做得非常漂亮，当牧师和他的妻子坐下来时，他们齐声惊叹它的可爱。

paragraphs.en: "It's Anne's doings," said Marilla, grimly just; and Anne felt that Mrs. Allan's approving smile was almost too much happiness for this world.
paragraphs.zh: “这是安妮干的，”玛丽拉严肃地说。安妮觉得艾伦夫人赞许的微笑对于这个世界来说简直是太幸福了。

paragraphs.en: Matthew was there, having been inveigled into the party only goodness and Anne knew how. He had been in such a state of shyness and nervousness that Marilla had given him up in despair, but Anne took him in hand so successfully that he now sat at the table in his best clothes and white collar and talked to the minister not uninterestingly. He never said a word to Mrs. Allan, but that perhaps was not to be expected.
paragraphs.zh: 马修也在场，他只是被善意地骗进了聚会，而安妮也知道是怎么回事。他一直处于如此害羞和紧张的状态，以至于玛丽拉绝望地放弃了他，但安妮成功地抓住了他，以至于他现在穿着最好的衣服和白领坐在桌旁，与部长交谈起来并不无趣。他从未对艾伦夫人说过一句话，但这也许是出乎意料的。

paragraphs.en: All went merry as a marriage bell until Anne's layer cake was passed. Mrs. Allan, having already been helped to a bewildering variety, declined it. But Marilla, seeing the disappointment on Anne's face, said smilingly:
paragraphs.zh: 一切都像结婚的钟声一样欢乐，直到安妮的夹心蛋糕被递过去。艾伦夫人已经被帮助做了一些令人眼花缭乱的事情，所以拒绝了。但玛丽拉看到安妮脸上的失望，却微笑着说道：

paragraphs.en: "Oh, you must take a piece of this, Mrs. Allan. Anne made it on purpose for you."
paragraphs.zh: “噢，你一定要吃一块，艾伦夫人。安妮是特意为你做的。”

paragraphs.en: "In that case I must sample it," laughed Mrs. Allan, helping herself to a plump triangle, as did also the minister and Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “既然如此，我就必须尝尝。”艾伦夫人笑道，一边给自己拿了一个丰满的三角形，部长和玛丽拉也这么做了。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan took a mouthful of hers and a most peculiar expression crossed her face; not a word did she say, however, but steadily ate away at it. Marilla saw the expression and hastened to taste the cake.
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太抿了一口，脸上浮现出一种极为奇特的表情。然而，她什么也没说，只是慢慢地吃下去。玛丽拉看到这表情，赶紧尝了尝蛋糕。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley!" she exclaimed, "what on earth did you put into that cake?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉！”她惊呼道：“你到底在蛋糕里放了什么？”

paragraphs.en: "Nothing but what the recipe said, Marilla," cried Anne with a look of anguish. "Oh, isn't it all right?"
paragraphs.zh: “除了菜谱上说的，什么都没有，玛丽拉，”安妮一脸痛苦地喊道。 “哦，没事儿吧？”

paragraphs.en: "All right! It's simply horrible. Mr. Allan, don't try to eat it. Anne, taste it yourself. What flavoring did you use?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧！简直太可怕了。艾伦先生，你别想吃它。安妮，你自己尝尝，你用的是什么调味料？”

paragraphs.en: "Vanilla," said Anne, her face scarlet with mortification after tasting the cake. "Only vanilla. Oh, Marilla, it must have been the baking powder. I had my suspicions of that bak—"
paragraphs.zh: “香草味的，”安妮尝完蛋糕后，她的​​脸因羞愧而涨得通红。 “只有香草。哦，玛丽拉，一定是发酵粉的问题。我怀疑那个面包——”

paragraphs.en: "Baking powder fiddlesticks! Go and bring me the bottle of vanilla you used."
paragraphs.zh: “泡打粉摆弄！去把你用过的那瓶香草拿来给我。”

paragraphs.en: Anne fled to the pantry and returned with a small bottle partially filled with a brown liquid and labeled yellowly, "Best Vanilla."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮逃到食品储藏室，带着一个小瓶子回来，瓶子里装着部分棕色液体，上面贴着黄色标签，“最好的香草”。

paragraphs.en: Marilla took it, uncorked it, smelled it.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉接过它，打开瓶塞，闻了闻。

paragraphs.en: "Mercy on us, Anne, you've flavored that cake with ANODYNE LINIMENT. I broke the liniment bottle last week and poured what was left into an old empty vanilla bottle. I suppose it's partly my fault—I should have warned you—but for pity's sake why couldn't you have smelled it?"
paragraphs.zh: “可怜我们吧，安妮，你用安诺达搽剂给蛋糕调味了。上周我打破了搽剂瓶子，把剩下的东西倒进了一个旧的空香草瓶里。我想这部分是我的错——我应该警告你——但看在怜悯的份上，你为什么不能闻到它的味道呢？”

paragraphs.en: Anne dissolved into tears under this double disgrace.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在这双重耻辱下泪流满面。

paragraphs.en: "I couldn't—I had such a cold!" and with this she fairly fled to the gable chamber, where she cast herself on the bed and wept as one who refuses to be comforted.
paragraphs.zh: “我不能——我感冒了！”说完，她就逃到了山墙房间，倒在床上，哭了起来，就像一个不肯接受安慰的人。

paragraphs.en: Presently a light step sounded on the stairs and somebody entered the room.
paragraphs.zh: 不一会儿，楼梯上响起了轻微的脚步声，有人走进了房间。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla," sobbed Anne, without looking up, "I'm disgraced forever. I shall never be able to live this down. It will get out—things always do get out in Avonlea. Diana will ask me how my cake turned out and I shall have to tell her the truth. I shall always be pointed at as the girl who flavored a cake with anodyne liniment. Gil—the boys in school will never get over laughing at it. Oh, Marilla, if you have a spark of Christian pity don't tell me that I must go down and wash the dishes after this. I'll wash them when the minister and his wife are gone, but I cannot ever look Mrs. Allan in the face again. Perhaps she'll think I tried to poison her. Mrs. Lynde says she knows an orphan girl who tried to poison her benefactor. But the liniment isn't poisonous. It's meant to be taken internally—although not in cakes. Won't you tell Mrs. Allan so, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “噢，玛丽拉，”安妮头也不回地抽泣着，“我永远蒙羞了。我永远无法忍受这一切。它会传出去的——在埃文利，事情总是会传出去。戴安娜会问我的蛋糕结果如何，我必须告诉她真相。我将永远被指责为用止痛搽剂给蛋糕调味的女孩。吉尔——学校里的男孩们永远不会笑到这。哦，玛丽拉，如果你有一点点基督徒的怜悯之心别告诉我，等牧师和他的妻子走后，我会洗碗的。也许她会认为我试图毒害她。林德夫人说她认识一个试图毒害她的恩人的人。但这种搽剂是内服的，但你不会告诉我吧。艾伦太太，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: "Suppose you jump up and tell her so yourself," said a merry voice.
paragraphs.zh: “假设你跳起来亲自告诉她，”一个快乐的声音说道。

paragraphs.en: Anne flew up, to find Mrs. Allan standing by her bed, surveying her with laughing eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮飞了起来，发现艾伦夫人站在她的床边，用笑着的眼睛打量着她。

paragraphs.en: "My dear little girl, you mustn't cry like this," she said, genuinely disturbed by Anne's tragic face. "Why, it's all just a funny mistake that anybody might make."
paragraphs.zh: “我亲爱的小女孩，你不可以这样哭，”她说，对安妮悲惨的脸感到真正的不安。 “为什么，这只是任何人都可能犯的一个有趣的错误。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, no, it takes me to make such a mistake," said Anne forlornly. "And I wanted to have that cake so nice for you, Mrs. Allan."
paragraphs.zh: “噢，不，我才犯了这样的错误。”安妮悲凉地说。 “我想为你准备一个美味的蛋糕，艾伦夫人。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I know, dear. And I assure you I appreciate your kindness and thoughtfulness just as much as if it had turned out all right. Now, you mustn't cry any more, but come down with me and show me your flower garden. Miss Cuthbert tells me you have a little plot all your own. I want to see it, for I'm very much interested in flowers."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我知道，亲爱的。我向你保证，我很感激你的善良和体贴，就好像一切都很好一样。现在，你不能再哭了，跟我一起下来，带我看看你的花园。库斯伯特小姐告诉我，你有一块属于你自己的小土地。我想看看，因为我对花很感兴趣。”

paragraphs.en: Anne permitted herself to be led down and comforted, reflecting that it was really providential that Mrs. Allan was a kindred spirit. Nothing more was said about the liniment cake, and when the guests went away Anne found that she had enjoyed the evening more than could have been expected, considering that terrible incident. Nevertheless, she sighed deeply.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮允许自己被引导下去并得到安慰，她反思说，艾伦夫人志同道合真是天意。关于搽剂蛋糕，没有再多说什么，当客人们离开时，安妮发现，考虑到那次可怕的事件，她比预期的更享受这个夜晚。尽管如此，她还是深深地叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "Marilla, isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?"
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，想到明天又是新的一天，还没有犯任何错误，这不是很好吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I'll warrant you'll make plenty in it," said Marilla. "I never saw your beat for making mistakes, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “我保证你会赚很多，”玛丽拉说。 “我从来没有见过你因犯错误而受到惩罚，安妮。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, and well I know it," admitted Anne mournfully. "But have you ever noticed one encouraging thing about me, Marilla? I never make the same mistake twice."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我知道，”安妮悲伤地承认。 “但是你有没有注意到我身上一件令人鼓舞的事情，玛丽拉？我从来不会犯第二次同样的错误。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't know as that's much benefit when you're always making new ones."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，因为当你总是在制作新的东西时，这有多大好处。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, don't you see, Marilla? There must be a limit to the mistakes one person can make, and when I get to the end of them, then I'll be through with them. That's a very comforting thought."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，你没看到吗，玛丽拉？一个人所犯的错误一定是有限度的，当我犯完这些错误时，我就会结束这些错误。这是一个非常令人欣慰的想法。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, you'd better go and give that cake to the pigs," said Marilla. "It isn't fit for any human to eat, not even Jerry Boute."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你最好去把那块蛋糕给猪们，”玛丽拉说。 “它不适合任何人食用，甚至杰里·布特也不适合。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXII. Anne is Invited Out to Tea
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 22 章：安妮受邀去应酬喝茶

paragraphs.en: "And what are your eyes popping out of your head about. Now?" asked Marilla, when Anne had just come in from a run to the post office. "Have you discovered another kindred spirit?" Excitement hung around Anne like a garment, shone in her eyes, kindled in every feature. She had come dancing up the lane, like a wind-blown sprite, through the mellow sunshine and lazy shadows of the August evening.
paragraphs.zh: “那你的眼睛从你的脑袋里跳出来是为了什么呢？现在？”当安妮刚从邮局跑步回来时，玛丽拉问道。 “你有没有发现另一个志同道合的人？”兴奋像一件衣服一样笼罩着安妮，在她的眼睛里闪闪发光，每一个特征都被点燃。她像一个被风吹动的精灵，穿过八月傍晚柔和的阳光和慵懒的阴影，沿着小巷翩翩起舞。

paragraphs.en: "No, Marilla, but oh, what do you think? I am invited to tea at the manse tomorrow afternoon! Mrs. Allan left the letter for me at the post office. Just look at it, Marilla. 'Miss Anne Shirley, Green Gables.' That is the first time I was ever called 'Miss.' Such a thrill as it gave me! I shall cherish it forever among my choicest treasures."
paragraphs.zh: “不，玛丽拉，但是哦，你觉得怎么样？我被邀请明天下午去庄园喝茶！艾伦夫人把信留给了我在邮局。玛丽拉，你看一下。‘安妮·雪莉小姐，绿山墙。’这是我第一次被称为“小姐”。它给了我如此激动！我将把它永远珍藏在我最珍贵的珍宝中。”

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Allan told me she meant to have all the members of her Sunday-school class to tea in turn," said Marilla, regarding the wonderful event very coolly. "You needn't get in such a fever over it. Do learn to take things calmly, child."
paragraphs.zh: “艾伦夫人告诉我，她打算让主日学校班级的所有成员轮流喝茶，”玛丽拉非常冷静地说道。 “你不必为此如此狂热。一定要学会冷静地对待事情，孩子。”

paragraphs.en: For Anne to take things calmly would have been to change her nature. All "spirit and fire and dew," as she was, the pleasures and pains of life came to her with trebled intensity. Marilla felt this and was vaguely troubled over it, realizing that the ups and downs of existence would probably bear hardly on this impulsive soul and not sufficiently understanding that the equally great capacity for delight might more than compensate. Therefore Marilla conceived it to be her duty to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition as impossible and alien to her as to a dancing sunbeam in one of the brook shallows. She did not make much headway, as she sorrowfully admitted to herself. The downfall of some dear hope or plan plunged Anne into "deeps of affliction." The fulfillment thereof exalted her to dizzy realms of delight. Marilla had almost begun to despair of ever fashioning this waif of the world into her model little girl of demure manners and prim deportment. Neither would she have believed that she really liked Anne much better as she was.
paragraphs.zh: 对安妮来说，冷静地对待事情就等于改变了她的本性。所有的“精神、火与露”，就像她一样，生活中的快乐和痛苦以三倍的强度降临到她身上。玛丽拉感觉到了这一点，并隐约感到困扰，意识到生活的起起落落可能对这个冲动的灵魂来说很难承受，但她没有充分理解同样强大的快乐能力可能会弥补这一点。因此，玛丽拉认为，她有责任让安妮养成一种平静、统一的性格，这对她来说是不可能的，也是陌生的，就像小溪浅滩上舞动的阳光一样。正如她悲伤地向自己承认的那样，她并没有取得多大进展。一些美好的希望或计划的破灭使安妮陷入了“痛苦的深渊”。这一愿望的实现使她欣喜若狂。玛丽拉几乎开始对把这个世界上的流浪儿塑造成举止端庄、举止拘谨的模范小女孩感到绝望。她也不会相信她真的更喜欢安妮。

paragraphs.en: Anne went to bed that night speechless with misery because Matthew had said the wind was round northeast and he feared it would be a rainy day tomorrow. The rustle of the poplar leaves about the house worried her, it sounded so like pattering raindrops, and the full, faraway roar of the gulf, to which she listened delightedly at other times, loving its strange, sonorous, haunting rhythm, now seemed like a prophecy of storm and disaster to a small maiden who particularly wanted a fine day. Anne thought that the morning would never come.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，安妮痛苦地上床睡觉，因为马修说风是东北风，他担心明天会下雨。房子周围杨树叶的沙沙声让她担心，听起来就像雨滴的啪嗒啪嗒声，而海湾的全面、遥远的咆哮声，她以前很高兴地听着，喜欢它奇怪的、铿锵的、令人难以忘怀的节奏，现在对一个特别想要美好的一天的小姑娘来说，这似乎是暴风雨和灾难的预言。安妮认为早晨永远不会到来。

paragraphs.en: But all things have an end, even nights before the day on which you are invited to take tea at the manse. The morning, in spite of Matthew's predictions, was fine and Anne's spirits soared to their highest. "Oh, Marilla, there is something in me today that makes me just love everybody I see," she exclaimed as she washed the breakfast dishes. "You don't know how good I feel! Wouldn't it be nice if it could last? I believe I could be a model child if I were just invited out to tea every day. But oh, Marilla, it's a solemn occasion too. I feel so anxious. What if I shouldn't behave properly? You know I never had tea at a manse before, and I'm not sure that I know all the rules of etiquette, although I've been studying the rules given in the Etiquette Department of the Family Herald ever since I came here. I'm so afraid I'll do something silly or forget to do something I should do. Would it be good manners to take a second helping of anything if you wanted to VERY much?"
paragraphs.zh: 但万事都有结束的时候，即使是在你被邀请去庄园喝茶的前一天晚上也是如此。尽管马修预言，早上天气晴朗，安妮的精神也达到了最高点。 “哦，玛丽拉，今天我身上有一种东西让我爱我所见到的每一个人，”她在洗早餐盘子时大声说道。 “你不知道我的感觉有多好！如果能持续下去不是很好吗？我相信如果我每天都被邀请出去喝茶，我可以成为一个模范孩子。但是哦，玛丽拉，这也是一个庄严的场合。我感到很焦虑。如果我不应该表现得好怎么办？你知道我以前从未在豪宅喝过茶，我不确定我是否了解所有的礼仪规则，尽管我一直在研究礼仪中的规则。自从我来到这里之后，我就很担心我会做一些愚蠢的事情或者忘记做一些我应该做的事情，如果你非常想要的话，再拿一点东西是有礼貌的吗？”

paragraphs.en: "The trouble with you, Anne, is that you're thinking too much about yourself. You should just think of Mrs. Allan and what would be nicest and most agreeable to her," said Marilla, hitting for once in her life on a very sound and pithy piece of advice. Anne instantly realized this.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你的问题在于你想得太多了。你应该只想到艾伦太太，想想什么对她来说是最好、最舒服的，”玛丽拉说，她一生中第一次提出了一个非常合理和简洁的建议。安妮立刻意识到了这一点。

paragraphs.en: "You are right, Marilla. I'll try not to think about myself at all."
paragraphs.zh: “你是对的，玛丽拉。我会尽量不去想我自己。”

paragraphs.en: Anne evidently got through her visit without any serious breach of "etiquette," for she came home through the twilight, under a great, high-sprung sky gloried over with trails of saffron and rosy cloud, in a beatified state of mind and told Marilla all about it happily, sitting on the big red-sandstone slab at the kitchen door with her tired curly head in Marilla's gingham lap.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮显然没有严重违反“礼节”，因为她在暮色中回到家，在一片藏红花和玫瑰色云彩映照下的伟大、高耸的天空下，带着一种幸福的心态，高兴地告诉玛丽拉这一切，坐在厨房门口的大红砂岩板上，把疲惫的卷发头枕在玛丽拉的格子腿上。

paragraphs.en: A cool wind was blowing down over the long harvest fields from the rims of firry western hills and whistling through the poplars. One clear star hung over the orchard and the fireflies were flitting over in Lover's Lane, in and out among the ferns and rustling boughs. Anne watched them as she talked and somehow felt that wind and stars and fireflies were all tangled up together into something unutterably sweet and enchanting.
paragraphs.zh: 一阵凉爽的风从西部冷杉山的边缘吹过长长的收割田，呼啸着穿过白杨树。一颗清澈的星星悬挂在果园上空，萤火虫在情人巷飞过，在蕨类植物和沙沙作响的树枝间穿梭。安妮看着他们说话，不知怎的，感觉风、星星、萤火虫都纠缠在一起，组成了一种说不出的甜蜜和迷人。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, I've had a most FASCINATING time. I feel that I have not lived in vain and I shall always feel like that even if I should never be invited to tea at a manse again. When I got there Mrs. Allan met me at the door. She was dressed in the sweetest dress of pale-pink organdy, with dozens of frills and elbow sleeves, and she looked just like a seraph. I really think I'd like to be a minister's wife when I grow up, Marilla. A minister mightn't mind my red hair because he wouldn't be thinking of such worldly things. But then of course one would have to be naturally good and I'll never be that, so I suppose there's no use in thinking about it. Some people are naturally good, you know, and others are not. I'm one of the others. Mrs. Lynde says I'm full of original sin. No matter how hard I try to be good I can never make such a success of it as those who are naturally good. It's a good deal like geometry, I expect. But don't you think the trying so hard ought to count for something? Mrs. Allan is one of the naturally good people. I love her passionately. You know there are some people, like Matthew and Mrs. Allan that you can love right off without any trouble. And there are others, like Mrs. Lynde, that you have to try very hard to love. You know you OUGHT to love them because they know so much and are such active workers in the church, but you have to keep reminding yourself of it all the time or else you forget. There was another little girl at the manse to tea, from the White Sands Sunday school. Her name was Laurette Bradley, and she was a very nice little girl. Not exactly a kindred spirit, you know, but still very nice. We had an elegant tea, and I think I kept all the rules of etiquette pretty well. After tea Mrs. Allan played and sang and she got Lauretta and me to sing too. Mrs. Allan says I have a good voice and she says I must sing in the Sunday-school choir after this. You can't think how I was thrilled at the mere thought. I've longed so to sing in the Sunday-school choir, as Diana does, but I feared it was an honor I could never aspire to. Lauretta had to go home early because there is a big concert in the White Sands Hotel tonight and her sister is to recite at it. Lauretta says that the Americans at the hotel give a concert every fortnight in aid of the Charlottetown hospital, and they ask lots of the White Sands people to recite. Lauretta said she expected to be asked herself someday. I just gazed at her in awe. After she had gone Mrs. Allan and I had a heart-to-heart talk. I told her everything—about Mrs. Thomas and the twins and Katie Maurice and Violetta and coming to Green Gables and my troubles over geometry. And would you believe it, Marilla? Mrs. Allan told me she was a dunce at geometry too. You don't know how that encouraged me. Mrs. Lynde came to the manse just before I left, and what do you think, Marilla? The trustees have hired a new teacher and it's a lady. Her name is Miss Muriel Stacy. Isn't that a romantic name? Mrs. Lynde says they've never had a female teacher in Avonlea before and she thinks it is a dangerous innovation. But I think it will be splendid to have a lady teacher, and I really don't see how I'm going to live through the two weeks before school begins. I'm so impatient to see her."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，我度过了一段最迷人的时光。我觉得我没有白活，即使我再也不会被邀请到豪宅喝茶，我也会永远有这样的感觉。当我到达那里时，艾伦夫人在门口迎接了我。她穿着最甜美的淡粉色透明纱连衣裙，有几十条褶边和肘袖，她看起来就像一个六翼天使。我真的想我想成为一个玛丽拉，当我长大后，牧师可能不会介意我的红头发，因为他不会考虑这些世俗的事情，但当然，一个人必须天生善良，而我永远不会那样，所以我认为有些人天生善良是没有用的，你知道，我是其他人之一。我认为，像几何学那样的成功是很重要的，但你不认为艾伦夫人是天生善良的人之一吗？你知道有些人，比如马修和艾伦夫人，你可以毫不费力地去爱他们，因为你知道你应该努力去爱他们。他们知道很多，而且在教堂里很活跃，但你必须一直提醒自己，否则你会忘记。还有另一个小女孩在喝茶，她的名字叫劳雷特·布拉德利，她是一个非常好的小女孩，你知道，但仍然非常好。我们喝了一杯优雅的茶，我认为我很好地遵守了茶后的礼仪。她让劳雷塔和我也唱歌，她说我一定要在主日学校合唱团唱歌，你无法想象我多么渴望能像戴安娜那样在主日学校唱诗班唱歌，但我担心这是我永远无法企及的荣誉。劳雷塔必须早点回家，因为今晚白沙酒店有一场大型音乐会。劳雷塔说，美国人每两周都会为夏洛特敦医院举办一场音乐会，他们要求很多白沙人来朗诵。劳雷塔说，在她离开后，我和艾伦夫人进行了一次交心的谈话，我告诉了她关于托马斯夫人和双胞胎以及凯蒂·莫里斯和维奥莱塔的一切。盖布尔斯和我在几何学方面的麻烦，你相信吗？艾伦夫人告诉我，林德夫人在我离开之前来到了庄园，你觉得怎么样？她的名字叫穆里尔·史黛西小姐，这不是一个浪漫的名字吗？以前在埃文利，她认为这是一个危险的创新，但我认为有一位女老师真是太棒了，我真的不知道我将如何度过开学前的两周。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 23 章：关于荣誉冒险的悲剧

paragraphs.en: Anne had to live through more than two weeks, as it happened. Almost a month having elapsed since the liniment cake episode, it was high time for her to get into fresh trouble of some sort, little mistakes, such as absentmindedly emptying a pan of skim milk into a basket of yarn balls in the pantry instead of into the pigs' bucket, and walking clean over the edge of the log bridge into the brook while wrapped in imaginative reverie, not really being worth counting.
paragraphs.zh: 碰巧，安妮不得不熬过两个多星期。搽剂糕事件过去快一个月了，她又要遇到新的麻烦了，一些小错误，比如心不在焉地将一锅脱脂牛奶倒进食品储藏室里的一篮子毛线球里，而不是倒进猪桶里，或者带着幻想从独木桥边走入小溪，实在不值一提。

paragraphs.en: A week after the tea at the manse Diana Barry gave a party.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜·巴里在庄园喝茶一周后举办了一场聚会。

paragraphs.en: "Small and select," Anne assured Marilla. "Just the girls in our class."
paragraphs.zh: “小而精选，”安妮向玛丽拉保证。 “就我们班的女生。”

paragraphs.en: They had a very good time and nothing untoward happened until after tea, when they found themselves in the Barry garden, a little tired of all their games and ripe for any enticing form of mischief which might present itself. This presently took the form of "daring."
paragraphs.zh: 他们度过了一段愉快的时光，没有发生任何不愉快的事情，直到喝完茶后，他们发现自己来到了巴里花园，对所有的游戏都感到有点厌倦，并准备好进行任何可能出现的诱人恶作剧。这现在表现为“大胆”。

paragraphs.en: Daring was the fashionable amusement among the Avonlea small fry just then. It had begun among the boys, but soon spread to the girls, and all the silly things that were done in Avonlea that summer because the doers thereof were "dared" to do them would fill a book by themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 当时，大胆是埃文利小混混中流行的娱乐活动。它在男孩中开始，但很快就蔓延到女孩们，那年夏天在埃文利所做的所有愚蠢的事情，因为这些事情的实施者“敢于”做，这些事情本身就可以写成一本书。

paragraphs.en: First of all Carrie Sloane dared Ruby Gillis to climb to a certain point in the huge old willow tree before the front door; which Ruby Gillis, albeit in mortal dread of the fat green caterpillars with which said tree was infested and with the fear of her mother before her eyes if she should tear her new muslin dress, nimbly did, to the discomfiture of the aforesaid Carrie Sloane. Then Josie Pye dared Jane Andrews to hop on her left leg around the garden without stopping once or putting her right foot to the ground; which Jane Andrews gamely tried to do, but gave out at the third corner and had to confess herself defeated.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，凯莉·斯隆（Carrie Sloane）向鲁比·吉利斯（Ruby Gillis）发起挑战，让她爬到前门前那棵巨大的老柳树上的某个位置；鲁比·吉利斯虽然非常害怕那棵树上长满了肥大的绿色毛毛虫，也担心她的母亲会撕破她的新平纹细布裙子，但她还是敏捷地做到了，这让前面提到的凯丽·斯隆感到很沮丧。然后乔西·派伊（Josie Pye）向简·安德鲁斯（Jane Andrews）挑战，用她的左腿在花园里跳来跳去，一次也没有停下来，右脚也没有着地。简·安德鲁斯勇敢地尝试这样做，但在第三个拐角处失败了，不得不承认自己失败了。

paragraphs.en: Josie's triumph being rather more pronounced than good taste permitted, Anne Shirley dared her to walk along the top of the board fence which bounded the garden to the east. Now, to "walk" board fences requires more skill and steadiness of head and heel than one might suppose who has never tried it. But Josie Pye, if deficient in some qualities that make for popularity, had at least a natural and inborn gift, duly cultivated, for walking board fences. Josie walked the Barry fence with an airy unconcern which seemed to imply that a little thing like that wasn't worth a "dare." Reluctant admiration greeted her exploit, for most of the other girls could appreciate it, having suffered many things themselves in their efforts to walk fences. Josie descended from her perch, flushed with victory, and darted a defiant glance at Anne.
paragraphs.zh: 乔西的胜利过于明显，超出了良好品味所允许的范围，安妮·雪莉鼓励她沿着东边花园的木板栅栏的顶部行走。现在，“行走”木板栅栏需要更多的技巧以及头和脚跟的稳定性，这比从未尝试过的人可能想象的要多。但乔西·派伊（Josie Pye）虽然缺乏某些受欢迎的品质，但至少有一种天生的、与生俱来的天赋，经过适当的培养，可以做走木板栅栏。乔西在巴里的栅栏上走着，神情淡漠，似乎暗示这样的小事不值得“冒险”。她的功绩得到了不情愿的钦佩，因为大多数其他女孩都能够欣赏她的这一点，因为她们自己在努力跨越栅栏的过程中遭受了很多苦难。乔西从座位上下来，胜利的脸红了，挑衅地看了安妮一眼。

paragraphs.en: Anne tossed her red braids.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮甩动她的红辫子。

paragraphs.en: "I don't think it's such a very wonderful thing to walk a little, low, board fence," she said. "I knew a girl in Marysville who could walk the ridgepole of a roof."
paragraphs.zh: “我不认为在低矮的木板栅栏上行走并不是一件多么美妙的事情，”她说。 “我在马里斯维尔认识一个女孩，她可以爬上屋顶的屋脊。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't believe it," said Josie flatly. "I don't believe anybody could walk a ridgepole. YOU couldn't, anyhow."
paragraphs.zh: “我不相信，”乔西淡淡地说。 “我不相信有人能走上屋脊。无论如何，你不能。”

paragraphs.en: "Couldn't I?" cried Anne rashly.
paragraphs.zh: “我不能吗？”安妮急忙喊道。

paragraphs.en: "Then I dare you to do it," said Josie defiantly. "I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof."
paragraphs.zh: “那我敢说你敢这么做。”乔西挑衅地说。 “我敢说你敢爬上去，走在巴里先生厨房屋顶的屋脊上。”

paragraphs.en: Anne turned pale, but there was clearly only one thing to be done. She walked toward the house, where a ladder was leaning against the kitchen roof. All the fifth-class girls said, "Oh!" partly in excitement, partly in dismay.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮脸色惨白，但显然只有一件事要做。她朝房子走去，厨房的屋顶上斜靠着一架梯子。五年级的女生们齐声说道：“哦！”一半是兴奋，一半是沮丧。

paragraphs.en: "Don't you do it, Anne," entreated Diana. "You'll fall off and be killed. Never mind Josie Pye. It isn't fair to dare anybody to do anything so dangerous."
paragraphs.zh: “你别这么做，安妮，”戴安娜恳求道。 “你会摔下来并被杀。别介意乔西·派伊。敢于任何人做如此危险的事情是不公平的。”

paragraphs.en: "I must do it. My honor is at stake," said Anne solemnly. "I shall walk that ridgepole, Diana, or perish in the attempt. If I am killed you are to have my pearl bead ring."
paragraphs.zh: “我必须这么做，我的荣誉受到威胁。”安妮严肃地说。 “戴安娜，我将走上那根屋脊，否则就会丧命。如果我死了，你将得到我的珍珠戒指。”

paragraphs.en: Anne climbed the ladder amid breathless silence, gained the ridgepole, balanced herself uprightly on that precarious footing, and started to walk along it, dizzily conscious that she was uncomfortably high up in the world and that walking ridgepoles was not a thing in which your imagination helped you out much. Nevertheless, she managed to take several steps before the catastrophe came. Then she swayed, lost her balance, stumbled, staggered, and fell, sliding down over the sun-baked roof and crashing off it through the tangle of Virginia creeper beneath—all before the dismayed circle below could give a simultaneous, terrified shriek.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在令人窒息的寂静中爬上梯子，爬上屋脊，在不稳定的基础上保持平衡，然后开始沿着梯子行走，她头晕地意识到自己在世界的高处，感到不舒服，而行走屋脊并不是你的想象力能帮助你的事情。尽管如此，她还是在灾难到来之前成功迈出了几步。然后她摇摇晃晃，失去平衡，踉踉跄跄，踉踉跄跄，摔倒了，从阳光炙烤的屋顶上滑下来，穿过下面缠结的弗吉尼亚爬山虎，从屋顶上摔了下来——所有这一切都发生在下面惊慌失措的圆圈同时发出一声惊恐的尖叫之前。

paragraphs.en: If Anne had tumbled off the roof on the side up which she had ascended Diana would probably have fallen heir to the pearl bead ring then and there. Fortunately she fell on the other side, where the roof extended down over the porch so nearly to the ground that a fall therefrom was a much less serious thing. Nevertheless, when Diana and the other girls had rushed frantically around the house—except Ruby Gillis, who remained as if rooted to the ground and went into hysterics—they found Anne lying all white and limp among the wreck and ruin of the Virginia creeper.
paragraphs.zh: 如果安妮从她所登上的一侧的屋顶上摔下来，戴安娜可能会当场成为珍珠珠戒指的继承人。幸运的是，她是从另一边摔下来的，那里的屋顶一直延伸到门廊上方，离地面很近，所以从那里摔下来并不是什么严重的事情。然而，当戴安娜和其他女孩在房子里疯狂地冲来冲去时——除了鲁比·吉利斯，她仍然像根扎在地上一样，陷入歇斯底里——她们发现安妮全身苍白、软弱无力地躺在弗吉尼亚爬山虎的残骸和废墟中。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, are you killed?" shrieked Diana, throwing herself on her knees beside her friend. "Oh, Anne, dear Anne, speak just one word to me and tell me if you're killed."
paragraphs.zh: “安安，你被杀了？”戴安娜尖叫着，跪倒在她朋友身边。 “哦，安妮，亲爱的安妮，只要对我说一句话，告诉我你是否被杀了。”

paragraphs.en: To the immense relief of all the girls, and especially of Josie Pye, who, in spite of lack of imagination, had been seized with horrible visions of a future branded as the girl who was the cause of Anne Shirley's early and tragic death, Anne sat dizzily up and answered uncertainly:
paragraphs.zh: 让所有女孩们都松了口气，尤其是乔西·派伊，尽管她缺乏想象力，但她还是对未来充满了可怕的幻想，而这个未来被认为是造成安妮·雪莉早年悲惨死亡的原因。安妮头晕目眩地坐了起来，不确定地回答道：

paragraphs.en: "No, Diana, I am not killed, but I think I am rendered unconscious."
paragraphs.zh: “不，戴安娜，我没有被杀，但我想我失去了知觉。”

paragraphs.en: "Where?" sobbed Carrie Sloane. "Oh, where, Anne?" Before Anne could answer Mrs. Barry appeared on the scene. At sight of her Anne tried to scramble to her feet, but sank back again with a sharp little cry of pain.
paragraphs.zh: “在哪里？”嘉莉·斯隆抽泣着。 “噢，安妮，去哪儿？”安妮还没来得及回答，巴里夫人就出现了。安妮一看到她，就想爬起来，但又因疼痛而发出一声尖锐的小叫声，又倒了回去。

paragraphs.en: "What's the matter? Where have you hurt yourself?" demanded Mrs. Barry.
paragraphs.zh: “怎么了？哪里受伤了？”巴里夫人问道。

paragraphs.en: "My ankle," gasped Anne. "Oh, Diana, please find your father and ask him to take me home. I know I can never walk there. And I'm sure I couldn't hop so far on one foot when Jane couldn't even hop around the garden."
paragraphs.zh: “我的脚踝，”安妮喘着气说。 “哦，戴安娜，请找到你的父亲，请他带我回家。我知道我永远无法走到那里。而且我确信，当简甚至无法在花园里跳来跳去时，我也无法用一只脚跳那么远。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla was out in the orchard picking a panful of summer apples when she saw Mr. Barry coming over the log bridge and up the slope, with Mrs. Barry beside him and a whole procession of little girls trailing after him. In his arms he carried Anne, whose head lay limply against his shoulder.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉正在果园里采摘一盘夏季苹果，这时她看到巴里先生走过独木桥，爬上了斜坡，巴里太太在他身边，一队小女孩跟在他后面。他怀里抱着安妮，安妮的头无力地靠在他的肩膀上。

paragraphs.en: At that moment Marilla had a revelation. In the sudden stab of fear that pierced her very heart she realized what Anne had come to mean to her. She would have admitted that she liked Anne—nay, that she was very fond of Anne. But now she knew as she hurried wildly down the slope that Anne was dearer to her than anything else on earth.
paragraphs.zh: 就在那一刻，玛丽拉有了一个启示。 In the sudden stab of fear that pierced her very heart she realized what Anne had come to mean to her. She would have admitted that she liked Anne—nay, that she was very fond of Anne. But now she knew as she hurried wildly down the slope that Anne was dearer to her than anything else on earth.

paragraphs.en: "Mr. Barry, what has happened to her?" she gasped, more white and shaken than the self-contained, sensible Marilla had been for many years.
paragraphs.zh: “巴里先生，她怎么了？”她喘着气，脸色比多年来自持、理智的玛丽拉更加苍白和颤抖。

paragraphs.en: Anne herself answered, lifting her head.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮抬起头回答道。

paragraphs.en: "Don't be very frightened, Marilla. I was walking the ridgepole and I fell off. I expect I have sprained my ankle. But, Marilla, I might have broken my neck. Let us look on the bright side of things."
paragraphs.zh: “别太害怕，玛丽拉。我在屋脊上行走时摔了下来。我想我扭伤了脚踝。但是，玛丽拉，我可能摔断了脖子。让我们看看事情光明的一面。”

paragraphs.en: "I might have known you'd go and do something of the sort when I let you go to that party," said Marilla, sharp and shrewish in her very relief. "Bring her in here, Mr. Barry, and lay her on the sofa. Mercy me, the child has gone and fainted!"
paragraphs.zh: “当我让你去参加那个聚会时，我可能就知道你会去做类似的事情，”马里拉说道，她的语气中充满了宽慰，语气尖锐而泼辣。 “把她带进来，巴里先生，把她放在沙发上。可怜我，孩子已经走了，晕倒了！”

paragraphs.en: It was quite true. Overcome by the pain of her injury, Anne had one more of her wishes granted to her. She had fainted dead away.
paragraphs.zh: 这是千真万确的。安妮克服了受伤的痛苦，她的一个愿望又实现了。她已经昏过去了。
