paragraphs.en: Matthew, hastily summoned from the harvest field, was straightway dispatched for the doctor, who in due time came, to discover that the injury was more serious than they had supposed. Anne's ankle was broken.
paragraphs.zh: 马修从收割地里被匆匆叫来，立即被派去见医生，医生及时赶到，发现伤势比他们想象的更严重。安妮的脚踝骨折了。

paragraphs.en: That night, when Marilla went up to the east gable, where a white-faced girl was lying, a plaintive voice greeted her from the bed.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，当玛丽拉登上东山墙时，那里躺着一个白脸女孩，床上传来了一个哀怨的声音。

paragraphs.en: "Aren't you very sorry for me, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “你不是很为我难过吗，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: "It was your own fault," said Marilla, twitching down the blind and lighting a lamp.
paragraphs.zh: “这是你自己的错。”玛丽拉拉下百叶窗，点着一盏灯说道。

paragraphs.en: "And that is just why you should be sorry for me," said Anne, "because the thought that it is all my own fault is what makes it so hard. If I could blame it on anybody I would feel so much better. But what would you have done, Marilla, if you had been dared to walk a ridgepole?"
paragraphs.zh: “这就是为什么你应该为我感到难过，”安妮说，“因为一想到这一切都是我自己的错，那就让事情变得如此困难。如果我能把这一切归咎于任何人，我会感觉好多了。但是，玛丽拉，如果你敢于走上屋脊，你会怎么做呢？”

paragraphs.en: "I'd have stayed on good firm ground and let them dare away. Such absurdity!" said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “我本来会站在坚实的地面上，让他们胆敢离开。这真是荒谬！”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "But you have such strength of mind, Marilla. I haven't. I just felt that I couldn't bear Josie Pye's scorn. She would have crowed over me all my life. And I think I have been punished so much that you needn't be very cross with me, Marilla. It's not a bit nice to faint, after all. And the doctor hurt me dreadfully when he was setting my ankle. I won't be able to go around for six or seven weeks and I'll miss the new lady teacher. She won't be new any more by the time I'm able to go to school. And Gil—everybody will get ahead of me in class. Oh, I am an afflicted mortal. But I'll try to bear it all bravely if only you won't be cross with me, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “但是你的意志力如此坚强，玛丽拉。我没有。我只是觉得我无法忍受乔西·派伊的蔑视。她会在我的一生中夸耀我。而且我想我已经受到了如此多的惩罚，你不必对我很生气，玛丽拉。毕竟晕倒可不太好。医生在固定我的脚踝时把我伤得很厉害。我将在六七个星期内无法行走，而且当我能去学校的时候，我会想念新来的女老师的，还有吉尔——哦，我是一个痛苦的凡人，但只要你不生我的气，我就会勇敢地承受这一切。”

paragraphs.en: "There, there, I'm not cross," said Marilla. "You're an unlucky child, there's no doubt about that; but as you say, you'll have the suffering of it. Here now, try and eat some supper."
paragraphs.zh: “好了，好了，我没有生气，”玛丽拉说。 “你是个不幸的孩子，这是毫无疑问的；但正如你所说，你会受苦受难的。现在，试着吃点晚饭吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Isn't it fortunate I've got such an imagination?" said Anne. "It will help me through splendidly, I expect. What do people who haven't any imagination do when they break their bones, do you suppose, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “我有这样的想象力，难道不是很幸运吗？”安妮说。 “我希望这会帮助我顺利度过难关。你认为那些没有想象力的人骨折后会做什么，你觉得吗，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: Anne had good reason to bless her imagination many a time and oft during the tedious seven weeks that followed. But she was not solely dependent on it. She had many visitors and not a day passed without one or more of the schoolgirls dropping in to bring her flowers and books and tell her all the happenings in the juvenile world of Avonlea.
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来的乏味的七周里，安妮有充分的理由多次祝福她的想象力。但她不仅仅依赖于此。她有很多访客，每天都会有一个或多个女学生来给她带来鲜花和书籍，并向她讲述埃文利少年世界中发生的所有事情。

paragraphs.en: "Everybody has been so good and kind, Marilla," sighed Anne happily, on the day when she could first limp across the floor. "It isn't very pleasant to be laid up; but there is a bright side to it, Marilla. You find out how many friends you have. Why, even Superintendent Bell came to see me, and he's really a very fine man. Not a kindred spirit, of course; but still I like him and I'm awfully sorry I ever criticized his prayers. I believe now he really does mean them, only he has got into the habit of saying them as if he didn't. He could get over that if he'd take a little trouble. I gave him a good broad hint. I told him how hard I tried to make my own little private prayers interesting. He told me all about the time he broke his ankle when he was a boy. It does seem so strange to think of Superintendent Bell ever being a boy. Even my imagination has its limits, for I can't imagine THAT. When I try to imagine him as a boy I see him with gray whiskers and spectacles, just as he looks in Sunday school, only small. Now, it's so easy to imagine Mrs. Allan as a little girl. Mrs. Allan has been to see me fourteen times. Isn't that something to be proud of, Marilla? When a minister's wife has so many claims on her time! She is such a cheerful person to have visit you, too. She never tells you it's your own fault and she hopes you'll be a better girl on account of it. Mrs. Lynde always told me that when she came to see me; and she said it in a kind of way that made me feel she might hope I'd be a better girl but didn't really believe I would. Even Josie Pye came to see me. I received her as politely as I could, because I think she was sorry she dared me to walk a ridgepole. If I had been killed she would had to carry a dark burden of remorse all her life. Diana has been a faithful friend. She's been over every day to cheer my lonely pillow. But oh, I shall be so glad when I can go to school for I've heard such exciting things about the new teacher. The girls all think she is perfectly sweet. Diana says she has the loveliest fair curly hair and such fascinating eyes. She dresses beautifully, and her sleeve puffs are bigger than anybody else's in Avonlea. Every other Friday afternoon she has recitations and everybody has to say a piece or take part in a dialogue. Oh, it's just glorious to think of it. Josie Pye says she hates it but that is just because Josie has so little imagination. Diana and Ruby Gillis and Jane Andrews are preparing a dialogue, called 'A Morning Visit,' for next Friday. And the Friday afternoons they don't have recitations Miss Stacy takes them all to the woods for a 'field' day and they study ferns and flowers and birds. And they have physical culture exercises every morning and evening. Mrs. Lynde says she never heard of such goings on and it all comes of having a lady teacher. But I think it must be splendid and I believe I shall find that Miss Stacy is a kindred spirit."
paragraphs.zh: “每个人都那么善良，玛丽拉，”安妮高兴地叹了口气，那天她第一次一瘸一拐地走过地板。 “卧床不起，但也有好的一面，玛丽拉。你看看你有多少朋友。哎呀，连贝尔警长都来看我了，他真的是一个很好的人。当然，不是志同道合的人；但我仍然喜欢他，我很抱歉我曾经批评过他的祈祷。我相信现在他确实是认真的，只是他养成了说这些话的习惯，就好像他没有那样。他可以克服这个问题，如果我给了他一个很好的暗示。我告诉他我多么努力地让自己的小私人祈祷变得有趣。他告诉我他小时候摔断脚踝的事情，即使我的想象力也有其局限性，因为我无法想象他是一个男孩，就像他在主日学校的样子一样。现在，很容易想象艾伦夫人来见我十四次了，玛丽拉，她也是一个很高兴的人，她从来没有告诉过你这是你自己的错，她希望你会因此而成为一个更好的女孩，她说：这让我觉得她可能希望我能成为一个更好的女孩，但我并不真的相信我会这样做。即使是乔西·派伊，我也尽可能礼貌地接待了她，因为我认为她很抱歉她敢于让我走上屋脊，如果我被杀了，她将不得不背负着悔恨的重担。戴安娜一直是我的忠实朋友，但哦，我会很高兴。当我上学时，我听到了关于新老师的令人兴奋的事情。戴安娜说她有最可爱的金发和迷人的眼睛，她的袖子比埃文利的其他人都大。哦，想到这一点乔西·派伊说她讨厌它，这真是太棒了。乔西和鲁比·吉利斯以及简·安德鲁斯正在为下周五准备一场名为“早晨访问”的对话，而周五下午，史黛西小姐会带他们去树林里进行“田野”活动，他们每天早上和晚上都会进行体育锻炼。太棒了，我相信我会发现史黛西小姐是志同道合的人。”

paragraphs.en: "There's one thing plain to be seen, Anne," said Marilla, "and that is that your fall off the Barry roof hasn't injured your tongue at all."
paragraphs.zh: “有一点是显而易见的，安妮，”玛丽拉说，“那就是你从巴里屋顶上摔下来根本没有伤到你的舌头。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 24 章：史黛西老师与音乐会

paragraphs.en: It was October again when Anne was ready to go back to school—a glorious October, all red and gold, with mellow mornings when the valleys were filled with delicate mists as if the spirit of autumn had poured them in for the sun to drain—amethyst, pearl, silver, rose, and smoke-blue. The dews were so heavy that the fields glistened like cloth of silver and there were such heaps of rustling leaves in the hollows of many-stemmed woods to run crisply through. The Birch Path was a canopy of yellow and the ferns were sear and brown all along it. There was a tang in the very air that inspired the hearts of small maidens tripping, unlike snails, swiftly and willingly to school; and it WAS jolly to be back again at the little brown desk beside Diana, with Ruby Gillis nodding across the aisle and Carrie Sloane sending up notes and Julia Bell passing a "chew" of gum down from the back seat. Anne drew a long breath of happiness as she sharpened her pencil and arranged her picture cards in her desk. Life was certainly very interesting.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮准备回学校的时候，又到了十月——一个光荣的十月，一切都是红色和金色，早晨是柔和的，山谷里弥漫着淡淡的薄雾，仿佛秋天的精灵把它们倾注进来，让阳光流干——紫水晶、珍珠、银色、玫瑰色和烟蓝色。露水如此浓重，田野像银布一样闪闪发光，多茎树林的空洞里有一堆堆沙沙作响的树叶，清脆地穿过。白桦林小径是一片黄色的树冠，沿途的蕨类植物都是焦黄的。空气中弥漫着一股腥味，激发了小姑娘们的心，不像蜗牛，迅速而心甘情愿地去上学；再次回到戴安娜旁边的棕色小桌子旁，真是令人高兴，鲁比·吉利斯在过道对面点头，凯莉·斯隆发来纸条，朱莉娅·贝尔从后座上递下一块“嚼”口香糖。安妮幸福地长长地吸了一口气，削尖了铅笔，把画卡放在书桌上。生活当然非常有趣。

paragraphs.en: In the new teacher she found another true and helpful friend. Miss Stacy was a bright, sympathetic young woman with the happy gift of winning and holding the affections of her pupils and bringing out the best that was in them mentally and morally. Anne expanded like a flower under this wholesome influence and carried home to the admiring Matthew and the critical Marilla glowing accounts of schoolwork and aims.
paragraphs.zh: 在新老师身上，她找到了另一个真正的、乐于助人的朋友。史黛西小姐是一位聪明、富有同情心的年轻女子，她拥有赢得和保持学生们的喜爱、并在精神和道德上发挥出他们最好的一面的幸福天赋。在这种有益健康的影响下，安妮像一朵花一样绽放，并带回了令人钦佩的马修和玛丽拉对学业和目标的批判性热情描述。

paragraphs.en: "I love Miss Stacy with my whole heart, Marilla. She is so ladylike and she has such a sweet voice. When she pronounces my name I feel INSTINCTIVELY that she's spelling it with an E. We had recitations this afternoon. I just wish you could have been there to hear me recite 'Mary, Queen of Scots.' I just put my whole soul into it. Ruby Gillis told me coming home that the way I said the line, 'Now for my father's arm,' she said, 'my woman's heart farewell,' just made her blood run cold."
paragraphs.zh: “我全心全意地爱史黛西小姐，玛丽拉。她是如此淑女，声音如此甜美。当她念出我的名字时，我本能地感觉到她用的是 E。今天下午我们进行了朗诵。我只是希望你能在那里听我朗诵‘苏格兰女王玛丽’。”我只是全身心地投入其中。鲁比·吉利斯（Ruby Gillis）回家后告诉我，我说“现在拥抱我父亲的手臂”，“我女人的心告别”，让她浑身发冷。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, you might recite it for me some of these days, out in the barn," suggested Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你可以找几天在谷仓里给我背诵一下，”马修建议道。

paragraphs.en: "Of course I will," said Anne meditatively, "but I won't be able to do it so well, I know. It won't be so exciting as it is when you have a whole schoolful before you hanging breathlessly on your words. I know I won't be able to make your blood run cold."
paragraphs.zh: “我当然会，”安妮若有所思地说，“但我知道，我不会做得这么好。在你气喘吁吁地坚持自己的话之前，它不会像整个学校那样令人兴奋。我知道我无法让你热血沸腾。”

paragraphs.en: "Mrs. Lynde says it made HER blood run cold to see the boys climbing to the very tops of those big trees on Bell's hill after crows' nests last Friday," said Marilla. "I wonder at Miss Stacy for encouraging it."
paragraphs.zh: “林德夫人说，上周五看到孩子们在鸟巢后爬到贝尔山上那些大树的树顶上，她感到很冷，”马里拉说。 “我想知道史黛西小姐是否鼓励这样做。”

paragraphs.en: "But we wanted a crow's nest for nature study," explained Anne. "That was on our field afternoon. Field afternoons are splendid, Marilla. And Miss Stacy explains everything so beautifully. We have to write compositions on our field afternoons and I write the best ones."
paragraphs.zh: “但我们想要一个用于自然研究的瞭望台，”安妮解释道。 “那是在我们的田野下午。田野的下午真是太棒了，玛丽拉。史黛西小姐把一切都解释得那么漂亮。我们必须在田野的下午写作文，而我写的最好。”

paragraphs.en: "It's very vain of you to say so then. You'd better let your teacher say it."
paragraphs.zh: “你这么说实在是太虚荣了，还是让你的老师说吧。”

paragraphs.en: "But she DID say it, Marilla. And indeed I'm not vain about it. How can I be, when I'm such a dunce at geometry? Although I'm really beginning to see through it a little, too. Miss Stacy makes it so clear. Still, I'll never be good at it and I assure you it is a humbling reflection. But I love writing compositions. Mostly Miss Stacy lets us choose our own subjects; but next week we are to write a composition on some remarkable person. It's hard to choose among so many remarkable people who have lived. Mustn't it be splendid to be remarkable and have compositions written about you after you're dead? Oh, I would dearly love to be remarkable. I think when I grow up I'll be a trained nurse and go with the Red Crosses to the field of battle as a messenger of mercy. That is, if I don't go out as a foreign missionary. That would be very romantic, but one would have to be very good to be a missionary, and that would be a stumbling block. We have physical culture exercises every day, too. They make you graceful and promote digestion."
paragraphs.zh: “但她确实这么说过，玛丽拉。事实上，我对此并不自负。当我对几何学这么笨的时候，我怎么能自负呢？虽然我也真的开始有点看穿它了。史黛西小姐说得很清楚。不过，我永远不会擅长它，我向你保证，这是一个令人谦卑的反思。但我喜欢写作文。史黛西小姐大多让我们选择自己的主题；但下周我们要写一篇关于某个杰出人物的作文。在这么多杰出的人中做出选择，在你死后留下关于你的文章不是很美妙吗？哦，我想当我长大后，我会成为一名训练有素的护士，作为一名仁慈的使者，那将是非常浪漫的，但必须是一名优秀的人。传教士，这将是一个绊脚石，我们也每天进行体育锻炼，它们让你变得优雅并促进消化。”

paragraphs.en: "Promote fiddlesticks!" said Marilla, who honestly thought it was all nonsense.
paragraphs.zh: “推广小提琴！”玛丽拉说，她真的认为这都是无稽之谈。

paragraphs.en: But all the field afternoons and recitation Fridays and physical culture contortions paled before a project which Miss Stacy brought forward in November. This was that the scholars of Avonlea school should get up a concert and hold it in the hall on Christmas Night, for the laudable purpose of helping to pay for a schoolhouse flag. The pupils one and all taking graciously to this plan, the preparations for a program were begun at once. And of all the excited performers-elect none was so excited as Anne Shirley, who threw herself into the undertaking heart and soul, hampered as she was by Marilla's disapproval. Marilla thought it all rank foolishness.
paragraphs.zh: 但在史黛西小姐十一月份提出的一个项目面前，所有的下午田野活动、周五的背诵和体育训练都显得黯然失色。埃文利学校的学者们应该在圣诞节晚上在大厅举行一场音乐会，以帮助支付校舍旗帜的值得称赞的目的。学生们都欣然接受了这个计划，节目的准备工作立刻开始了。在所有激动的当选表演者中，没有人比安妮·雪莉更兴奋了，她全心全意地投入到这项事业中，但玛丽拉的反对却让她受到了阻碍。玛丽拉认为这一切都是愚蠢的。

paragraphs.en: "It's just filling your heads up with nonsense and taking time that ought to be put on your lessons," she grumbled. "I don't approve of children's getting up concerts and racing about to practices. It makes them vain and forward and fond of gadding."
paragraphs.zh: “这只是让你脑子里充满了废话，占用了你应该花在功课上的时间，”她抱怨道。 “我不赞成孩子们在音乐会上起床后赶着去练习。这让他们变得虚荣、向前、喜欢闲逛。”

paragraphs.en: "But think of the worthy object," pleaded Anne. "A flag will cultivate a spirit of patriotism, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “但是想想有价值的东西，”安妮恳求道。 “国旗会培养爱国主义精神，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: "Fudge! There's precious little patriotism in the thoughts of any of you. All you want is a good time."
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道！你们每个人的思想中都没有一点宝贵的爱国主义。你们想要的只是一段美好时光。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, when you can combine patriotism and fun, isn't it all right? Of course it's real nice to be getting up a concert. We're going to have six choruses and Diana is to sing a solo. I'm in two dialogues—'The Society for the Suppression of Gossip' and 'The Fairy Queen.' The boys are going to have a dialogue too. And I'm to have two recitations, Marilla. I just tremble when I think of it, but it's a nice thrilly kind of tremble. And we're to have a tableau at the last—'Faith, Hope and Charity.' Diana and Ruby and I are to be in it, all draped in white with flowing hair. I'm to be Hope, with my hands clasped—so—and my eyes uplifted. I'm going to practice my recitations in the garret. Don't be alarmed if you hear me groaning. I have to groan heartrendingly in one of them, and it's really hard to get up a good artistic groan, Marilla. Josie Pye is sulky because she didn't get the part she wanted in the dialogue. She wanted to be the fairy queen. That would have been ridiculous, for who ever heard of a fairy queen as fat as Josie? Fairy queens must be slender. Jane Andrews is to be the queen and I am to be one of her maids of honor. Josie says she thinks a red-haired fairy is just as ridiculous as a fat one, but I do not let myself mind what Josie says. I'm to have a wreath of white roses on my hair and Ruby Gillis is going to lend me her slippers because I haven't any of my own. It's necessary for fairies to have slippers, you know. You couldn't imagine a fairy wearing boots, could you? Especially with copper toes? We are going to decorate the hall with creeping spruce and fir mottoes with pink tissue-paper roses in them. And we are all to march in two by two after the audience is seated, while Emma White plays a march on the organ. Oh, Marilla, I know you are not so enthusiastic about it as I am, but don't you hope your little Anne will distinguish herself?"
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，当你能把爱国主义和乐趣结合起来时，不是吗？当然，能举办一场音乐会真是太好了。我们将有六个合唱团，戴安娜将独唱。我有两个对话——《平息流言协会》和《仙女女王》。男孩们也将进行对话。我要朗诵两遍，玛丽拉。我一想到它就浑身颤抖，但那是一种令人兴奋的颤抖。最后我们将看到一个画面——“信仰、希望和慈善。”戴安娜、鲁比和我都在里面，都穿着白色的衣服，头发飘逸。我要成为希望，双手紧握——就这样——并且我的眼睛抬起来。我要去阁楼里练习念诵。如果你听到我的呻吟，请不要惊慌。我不得不在其中一个中发出令人心碎的呻吟，而要发出良好的艺术呻吟确实很难，玛丽拉。乔西·派伊很生气，因为她在对话中没有得到她想要的部分。她想成为仙女女王。这太荒谬了，因为谁听说过像乔西这样胖的仙女女王呢？仙女女王一定是苗条的。简·安德鲁斯将成为女王，而我将成为她的伴娘之一。乔西说她认为红发仙子和胖仙子一样可笑，但我并不介意乔西说的话。我的头发上要戴一顶白玫瑰花环，鲁比·吉利斯会把她的拖鞋借给我，因为我没有自己的拖鞋。仙女们必备拖鞋，你懂的。你无法想象仙女穿着靴子，不是吗？尤其是铜脚趾？我们要用匍匐云杉和冷杉的座右铭来装饰大厅，里面还有粉红色的薄纸玫瑰。观众入座后，我们要两两列队行进，艾玛·怀特则用管风琴演奏进行曲。哦，玛丽拉，我知道你不像我那么热心，但是你不希望你的小安妮能脱颖而出吗？”

paragraphs.en: "All I hope is that you'll behave yourself. I'll be heartily glad when all this fuss is over and you'll be able to settle down. You are simply good for nothing just now with your head stuffed full of dialogues and groans and tableaus. As for your tongue, it's a marvel it's not clean worn out."
paragraphs.zh: “我只希望你能规矩点。等这一切大惊小怪结束，你就能安定下来，我会由衷地高兴。你现在简直一无是处，脑子里塞满了对话、呻吟和场面。至于你的舌头，它没有完全磨损真是奇迹。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed and betook herself to the back yard, over which a young new moon was shining through the leafless poplar boughs from an apple-green western sky, and where Matthew was splitting wood. Anne perched herself on a block and talked the concert over with him, sure of an appreciative and sympathetic listener in this instance at least.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，走到后院，苹果绿的西方天空中，一轮新月正透过光秃秃的白杨树枝照耀着，马修正在那里劈柴。安妮坐在一个街区上，与他谈论音乐会，至少在这种情况下，她确信她是一位欣赏和同情的听众。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I reckon it's going to be a pretty good concert. And I expect you'll do your part fine," he said, smiling down into her eager, vivacious little face. Anne smiled back at him. Those two were the best of friends and Matthew thanked his stars many a time and oft that he had nothing to do with bringing her up. That was Marilla's exclusive duty; if it had been his he would have been worried over frequent conflicts between inclination and said duty. As it was, he was free to, "spoil Anne"—Marilla's phrasing—as much as he liked. But it was not such a bad arrangement after all; a little "appreciation" sometimes does quite as much good as all the conscientious "bringing up" in the world.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我认为这将是一场非常精彩的音乐会。我希望你能很好地完成你的部分，”他说，微笑着看着她热切、活泼的小脸。安妮也对他微笑。这两个人是最好的朋友，马修多次感谢他的明星们，因为他与抚养她无关。这是玛丽拉的专属职责。如果是他的话，他一定会担心自己的倾向和义务之间经常发生冲突。事实上，他可以随心所欲地“宠坏安妮”（玛丽拉的说法）。但这毕竟不是一个糟糕的安排。一点点“欣赏”有时与世界上所有认真的“教养”一样有效。

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 25 章：马修坚持要泡泡袖

paragraphs.en: Matthew was having a bad ten minutes of it. He had come into the kitchen, in the twilight of a cold, gray December evening, and had sat down in the woodbox corner to take off his heavy boots, unconscious of the fact that Anne and a bevy of her schoolmates were having a practice of "The Fairy Queen" in the sitting room. Presently they came trooping through the hall and out into the kitchen, laughing and chattering gaily. They did not see Matthew, who shrank bashfully back into the shadows beyond the woodbox with a boot in one hand and a bootjack in the other, and he watched them shyly for the aforesaid ten minutes as they put on caps and jackets and talked about the dialogue and the concert. Anne stood among them, bright eyed and animated as they; but Matthew suddenly became conscious that there was something about her different from her mates. And what worried Matthew was that the difference impressed him as being something that should not exist. Anne had a brighter face, and bigger, starrier eyes, and more delicate features than the other; even shy, unobservant Matthew had learned to take note of these things; but the difference that disturbed him did not consist in any of these respects. Then in what did it consist?
paragraphs.zh: 马修经历了很糟糕的十分钟。他在十二月一个寒冷、灰暗的夜晚的暮色中走进厨房，坐在木箱角落里脱掉沉重的靴子，没有意识到安妮和她的一群同学正在客厅里练习“仙女女王”。不久，他们成群结队地穿过大厅，走进厨房，欢快地笑着、闲聊着。他们没有看到马修，他一手拿着靴子，另一只手拿着脱鞋器，害羞地缩回木箱外面的阴影里，他害羞地看着他们在上述十分钟里戴上帽子和夹克，谈论对话和音乐会。安妮站在他们中间，和他们一样眼睛明亮，充满活力。但马修突然意识到她和她的伙伴们有些不同。让马修担心的是，这种差异给他留下的印象是不应该存在的。安妮的脸比其他人更明亮，眼睛更大，更有星星，五官也更精致。即使是害羞、不善于观察的马修也学会了注意这些事情。但令他不安的差异并不在于这些方面。那么它的内容是什么？

paragraphs.en: Matthew was haunted by this question long after the girls had gone, arm in arm, down the long, hard-frozen lane and Anne had betaken herself to her books. He could not refer it to Marilla, who, he felt, would be quite sure to sniff scornfully and remark that the only difference she saw between Anne and the other girls was that they sometimes kept their tongues quiet while Anne never did. This, Matthew felt, would be no great help.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们手挽着手沿着长长的、结冰的小巷走去，安妮则专心致志地读书之后，马修一直被这个问题困扰着。他不能把这件事交给玛丽拉，他觉得她肯定会轻蔑地嗤之以鼻，并说她在安妮和其他女孩之间看到的唯一区别是她们有时会保持沉默，而安妮却从不这样做。马修觉得这不会有太大帮助。

paragraphs.en: He had recourse to his pipe that evening to help him study it out, much to Marilla's disgust. After two hours of smoking and hard reflection Matthew arrived at a solution of his problem. Anne was not dressed like the other girls!
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上他求助于烟斗来帮助他研究它，这让玛丽拉很反感。经过两个小时的吸烟和认真思考后，马修找到了解决问题的办法。安妮的穿着和其他女孩不一样！

paragraphs.en: The more Matthew thought about the matter the more he was convinced that Anne never had been dressed like the other girls—never since she had come to Green Gables. Marilla kept her clothed in plain, dark dresses, all made after the same unvarying pattern. If Matthew knew there was such a thing as fashion in dress it was as much as he did; but he was quite sure that Anne's sleeves did not look at all like the sleeves the other girls wore. He recalled the cluster of little girls he had seen around her that evening—all gay in waists of red and blue and pink and white—and he wondered why Marilla always kept her so plainly and soberly gowned.
paragraphs.zh: 马修越想这件​​事，就越确信安妮从来没有像其他女孩那样穿着——自从她来到绿山墙以来，从来没有像其他女孩那样穿着。玛丽拉让她穿着朴素的深色衣服，所有衣服都是按照同样不变的图案制作的。如果马修知道衣着时尚这回事，他也知道。但他很确定安妮的袖子看起来一点也不像其他女孩穿的袖子。他回想起那天晚上他在她周围看到的一群小女孩——全都是穿着红色、蓝色、粉色和白色的腰部的欢快的女孩——他想知道为什么玛丽拉总是让她穿得那么朴素、朴素。

paragraphs.en: Of course, it must be all right. Marilla knew best and Marilla was bringing her up. Probably some wise, inscrutable motive was to be served thereby. But surely it would do no harm to let the child have one pretty dress—something like Diana Barry always wore. Matthew decided that he would give her one; that surely could not be objected to as an unwarranted putting in of his oar. Christmas was only a fortnight off. A nice new dress would be the very thing for a present. Matthew, with a sigh of satisfaction, put away his pipe and went to bed, while Marilla opened all the doors and aired the house.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，一定是没问题的。玛丽拉最清楚，是玛丽拉抚养她长大的。也许这样做是为了达到某种明智的、难以理解的动机。但让孩子拥有一件漂亮的衣服肯定不会有什么坏处——就像戴安娜·巴里总是穿的那样。马修决定给她一个。这肯定不会被认为是他无理划桨。圣诞节只剩下两周了。一件漂亮的新衣服非常适合作为礼物。马修满意地叹了口气，收起烟斗上床睡觉，而玛丽拉则打开所有的门，给屋里通风。

paragraphs.en: The very next evening Matthew betook himself to Carmody to buy the dress, determined to get the worst over and have done with it. It would be, he felt assured, no trifling ordeal. There were some things Matthew could buy and prove himself no mean bargainer; but he knew he would be at the mercy of shopkeepers when it came to buying a girl's dress.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，马修就去卡莫迪买了这件衣服，决心克服最坏的情况并结束这一切。他确信，这不会是一个微不足道的考验。有些东西马修可以买，并证明自己不是一个卑鄙的讨价还价者。但他知道，在购买女孩的衣服时，他会受到店主的摆布。

paragraphs.en: After much cogitation Matthew resolved to go to Samuel Lawson's store instead of William Blair's. To be sure, the Cuthberts always had gone to William Blair's; it was almost as much a matter of conscience with them as to attend the Presbyterian church and vote Conservative. But William Blair's two daughters frequently waited on customers there and Matthew held them in absolute dread. He could contrive to deal with them when he knew exactly what he wanted and could point it out; but in such a matter as this, requiring explanation and consultation, Matthew felt that he must be sure of a man behind the counter. So he would go to Lawson's, where Samuel or his son would wait on him.
paragraphs.zh: 经过深思熟虑，马修决定去塞缪尔·劳森的商店而不是威廉·布莱尔的商店。可以肯定的是，卡斯伯特一家总是去威廉·布莱尔家。对他们来说，这几乎与参加长老会教堂并投票给保守党一样是一个良心问题。但威廉·布莱尔的两个女儿经常在那里接待顾客，马修让她们感到绝对的恐惧。当他确切地知道自己想要什么并能指出来时，他就能设法对付他们。但在这种需要解释和咨询的事情上，马修觉得他必须确定柜台后面有一个人。所以他会去劳森店，塞缪尔或他的儿子会在那里伺候他。

paragraphs.en: Alas! Matthew did not know that Samuel, in the recent expansion of his business, had set up a lady clerk also; she was a niece of his wife's and a very dashing young person indeed, with a huge, drooping pompadour, big, rolling brown eyes, and a most extensive and bewildering smile. She was dressed with exceeding smartness and wore several bangle bracelets that glittered and rattled and tinkled with every movement of her hands. Matthew was covered with confusion at finding her there at all; and those bangles completely wrecked his wits at one fell swoop.
paragraphs.zh: 唉!马修并不知道，塞缪尔最近为了扩大生意，还设立了一名女职员。她是他妻子的侄女，确实是一位风度翩翩的年轻人，有着大而下垂的蓬巴杜，棕色的大眼睛，转动着的眼睛，以及灿烂而令人迷惑的微笑。她穿着极其漂亮，戴着几只手镯，随着她双手的每一个动作，手镯闪闪发光、叮当作响。当马修发现她在那里时，他感到很困惑。而那些手镯一下子就让他彻底失去了理智。

paragraphs.en: "What can I do for you this evening, Mr. Cuthbert?" Miss Lucilla Harris inquired, briskly and ingratiatingly, tapping the counter with both hands.
paragraphs.zh: “今晚我能为您做点什么，卡斯伯特先生？”露西拉·哈里斯小姐用双手敲着柜台，轻快而讨好地问道。

paragraphs.en: "Have you any—any—any—well now, say any garden rakes?" stammered Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: “你有任何——任何——任何——好吧，比如说花园耙子吗？”马修结结巴巴地说。

paragraphs.en: Miss Harris looked somewhat surprised, as well she might, to hear a man inquiring for garden rakes in the middle of December.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里斯小姐在十二月中旬听到一个男人询问花园耙子时，看起来有些惊讶，她也可能会感到惊讶。

paragraphs.en: "I believe we have one or two left over," she said, "but they're upstairs in the lumber room. I'll go and see." During her absence Matthew collected his scattered senses for another effort.
paragraphs.zh: “我相信我们还剩下一两个，”她说，“但它们在楼上的杂物间里。我去看看。”在她不在的这段时间里，马修集中起分散的感官来进行另一项努力。

paragraphs.en: When Miss Harris returned with the rake and cheerfully inquired: "Anything else tonight, Mr. Cuthbert?" Matthew took his courage in both hands and replied: "Well now, since you suggest it, I might as well—take—that is—look at—buy some—some hayseed."
paragraphs.zh: 当哈里斯小姐拿着耙子回来时，高兴地问道：“库斯伯特先生，今晚还有什么事情吗？”马修鼓起勇气回答道：“好吧，既然你这么建议，那我不妨——拿——也就是——看看——买一些——一些干草籽。”

paragraphs.en: Miss Harris had heard Matthew Cuthbert called odd. She now concluded that he was entirely crazy.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里斯小姐曾听人说马修·库斯伯特很奇怪。她现在断定他完全疯了。

paragraphs.en: "We only keep hayseed in the spring," she explained loftily. "We've none on hand just now."
paragraphs.zh: “我们只在春天保留干草籽，”她傲慢地解释道。 “我们现在手头没有。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, certainly—certainly—just as you say," stammered unhappy Matthew, seizing the rake and making for the door. At the threshold he recollected that he had not paid for it and he turned miserably back. While Miss Harris was counting out his change he rallied his powers for a final desperate attempt.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，当然——当然——正如你所说，”马修不高兴地结结巴巴地说，抓起耙子向门口走去。到了门口，他才想起自己还没有付钱，便痛苦地转身回去。当哈里斯小姐正在数着他的改变时，他集结力量进行了最后的绝望尝试。

paragraphs.en: "Well now—if it isn't too much trouble—I might as well—that is—I'd like to look at—at—some sugar."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧——如果不是太麻烦的话——我不妨——也就是说——我想看看——一些糖。”

paragraphs.en: "White or brown?" queried Miss Harris patiently.
paragraphs.zh: “白色还是棕色？”哈里斯小姐耐心地询问。

paragraphs.en: "Oh—well now—brown," said Matthew feebly.
paragraphs.zh: “哦——好吧——棕色，”马修有气无力地说。

paragraphs.en: "There's a barrel of it over there," said Miss Harris, shaking her bangles at it. "It's the only kind we have."
paragraphs.zh: “那边有一桶，”哈里斯小姐一边说，一边对着它晃动手镯。 “这是我们唯一拥有的一种。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll—I'll take twenty pounds of it," said Matthew, with beads of perspiration standing on his forehead.
paragraphs.zh: “我要——我要二十磅，”马修说，额头上冒出了汗珠。

paragraphs.en: Matthew had driven halfway home before he was his own man again. It had been a gruesome experience, but it served him right, he thought, for committing the heresy of going to a strange store. When he reached home he hid the rake in the tool house, but the sugar he carried in to Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 马修已经开车回家一半了，才又恢复了正常。这是一次可怕的经历，但他认为，他犯了去一家陌生商店的异端邪说，这是对的。当他回到家时，他把耙子藏在工具房里，但把糖带给了玛丽拉。

paragraphs.en: "Brown sugar!" exclaimed Marilla. "Whatever possessed you to get so much? You know I never use it except for the hired man's porridge or black fruit cake. Jerry's gone and I've made my cake long ago. It's not good sugar, either—it's coarse and dark—William Blair doesn't usually keep sugar like that."
paragraphs.zh: “红糖！” “玛丽拉喊道。 “到底是什么让你得到这么多？你知道除了雇工的粥或黑果蛋糕之外，我从来不使用它。杰里走了，我很久以前就做好了蛋糕。这也不是好糖——又粗又黑——威廉·布莱尔通常不那样保留糖。”

paragraphs.en: "I—I thought it might come in handy sometime," said Matthew, making good his escape.
paragraphs.zh: “我——我想它有时可能会派上用场，”马修一边说，一边成功逃脱。

paragraphs.en: When Matthew came to think the matter over he decided that a woman was required to cope with the situation. Marilla was out of the question. Matthew felt sure she would throw cold water on his project at once. Remained only Mrs. Lynde; for of no other woman in Avonlea would Matthew have dared to ask advice. To Mrs. Lynde he went accordingly, and that good lady promptly took the matter out of the harassed man's hands.
paragraphs.zh: 当马修仔细考虑这件事时，他决定需要一个女人来应对这种情况。玛丽拉是不可能的。马修确信她会立刻给他的项目泼冷水。只剩下林德太太了。因为埃文利没有其他女人马修敢于征求建议。他相应地去找了林德太太，那位好心的女士立即把这件事从这个受骚扰的人手中接了过来。

paragraphs.en: "Pick out a dress for you to give Anne? To be sure I will. I'm going to Carmody tomorrow and I'll attend to it. Have you something particular in mind? No? Well, I'll just go by my own judgment then. I believe a nice rich brown would just suit Anne, and William Blair has some new gloria in that's real pretty. Perhaps you'd like me to make it up for her, too, seeing that if Marilla was to make it Anne would probably get wind of it before the time and spoil the surprise? Well, I'll do it. No, it isn't a mite of trouble. I like sewing. I'll make it to fit my niece, Jenny Gillis, for she and Anne are as like as two peas as far as figure goes."
paragraphs.zh: “给你挑一件衣服送给安妮？我当然会的。我明天要去卡莫迪，我会去处理它。你有什么特别的想法吗？没有？好吧，那么我就按照自己的判断去做吧。我相信漂亮的深棕色很适合安妮，威廉·布莱尔有一些新的格洛丽亚，那真的很漂亮。也许你也想让我给她做点什么，看看如果玛丽拉做了的话，安妮可能会在之前听到风声。好吧，我会做的，这不是什么麻烦事，我会做适合我侄女珍妮·吉利斯的衣服，因为就身材而言，她和安妮就像两颗豌豆。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I'm much obliged," said Matthew, "and—and—I dunno—but I'd like—I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be. If it wouldn't be asking too much I—I'd like them made in the new way."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，我非常感激，”马修说，“而且——还有——我不知道——但我想——我认为他们现在的袖子与以前不同了。如果要求不是太高的话，我——我希望它们能用新的方式制作。”

paragraphs.en: "Puffs? Of course. You needn't worry a speck more about it, Matthew. I'll make it up in the very latest fashion," said Mrs. Lynde. To herself she added when Matthew had gone:
paragraphs.zh: “泡芙？当然。你不用再担心了，马修。我会用最新的时尚来弥补它，”林德夫人说。马修走后，她对自己补充道：

paragraphs.en: "It'll be a real satisfaction to see that poor child wearing something decent for once. The way Marilla dresses her is positively ridiculous, that's what, and I've ached to tell her so plainly a dozen times. I've held my tongue though, for I can see Marilla doesn't want advice and she thinks she knows more about bringing children up than I do for all she's an old maid. But that's always the way. Folks that has brought up children know that there's no hard and fast method in the world that'll suit every child. But them as never have think it's all as plain and easy as Rule of Three—just set your three terms down so fashion, and the sum'll work out correct. But flesh and blood don't come under the head of arithmetic and that's where Marilla Cuthbert makes her mistake. I suppose she's trying to cultivate a spirit of humility in Anne by dressing her as she does; but it's more likely to cultivate envy and discontent. I'm sure the child must feel the difference between her clothes and the other girls'. But to think of Matthew taking notice of it! That man is waking up after being asleep for over sixty years."
paragraphs.zh: “看到那个可怜的孩子一次穿得像样的衣服，我真的会感到很满足。玛丽拉的穿着实在是太可笑了，就是这样，我已经很想坦白地告诉她十几次了。不过我一直保持沉默，因为我看得出来玛丽拉不想要建议，而且她认为她比我更懂得如何抚养孩子，尽管她是个老处女。但事情总是这样。抚养过孩子的人都知道，没有什么难事。”但他们从来没有想到这一切都像“三法则”那样简单明了——只要把三个术语写下来，就能得出正确的结果，但血肉之躯并不属于算术范畴，我想她是想通过这样的打扮来培养安妮的谦逊精神，但我确信这更有可能培养她的嫉妒和不满。孩子一定能感觉到她的衣服和其他女孩的衣服有什么不同，但想想马修竟然注意到了这一点！”

paragraphs.en: Marilla knew all the following fortnight that Matthew had something on his mind, but what it was she could not guess, until Christmas Eve, when Mrs. Lynde brought up the new dress. Marilla behaved pretty well on the whole, although it is very likely she distrusted Mrs. Lynde's diplomatic explanation that she had made the dress because Matthew was afraid Anne would find out about it too soon if Marilla made it.
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来的两周里，马修知道马修心里有事，但她猜不出来到底是什么，直到圣诞节前夕，林德太太提出了那件新衣服。玛丽拉总的来说表现得很好，尽管她很可能不相信林德夫人关于她做这件衣服的外交解释，因为马修担心如果玛丽拉做了这件事，安妮会很快发现这件事。

paragraphs.en: "So this is what Matthew has been looking so mysterious over and grinning about to himself for two weeks, is it?" she said a little stiffly but tolerantly. "I knew he was up to some foolishness. Well, I must say I don't think Anne needed any more dresses. I made her three good, warm, serviceable ones this fall, and anything more is sheer extravagance. There's enough material in those sleeves alone to make a waist, I declare there is. You'll just pamper Anne's vanity, Matthew, and she's as vain as a peacock now. Well, I hope she'll be satisfied at last, for I know she's been hankering after those silly sleeves ever since they came in, although she never said a word after the first. The puffs have been getting bigger and more ridiculous right along; they're as big as balloons now. Next year anybody who wears them will have to go through a door sideways."
paragraphs.zh: “这就是马修两周来一直显得如此神秘并自顾自微笑的原因，是吗？”她有些生硬但宽容地说。 “我知道他有些愚蠢。好吧，我必须说，我认为安妮不需要更多的衣服了。今年秋天我给她做了三件又好又暖和又实用的衣服，再多一点就纯粹是奢侈了。光是那些袖子里就有足够的材料来制作腰部，我声明有。你只是纵容安妮的虚荣心，马修，她现在像孔雀一样虚荣。好吧，我希望她最终会满意，因为我知道自从那些愚蠢的袖子进来后，她就一直渴望着，尽管在第一次之后她再也没有说过一句话。这些泡泡已经变得越来越大，现在已经像气球一样大了，明年任何穿着它们的人都必须侧身穿过门。”

paragraphs.en: Christmas morning broke on a beautiful white world. It had been a very mild December and people had looked forward to a green Christmas; but just enough snow fell softly in the night to transfigure Avonlea. Anne peeped out from her frosted gable window with delighted eyes. The firs in the Haunted Wood were all feathery and wonderful; the birches and wild cherry trees were outlined in pearl; the plowed fields were stretches of snowy dimples; and there was a crisp tang in the air that was glorious. Anne ran downstairs singing until her voice reechoed through Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: 圣诞节的早晨迎来了美丽的白色世界。那是一个非常温和的十二月，人们期待着一个绿色的圣诞节。但夜里飘落的雪花刚好足以让埃文利焕然一新。安妮从磨砂的山墙窗里向外张望，眼睛里充满了喜悦。鬼林里的冷杉长得像羽毛一样，美丽极了。桦树和野樱桃树被珍珠勾勒出轮廓。犁过的田地是一片片雪坑。空气中弥漫着一种令人愉悦的清脆味道。安妮唱着歌跑下楼，直到她的歌声回荡在绿山墙里。

paragraphs.en: "Merry Christmas, Marilla! Merry Christmas, Matthew! Isn't it a lovely Christmas? I'm so glad it's white. Any other kind of Christmas doesn't seem real, does it? I don't like green Christmases. They're not green—they're just nasty faded browns and grays. What makes people call them green? Why—why—Matthew, is that for me? Oh, Matthew!"
paragraphs.zh: “圣诞快乐，玛丽拉！圣诞快乐，马修！这不是一个可爱的圣诞节吗？我很高兴它是白色的。任何其他形式的圣诞节看起来都不真实，不是吗？我不喜欢绿色的圣诞节。它们不是绿色的——它们只是令人讨厌的褪色的棕色和灰色。是什么让人们称它们为绿色？为什么——为什么——马修，那是给我的吗？哦，马修！”

paragraphs.en: Matthew had sheepishly unfolded the dress from its paper swathings and held it out with a deprecatory glance at Marilla, who feigned to be contemptuously filling the teapot, but nevertheless watched the scene out of the corner of her eye with a rather interested air.
paragraphs.zh: 马修羞涩地把裙子从纸巾里展开，递过来，鄙视地看了玛丽拉一眼，玛丽拉假装轻蔑地往茶壶里倒茶，但仍然用眼角余光饶有兴趣地看着这一幕。

paragraphs.en: Anne took the dress and looked at it in reverent silence. Oh, how pretty it was—a lovely soft brown gloria with all the gloss of silk; a skirt with dainty frills and shirrings; a waist elaborately pintucked in the most fashionable way, with a little ruffle of filmy lace at the neck. But the sleeves—they were the crowning glory! Long elbow cuffs, and above them two beautiful puffs divided by rows of shirring and bows of brown-silk ribbon.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮接过裙子，虔诚地沉默着看着它。哦，多么漂亮啊——一顶可爱的、柔软的棕色格洛丽亚，带着丝绸般的光泽；带有精致褶边和褶边的裙子；腰部以最时尚的方式精心褶皱，颈部饰有薄薄蕾丝的小荷叶边。但袖子——它们是至高无上的荣耀！长长的肘部袖口，上面有两个漂亮的泡泡，被一排排的抽褶和棕色丝带蝴蝶结分开。

paragraphs.en: "That's a Christmas present for you, Anne," said Matthew shyly. "Why—why—Anne, don't you like it? Well now—well now."
paragraphs.zh: “这是给你的圣诞礼物，安妮，”马修害羞地说。 “为什么——为什么——安妮，你不喜欢吗？好吧——好吧。”

paragraphs.en: For Anne's eyes had suddenly filled with tears.
paragraphs.zh: 因为安妮的眼里突然充满了泪水。

paragraphs.en: "Like it! Oh, Matthew!" Anne laid the dress over a chair and clasped her hands. "Matthew, it's perfectly exquisite. Oh, I can never thank you enough. Look at those sleeves! Oh, it seems to me this must be a happy dream."
paragraphs.zh: “喜欢！哦，马修！”安妮把裙子放在椅子上，双手紧握。 “马修，它非常精致。哦，我对你感激不尽。看看那些袖子！哦，在我看来，这一定是一个幸福的梦。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, well, let us have breakfast," interrupted Marilla. "I must say, Anne, I don't think you needed the dress; but since Matthew has got it for you, see that you take good care of it. There's a hair ribbon Mrs. Lynde left for you. It's brown, to match the dress. Come now, sit in."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，好吧，我们吃早餐吧。”玛丽拉打断道。 “我必须说，安妮，我认为你不需要这件衣服；但是既然马修已经给你买了它，你一定要好好保管它。林德夫人给你留了一条发带。它是棕色的，与这件衣服相配。现在过来，坐进去。”

paragraphs.en: "I don't see how I'm going to eat breakfast," said Anne rapturously. "Breakfast seems so commonplace at such an exciting moment. I'd rather feast my eyes on that dress. I'm so glad that puffed sleeves are still fashionable. It did seem to me that I'd never get over it if they went out before I had a dress with them. I'd never have felt quite satisfied, you see. It was lovely of Mrs. Lynde to give me the ribbon too. I feel that I ought to be a very good girl indeed. It's at times like this I'm sorry I'm not a model little girl; and I always resolve that I will be in future. But somehow it's hard to carry out your resolutions when irresistible temptations come. Still, I really will make an extra effort after this."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道该怎么吃早餐，”安妮兴高采烈地说。 “在这样一个激动人心的时刻，吃早餐似乎是很平常的事情。我宁愿大饱眼福那件衣服。我很高兴泡泡袖仍然很时尚。在我看来，如果他们在我穿上衣服之前出去，我永远不会忘记它。我永远不会感到很满意，你看。林德夫人也把丝带送给我，真是太可爱了。我觉得我确实应该是一个非常好的女孩。有时就是这样。很抱歉，我不是一个模范小女孩；而且我总是下定决心，将来我会成为一个模范小女孩，但不知怎的，当不可抗拒的诱惑来临时，我很难实现你的决心，但在这之后我真的会付出额外的努力。”

paragraphs.en: When the commonplace breakfast was over Diana appeared, crossing the white log bridge in the hollow, a gay little figure in her crimson ulster. Anne flew down the slope to meet her.
paragraphs.zh: 当普通的早餐结束后，黛安娜出现了，穿过山谷中的白色木桥，她穿着深红色的羊毛衫，身材娇小，性格开朗。安妮飞下斜坡去迎接她。

paragraphs.en: "Merry Christmas, Diana! And oh, it's a wonderful Christmas. I've something splendid to show you. Matthew has given me the loveliest dress, with SUCH sleeves. I couldn't even imagine any nicer."
paragraphs.zh: “圣诞快乐，戴安娜！哦，这是一个美妙的圣诞节。我有一些很棒的东西要给你看。马修给了我一件最可爱的衣服，还有这样的袖子。我什至无法想象更好的了。”

paragraphs.en: "I've got something more for you," said Diana breathlessly. "Here—this box. Aunt Josephine sent us out a big box with ever so many things in it—and this is for you. I'd have brought it over last night, but it didn't come until after dark, and I never feel very comfortable coming through the Haunted Wood in the dark now."
paragraphs.zh: “我还给你准备了更多东西，”黛安娜气喘吁吁地说。 “这里——这个盒子。约瑟芬姨妈给我们送来了一个大盒子，里面装了那么多东西——这是给你的。我昨晚就已经把它送过来了，但直到天黑之后才送来，现在在黑暗中穿过闹鬼的森林，我从来没有感到很舒服。”

paragraphs.en: Anne opened the box and peeped in. First a card with "For the Anne-girl and Merry Christmas," written on it; and then, a pair of the daintiest little kid slippers, with beaded toes and satin bows and glistening buckles.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮打开盒子往里看。首先是一张卡片，上面写着“致安妮女孩，圣诞快乐”；然后是一双最精致的儿童拖鞋，脚趾上有串珠，缎面蝴蝶结和闪闪发光的搭扣。

paragraphs.en: "Oh," said Anne, "Diana, this is too much. I must be dreaming."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”安妮说，“戴安娜，这太过分了。我一定是在做梦。”

paragraphs.en: "I call it providential," said Diana. "You won't have to borrow Ruby's slippers now, and that's a blessing, for they're two sizes too big for you, and it would be awful to hear a fairy shuffling. Josie Pye would be delighted. Mind you, Rob Wright went home with Gertie Pye from the practice night before last. Did you ever hear anything equal to that?"
paragraphs.zh: “我称之为天意，”戴安娜说。 “现在你不用借鲁比的拖鞋了，这是一件幸事，因为它们对你来说太大了两号，而且听到仙女拖着脚步的声音会很糟糕。乔西·派伊会很高兴。请注意，罗布·赖特前天晚上训练结束后和格蒂·派伊一起回家了。你听过类似的事情吗？”

paragraphs.en: All the Avonlea scholars were in a fever of excitement that day, for the hall had to be decorated and a last grand rehearsal held.
paragraphs.zh: 那天，所有埃文利学者都兴奋不已，因为大厅要装饰，还要进行最后一次盛大的排练。

paragraphs.en: The concert came off in the evening and was a pronounced success. The little hall was crowded; all the performers did excellently well, but Anne was the bright particular star of the occasion, as even envy, in the shape of Josie Pye, dared not deny.
paragraphs.zh: 音乐会于当晚举行，取得了巨大成功。小小的大厅里挤满了人。所有表演者都表现出色，但安妮是这次活动中最耀眼的明星，就连乔西·派伊（Josie Pye）这样的嫉妒者也不敢否认。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, hasn't it been a brilliant evening?" sighed Anne, when it was all over and she and Diana were walking home together under a dark, starry sky.
paragraphs.zh: “噢，这不是一个美好的夜晚吗？”安妮叹了口气，一切都结束了，她和戴安娜在黑暗的星空下一起走回家。

paragraphs.en: "Everything went off very well," said Diana practically. "I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers."
paragraphs.zh: “一切都很顺利，”戴安娜实际上说道。 “我想我们肯定赚了十美元。请注意，艾伦先生将把此事发给夏洛特敦的报纸。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Diana, will we really see our names in print? It makes me thrill to think of it. Your solo was perfectly elegant, Diana. I felt prouder than you did when it was encored. I just said to myself, 'It is my dear bosom friend who is so honored.'"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，戴安娜，我们真的会在印刷品上看到我们的名字吗？一想到这一点就让我兴奋不已。戴安娜，你的独奏非常优雅。当它被加演时，我比你感到更加自豪。我只是对自己说，‘这是我亲爱的知音，我感到非常荣幸。’”

paragraphs.en: "Well, your recitations just brought down the house, Anne. That sad one was simply splendid."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，安妮，你的朗诵让全场沸腾了。那个悲伤的朗诵简直太精彩了。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I was so nervous, Diana. When Mr. Allan called out my name I really cannot tell how I ever got up on that platform. I felt as if a million eyes were looking at me and through me, and for one dreadful moment I was sure I couldn't begin at all. Then I thought of my lovely puffed sleeves and took courage. I knew that I must live up to those sleeves, Diana. So I started in, and my voice seemed to be coming from ever so far away. I just felt like a parrot. It's providential that I practiced those recitations so often up in the garret, or I'd never have been able to get through. Did I groan all right?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我太紧张了，戴安娜。当艾伦先生喊出我的名字时，我真的不知道自己是怎么登上那个站台的。我感觉好像有一百万只眼睛在看着我，透过我，在一个可怕的时刻，我确信我根本无法开始。然后我想到了我可爱的泡泡袖，鼓起勇气。我知道我必须辜负那些袖子，戴安娜。所以我开始了，我的声音似乎来自遥远的地方。我只是幸好我经常在阁楼上练习这些背诵，否则我永远都无法完成，好吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, indeed, you groaned lovely," assured Diana.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，确实，你的呻吟声很可爱，”戴安娜保证道。

paragraphs.en: "I saw old Mrs. Sloane wiping away tears when I sat down. It was splendid to think I had touched somebody's heart. It's so romantic to take part in a concert, isn't it? Oh, it's been a very memorable occasion indeed."
paragraphs.zh: “当我坐下时，我看到斯隆老太太在擦眼泪。想到我触动了某人的心，真是太棒了。参加音乐会真是太浪漫了，不是吗？哦，这确实是一个非常难忘的时刻。”

paragraphs.en: "Wasn't the boys' dialogue fine?" said Diana. "Gilbert Blythe was just splendid. Anne, I do think it's awful mean the way you treat Gil. Wait till I tell you. When you ran off the platform after the fairy dialogue one of your roses fell out of your hair. I saw Gil pick it up and put it in his breast pocket. There now. You're so romantic that I'm sure you ought to be pleased at that."
paragraphs.zh: “男孩子们的对话不是很好吗？”戴安娜说。 “吉尔伯特·布莱斯真是太棒了。安妮，我确实认为你对待吉尔的方式太卑鄙了。等我告诉你。当你在仙女对话后跑下站台时，你的一朵玫瑰从你的头发上掉了下来。我看到吉尔把它捡起来放在胸前的口袋里。现在。你是如此浪漫，我相信你应该对此感到高兴。”

paragraphs.en: "It's nothing to me what that person does," said Anne loftily. "I simply never waste a thought on him, Diana."
paragraphs.zh: “那个人做了什么，对我来说无关紧要。”安妮傲慢地说。 “我从来没有在他身上浪费过心思，戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: That night Marilla and Matthew, who had been out to a concert for the first time in twenty years, sat for a while by the kitchen fire after Anne had gone to bed.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，安妮上床睡觉后，玛丽拉和马修在厨房的炉火旁坐了一会儿，这是二十年来第一次出去听音乐会。

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I guess our Anne did as well as any of them," said Matthew proudly.
paragraphs.zh: “现在，我想我们的安妮做得和他们中的任何一个一样好，”马修自豪地说。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, she did," admitted Marilla. "She's a bright child, Matthew. And she looked real nice too. I've been kind of opposed to this concert scheme, but I suppose there's no real harm in it after all. Anyhow, I was proud of Anne tonight, although I'm not going to tell her so."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，她做到了，”玛丽拉承认。 “她是个聪明的孩子，马修。而且她看起来也很漂亮。我一直反对这个音乐会计划，但我想这毕竟没有什么真正的坏处。无论如何，今晚我为安妮感到骄傲，尽管我不会告诉她这一点。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I was proud of her and I did tell her so 'fore she went upstairs," said Matthew. "We must see what we can do for her some of these days, Marilla. I guess she'll need something more than Avonlea school by and by."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，我为她感到骄傲，在她上楼之前我确实告诉了她，”马修说。 “我们必须看看这些天我们能为她做些什么，玛丽拉。我想她渐渐需要的不仅仅是埃文利学校。”

paragraphs.en: "There's time enough to think of that," said Marilla. "She's only thirteen in March. Though tonight it struck me she was growing quite a big girl. Mrs. Lynde made that dress a mite too long, and it makes Anne look so tall. She's quick to learn and I guess the best thing we can do for her will be to send her to Queen's after a spell. But nothing need be said about that for a year or two yet."
paragraphs.zh: “有足够的时间考虑这一点，”玛丽拉说。 “三月份她才十三岁。不过今晚我突然意识到她长成了一个大女孩了。林德太太把那件衣服做得有点太长了，这让安妮看起来很高。她学得很快，我想我们能为她做的最好的事情就是在一段时间后把她送到女王学院去。但一两年内还不需要说什么。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, it'll do no harm to be thinking it over off and on," said Matthew. "Things like that are all the better for lots of thinking over."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，断断续续地思考一下也没什么坏处，”马修说。 “这样的事情多思考一下就会更好。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 26 章：故事俱乐部的成立

paragraphs.en: Junior Avonlea found it hard to settle down to humdrum existence again. To Anne in particular things seemed fearfully flat, stale, and unprofitable after the goblet of excitement she had been sipping for weeks. Could she go back to the former quiet pleasures of those faraway days before the concert? At first, as she told Diana, she did not really think she could.
paragraphs.zh: 小埃冯利发现很难再次安定下来过单调的生活。尤其是对安妮来说，在她喝了几个星期的兴奋之杯之后，一切似乎都极其平淡、陈旧、无利可图。她还能回到演唱会前那段遥远的日子里的安静快乐吗？起初，正如她告诉戴安娜的那样，她真的认为自己做不到。

paragraphs.en: "I'm positively certain, Diana, that life can never be quite the same again as it was in those olden days," she said mournfully, as if referring to a period of at least fifty years back. "Perhaps after a while I'll get used to it, but I'm afraid concerts spoil people for everyday life. I suppose that is why Marilla disapproves of them. Marilla is such a sensible woman. It must be a great deal better to be sensible; but still, I don't believe I'd really want to be a sensible person, because they are so unromantic. Mrs. Lynde says there is no danger of my ever being one, but you can never tell. I feel just now that I may grow up to be sensible yet. But perhaps that is only because I'm tired. I simply couldn't sleep last night for ever so long. I just lay awake and imagined the concert over and over again. That's one splendid thing about such affairs—it's so lovely to look back to them."
paragraphs.zh: “我确信，戴安娜，生活再也不会像以前那样了，”她悲伤地说，仿佛指的是至少五十年前的一段时光。 “也许过一段时间我就会习惯了，但我担心音乐会会破坏人们的日常生活。我想这就是玛丽拉不赞成音乐会的原因。玛丽拉是一个如此明智的女人。明智一定会好很多；但我仍然不相信我真的想成为一个明智的人，因为他们太不浪漫了。林德夫人说我永远不会有危险，但你永远不可能我现在觉得我可能已经长大了，懂事了，但也许只是因为我昨晚睡不着，一遍又一遍地想象着音乐会——回顾它们真是太美妙了。”

paragraphs.en: Eventually, however, Avonlea school slipped back into its old groove and took up its old interests. To be sure, the concert left traces. Ruby Gillis and Emma White, who had quarreled over a point of precedence in their platform seats, no longer sat at the same desk, and a promising friendship of three years was broken up. Josie Pye and Julia Bell did not "speak" for three months, because Josie Pye had told Bessie Wright that Julia Bell's bow when she got up to recite made her think of a chicken jerking its head, and Bessie told Julia. None of the Sloanes would have any dealings with the Bells, because the Bells had declared that the Sloanes had too much to do in the program, and the Sloanes had retorted that the Bells were not capable of doing the little they had to do properly. Finally, Charlie Sloane fought Moody Spurgeon MacPherson, because Moody Spurgeon had said that Anne Shirley put on airs about her recitations, and Moody Spurgeon was "licked"; consequently Moody Spurgeon's sister, Ella May, would not "speak" to Anne Shirley all the rest of the winter. With the exception of these trifling frictions, work in Miss Stacy's little kingdom went on with regularity and smoothness.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，最终，埃文利学校又回到了原来的轨道，并恢复了原来的兴趣。可以肯定的是，音乐会留下了痕迹。鲁比·吉利斯（Ruby Gillis）和艾玛·怀特（Emma White）曾在站台座位上为优先权发生争执，但他们不再坐在同一张桌子上，三年来充满希望的友谊也因此破裂。乔西·派伊和朱莉娅·贝尔三个月没有“说话”，因为乔西·派伊告诉贝西·赖特，朱莉娅·贝尔起身背诵时的鞠躬让她想起一只鸡在摇头，贝西告诉朱莉娅。斯隆家族中没有人会与贝尔家族有任何往来，因为贝尔家族宣称斯隆家族在计划中要做的事情太多，而斯隆家族反驳说贝尔家族没有能力做好他们必须做的那一点点事情。最后，查理·斯隆与穆迪·司布真·麦克弗森对战，因为穆迪·司布真曾说过安妮·雪莉在她的朗诵上摆架子，穆迪·司布真被“舔了”；因此，穆迪·司布真 (Moody Spurgeon) 的妹妹埃拉·梅 (Ella May) 在整个冬天都不会与安妮·雪莉“说话”。除了这些琐碎的摩擦之外，史黛西小姐的小王国里的工作都进行得有规律、顺利。

paragraphs.en: The winter weeks slipped by. It was an unusually mild winter, with so little snow that Anne and Diana could go to school nearly every day by way of the Birch Path. On Anne's birthday they were tripping lightly down it, keeping eyes and ears alert amid all their chatter, for Miss Stacy had told them that they must soon write a composition on "A Winter's Walk in the Woods," and it behooved them to be observant.
paragraphs.zh: 冬天的几周过去了。那是一个异常温和的冬天，雪很少，安妮和戴安娜几乎每天都可以取道桦树路去上学。安妮生日那天，他们轻轻地走在上面，在他们的喋喋不休中保持眼睛和耳朵的警惕，因为史黛西小姐告诉他们，他们必须很快写一篇关于“冬天的树林里的散步”的作文，他们应该保持警惕。

paragraphs.en: "Just think, Diana, I'm thirteen years old today," remarked Anne in an awed voice. "I can scarcely realize that I'm in my teens. When I woke this morning it seemed to me that everything must be different. You've been thirteen for a month, so I suppose it doesn't seem such a novelty to you as it does to me. It makes life seem so much more interesting. In two more years I'll be really grown up. It's a great comfort to think that I'll be able to use big words then without being laughed at."
paragraphs.zh: “想一想，戴安娜，我今天十三岁了，”安妮用敬畏的声音说道。 “我几乎没有意识到自己已经十几岁了。今天早上我醒来时，我觉得一切都不同了。你已经十三岁了，所以我想这对你来说并不像对我那么新鲜。它让生活变得更加有趣。再过两年我就会真正长大了。想到那时我将能够使用大词而不被嘲笑，这是一种极大的安慰。”

paragraphs.en: "Ruby Gillis says she means to have a beau as soon as she's fifteen," said Diana.
paragraphs.zh: “鲁比·吉利斯说她一到十五岁就打算找一个男朋友，”戴安娜说。

paragraphs.en: "Ruby Gillis thinks of nothing but beaus," said Anne disdainfully. "She's actually delighted when anyone writes her name up in a take-notice for all she pretends to be so mad. But I'm afraid that is an uncharitable speech. Mrs. Allan says we should never make uncharitable speeches; but they do slip out so often before you think, don't they? I simply can't talk about Josie Pye without making an uncharitable speech, so I never mention her at all. You may have noticed that. I'm trying to be as much like Mrs. Allan as I possibly can, for I think she's perfect. Mr. Allan thinks so too. Mrs. Lynde says he just worships the ground she treads on and she doesn't really think it right for a minister to set his affections so much on a mortal being. But then, Diana, even ministers are human and have their besetting sins just like everybody else. I had such an interesting talk with Mrs. Allan about besetting sins last Sunday afternoon. There are just a few things it's proper to talk about on Sundays and that is one of them. My besetting sin is imagining too much and forgetting my duties. I'm striving very hard to overcome it and now that I'm really thirteen perhaps I'll get on better."
paragraphs.zh: “鲁比·吉利斯只想着情人。”安妮轻蔑地说。 “当有人把她的名字写在记事本上时，她假装很生气，她实际上很高兴。但我担心这是一次无情的演讲。艾伦夫人说我们永远不应该发表无情的演讲；但它们确实经常在你想到之前就溜走，不是吗？我根本无法在不做无情的演讲的情况下谈论乔西·派伊，所以我从来没有提到过她。你可能已经注意到了。我正在努力做到这一点。尽可能地像艾伦夫人一样，因为我认为艾伦先生也这么认为，林德夫人说他只是崇拜她所踏过的土地，她并不认为牧师将自己的感情如此之多地放在凡人身上，但是，戴安娜，即使是牧师也是人，就像其他人一样，我与艾伦夫人进行了一次非常有趣的谈话。这只是周日应该谈论的几件事，其中之一是我的罪恶是想象太多，忘记了我的职责，我正在努力克服它，现在我真的十三岁了，也许我会过得更好。”

paragraphs.en: "In four more years we'll be able to put our hair up," said Diana. "Alice Bell is only sixteen and she is wearing hers up, but I think that's ridiculous. I shall wait until I'm seventeen."
paragraphs.zh: “再过四年，我们就能把头发盘起来了，”戴安娜说。 “爱丽丝·贝尔才十六岁，她已经把自己的衣服穿坏了，但我认为这很荒谬。我会等到我十七岁。”

paragraphs.en: "If I had Alice Bell's crooked nose," said Anne decidedly, "I wouldn't—but there! I won't say what I was going to because it was extremely uncharitable. Besides, I was comparing it with my own nose and that's vanity. I'm afraid I think too much about my nose ever since I heard that compliment about it long ago. It really is a great comfort to me. Oh, Diana, look, there's a rabbit. That's something to remember for our woods composition. I really think the woods are just as lovely in winter as in summer. They're so white and still, as if they were asleep and dreaming pretty dreams."
paragraphs.zh: “如果我有爱丽丝·贝尔的歪鼻子，”安妮斩钉截铁地说，“我不会——但是呢！我不会说出我要做什么，因为那是极其无情的。此外，我把它与我自己的鼻子进行比较，那是虚荣心。自从我很久以前听到关于我的鼻子的赞美以来，我担心我对我的鼻子想得太多了。这对我来说真的是一个很大的安慰。哦，戴安娜，看，有一只兔子。这是我们要记住的事情。我真的认为冬天和夏天的树林一样可爱，它们是那么的白色和静止，就好像它们睡着了，做着美丽的梦。”

paragraphs.en: "I won't mind writing that composition when its time comes," sighed Diana. "I can manage to write about the woods, but the one we're to hand in Monday is terrible. The idea of Miss Stacy telling us to write a story out of our own heads!"
paragraphs.zh: “我不介意到时候写那篇文章，”戴安娜叹了口气。 “我可以写关于树林的故事，但是我们周一要交的那篇太糟糕了。史黛西小姐告诉我们用自己的头脑写一个故事！”

paragraphs.en: "Why, it's as easy as wink," said Anne.
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀，这就像眨眼一样简单，”安妮说。

paragraphs.en: "It's easy for you because you have an imagination," retorted Diana, "but what would you do if you had been born without one? I suppose you have your composition all done?"
paragraphs.zh: “这对你来说很容易，因为你有想象力，”黛安娜反驳道，“但如果你生来就没有想象力，你会怎么做？我想你已经完成了你的作文吧？”

paragraphs.en: Anne nodded, trying hard not to look virtuously complacent and failing miserably.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮点点头，努力不让自己看起来显得自满自满，但失败得很惨。

paragraphs.en: "I wrote it last Monday evening. It's called 'The Jealous Rival; or In Death Not Divided.' I read it to Marilla and she said it was stuff and nonsense. Then I read it to Matthew and he said it was fine. That is the kind of critic I like. It's a sad, sweet story. I just cried like a child while I was writing it. It's about two beautiful maidens called Cordelia Montmorency and Geraldine Seymour who lived in the same village and were devotedly attached to each other. Cordelia was a regal brunette with a coronet of midnight hair and duskly flashing eyes. Geraldine was a queenly blonde with hair like spun gold and velvety purple eyes."
paragraphs.zh: “我上周一晚上写的。它的名字是‘嫉妒的对手；或者死不分离’。”我把它读给玛丽拉听，她说这是胡说八道。然后我把它读给马修听，他说很好。这就是我喜欢的批评家。这是一个悲伤又甜蜜的故事。当我写这篇文章的时候，我就像个孩子一样哭了。这是关于两个美丽的少女科迪莉亚·蒙莫朗西和杰拉尔丁·西摩的故事，她们住在同一个村庄，彼此忠诚。科迪莉亚是一位高贵的黑发女郎，有着一顶午夜般的头发和一双闪烁着昏暗光芒的眼睛。杰拉尔丁是一位女王般的金发女郎，有着金丝般的头发和天鹅绒般的紫色眼睛。”

paragraphs.en: "I never saw anybody with purple eyes," said Diana dubiously.
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没见过有紫色眼睛的人，”戴安娜怀疑地说。

paragraphs.en: "Neither did I. I just imagined them. I wanted something out of the common. Geraldine had an alabaster brow too. I've found out what an alabaster brow is. That is one of the advantages of being thirteen. You know so much more than you did when you were only twelve."
paragraphs.zh: “我也没有。我只是想象出来的。我想要一些不寻常的东西。杰拉尔丁也有雪花石膏眉毛。我已经知道雪花石膏眉毛是什么了。这是十三岁的优势之一。你比十二岁时知道的要多得多。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, what became of Cordelia and Geraldine?" asked Diana, who was beginning to feel rather interested in their fate.
paragraphs.zh: “那么，科迪莉亚和杰拉尔丁怎么样了？”黛安娜问道，她开始对他们的命运很感兴趣。

paragraphs.en: "They grew in beauty side by side until they were sixteen. Then Bertram DeVere came to their native village and fell in love with the fair Geraldine. He saved her life when her horse ran away with her in a carriage, and she fainted in his arms and he carried her home three miles; because, you understand, the carriage was all smashed up. I found it rather hard to imagine the proposal because I had no experience to go by. I asked Ruby Gillis if she knew anything about how men proposed because I thought she'd likely be an authority on the subject, having so many sisters married. Ruby told me she was hid in the hall pantry when Malcolm Andres proposed to her sister Susan. She said Malcolm told Susan that his dad had given him the farm in his own name and then said, 'What do you say, darling pet, if we get hitched this fall?' And Susan said, 'Yes—no—I don't know—let me see'—and there they were, engaged as quick as that. But I didn't think that sort of a proposal was a very romantic one, so in the end I had to imagine it out as well as I could. I made it very flowery and poetical and Bertram went on his knees, although Ruby Gillis says it isn't done nowadays. Geraldine accepted him in a speech a page long. I can tell you I took a lot of trouble with that speech. I rewrote it five times and I look upon it as my masterpiece. Bertram gave her a diamond ring and a ruby necklace and told her they would go to Europe for a wedding tour, for he was immensely wealthy. But then, alas, shadows began to darken over their path. Cordelia was secretly in love with Bertram herself and when Geraldine told her about the engagement she was simply furious, especially when she saw the necklace and the diamond ring. All her affection for Geraldine turned to bitter hate and she vowed that she should never marry Bertram. But she pretended to be Geraldine's friend the same as ever. One evening they were standing on the bridge over a rushing turbulent stream and Cordelia, thinking they were alone, pushed Geraldine over the brink with a wild, mocking, 'Ha, ha, ha.' But Bertram saw it all and he at once plunged into the current, exclaiming, 'I will save thee, my peerless Geraldine.' But alas, he had forgotten he couldn't swim, and they were both drowned, clasped in each other's arms. Their bodies were washed ashore soon afterwards. They were buried in the one grave and their funeral was most imposing, Diana. It's so much more romantic to end a story up with a funeral than a wedding. As for Cordelia, she went insane with remorse and was shut up in a lunatic asylum. I thought that was a poetical retribution for her crime."
paragraphs.zh: “他们并肩成长，直到十六岁。然后伯特伦·德维尔来到了他们的家乡，爱上了美丽的杰拉尔丁。当她的马带着她乘坐马车逃跑时，他救了她的命，她晕倒在他怀里，他把她抱回家三英里；因为，你知道，马车都被砸坏了。我发现很难想象这个求婚，因为我没有经验可循。我问鲁比·吉利斯，她是否知道男人如何求婚，因为我认为鲁比告诉我，当马尔科姆·安德烈斯向她的妹妹苏珊求婚时，她可能是这个问题的权威。鲁比告诉我，马尔科姆告诉苏珊，他的父亲以他自己的名义把农场给了他，然后说，“亲爱的宠物，如果我们今年秋天结婚，你觉得怎么样？”苏珊说，“是的——不——我不知道——让我想想”——然后他们就在那里，很快就订婚了。但我不认为这种求婚是一个非常浪漫的求婚，所以最后我不得不尽我所能地想象它。我把它做得非常华丽和诗意，伯特伦跪下了，尽管鲁比·吉利斯说现在还没有这样做。杰拉尔丁在长达一页的演讲中接受了他。我可以告诉你，我在演讲中花了很多功夫。我重写了五次，我把它视为我的杰作。伯特伦送给她一枚钻戒和一条红宝石项链，并告诉她他们将去欧洲进行婚礼旅行，因为他非常富有。但随后，唉，他们的道路上的阴影开始变暗。科迪莉亚本人暗恋着伯特伦，当杰拉尔丁告诉她订婚的消息时，她非常愤怒，尤其是当她看到项链和钻戒时。她对杰拉尔丁的所有感情都变成了苦涩的仇恨，她发誓永远不会嫁给伯特伦。但她一如既往地假装是杰拉尔丁的朋友。一天晚上，他们站在桥上，横跨一条湍急的溪流，科迪莉亚以为只有他们俩，便用狂野而嘲讽的“哈、哈、哈”把杰拉尔丁推到了悬崖边。但伯特伦看到了这一切，他立即跳入水流中，大声喊道：“我会救你，我无与伦比的杰拉尔丁。”但可惜的是，他忘记了自己不会游泳，结果他们双双被淹死，互相拥抱着。他们的尸体很快就被冲上岸。他们被埋葬在一个坟墓里，他们的葬礼最为隆重，戴安娜。以葬礼结束故事比以婚礼结束要浪漫得多。至于科迪莉亚，她悔恨得发疯，被关进了疯人院。我认为这是对她的罪行的诗意的报应。”

paragraphs.en: "How perfectly lovely!" sighed Diana, who belonged to Matthew's school of critics. "I don't see how you can make up such thrilling things out of your own head, Anne. I wish my imagination was as good as yours."
paragraphs.zh: “多么可爱呀！”属于马修批评派的戴安娜叹了口气。 “我不明白你怎么能凭自己的头脑编出如此惊心动魄的事情，安妮。我希望我的想象力和你一样丰富。”

paragraphs.en: "It would be if you'd only cultivate it," said Anne cheeringly. "I've just thought of a plan, Diana. Let you and me have a story club all our own and write stories for practice. I'll help you along until you can do them by yourself. You ought to cultivate your imagination, you know. Miss Stacy says so. Only we must take the right way. I told her about the Haunted Wood, but she said we went the wrong way about it in that."
paragraphs.zh: “只要你能培养它就好了。”安妮高兴地说。 “我刚刚想到了一个计划，黛安娜。让你和我成立一个属于我们自己的故事俱乐部，写故事练习。我会帮助你，直到你能自己做。你知道，你应该培养你的想象力。斯泰西小姐这么说。只是我们必须走正确的路。我告诉她关于鬼林的事，但她说我们在这方面走错了路。”

paragraphs.en: This was how the story club came into existence. It was limited to Diana and Anne at first, but soon it was extended to include Jane Andrews and Ruby Gillis and one or two others who felt that their imaginations needed cultivating. No boys were allowed in it—although Ruby Gillis opined that their admission would make it more exciting—and each member had to produce one story a week.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是故事俱乐部的诞生。起初仅限于戴安娜和安妮，但很快就扩展到包括简·安德鲁斯和鲁比·吉利斯以及其他一两个认为自己的想象力需要培养的人。不允许男孩参与——尽管鲁比·吉利斯认为男孩的加入会让故事变得更令人兴奋——而且每个成员必须每周创作一个故事。

paragraphs.en: "It's extremely interesting," Anne told Marilla. "Each girl has to read her story out loud and then we talk it over. We are going to keep them all sacredly and have them to read to our descendants. We each write under a nom-de-plume. Mine is Rosamond Montmorency. All the girls do pretty well. Ruby Gillis is rather sentimental. She puts too much lovemaking into her stories and you know too much is worse than too little. Jane never puts any because she says it makes her feel so silly when she had to read it out loud. Jane's stories are extremely sensible. Then Diana puts too many murders into hers. She says most of the time she doesn't know what to do with the people so she kills them off to get rid of them. I mostly always have to tell them what to write about, but that isn't hard for I've millions of ideas."
paragraphs.zh: “这非常有趣，”安妮告诉玛丽拉。 “每个女孩都必须大声朗读她的故事，然后我们再讨论。我们将把它们都神圣地保存下来，并让它们读给我们的后代听。我们每个人都以化名写作。我的名字是罗莎蒙德·蒙莫朗西。所有女孩都做得很好。鲁比·吉利斯相当多愁善感。她在她的故事中加入了太多的爱，你知道太多比太少更糟糕。简从来不放任何东西，因为她说当她不得不读出来时，这让她觉得自己很傻简的故事非常明智，然后戴安娜在她的故事中加入了太多的谋杀，她说大多数时候她不知道如何处理这些人，所以她总是要告诉他们要写什么，但这并不难，因为我有数以百万计的想法。”

paragraphs.en: "I think this story-writing business is the foolishest yet," scoffed Marilla. "You'll get a pack of nonsense into your heads and waste time that should be put on your lessons. Reading stories is bad enough but writing them is worse."
paragraphs.zh: “我认为这种写故事的行为是迄今为止最愚蠢的，”玛丽拉嘲笑道。 “你的脑子里会充斥着一堆废话，浪费了本该用来上课的时间。读故事已经够糟糕的了，写故事更糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: "But we're so careful to put a moral into them all, Marilla," explained Anne. "I insist upon that. All the good people are rewarded and all the bad ones are suitably punished. I'm sure that must have a wholesome effect. The moral is the great thing. Mr. Allan says so. I read one of my stories to him and Mrs. Allan and they both agreed that the moral was excellent. Only they laughed in the wrong places. I like it better when people cry. Jane and Ruby almost always cry when I come to the pathetic parts. Diana wrote her Aunt Josephine about our club and her Aunt Josephine wrote back that we were to send her some of our stories. So we copied out four of our very best and sent them. Miss Josephine Barry wrote back that she had never read anything so amusing in her life. That kind of puzzled us because the stories were all very pathetic and almost everybody died. But I'm glad Miss Barry liked them. It shows our club is doing some good in the world. Mrs. Allan says that ought to be our object in everything. I do really try to make it my object but I forget so often when I'm having fun. I hope I shall be a little like Mrs. Allan when I grow up. Do you think there is any prospect of it, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: “但我们非常小心地把道德灌输给他们所有人，玛丽拉，”安妮解释道。 “我坚持这一点。所有好人都会得到奖赏，所有坏人都会受到适当的惩罚。我相信这一定会产生有益的效果。道德是伟大的事情。艾伦先生是这么说的。我给他和艾伦夫人读了我的一个故事，他们都认为道德很好。只是他们笑错了地方。我更喜欢人们哭泣。当我谈到可悲的部分时，简和鲁比几乎总是哭。戴安娜给她的约瑟芬姨妈写了关于我们俱乐部的事。她的姨妈约瑟芬回信说，我们要寄给她一些最好的故事，然后寄给我们，她一生中从未读过如此有趣的故事，因为这些故事都很可悲，而且几乎每个人都死了，但这表明我们的俱乐部正在为世界做一些好事。我反对，但当我玩得开心时，我经常忘记，我希望长大后我能像艾伦夫人那样，你认为有希望吗，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: "I shouldn't say there was a great deal" was Marilla's encouraging answer. "I'm sure Mrs. Allan was never such a silly, forgetful little girl as you are."
paragraphs.zh: “我不应该说有很多”，玛丽拉令人鼓舞的回答。 “我确信艾伦太太从来都不是像你这样愚蠢、健忘的小女孩。”

paragraphs.en: "No; but she wasn't always so good as she is now either," said Anne seriously. "She told me so herself—that is, she said she was a dreadful mischief when she was a girl and was always getting into scrapes. I felt so encouraged when I heard that. Is it very wicked of me, Marilla, to feel encouraged when I hear that other people have been bad and mischievous? Mrs. Lynde says it is. Mrs. Lynde says she always feels shocked when she hears of anyone ever having been naughty, no matter how small they were. Mrs. Lynde says she once heard a minister confess that when he was a boy he stole a strawberry tart out of his aunt's pantry and she never had any respect for that minister again. Now, I wouldn't have felt that way. I'd have thought that it was real noble of him to confess it, and I'd have thought what an encouraging thing it would be for small boys nowadays who do naughty things and are sorry for them to know that perhaps they may grow up to be ministers in spite of it. That's how I'd feel, Marilla."
paragraphs.zh: “不；但她也不总是像现在这样优秀。”安妮严肃地说。 “她亲自告诉我的——也就是说，她说她小时候很顽皮，总是惹麻烦。当我听到这句话时，我感到很受鼓舞。当我听到其他人很坏、很顽皮时，我感到受到鼓舞，我是不是太邪恶了，玛丽拉？林德太太说是的。林德太太说，当她听到有人淘气时，无论他们有多小，她总是感到震惊。林德夫人说，她曾经听一位牧师承认，当他还是个孩子的时候，他从姨妈的储藏室里偷了一个草莓馅饼，而她再也没有对那位牧师有任何尊重。现在，我不会再有这样的感觉了，我以为他承认这件事是真正高尚的，而且我想，对于现在做顽皮事情的小男孩来说，如果他们知道也许他们长大后可能会成为牧师，那将是一件多么令人鼓舞的事情。这就是我的感受，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: "The way I feel at present, Anne," said Marilla, "is that it's high time you had those dishes washed. You've taken half an hour longer than you should with all your chattering. Learn to work first and talk afterwards."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，我现在的感觉是，你该洗碗了。你喋喋不休，比你应该多花的时间多了半个小时。学会先工作，然后再说话。”

chapters.title: CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 27 章：虚荣与心灵的烦恼

paragraphs.en: Marilla, walking home one late April evening from an Aid meeting, realized that the winter was over and gone with the thrill of delight that spring never fails to bring to the oldest and saddest as well as to the youngest and merriest. Marilla was not given to subjective analysis of her thoughts and feelings. She probably imagined that she was thinking about the Aids and their missionary box and the new carpet for the vestry room, but under these reflections was a harmonious consciousness of red fields smoking into pale-purply mists in the declining sun, of long, sharp-pointed fir shadows falling over the meadow beyond the brook, of still, crimson-budded maples around a mirrorlike wood pool, of a wakening in the world and a stir of hidden pulses under the gray sod. The spring was abroad in the land and Marilla's sober, middle-aged step was lighter and swifter because of its deep, primal gladness.
paragraphs.zh: 四月底的一个晚上，玛丽拉在参加完援助会议回家时，意识到冬天已经过去了，春天总是给最年长、最悲伤的人和最年轻、最快乐的人带来喜悦的兴奋。马里拉不喜欢对自己的想法和感受进行主观分析。她可能想象自己正在思考艾滋、他们的传教士箱和礼拜室的新地毯，但在这些反射下，是一种和谐的意识：红色的田野在夕阳下冒着烟，化为淡紫色的薄雾，长长的、尖锐的冷杉树影落在小溪对面的草地上，静谧的、在镜子般的木池周围发芽的深红色枫树，世界的苏醒和灰色草皮下隐藏的脉动的骚动。大地春意盎然，马瑞拉中年人清醒的脚步更加轻快，因为其中充满了深沉的、原始的快乐。

paragraphs.en: Her eyes dwelt affectionately on Green Gables, peering through its network of trees and reflecting the sunlight back from its windows in several little coruscations of glory. Marilla, as she picked her steps along the damp lane, thought that it was really a satisfaction to know that she was going home to a briskly snapping wood fire and a table nicely spread for tea, instead of to the cold comfort of old Aid meeting evenings before Anne had come to Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: 她的目光深情地注视着绿山墙，透过树木的网络凝视着，将阳光从窗户反射回来，形成几道小小的光辉。玛丽拉沿着潮湿的小巷小心翼翼地迈着脚步，她想，知道自己要回家，面对着熊熊燃烧的柴火，桌子上铺着茶，而不是安妮来绿山墙之前的旧援助会议晚上的寒冷舒适，这真是一种满足。

paragraphs.en: Consequently, when Marilla entered her kitchen and found the fire black out, with no sign of Anne anywhere, she felt justly disappointed and irritated. She had told Anne to be sure and have tea ready at five o'clock, but now she must hurry to take off her second-best dress and prepare the meal herself against Matthew's return from plowing.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，当玛丽拉走进厨房，发现火已经灭了，安妮也不见踪影时，她感到失望和恼怒。她已经告诉安妮一定要在五点钟准备好茶，但现在她必须赶紧脱掉她第二好的衣服，自己准备饭菜，等待马修耕地回来。

paragraphs.en: "I'll settle Miss Anne when she comes home," said Marilla grimly, as she shaved up kindlings with a carving knife and with more vim than was strictly necessary. Matthew had come in and was waiting patiently for his tea in his corner. "She's gadding off somewhere with Diana, writing stories or practicing dialogues or some such tomfoolery, and never thinking once about the time or her duties. She's just got to be pulled up short and sudden on this sort of thing. I don't care if Mrs. Allan does say she's the brightest and sweetest child she ever knew. She may be bright and sweet enough, but her head is full of nonsense and there's never any knowing what shape it'll break out in next. Just as soon as she grows out of one freak she takes up with another. But there! Here I am saying the very thing I was so riled with Rachel Lynde for saying at the Aid today. I was real glad when Mrs. Allan spoke up for Anne, for if she hadn't I know I'd have said something too sharp to Rachel before everybody. Anne's got plenty of faults, goodness knows, and far be it from me to deny it. But I'm bringing her up and not Rachel Lynde, who'd pick faults in the Angel Gabriel himself if he lived in Avonlea. Just the same, Anne has no business to leave the house like this when I told her she was to stay home this afternoon and look after things. I must say, with all her faults, I never found her disobedient or untrustworthy before and I'm real sorry to find her so now."
paragraphs.zh: “等安妮小姐回家，我会解决她的问题。”玛丽拉冷酷地说，同时她用一把切肉刀削掉引火物，语气比严格必要的还要激烈。马修进来了，正在角落里耐心地等着喝茶。 “她和戴安娜一起在某个地方闲逛，写故事或练习对话或诸如此类的蠢事，从来没有考虑过时间或她的职责。她只是在这种事情上突然被拉起来。我不在乎艾伦夫人是否说她是她所认识的最聪明、最可爱的孩子。她可能足够聪明和可爱，但她的脑子里充满了废话，永远不知道它会变成什么样子。就在她从一个怪胎中长大后，她又开始接受另一个怪胎了，我今天在救助站时对雷切尔·林德说的话我感到非常高兴，因为如果她不这样做，我知道我会在大家面前对雷切尔说一些过于尖锐的话，天知道，我绝不会否认这一点。雷切尔·林德，如果天使加百列住在埃文利，他也会挑剔他的。同样，当我告诉安妮今天下午她要留在家里照顾事情时，我必须说，我以前从未发现她不听话或不值得信任，现在我真的很抱歉发现她这样。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I dunno," said Matthew, who, being patient and wise and, above all, hungry, had deemed it best to let Marilla talk her wrath out unhindered, having learned by experience that she got through with whatever work was on hand much quicker if not delayed by untimely argument. "Perhaps you're judging her too hasty, Marilla. Don't call her untrustworthy until you're sure she has disobeyed you. Mebbe it can all be explained—Anne's a great hand at explaining."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我不知道，”马修说，他很有耐心，很聪明，最重要的是，他很饿，他认为最好让玛丽拉不受阻碍地发泄她的愤怒，因为经验告诉她，无论不及时的争论，她都能更快地完成手头的工作。 “也许你对她的判断太仓促了，玛丽拉。在你确定她不服从你之前，不要说她不值得信任。也许这一切都是可以解释的——安妮很擅长解释。”

paragraphs.en: "She's not here when I told her to stay," retorted Marilla. "I reckon she'll find it hard to explain THAT to my satisfaction. Of course I knew you'd take her part, Matthew. But I'm bringing her up, not you."
paragraphs.zh: “当我让她留下来时，她并不在这里，”玛丽拉反驳道。 “我想她会发现很难解释得令我满意。我当然知道你会支持她，马修。但我是在抚养她，而不是你。”

paragraphs.en: It was dark when supper was ready, and still no sign of Anne, coming hurriedly over the log bridge or up Lover's Lane, breathless and repentant with a sense of neglected duties. Marilla washed and put away the dishes grimly. Then, wanting a candle to light her way down the cellar, she went up to the east gable for the one that generally stood on Anne's table. Lighting it, she turned around to see Anne herself lying on the bed, face downward among the pillows.
paragraphs.zh: 晚饭准备好了，天已经黑了，安妮仍然没有踪影，她匆匆走过独木桥或情人巷，气喘吁吁，带着一种被忽视的责任感悔恨不已。玛丽拉洗完盘子，严肃地收起来。然后，她想要一支蜡烛照亮地窖里的路，于是她走到东山墙去拿安妮桌子上通常放的那根蜡烛。点着灯，她转过身，看到安妮自己躺在床上，脸朝下埋在枕头里。

paragraphs.en: "Mercy on us," said astonished Marilla, "have you been asleep, Anne?"
paragraphs.zh: “上帝啊，”玛丽拉惊讶地说，“安妮，你睡着了吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No," was the muffled reply.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”低沉的回答。

paragraphs.en: "Are you sick then?" demanded Marilla anxiously, going over to the bed.
paragraphs.zh: “那你有病吗？”玛丽拉走到床边焦急地问道。

paragraphs.en: Anne cowered deeper into her pillows as if desirous of hiding herself forever from mortal eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮更加蜷缩在枕头里，仿佛渴望永远隐藏自己，避开凡人的目光。

paragraphs.en: "No. But please, Marilla, go away and don't look at me. I'm in the depths of despair and I don't care who gets head in class or writes the best composition or sings in the Sunday-school choir any more. Little things like that are of no importance now because I don't suppose I'll ever be able to go anywhere again. My career is closed. Please, Marilla, go away and don't look at me."
paragraphs.zh: “不。但是，玛丽拉，请走开，别看我。我正处于绝望的深渊，我不在乎谁在课堂上领先，谁写出最好的作文，或者在主日学校唱诗班唱歌。这样的小事现在都不重要了，因为我想我再也不能去任何地方了。我的职业生涯已经结束了。求求你，玛丽拉，走开，别看我。”

paragraphs.en: "Did anyone ever hear the like?" the mystified Marilla wanted to know. "Anne Shirley, whatever is the matter with you? What have you done? Get right up this minute and tell me. This minute, I say. There now, what is it?"
paragraphs.zh: “有人听过类似的话吗？”困惑的玛丽拉想知道。 “安妮·雪莉，你怎么了？你做了什么？马上站起来告诉我。我说，现在就告诉我。现在，怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: Anne had slid to the floor in despairing obedience.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮绝望地顺从地滑到了地板上。

paragraphs.en: "Look at my hair, Marilla," she whispered.
paragraphs.zh: “看看我的头发，玛丽拉，”她低声说道。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, Marilla lifted her candle and looked scrutinizingly at Anne's hair, flowing in heavy masses down her back. It certainly had a very strange appearance.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，玛丽拉举起了蜡烛，仔细地看着安妮的头发，浓密的头发从她的背上垂下来。它的外观确实非常奇怪。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, what have you done to your hair? Why, it's GREEN!"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮雪莉，你对你的头发做了什么？为什么，它是绿色的！”

paragraphs.en: Green it might be called, if it were any earthly color—a queer, dull, bronzy green, with streaks here and there of the original red to heighten the ghastly effect. Never in all her life had Marilla seen anything so grotesque as Anne's hair at that moment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果它是任何地球上的颜色的话，它可以被称为绿色——一种奇怪的、暗淡的、古铜色的绿色，到处都有原来的红色条纹，以增强可怕的效果。玛丽拉一生中从未见过像安妮的头发那样怪异的东西。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, it's green," moaned Anne. "I thought nothing could be as bad as red hair. But now I know it's ten times worse to have green hair. Oh, Marilla, you little know how utterly wretched I am."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，它是绿色的，”安妮呻吟道。 “我以为没有什么比红头发更糟糕了。但现在我知道绿头发的情况要糟糕十倍。哦，玛丽拉，你根本不知道我有多么可怜。”

paragraphs.en: "I little know how you got into this fix, but I mean to find out," said Marilla. "Come right down to the kitchen—it's too cold up here—and tell me just what you've done. I've been expecting something queer for some time. You haven't got into any scrape for over two months, and I was sure another one was due. Now, then, what did you do to your hair?"
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道你是如何解决这个问题的，但我想找出答案，”玛丽拉说。 “快到厨房来吧——这里太冷了——告诉我你做了什么。我已经期待会发生一些奇怪的事情有一段时间了。你已经两个多月没有受过任何擦伤了，我确信又会发生一次。现在，那么，你对你的头发做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: "I dyed it."
paragraphs.zh: “我染的。”

paragraphs.en: "Dyed it! Dyed your hair! Anne Shirley, didn't you know it was a wicked thing to do?"
paragraphs.zh: “染了！染了你的头发！安妮雪莉，你不知道这是一件邪恶的事情吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, I knew it was a little wicked," admitted Anne. "But I thought it was worth while to be a little wicked to get rid of red hair. I counted the cost, Marilla. Besides, I meant to be extra good in other ways to make up for it."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我知道这有点邪恶，”安妮承认。 “但我觉得为了去掉红头发而做点坏事是值得的。我计算过代价，玛丽拉。此外，我还想在其他方面做得特别好来弥补。”

paragraphs.en: "Well," said Marilla sarcastically, "if I'd decided it was worth while to dye my hair I'd have dyed it a decent color at least. I wouldn't have dyed it green."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”玛丽拉讽刺地说，“如果我认为值得染头发，我至少会把它染成像样的颜色。我不会把它染成绿色。”

paragraphs.en: "But I didn't mean to dye it green, Marilla," protested Anne dejectedly. "If I was wicked I meant to be wicked to some purpose. He said it would turn my hair a beautiful raven black—he positively assured me that it would. How could I doubt his word, Marilla? I know what it feels like to have your word doubted. And Mrs. Allan says we should never suspect anyone of not telling us the truth unless we have proof that they're not. I have proof now—green hair is proof enough for anybody. But I hadn't then and I believed every word he said IMPLICITLY."
paragraphs.zh: “但我并不是故意把它染成绿色的，玛丽拉，”安妮沮丧地抗议道。 “如果我是邪恶的，我就意味着为了某种目的而邪恶。他说这会让我的头发变成美丽的乌鸦般的黑色——他肯定地向我保证它会的。我怎么能怀疑他的话，玛丽拉？我知道你的诺言受到怀疑是什么感觉。艾伦太太说，我们永远不应该怀疑有人没有告诉我们真相，除非我们有证据证明他们没有告诉我们真相。我现在有证据了——绿色的头发对任何人来说都足够证明了。但当时我没有，我相信他的每一句话。含蓄地说。”

paragraphs.en: "Who said? Who are you talking about?"
paragraphs.zh: “谁说的？你说谁？”

paragraphs.en: "The peddler that was here this afternoon. I bought the dye from him."
paragraphs.zh: “今天下午来的那个小贩。我从他那里买了染料。”

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley, how often have I told you never to let one of those Italians in the house! I don't believe in encouraging them to come around at all."
paragraphs.zh: “安妮·雪莉，我已经告诉过你多少次了，永远不要让那些意大利人进来！我根本不相信鼓励他们过来。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I didn't let him in the house. I remembered what you told me, and I went out, carefully shut the door, and looked at his things on the step. Besides, he wasn't an Italian—he was a German Jew. He had a big box full of very interesting things and he told me he was working hard to make enough money to bring his wife and children out from Germany. He spoke so feelingly about them that it touched my heart. I wanted to buy something from him to help him in such a worthy object. Then all at once I saw the bottle of hair dye. The peddler said it was warranted to dye any hair a beautiful raven black and wouldn't wash off. In a trice I saw myself with beautiful raven-black hair and the temptation was irresistible. But the price of the bottle was seventy-five cents and I had only fifty cents left out of my chicken money. I think the peddler had a very kind heart, for he said that, seeing it was me, he'd sell it for fifty cents and that was just giving it away. So I bought it, and as soon as he had gone I came up here and applied it with an old hairbrush as the directions said. I used up the whole bottle, and oh, Marilla, when I saw the dreadful color it turned my hair I repented of being wicked, I can tell you. And I've been repenting ever since."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我没让他进屋。我记得你告诉我的话，然后我出去，小心地关上门，看看台阶上他的东西。此外，他不是意大利人——他是德国犹太人。他有一个大盒子，里面装满了非常有趣的东西，他告诉我他正在努力工作，赚足够的钱把他的妻子和孩子从德国带出来。他谈到他们时非常有感情，这触动了我的心。我想从他那里买一些东西来帮助他完成这样一个有价值的目标。然后我突然看到那瓶染发剂，说它可以把任何头发染成漂亮的乌黑，而且洗不掉，一瞬间我就看到了自己的乌黑头发，诱惑是不可抗拒的，但那瓶的价格是七十五美分，我的鸡钱只剩下五十美分了，因为他说，看到是我，他就了。卖掉它只要五十美分，那就等于白送了，他一走我就赶到这里，按照说明用了整瓶，哦，玛丽拉，当我看到它让我的头发变成可怕的颜色时，我就后悔了，我可以告诉你，从那时起我就一直在后悔。”

paragraphs.en: "Well, I hope you'll repent to good purpose," said Marilla severely, "and that you've got your eyes opened to where your vanity has led you, Anne. Goodness knows what's to be done. I suppose the first thing is to give your hair a good washing and see if that will do any good."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我希望你能善意地悔改，”玛丽拉严厉地说，“安妮，希望你能认清自己的虚荣心把你引向了何方。天知道该怎么做。我想第一件事就是把你的头发好好洗一下，看看有没有什么好处。”

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, Anne washed her hair, scrubbing it vigorously with soap and water, but for all the difference it made she might as well have been scouring its original red. The peddler had certainly spoken the truth when he declared that the dye wouldn't wash off, however his veracity might be impeached in other respects.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，安妮洗了头发，用肥皂和水用力擦洗，但尽管如此，她还不如洗掉原来的红色。当小贩宣称染料洗不掉时，他确实说的是实话，但他的真实性可能会在其他方面受到质疑。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, what shall I do?" questioned Anne in tears. "I can never live this down. People have pretty well forgotten my other mistakes—the liniment cake and setting Diana drunk and flying into a temper with Mrs. Lynde. But they'll never forget this. They will think I am not respectable. Oh, Marilla, 'what a tangled web we weave when first we practice to deceive.' That is poetry, but it is true. And oh, how Josie Pye will laugh! Marilla, I CANNOT face Josie Pye. I am the unhappiest girl in Prince Edward Island."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，我该怎么办？”安妮流着泪问道。 “我永远不会忘记这一点。人们已经忘记了我的其他错误——搽剂蛋糕、让戴安娜喝醉以及对林德夫人发脾气。但他们永远不会忘记这一点。他们会认为我不值得尊敬。哦，玛丽拉，‘当我们第一次练习欺骗时，我们编织了多么混乱的网啊。’那是诗，但却是真实的。哦，乔西·派伊会笑得多么开心啊！玛丽拉，我无法面对乔西·派伊。我是爱德华王子岛最不幸福的女孩。”
